nodes.label: Georg Bühler
variants: ゲオルグ・ビューラー
ゲオルク・ビューラー
ヨハン・ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.summary: Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Benfey, Sauppe, Curtius, and Ewald. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (1863–1880) before taking a chair at the University of Vienna.

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der Indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
インド・アーリア文献学・考古学概要

nodes.label: Franz Kielhorn
variants: フランツ・キールホルン
nodes.summary: Franz Kielhorn (1840–1908) was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866–1881) before holding the Indology chair at the University of Göttingen from 1881.

nodes.label: Ernst Kuhn
nodes.image: Ernst Kuhn - Aufsätze zur Kultur- und Sprachgeschichte.jpg
nodes.description: German indologist, linguist, philologist and orientalist (1846–1920)
nodes.summary: Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning degrees at Tübingen and Halle and studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held professorships at Heidelberg (1875) and Munich (1877–1917).

nodes.label: Lucian Scherman
nodes.summary: Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a professor at Munich (c. 1901–1933) and directed the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907).

nodes.label: Ernst Windisch
variants: エルンスト・ヴィルヘルム・オスカー・ヴィンディシュ
エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ernst Windisch completed his doctorate at Leipzig University, studying under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and was a long-serving faculty member at Leipzig.

nodes.label: Willem Caland
variants: ウィレム・カーランド
nodes.summary: Willem Caland was an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Hendrik Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held positions as lecturer of Indology (1903) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906-1929) at Utrecht University, and at Leiden (1913-1914).

nodes.label: Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze
nodes.image: Portrait Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze (Pesne workshop).jpg

nodes.label: August Hermann Francke
nodes.summary: August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Habilitation c. 1921–1922), where he became a Privatdozent in 1922 and an extraordinary professor in 1925.

nodes.label: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres
variants: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres
Akademie der schönen Wissenschaften zu Paris

nodes.label: Alexander Johnston
nodes.summary: Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795) and Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1798), founded the Royal Asiatic Society, and served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

nodes.label: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron
variants: アンクティル・デュペロン
アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.image: David d'Angers - Portrait d'Abraham-Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731-1805), orientaliste.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731–1805) was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Amersfoort Seminary, and under Dastur Darab, later holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, Académie Française, and Institut de France.

nodes.label: Johann III Bernoulli
nodes.summary: Johann III Bernoulli was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Basel, University of Neuchâtel, and under Daniel Bernoulli. He was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Russian Academy of Sciences, and Naturforschende Gesellschaft in Danzig.

nodes.label: Joseph Tiefenthaler
nodes.summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held a post as rector at St. Peter's College, Agra.

nodes.label: James Rennell
nodes.summary: James Rennell was an expert in history and archaeology. He served in the Bengal Engineer Group (1764) and worked as a surveyor for the East India Company from 1764 to 1777, later founding the Royal Geographical Society in 1830.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed
nodes.description: Civilian of the British East India Company (1751-1830)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford (1768). He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

nodes.label: East India Company
variants: イギリス東インド会社

nodes.label: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio, later serving in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), the Congregation of the Index, and the Pontifical Urban University.

nodes.label: University of Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学
オックスフォード大學
Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Charles Wilkins
variants: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.summary: Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha (~1778–1786). He co-founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company and the India Office Library from the 1770s to 1836.

nodes.label: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
variants: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.summary: Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke studied under Citrapati. He served with the East India Company, held a professorship of Sanskrit at Fort William College, sat on the Supreme Council of Bengal, and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society and Royal Astronomical Society.

nodes.label: William Jones
variants: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ (言語学者)
nodes.description: Anglo-Welsh philologist and scholar of ancient India (1746–1794)
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Jones studied at Oxford and Middle Temple under teachers including I'tisam-ud-Din, Swinton, Ramachandra Vidyalankara, and Rāmalocana. He became a barrister, Chief Justice in Fort William (1783), and founded the Asiatic Society.

nodes.id: I:Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
nodes.label: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
variants: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William

nodes.label: Robert Chambers
nodes.summary: Robert Chambers was an Indology scholar who studied at the Royal Grammar School and Lincoln College. At Oxford, he was Vinerian Professor of English Law (1766) and Principal of New Inn Hall (1766). He later served as Chief Justice of Bengal (~1789–1798).

nodes.label: John Shore, 1st Baron Teignmouth
nodes.summary: John Shore, 1st Baron Teignmouth, was active in Indology and history and archaeology. He succeeded William Jones and served as president of the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Fort William College
variants: College von Fort William in Kalkutta
College of Fort William in Calcutta

nodes.label: William Carey
variants: ウィリアム・ケアリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ケアリー (宣教師)
nodes.description: English Baptist missionary and Particular Baptist minister (1761-1834)
nodes.summary: William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma and Ramram Basu (~1793-1801). In 1801, he held a post as Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College.

nodes.label: Otto von Böhtlingk
variants: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.summary: Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

nodes.label: Charles Rieu
nodes.summary: Charles Rieu (1820–1902) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Geneva and Bonn under Lassen, Humbert, Freytag, and Gildemeister, he served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

nodes.label: George Thibaut
nodes.summary: Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Muir Central College, Sanskrit College and University, The Queen's College, Oxford, and served as registrar at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.

nodes.label: Sudhakara Dvivedi
nodes.summary: Sudhakara Dvivedi (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He succeeded Bapu Deva Sastri in 1889 and served as librarian, professor, and head of the mathematics faculty at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1883 to circa 1905.

nodes.label: Horace Hayman Wilson
variants: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.jawiki: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.summary: Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He served the East India Company and Kolkata Mint, and was Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford from 1831 to 1860.

nodes.label: Monier Monier-Williams
variants: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.jawiki: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Oxford. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

nodes.label: Sanskrit College and University
variants: Department of Postgraduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta
Postgraduate Training and Research Department of the Sanskrit College

nodes.label: Vans Kennedy
nodes.description: Scottish major-general of the British Army
nodes.summary: Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general for the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and held the presidency of both the Literary Society of Bombay and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

nodes.label: James Prinsep
variants: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.summary: James Prinsep worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819; 1830–1838) and the Benares Mint (~1820–1830), and led the Asiatic Society from 1832 to 1838.

nodes.label: Arthur Schopenhauer
variants: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
アルトゥール・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.jawiki: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha, Göttingen, Berlin (under Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Böckh, and Friedrich August Wolf), and Jena (PhD ~1813). He held a teaching post at the University of Berlin from ~1820 to 1831.

nodes.label: Paul Regnaud
nodes.summary: Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1869 and held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

nodes.label: École Pratique des Hautes Études
variants: École des Hautes Études in Paris
高等研究実習院第4部門
フランス國立高等研究院
École Pratique des Hautes Études, SHP

nodes.label: John Muir
nodes.summary: John Muir was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, East India Company College, and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Johannes Klatt
nodes.summary: Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned a doctorate at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. From 1872 onward, he held positions at the Berlin State Library, serving as assistant, custodian, and librarian.

nodes.label: Albrecht Weber
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
アルブレヒト・フリードリヒ・ヴェーバー
nodes.jawiki: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Weber was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1845). He served as a Privatdozent and adjunct professor of ancient Indian language and literature at Humboldt University of Berlin across 1848 to 1901.

nodes.label: Ignazio Guidi
nodes.summary: Ignazio Guidi worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

nodes.label: Emilio Teza
nodes.description: Italian translator, indo-europeanist, romanist, orientalist and linguist
nodes.summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller. He worked as a librarian at the Laurentian Library and Biblioteca Marciana, and held professorships at the universities of Bologna, Pisa, and Padua.

nodes.label: Ram Mohan Roy
nodes.image: Portrait of Raja Ram Mohun Roy, 1833.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.description: Indian religious, social, and educational reformer, and humanitarian
nodes.summary: Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded several influential organizations and institutions, including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency College, Kolkata (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

nodes.label: Alexander Hamilton
nodes.summary: Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist. He served at the East India Company College as Professor of Sanskrit in 1806 and as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature in 1808.

nodes.label: Louis-Mathieu Langlès
variants: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.jawiki: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.description: French academic, philologist, linguist, translator, author, librarian and orientalist
nodes.summary: Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Sinology, Indology, and Iranian studies, studying at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and directed the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1795–1824).

nodes.label: Henry Pitts Forster
nodes.summary: Henry Pitts Forster was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served in the East India Company's Bengal service and Bengal Civil Service from 1783 to 1815, and was Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.

nodes.label: Joshua Marshman
variants: ジョシュア・マーシュマン
nodes.summary: Joshua Marshman was an Indologist, sinologist, and linguist. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Hovhannes Ghazarian (~1806–1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Majer
variants: フリードリヒ・マイヤー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Majer specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1790-1794) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1798-1803), serving as a Privatdozent at Jena (~1799-1802).

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried von Herder
variants: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.summary: Herder worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Königsberg under Immanuel Kant. He held posts at the Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, and Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and served as General Superintendent in Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach in 1776.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Schlegel
variants: カール・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・フォン・シュレーゲル
フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, critic and scholar, editor
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Schlegel was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and in Paris under Alexander Hamilton and de Chézy. He later taught at the universities of Jena (1800), Cologne (1804), and TU Dresden (1828).

nodes.label: Bibliothèque nationale de France
variants: Bibliothèque Impériale, Département des Manuscrits Orientaux

nodes.label: East India Company College
variants: College of the Honourable the East India Company, Haileybury
East India Company's College at Haileybury
Honourable East India Company's College, Haileybury
Hon. East India Company's College, Haileybury
British East India Company’s Haileybury College

nodes.label: August Wilhelm von Schlegel
variants: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, translator, critic, and writer (1767–1845)
nodes.summary: August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He became a professor at Jena (1798) and held the first chair of Indology at Bonn (1818).

nodes.label: William Robertson
nodes.description: British historian, minister of religion, and principal of the University of Edinburgh (1721-1793)
nodes.summary: A historian and Indologist, Robertson studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He was appointed Principal of Edinburgh in 1762 and held memberships in the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren
nodes.summary: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian. Educated at the Athenaeum and the University of Göttingen (PhD 1779–1784) under Christian Gottlob Heyne, he taught at Göttingen as Privatdozent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).

nodes.label: Peter von Bohlen
nodes.summary: Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and Berlin under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg starting in 1825.

nodes.label: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier
nodes.summary: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist who studied under traditional teacher Ramachandra Vidyalankara and served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

nodes.label: Othmar Frank
nodes.summary: Othmar Frank (1770–1840) was an indologist who studied at the universities of Paris and London. He held professorships at the universities of Bamberg (~1807–1826), Würzburg (1821), and Munich (1826).

nodes.label: University of Bamberg
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Bamberg

nodes.label: Franz Bopp
nodes.summary: Franz Bopp (1791–1867) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Windischmann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

nodes.label: University of London
variants: Institute of Germanic Studies, University of London
Institute of Germanic Studies in London University

nodes.label: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann
variants: カール・ヴィンディシュマン
nodes.summary: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Würzburg. He taught at Kronberg-Gymnasium Aschaffenburg before becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Windischmann
nodes.summary: Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, Welcker, Niebuhr, Brandis, and K. J. H. Windischmann, and at Munich. He held posts at Munich, Freising, and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.

nodes.label: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
variants: Antoine Isaac, Baron Silvestre de Sacy
アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.summary: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held chairs in Arabic and Persian at INALCO, was Professor of Persian at Collège de France (1806–1838), and founded and presided over the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy
variants: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.summary: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

nodes.label: Collège de France
variants: コレージュ・ド・フランス
Institute of Indian Civilization of the University of Paris
コレジュ・ド・フランス
Centre d'études tibétaines am Collège de France
Institute of Tibetan Studies of the Collège de France

nodes.label: University of Göttingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Buddhismuskunde, Universität Göttingen

nodes.label: Wilhelm von Humboldt
variants: Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Carl Ferdinand von Humboldt
Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Karl Ferdinand von Humboldt
ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
カール・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.description: Prussian philosopher, government official, diplomat, and educator (1767–1835)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, and Jena, and under teachers including Engel, Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy, later holding a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Ernst Siecke
nodes.description: born:1846|died:1935|; Siecke, Ernst (Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl), 1846-; Siecke, Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl, 1846-1935

nodes.label: Alexandre Langlois
nodes.summary: Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He taught at the Lycée Charlemagne, served as an inspector for the Académie de Paris, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat
variants: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later holding the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

nodes.label: Jean-Louis Burnouf
variants: ジャン＝ルイ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Jean-Louis Burnouf was a linguist who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1817) and was Chair of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).

nodes.label: Eugène Burnouf
variants: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.jawiki: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A pupil of Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832), he served at the Collège de France (1832–1852) and the Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852).

nodes.label: Christian Gottlob Heyne
nodes.summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne worked in linguistics and history. After completing his master's degree at Leipzig University (1748–1752), he served at the University of Göttingen as Professor der Beredsamkeit und Dichtkunst (1763) and as director of its library (1764–1812).

nodes.label: Christian Lassen
variants: クリスチャン・ラッセン
nodes.jawiki: クリスチャン・ラッセン (東洋学者)
nodes.summary: Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at the University of Bonn. He spent his career at Bonn, serving as Privatdozent in 1830 and as professor of Old Indian language and literature from 1840 to 1876.

nodes.label: Paul Deussen
variants: パウル・ヤーコプ・ドイセン
nodes.summary: Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Christian Lassen and completed his Habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he served as Privatdocent (1881–1887) before becoming a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

nodes.label: Otto Strauß
nodes.summary: Otto Strauß specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Berlin, Munich, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He served as professor at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

nodes.label: Société Asiatique
variants: フランスのアジア協会

nodes.label: Alexander von Humboldt
variants: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.image: Stieler, Joseph Karl - Alexander von Humboldt - 1843.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.summary: Alexander von Humboldt worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the Universities of Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen (under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg), Jena, and TU Bergakademie Freiberg, later holding a post at the University of Jena.

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Freytag
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フライターク
nodes.summary: Georg Wilhelm Freytag worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1807–1811) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1815–1819), later holding posts at Göttingen (1811–1813), Königsberg (~1812–1814), and the University of Bonn (1819–1861).

nodes.label: University of Königsberg
variants: ケーニヒスベルク大学

nodes.label: Theodor Goldstücker
variants: テオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.summary: Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and Paris under von Bohlen, Rosenkranz, Lassen, and Burnouf. He served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London and University of London from 1851 to 1872.

nodes.label: Friedrich Rückert
variants: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
ヨーハン・ミヒャエル・フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.description: German poet, translator, and professor of Oriental languages (1788–1866)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Bopp and von Hammer-Purgstall. He held posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826), and Berlin (1841-1849).

nodes.label: Adolf Holtzmann the Elder
nodes.summary: Adolf Holtzmann the Elder was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Johann Andreas Schmeller
nodes.summary: Johann Andreas Schmeller was a linguistics scholar who studied at Königliches Erziehungsinstitut für Studierende. He held positions at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (1814–1826), Bavarian State Library (1829), and as a professor at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Heidelberg University
variants: South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University

nodes.label: Salomon Lefmann
nodes.summary: Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Berlin (Ph.D. ~1864) and attended Münster, Paris, and Heidelberg. He taught Sanskrit at Heidelberg University as an associate professor (1870) and honorary professor (1901).

nodes.label: Friedrich August Rosen
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Friedrich August Rosen studied at Leipzig and Berlin, the latter under Franz Bopp. He was a professor of oriental languages at University College London (1828–1831) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

nodes.label: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler
variants: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.jawiki: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and others. He worked at the India Office Library and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833–1872).

nodes.label: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Caussin de Perceval, and de Chézy. He held the chair of oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

nodes.label: Franz Ferdinand Benary
nodes.summary: Franz Ferdinand Benary (1805–1880) studied Indology at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin as a lecturer from 1829 and as an associate professor in theology from 1831.

nodes.label: Agathon Benary
nodes.summary: Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He served as a gymnasium teacher at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and became a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1839.

nodes.label: Köllnisches Gymnasium
variants: ケルン・ギムナジウム

nodes.label: Bernhard Hirzel
nodes.summary: Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, under Franz Bopp at Berlin (~1830–1832), Göttingen (~1832–1833), and Paris (~1833–1835). He held posts as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

nodes.label: Hermann Brockhaus
variants: ヘルマン・ブロックハウス
nodes.summary: Hermann Brockhaus was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel, later holding professorships at the University of Jena (1839) and Leipzig University (~1841-1877).

nodes.label: University of Zurich
variants: Völkerkundemuseum of the University of Zurich
Institute for Social Anthropology and Empirical Cultural Studies at the University of Zurich

nodes.label: Georg Martin Dursch
nodes.summary: Georg Martin Dursch (1800–1881) studied theology, philosophy, and Indology at the University of Tübingen and the University of Paris under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. In 1829, he became a professor at the Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Adelung
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Leipzig University (1787-1790), he held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), and administrative posts at the University of Vienna (1824) and Utrecht University (1825).

nodes.label: Johann Christoph Adelung
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・クリストフ・アーデルング
nodes.summary: Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguist who studied at Kloster Berge school and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts as a professor at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and chief librarian at Dresden's Saxon State Library (1787).

nodes.label: Colin Mackenzie
nodes.image: Colonel Colin Mackenzie and his Indian pandits by Thomas Hickey.jpg
nodes.summary: Colin Mackenzie was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.

nodes.label: William Ward
variants: ウィリアム・ウォード
nodes.description: English pioneer Baptist missionary, author, printer and translator
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Ward studied at Ewood Hall Academy (1797). He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Claude-Auguste Court
nodes.summary: Claude-Auguste Court was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr and served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army.

nodes.label: École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr
variants: サン・シール陸軍士官学校

nodes.label: George Turnour
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ターナー (歴史家)
nodes.summary: George Turnour was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service, becoming a Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

nodes.label: John Wilson
nodes.description: Christian missionary, orientalist, and educator in Maharashtra, India (1804-1875)
nodes.summary: John Wilson worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, and was educated at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He served as president of the Literary Society of Bombay (~1835–1842) and vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

nodes.label: Brian Houghton Hodgson
variants: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.image: Brian Houghton Hodgson by Louisa Starr-Canziani.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an indologist, tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at The King's School, Macclesfield, East India Company College, and Fort William College, he served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (~1833–1843).

nodes.label: Bhagwanlal Indraji
nodes.summary: Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in ~1884. He was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society (1877), a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (1882), and a member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Charles Masson
nodes.description: British East India Company soldier and explorer (1800–1853)

nodes.label: Edwin Norris
nodes.summary: Active in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology, Edwin Norris worked at the East India Company (1818–1837) and the Foreign Office (1847–1866). He also served as assistant secretary (1836) and Assistant-Honorary Secretary and Honorary Librarian (1856–1861) at the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Edward Upham
nodes.summary: Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Between approximately 1824 and 1834, he was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

nodes.label: Francis Wilford
nodes.summary: Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was a fellow member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Eugène Jacquet
nodes.summary: Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1828–1832) and Eugène Burnouf (~1832–1838).

nodes.label: Daniel Wright
nodes.description: Scottish surgeon and physician; resided in Nepal

nodes.label: William Wright
nodes.summary: William Wright worked in linguistics, studying at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held posts at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and was Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1870–1889).

nodes.label: Hendrik Kern
nodes.summary: Hendrik Kern studied at Utrecht, Leiden (doctorate under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Athenaeum Maastricht (1858–1862), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865), and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

nodes.label: Bunyiu Nanjio
nodes.summary: Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, studied at Oxford under Max Müller. He taught at the University of Tokyo and served as head of Otani University and rector of Ryukoku University (~1914–1923).

nodes.label: Edward Byles Cowell
variants: エドワード・バイルズ・コウェル
nodes.image: Portrait of Edward Byles Cowell by Charles Edmund Brock-1905.jpg
nodes.summary: Edward Byles Cowell studied at Magdalen College and the University of Oxford (1850-1854) under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian studies, he held posts at Presidency College, Calcutta, and Cambridge (1867-1903).

nodes.label: Julius Eggeling
nodes.summary: Julius Eggeling studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber at Breslau and Berlin. He taught Sanskrit at University College London (1872-1875) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1875-1914).

nodes.label: Robert Alexander Neil
nodes.image: R A Neil-R H Lord recto.tif
nodes.summary: Robert Alexander Neil was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Aberdeen under William Duguid Geddes and at Peterhouse, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, later serving as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884.

nodes.label: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma
variants: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.jawiki: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.summary: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen, and with traditional teachers in Tibet, later serving as librarian at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Isaak Jakob Schmidt
nodes.summary: Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire
nodes.description: French philosopher, journalist, statesman, and possible illegitimate son of Napoleon I of France (1805-1895)
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire studied at Bourbon College and Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838-1852).

nodes.id: I:Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
nodes.label: Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
variants: Académie des Sciences morales et politiques
Academy of Moral and Political Science

nodes.label: Julius Mohl
nodes.summary: Julius Mohl studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat in Paris. A scholar of Sinology and Iranian studies, he held professorships at the University of Tübingen (1826-1834) and the Collège de France (1847-1876).

nodes.label: Stanislas Julien
variants: エニャン＝スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.summary: Stanislas Julien, a sinologist and Indologist, studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France. He held posts at the Institut de France, Bibliothèque nationale, INALCO, and was Chair of Chinese at the Collège de France (1832-1873).

nodes.label: Robert Lenz
nodes.summary: Robert Lenz was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Tartu, Dorpat, and Humboldt University under Franz Bopp, he served at Ritter- und Domschule zu Reval (~1828–1830), Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Saint Petersburg State University
variants: Faculty of Oriental Languages at St. Petersburg
Faculty of Oriental languages at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Gaspare Gorresio
nodes.image: Gaspare Gorresio, post 1869 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0015 B.jpg
nodes.summary: Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the Diocesan Seminary of Mondovi and the University of Turin under Amedeo Peyron, later studying under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at Turin's Military Academy, University, and Royal Library.

nodes.label: Émile-Louis Burnouf
nodes.summary: An Indology and linguistics scholar, Émile-Louis Burnouf studied at ENS, University of Paris, and École française d'Athènes under Jean-Louis Burnouf and Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the University of Nancy (1854–1867) and directed the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

nodes.label: Théodore Pavie
nodes.image: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896), Orientalist, friend of the artist MET 31523.jpg
nodes.summary: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was an Indology and Sinology scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held the Sanskrit professorship at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

nodes.label: Adolphe Regnier
nodes.summary: Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology and linguistics and studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France (1838), the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), and served as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau from 1873.

nodes.label: Abel Bergaigne
variants: アベル・ベルゲーニュ
nodes.summary: Abel Bergaigne (1838–1888) was a French Indologist and linguist. He studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877) and the University of Paris as lecturer (1877) and professor (1885).

nodes.label: Theodor Benfey
variants: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.summary: Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen, completing his Ph.D. (~1828) and Habilitation (~1834). At Göttingen, he served as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

nodes.label: Friedrich Max Müller
variants: マックス・ミューラー
フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.description: German-born British philologist, orientalist and indologist (1823–1900)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Schelling, and Burnouf, and under Wilson. His main posts included professorships at the University of Oxford from 1854.

nodes.label: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud
nodes.summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1824-1858), INALCO (1838), and as president of the Société Asiatique (1847, 1852).

nodes.label: Heinrich Ewald
nodes.description: German orientalist, theologian, and Biblical exegete (1803–1875)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Ewald worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Göttingen under Eichhorn, Tychsen, and the Plancks, earning a doctorate in 1823. He served as professor at Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Ernst Trumpp
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・トランプ
nodes.summary: Ernst Trumpp was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Rudolf von Roth. After assisting at East India House, he became Privatdozent at Tübingen in 1871 and Professor at the University of Munich from around 1874 to 1885.

nodes.label: August Schleicher
variants: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.summary: August Schleicher was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others. He held academic posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (from 1850), and the University of Jena (1857).

nodes.label: Moritz Abraham Stern
variants: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.summary: Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist who studied under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller at Göttingen. He served as an extraordinarius professor at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

nodes.label: Rudolf von Roth
variants: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.jawiki: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.summary: Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald and in Paris under Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

nodes.label: William Dwight Whitney
variants: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.summary: William Dwight Whitney worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, and Roth, he held posts at Yale University as Professor of Sanskrit (1853, 1869-1894) and the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: James Tod
nodes.description: 1782-1835, English officer of the British East India Company and an Oriental scholar
nodes.summary: James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1798–1799) and under Yati Gyan Chandra (~1812–1822), serving with the East India Company (~1799–1822) and the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

nodes.id: I:Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
variants: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain

nodes.label: Adalbert Kuhn
variants: フランツ・フェーリクス・アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.jawiki: アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.summary: Adalbert Kuhn (1812–1881) was a German Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He had a long career at Köllnisches Gymnasium from 1837, serving as teacher, professor, and director, and was elected to the Russian and Prussian academies.

nodes.label: Andrzej Gawroński
nodes.summary: Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902-1906) and Leipzig University (~1903-1906). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916-1917) and the University of Lviv (1917), which he also founded.

nodes.label: Thomas Stamford Raffles
variants: トーマス・スタンフォード・ラッフルズ
nodes.summary: Thomas Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) was an administrator and scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He joined the East India Company in 1795, founded the Zoological Society of London (1825–1825), and served as its president in 1826.

nodes.label: John Crawfurd
nodes.summary: Working in linguistics, history, and archaeology, Crawfurd studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1801–1803). He served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and succeeded Thomas Stamford Raffles in 1823.

nodes.label: James Fergusson
nodes.summary: James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and held a post as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.

nodes.label: Christoph Theodosius Walther
nodes.summary: Christoph Theodosius Walther was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

nodes.label: Leipzig University
variants: ライプツィヒ大学インド学・中央アジア学研究所
Department of Indology and Central Asian Studies, University of Leipzig
Institute for the Study of Religions at Leipzig University
Sanskrit-Abteilung des Indogermanischen Forschungsinstituts der Königl. Sächsischen Forschungsinstitute zu Leipzig

nodes.label: Friedrich Bollensen
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bollensen, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied theology and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen. He later held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1851) and as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Geiger
nodes.native: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned his PhD and Habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel. He served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1891) and the University of Munich (1920–1924).

nodes.label: Friedrich von Spiegel
variants: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
フリードリヒ・（フォン・）シュピーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian and Indology scholar. He studied at Erlangen, Leipzig, Bonn, and Jena under Brockhaus, Rückert, Fleischer, Kinkel, and Lassen. He served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

nodes.label: Heinrich Uhle
nodes.summary: Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University (~1861–1867) under Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post teaching classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

nodes.label: Eduard Sachau
nodes.summary: Eduard Sachau (1845–1930) was an Orientalist and linguist. Educated at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke, he held professorships at the University of Vienna and the University of Berlin, and directed the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen.

nodes.label: Hermann Camillo Kellner
nodes.summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1866-1870). He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau (~1868-1904).

nodes.label: Kreuzschule
variants: Dresden College of the Sacred Cross

nodes.label: Richard Fritzsche
nodes.summary: Richard Fritzsche (born 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus between ~1873 and 1877. He served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (attested 1976).

nodes.label: University of Marburg
variants: マールブルク大学大学院

nodes.label: Niels Ludvig Westergaard
variants: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.image: Niels Ludvig Westergaard by Budtz Müller.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.summary: Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen as lektor (1844), full professor (1850), and rektor (1867–1868).

nodes.label: Albert Hoefer
nodes.summary: Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and the Humboldt University of Berlin (doctorate 1832–1837; habilitation ~1839–1840). He spent his academic career at the University of Greifswald, serving as professor from around 1840 to 1883.

nodes.label: University of Greifswald
variants: グライフスヴァルト大学

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
variants: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten studied under Ernst Moritz Arndt, Hermann Baier, at Greifswald, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Greifswald (adjunct 1815, professor 1824–1850) and Jena (professor 1817–1824).

nodes.label: Siegfried Samson Goldschmidt
nodes.summary: Siegfried Samson Goldschmidt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867) under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He became an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

nodes.label: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
variants: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca
variants: Anton Edmund Xavier Evarist Wollheim da Fonseca
nodes.image: PPN663949858 Bildnis von Anton Eduard Wollheim Dafonseca.jpg
nodes.summary: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca specialized in Indology and linguistics. After earning his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1828–1831), he lectured there on Oriental and modern Western languages (1849–1852) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Richard Pischel
variants: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.jawiki: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.summary: Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Kiel University (1875), Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908), and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

nodes.label: Alfred Hillebrandt
nodes.summary: Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He held associate and full professorships at the University of Breslau between 1883 and 1902.

nodes.label: Adalbert Bezzenberger
nodes.summary: Adalbert Bezzenberger (1851–1922) was a German linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, where he was a Privatdozent (1874) before becoming professor (1879) and later rector (1919–1921) at the University of Königsberg.

nodes.label: Hermann Oldenberg
variants: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.summary: Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889-1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

nodes.label: Jacob Wackernagel
variants: ヤコブ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Jacob Wackernagel studied at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford, learning from Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

nodes.label: Leo Meyer
nodes.summary: Leo Meyer (1830-1910) was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Benfey, Grimm, and Bopp. He served as a professor at the University of Göttingen (1862-1865, chair in 1898) and held the chair of German and comparative linguistics at Tartu/Dorpat (1865-1899).

nodes.label: Hermann Collitz
nodes.summary: Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under August Fick. He served on the faculty at Bryn Mawr College (1885-1907) and held the chair of Germanic Philology at Johns Hopkins University (1907-1928).

nodes.label: Friedrich Bechtel
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bechtel, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He worked as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) before becoming professor of comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg in 1895.

nodes.label: Berthold Delbrück
variants: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
ベルトルト・グスタフ・ゴットリープ・デルブリュック
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
nodes.description: German comparative linguist and Sanskrit scholar (1842–1922)
nodes.summary: Berthold Delbrück was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Halle and Berlin under Pott, Weber, Haym, Bopp, and Steinthal. He served as Privatdozent at Halle (1867–1870) and held a chair at the University of Jena (1870–1913).

nodes.label: University of Copenhagen
variants: University of Copenhagen, Department of Asian Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, University of Copenhagen
Center for Subjectivity Research at the University of Copenhagen

nodes.label: KU Leuven
variants: ルーヴァン・カトリック大学東洋学科
ルーヴァン・カトリック大学

nodes.label: August Leskien
variants: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.summary: August Leskien worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He taught at Göttingen and Jena before his long professorship at Leipzig University (1870, 1876–1915).

nodes.label: Leopold von Schroeder
nodes.summary: Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Tartu (1882, 1890), the University of Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (1899).

nodes.label: Anton Schiefner
variants: フランツ・アントン・シーフナー
nodes.summary: Anton Schiefner studied law at Saint Petersburg State University and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin. Active in Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology, he held posts at Saint Petersburg First Gymnasium, the Roman Catholic Theological Academy, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Carl Cappeller
nodes.summary: Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD), and Jena (Habilitation). In 1875, he became a professor at the University of Jena.

nodes.label: Karl Rosenkranz
variants: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied under G. W. F. Hegel in Berlin and at Halle and Heidelberg. He held an extraordinariat at Halle before taking a chair at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

nodes.label: Raymond West
variants: レイモンド・ウェスト
nodes.summary: Raymond West was an Indologist and jurist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1887–1892), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (~1895–1907).

nodes.label: University of Tübingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft, Universität Tübingen

nodes.label: Tübinger Stift
variants: テュービンゲン神学校

nodes.label: Martin Haug
nodes.summary: Martin Haug (1827–1876) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Deccan College (1859–1866) and the University of Munich, where he was appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology in 1868.

nodes.label: Karl Friedrich Geldner
variants: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner (1852–1929) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later holding posts at Tübingen, Halle, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Marburg (1907–1921).

nodes.label: Bruno Lindner
nodes.summary: Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig University and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as a Privatdozent at Leipzig University from 1878 to 1919.

nodes.label: Richard von Garbe
nodes.summary: Richard von Garbe was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Marienstiftsgymnasium, the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Hermann Günther Grassmann, and the University of Königsberg. He held posts at Königsberg and succeeded Roth at Tübingen (1895–1927).

nodes.label: Maurice Bloomfield
variants: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman, completing his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1878–1879). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

nodes.label: Julius Grill
nodes.summary: Julius Grill studied at the University of Tübingen and under Rudolf von Roth, earning a licentiate from Jena. A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he was Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at Tübingen (1888-1913).

nodes.label: Adolf Kaegi
nodes.summary: Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen, learning under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He spent his career at the University of Zurich, eventually serving as Ordinarius from 1893 to 1914.

nodes.label: Heinrich Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Scherer, Goldschmidt, Roth, Windisch, and Weber at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Berlin. He held professorships at Greifswald (1881), Heidelberg, and Berlin (chair of Celtic languages, 1901–1910).

nodes.label: Theodor Aufrecht
variants: テーオドール・アウフレヒト
nodes.summary: Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his dissertation at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He served as Privatdozent at Berlin (1850), worked at the Bodleian Library (1852), and held professorships at Edinburgh (1861–1875) and Bonn (1875–1889).

nodes.label: Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung
variants: Zeitschrift für Vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete des Deutschen, Griechischen und Lateinischen
Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiet der indogermanischen Sprachen
ドイツ、ギリシア、ラテン語比較研究誌

nodes.label: Wilhelm Schulze
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Schulze studied linguistics and Indology at Berlin under Schmidt, and at Greifswald under Zimmer, Kiessling, Kaibel, and Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held chairs at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1932), succeeding Schmidt.

nodes.label: Johannes Schmidt
variants: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.jawiki: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.summary: Johannes Schmidt worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Bonn, Jena, and under August Schleicher and Albrecht Weber. He held professorial posts at the University of Bonn (1868), University of Graz (1873–1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1876).

nodes.label: Gottfried Hermann
nodes.image: Gottfried Hermann, von Carl Christian Vogel von Vogelstein.jpg
nodes.summary: Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena, later serving at Leipzig University as an extraordinary professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

nodes.label: Moriz Haupt
nodes.summary: Moriz Haupt was a German linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig University. He served as a professor at Leipzig (1843–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1853), and as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Anton Westermann
nodes.summary: Anton Westermann studied at Leipzig University from 1825 to 1830. He subsequently served as co-director at Leipzig University from 1830 to 1865, where he taught Friedrich Max Müller.

nodes.label: Reinhold Klotz
nodes.summary: Reinhold Klotz was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University (1826–1831), where he served as assistant professor from 1832 and außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
variants: フリードリヒ・ヴィルヘルム・ヨーゼフ・フォン・シェリング
フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.image: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, 1848 daguerreotype - cropped.jpg
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798-1803), Würzburg (1803-1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820-1827), Munich (1827-1841), and Berlin (1841-1845), and led the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Hermann Brunnhofer
nodes.summary: Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, under Albrecht Weber, and completed a PhD at Zurich. His posts included Gymnasium Goldingen, University of Oxford, Saint Petersburg State University, and University of Bern (1901-1914).

nodes.label: Moriz Winternitz
variants: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.summary: Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist scholar who studied at Vienna under Georg Bühler and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the Association for Women in Oxford, Visva-Bharati University, and the German University of Prague (circa 1902–1934).

nodes.label: James Robert Ballantyne
nodes.summary: James Robert Ballantyne specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and under James Michael and Francis Johnson, later serving at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1841; 1845–1861) and as librarian for the India Office (~1861–1864).

nodes.label: Jean-Baptiste Biot
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at École Polytechnique. He served in the French Revolutionary Army and held professorships at École Centrale de Beauvais, the Collège de France, and the Science Faculty of Paris.

nodes.label: Ebenezer Burgess
nodes.description: United States missionary to the Mahrattas, in western India

nodes.label: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen
variants: Christian Charles Josias, Baron von Bunsen
nodes.summary: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen, Leiden, Copenhagen, and Munich, learning under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and founded the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

nodes.label: Ludwig Noire
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ
nodes.image: Plate 13 Ludwig Noiré, Photograph album of German and Austrian scientists (cropped).png
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ

nodes.label: Louis Havet
nodes.summary: Linguist Louis Havet studied at EPHE under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology department chair at the Collège de France (1885–1925) and vice-president of Association Guillaume Budé (1917).

nodes.label: Kenju Kasahara
nodes.summary: Kenju Kasahara (1851-1883) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and under Friedrich Max Müller (1879-1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell (~1879-1882).

nodes.label: Heinrich Wenzel
nodes.summary: Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Jena, earned a PhD at Tübingen, and completed his habilitation at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz, while also studying under Jäschke, Feer, and Max Müller. He habilitated at Leipzig in 1887.

nodes.label: Heinrich August Jäschke
variants: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.summary: Heinrich August Jäschke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1857 to 1868.

nodes.label: Bruno Liebich
nodes.summary: Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) was an Indologist. He studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen, completed his Habilitation at Breslau, and studied at Munich. He held posts at the University of Breslau (1921–1928) and Heidelberg University (~1921–1939).

nodes.label: Archibald Edward Gough
nodes.description: (1845-1915) British educationalist, translator, editor and academic administrator
nodes.summary: Archibald Edward Gough studied under Monier Monier-Williams before serving as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878). In Indology and philosophy, he later worked as Professor of Philosophy at Presidency College, Kolkata, and Principal of Aliah University (both ~1881–1895).

nodes.label: John Pickford
nodes.summary: John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a professor at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: University of Madras
variants: Department of Sanskrit, University of Madras
Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy
Department of Sanskrit in the University of Madras
Centre of Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras

nodes.label: Ralph T. H. Griffith
nodes.summary: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 1849 and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from approximately 1861 to 1876.

nodes.label: Robert Needham Cust
nodes.summary: Robert Needham Cust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1843–1867).

nodes.label: Aliah University
variants: Madrassa, il Collegio maomettano di Calcutta
カルカッタ・マドラサ・ムスリム・カレッジ
カルカッタ・マドラサ

nodes.label: James Sutherland Cotton
nodes.summary: James Sutherland Cotton specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Brighton College, Winchester College, and Trinity College, Oxford, he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and The Queen's College, Oxford (both 1871–1874).

nodes.label: William Wilson Hunter
variants: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.summary: An Indologist and historian, Hunter studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887), became Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886), and vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1895–1900).

nodes.label: Indian Institute, University of Oxford
variants: Indian Institute at the University of Oxford

nodes.label: University of Edinburgh
variants: Professur für Sanskrit und vergleichende Sprachwissenschaft an der Universität zu Edinburg

nodes.label: Adolf Kirchhoff
nodes.summary: Adolf Kirchhoff was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Böckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium before serving as ordinary professor at the University of Berlin from 1865 until around 1908.

nodes.label: Hermann Jacobi
variants: ヘルマン・ゲオルク・ヤコービ
nodes.summary: Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Berlin and Bonn under Albrecht Weber and Johann Gildemeister. He held professorships at the University of Münster (1876-1885), Kiel University (1885), and the University of Bonn (1889-1922).

nodes.label: Jarl Charpentier
nodes.summary: Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Hermann Jacobi, serving as Assistant Professor (1908), Deputy Professor (1925), and Professor (1927) at Uppsala.

nodes.label: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
variants: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.image: Young India; an interpretation and a history of the nationalist movement from within (1916) (14781987942).jpg
nodes.jawiki: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.description: Indian nationalist leader, writer and journalist (1856–1920)
nodes.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Deccan College and Government Law College, Mumbai. He taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and served as a mathematics teacher at Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

nodes.label: Reinhold Rost
nodes.image: Reinhold Rost, Porträt mit Signatur, um 1890.jpg
nodes.summary: Reinhold Rost was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He taught at St Augustine's College and served as Head Librarian at the India Office (1869–1893).

nodes.label: Heinrich Kiepert
nodes.description: German geographer, cartographer and university professor in Berlin (1818–1899)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Kiepert was a geographer and historian who studied at Frederick William University Berlin under August Böckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann, earning a doctorate at Jena. He worked at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and served as professor of geography at Berlin from 1874.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Deecke
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (1848–1849). He later served as director or head at Ernestinenschule, Gymnase Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée Lambert.

nodes.label: Ferdinand von Eckstein
nodes.summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1810–1812), was a member of the Société Asiatique (~1822–1861), and founded Le Catholique in 1826.

nodes.label: Ghent University
variants: Centre for Buddhist Studies, Ghent University

nodes.label: Josef Schick
nodes.summary: Josef Schick worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied under Albrecht Weber, at the University of Tübingen (~1878-1882), and earned a PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin (1887-1889), later holding posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and Munich (1896-1925).

nodes.label: Michael Viggo Fausbøll
variants: ミケール・ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.jawiki: ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.description: Danish educator, translator, orientalist and linguist (1821–1908)
nodes.summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was a Danish Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, he served there as an assistant librarian in 1861 and as professor of Indian philology from 1878 to 1902.

nodes.label: Emil Sieg
nodes.summary: Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Kiel, Berlin (PhD) under Albrecht Weber, and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: Walther Schubring
variants: ヴァルター・シュブリング
nodes.summary: Walther Schubring (1881–1969) was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann and earned his doctorate at Strasbourg. He worked at the Berlin State Library and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg from 1920 to 1951.

nodes.label: Ernst Leumann
variants: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Ernst Leumann studied at Zurich, Geneva, Berlin, Leipzig, and Strasbourg under Albrecht Weber. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford, became professor (1884) and rector (1909–1910) at Strasbourg, and later served as honorary professor at Freiburg.

nodes.label: Luigi Suali
nodes.summary: Luigi Suali was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi, and held a long-standing academic post at the University of Pavia from around 1907 to 1951.

nodes.label: Helmuth von Glasenapp
variants: ヘルムート・フォン・グラーゼナップ
nodes.summary: Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, and occupied chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

nodes.label: Yale University
variants: Yale University's Interdisciplinary Center for Bioethics
Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures at Yale University
Sheffield Scientific School at New Haven

nodes.label: Edward Elbridge Salisbury
nodes.summary: Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and under Woolsey, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Burnouf, Bopp, and Lassen. Active in Indology and linguistics, he was professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841-1854) and president of AOS.

nodes.label: Charles Rockwell Lanman
nodes.image: Charles Rockwell Lanman Professor of Sanskrit Harvard.jpg
nodes.summary: Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Yale and in Germany under Whitney, Weber, Roth, Curtius, and Leskien, he taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as professor at Harvard University (1880–1926).

nodes.label: John Avery
nodes.summary: John Avery was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Amherst, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

nodes.label: Ernst Haas
nodes.summary: Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, as well as at Bonn and Tübingen. He joined the British Museum in 1866 and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.

nodes.label: British Museum
variants: Department of Coins and Medals, the British Museum
Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum
Department of Oriental Antiquities, The British Museum
Department of Manuscripts der Bibliothek des British Museum
Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum

nodes.label: University College London
variants: Wellcome Trust Centre for the History of Medicine at University College London
Wellcome Trust Centre for the study of the History of Medicine at University College London
Institute of Archaeology, University of London

nodes.label: Wilhelm Pertsch
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Pertsch studied under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and at Berlin and Tübingen. A scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held leadership posts at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, Münzkabinett Gotha, and Wissenschaftliche Anstalten auf Schloss Friedenstein.

nodes.label: Fritz Johaentgen
nodes.summary: Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Hermann Günther Grassmann
nodes.summary: Hermann Günther Grassmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held teaching posts at several schools, serving as a professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium (~1836-1877; 1852).

nodes.label: Alfred Ludwig
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under scholars including Albrecht Weber. He qualified at Vienna in 1858 and served as a professor at Charles University from 1860 to 1871.

nodes.label: University of Vienna
variants: ウィーン大学インド学研究所
Institut für Indologie der Universität Wien

nodes.label: Friedrich Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・ミューラー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, under Anton Boller, and at Göttingen and Tübingen. He held posts at the Vienna University Library, Austrian National Library, and University of Vienna (1858-1898).

nodes.label: Anton Boller
nodes.summary: Anton Boller was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences as a corresponding member in 1848 and served at the University of Vienna from 1845, becoming professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Scherer
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Scherer studied at Vienna and Berlin under Moriz Haupt and Franz Bopp. A linguist, he held posts at the University of Vienna (1864; 1868–1872), the University of Strasbourg (1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1877).

nodes.label: University of Cambridge
variants: Mongolia and Inner Asia Studies Unit
Department of East Asian Studies of the University of Cambridge
Department of Social Anthropology at the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Edward Granville Browne
variants: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.summary: Edward Granville Browne studied at Newcastle, Cambridge, and St Bartholomew's under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. A scholar of Iranian studies, linguistics, and history, he became lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Franz Heinrich Trithen
nodes.summary: Franz Heinrich Trithen (1820–1854) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (circa 1844–1848) and was a professor of modern languages at Oxford (circa 1848–1854).

nodes.label: Friedrich Haag
nodes.description: Swiss classical philologist, linguist and teacher (1846-1914)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Haag worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, as well as at Göttingen and Berlin. His academic posts included Dozent at Zurich (1873-1884) and professor of classical philology at Bern (1887; 1891-1906).

nodes.label: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler
nodes.summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Hirzel, von Orelli, and Sauppe. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl (~1841–1889) and became Zurich's full professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics in 1864.

nodes.id: I:Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
nodes.label: Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
Georg Curtius
variants: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Ritschl, Lassen, Bopp, and Schlegel. He held professorships at Charles University (1849–1854), Kiel (1854–1862), and Leipzig University (1862–1885).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg, he held posts at Halle (~1829-1833), Breslau (1834), the University of Bonn (1839), and Leipzig University (~1865-1875).

nodes.label: Friedrich Karl Theodor Zarncke
nodes.summary: Friedrich Karl Theodor Zarncke worked in linguistics. He studied at Rostock and Leipzig, where he learned under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. At Leipzig University, he served as Privatdozent (1852) and Rektor (1869-1882).

nodes.label: Walter Elliot
nodes.summary: Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837–1842).

nodes.label: Hermann Reich
nodes.description: German writer, literary scholar and classical philologist

nodes.label: Johannes Hertel
