nodes.summary: Johannes Hertel studied at Leipzig University (1892–1897). In the field of Indology, he held a professorship at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (circa 1898–1920) and held the chair for Indian Philology at Leipzig University from 1919 to 1937.

nodes.label: August Friedrich Pott
variants: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.summary: August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. After lecturing in Berlin, he spent his career at Halle-Wittenberg as professor of general linguistics from 1833 and ordentlicher Professor from 1838.

nodes.label: Karl Brugmann
variants: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.jawiki: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.summary: Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Georg Curtius at Leipzig and Halle, later serving as an Ordinarius at the University of Freiburg (1884) and Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Leipzig University (1887–1919).

nodes.label: Eugen Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Eugen Wilhelm was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology who studied under August Schleicher. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

nodes.label: Carl Gaedicke
nodes.summary: Carl Gaedicke worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

nodes.label: Ferdinand de Saussure
variants: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.image: Ferdinand de Saussure by Jullien Restored.png
nodes.jawiki: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.summary: Ferdinand de Saussure (1857–1913) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (1880) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891), the University of Paris (~1881–1891), and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

nodes.label: Eduard Sievers
variants: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.summary: Eduard Sievers (1850–1932) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius and Leskien. He held professorships at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

nodes.label: Ernst Curtius
variants: エルンスト・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

nodes.label: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli
variants: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.image: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli, post 1861 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0066 B.jpg
nodes.jawiki: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.summary: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873.

nodes.id: I:Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
nodes.label: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
variants: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik

nodes.id: I:Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
nodes.label: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Hermann Osthoff
variants: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.summary: Hermann Osthoff studied linguistics and Indology at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn (under Hermann Usener), and Leipzig (under Georg Curtius). He served on the faculty at Leipzig University (~1875-1877) and as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University (1877).

nodes.label: University of Geneva
variants: ジュネーブ大学文学部

nodes.label: Pietro Merlo
nodes.summary: Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877, he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming an ordinary professor in 1885.

nodes.label: Michele Kerbaker
nodes.summary: Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Italian Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) and under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Bardelli
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Bardelli was an indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer of Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1853).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797). He served as a professor of languages at the University of Bologna (~1797–1831) and as Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library (1833).

nodes.label: Carlo Giussani
nodes.summary: Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore from circa 1859 to 1863, and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (circa 1864–1865).

nodes.label: Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano
variants: Academy of Science and Letters (Italian: Accademia scientifico-letteraria) in Milan
ミラノ科学・文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Francisco García Ayuso
nodes.image: 1897-05-30, La Ilustración Española y Americana, Francisco García Ayuso (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Munich (~1869–1871) under Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev
nodes.summary: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (1840–1890) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and under Albrecht Weber (1863), later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Garcin de Tassy
variants: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.dewiki: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.summary: Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Jean Daniel Kieffer, and held a chair in Indian languages at INALCO from approximately 1828 to 1878.

nodes.label: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux
variants: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.jawiki: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.summary: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1838, specializing in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, the University of Paris, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Léon Feer
nodes.summary: Léon Feer was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at INALCO (1864), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

nodes.label: Michel Bréal
nodes.summary: Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a French linguist and Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the EPHE (~1868–1882).

nodes.label: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel
nodes.summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, August Boeckh, and Franz Bopp. He held posts at Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and succeeded Bopp as comparative philology chair at Berlin in 1872.

nodes.label: Otto Blau
nodes.summary: Otto Blau worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Friedrich Pott (~1848–1851) at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1848) and at Leipzig University (~1850–1852).

nodes.label: József Budenz
nodes.summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, where he completed his doctorate in 1858 under Theodor Benfey. He later served as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

nodes.label: August Fick
variants: フリードリヒ・コンラート・アウグスト・フィック
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フィック
nodes.summary: August Fick was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (1852–1856). He later served as an extraordinary professor at Göttingen (1876) and full professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).

nodes.label: Ferdinand Justi
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and completed his habilitation at Marburg (~1861), where he served as professor and later Rektor (1887–1888).

nodes.label: Ludwig Lange
nodes.summary: Ludwig Lange was a classical philologist and historian who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Charles University (1853–1859), the University of Giessen (1859–1871), and Leipzig University (from 1871), where he served as rector (1879–1880).

nodes.label: Theodor Nöldeke
nodes.jawiki: テオドール・ネルデケ
nodes.summary: Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) was a linguist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studies at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, he held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University (1864, 1868–1872), and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

nodes.label: John Peile
nodes.summary: John Peile worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Repton School, St Bees School, Christ's College, Cambridge (~1856–1860), and under Theodor Benfey (~1869–1870). His career included posts at Christ's College (~1860–1910), Cambridge (1884–1891), and Newnham College (~1890–1909).

nodes.label: Émile Senart
variants: エミール・シャルル・マリー・スナール
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Émile Senart studied at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He later served as professor at the Collège de France and president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

nodes.label: Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander
nodes.summary: Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He later held posts as a Repetent at Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.

nodes.label: Carl Siegfried
nodes.summary: Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Halle, Bonn, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin and theological professor at Jena (1875–1901).

nodes.label: Julius Euting
nodes.summary: Julius Euting studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier. A linguist and historian, he served as honorary professor at the University of Strasbourg (1880) and director of its library (1900-1909).

nodes.label: Matthias von Lexer
nodes.summary: Matthias von Lexer studied linguistics and other fields at the University of Graz, under Franz Bopp, Moriz Haupt, and Albrecht Weber, earning a PhD from Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held professorships at Freiburg (~1863–1868), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

nodes.label: Sophus Bugge
nodes.summary: Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, University of Copenhagen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (Professor from 1866).

nodes.label: Angelo De Gubernatis
nodes.summary: Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (from 1890).

nodes.label: Henri Gaidoz
nodes.summary: Henri Gaidoz studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber. He taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as directeur d’études for Celtic philology at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1876.

nodes.label: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, at Elphinstone College, Mumbai University, and Göttingen (PhD). He served as professor at Elphinstone and Deccan Colleges, and as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hübschmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hübschmann was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Jena under Schleicher, Tübingen, Munich under Martin Haug, and Leipzig. He was associate professor at Leipzig (1876) and professor of comparative linguistics at Strasbourg (1877).

nodes.label: Julius Jolly
nodes.summary: Julius Jolly studied under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug at Munich, Berlin, and Leipzig, habilitating at Würzburg. An Indologist and linguist, he was a long-time professor at the University of Würzburg (1877-1920).

nodes.label: University of Florence
variants: Istituto dei Studi Superiori in Florenz
Istituto degli studii superiori in Florenz
Istituto di studi superiori di Firenze

nodes.label: Sapienza University of Rome
variants: Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza"

nodes.label: Trinity College Dublin
variants: ダブリン大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Frédéric Baudry
nodes.summary: Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian and administrative posts at the Institut agronomique de Versailles, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and Bibliothèque Mazarine, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions.

nodes.label: Peter Peterson
nodes.summary: Peter Peterson was an Indologist. From circa 1873 to 1899, he served as a professor at the University of Mumbai and as Bombay Professor and Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College.

nodes.label: James Burgess
nodes.summary: James Burgess worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and as director and Director General (1886–1889) of the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Robert Caesar Childers
nodes.summary: Robert Caesar Childers worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford, Wadham College, and under Yātrāmulle Śrī Dhammārāma. He served as sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor at University College London (~1872–1876).

nodes.label: A. F. Rudolf Hoernle
nodes.summary: A. F. Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director at Aliah University (~1881–1895) and as secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

nodes.label: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
nodes.description: Philosopher, academic, writer, translator, entrepreneur, social reformer and philanthropist (1820-1891)
nodes.summary: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, he held posts at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

オーストリア科学アカデミー
Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften Institut für Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens

Austrian Academy of Sciences in Vienna
Institute for Medieval Research of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna
Institute of Social Anthropology, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Malabar Mission
variants: Mission an der Küste von Malabar

nodes.label: Thomas William Rhys Davids
variants: トーマス・ウィリアム・リス・デイヴィッズ
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ウィリアム・リス・デイヴィッズ
nodes.description: British scholar of the Pāli language (1843–1922)
nodes.summary: Thomas William Rhys Davids (1843–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau (PhD). He founded the Pali Text Society, held posts at UCL and London, and held the Comparative Religion chair at Manchester (1904–1915).

nodes.label: Henri Hubert
nodes.summary: Henri Hubert studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (~1892–1895). He held appointments at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

nodes.label: Marcel Mauss
nodes.summary: Marcel Mauss studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, and others across Bordeaux, the EPHE, and Dutch and British universities. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Grube
variants: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Grube worked in Sinology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg under Vasilyev and Schiefner, and at Leipzig under von der Gabelentz. He held posts at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Leipzig University, and Humboldt University.

nodes.label: Karl Florenz
variants: カール・フローレンツ
カール・アドルフ・フローレンツ
nodes.jawiki: カール・フローレンツ
nodes.summary: Karl Florenz (1865–1939) worked in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917), Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut (~1914–1935), and the University of Hamburg (~1919–1935).

nodes.label: University of Tokyo
variants: 東京大学文学部印度哲学梵文学科
東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科
東京大学文学部印度哲学科

nodes.label: Fitzedward Hall
nodes.summary: Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University before holding a chair at King's College London (1862) and serving as India Office librarian (~1862–1869).

nodes.label: Arthur Berriedale Keith
nodes.summary: Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling, and Balliol College, Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as professor at Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

nodes.label: Junjiro Takakusu
nodes.summary: Junjiro Takakusu, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He held leadership roles and professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Otto Stein
nodes.summary: Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He spent his academic career at Charles University, serving as Privatdozent in 1922 and ordinary professor of Indian philology and archaeology from 1930 to 1939.

nodes.label: Joseph Estlin Carpenter
variants: エストリン・カーペンター
nodes.summary: Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at University College School (~1856-1860) and the University of London (~1860-1866), later serving at Harris Manchester College (~1876-1915) and the University of Oxford (~1906-1915).

nodes.label: Robert Chalmers
nodes.description: British civil servant, and Pali and Buddhist scholar (1858-1938)
nodes.summary: Robert Chalmers specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was educated at the City of London School and Oriel College, Oxford, and studied under Thomas William Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

nodes.label: Richard Morris
nodes.summary: Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Battersea Training College. He held posts at King's College School (1869), Dedham Grammar School (~1871–1875), and was headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

nodes.label: Edmund Hardy
nodes.summary: Edmund Hardy (1852–1904) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), and Freiburg, later serving as professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and chair at Fribourg (1894–1898).

nodes.label: Dines Andersen
nodes.summary: Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was a Danish scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and served there as professor of Indian philology (1903–1927).

nodes.label: William Henry Denham Rouse
nodes.summary: William Henry Denham Rouse worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge, held a fellowship at Christ's College (1888), and taught at Bedford School, Cheltenham College, Rugby School (~1895-1901), and The Perse School (1902-1928).

nodes.label: Caroline Rhys Davids
variants: キャロライン・オーガスタ・リス・デイヴィッズ
C. A. F. リス・デヴィッズ
nodes.summary: Caroline Rhys Davids was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. She studied at University College London under George Croom Robertson and T. W. Rhys Davids, later lecturing at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

nodes.label: Sylvain Lévi
nodes.summary: Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the EPHE, Sorbonne University, Collège de France (1894–1935), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

nodes.label: Louis de La Vallée Poussin
variants: ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
L・ドゥ・ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée Poussin
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée-Poussin
nodes.summary: Louis de La Vallée Poussin studied at Liège, KU Leuven, Paris, and Leiden under Lévi, Kern, and others. Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held a professorship at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.

nodes.label: Godefroy de Blonay
nodes.description: Swiss linguist and member of the International Olympic Committee (1869-1937)

nodes.label: Henry Clarke Warren
nodes.summary: Henry Clarke Warren was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard (A.B. ~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, under teachers including Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and Thomas William Rhys Davids.

nodes.label: Vincent Arthur Smith
nodes.image: The Early History of India by Vincent Arthur Smith.jpg
nodes.summary: Vincent Arthur Smith was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later held posts at the University of Oxford, including Curator of the Indian Institute (~1910–1920).

nodes.label: Sarat Chandra Das
variants: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.image: Sarat Chandra Das, C.I.E. photo from Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (page 10 crop).jpg
nodes.jawiki: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.description: Indian scholar of Tibetan language and culture (1849-1917)
nodes.summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Presidency Colleges and University of Calcutta. He directed Bhutia Boarding School (1874), served as Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904), and founded the Buddhist Text Society (1892).

nodes.label: Cecil Bendall
nodes.summary: Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and under Theodor Benfey. He served at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1903).

nodes.label: Unrai Wogihara
nodes.summary: Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University, under Junjiro Takakusu, and in Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He taught at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1930), Shukyo University, and Taisho University (~1926–1937).

nodes.label: Vasily Radlov
variants: ヴァシーリー・ヴァシーリエヴィチ・ラドロフ
ヴィルヘルム・ラドロフ
nodes.summary: Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist and historian. Educated at Berlin and Jena, he taught in Barnaul before serving as director of the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and director of the Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

nodes.label: Alexander von Staël-Holstein
variants: Alexander Wilhelm Freiherr Staël von Holstein
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Alexander von Staël-Holstein studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg (under Richard Pischel), and Harvard. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, Harvard, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute.

nodes.label: Rudolf Seydel
nodes.summary: Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Leipzig University (~1852–1856) and later held an academic post there (~1860–1892).

nodes.label: Masaharu Anesaki
nodes.summary: Masaharu Anesaki studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, working in religious and Buddhist studies. He became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 1904, serving as its library director from 1923 to 1934.

nodes.id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.label: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
variants: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.image: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.dewiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He served at Utrecht University from 1924 to 1957 and the University of Amsterdam from 1935 to 1944.

nodes.label: Richard Fick
nodes.summary: Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library, Berlin State Library, and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library while at the University of Göttingen (1921–1932).

nodes.label: Richard Schmidt
nodes.summary: Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, Karl Friedrich Geldner, and Ernst Mehliß. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1898–1908), the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910), and the University of Münster (1910).

nodes.label: Keshub Chunder Sen
nodes.summary: Keshub Chunder Sen worked in religious studies and Indology, and founded the Brahmo Samaj. He was educated at the Hindu School, Presidency College, Kolkata (~1856–1858), and the University of Calcutta (~1857–1858).

nodes.label: Helmer Smith
nodes.summary: Helmer Smith worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Dozent at Lund (1921) and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Uppsala (1936–1947).

nodes.label: Louis Finot
nodes.summary: Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. An alumnus of the École des Chartes, he served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898 and professeur honoraire at the Collège de France (1920–1930).

nodes.label: Édouard Huber
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology, Édouard Huber studied at the University of Paris, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and Collège de France, including under Sylvain Lévi and Johann Baptist Schibenegg. He directed a department at EFEO (1901–1905).

nodes.label: Kaigyoku Watanabe
nodes.summary: Kaigyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg and served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School and professor at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities.

nodes.label: Robert Gauthiot
nodes.summary: Robert Gauthiot was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1907) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

nodes.label: Max Lindenau
nodes.summary: Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.

nodes.label: Ludwig Heller
nodes.summary: Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served as professor at Greifswald (from 1904) and held a post at the University of Tartu (1918).

nodes.label: Theodor Zachariae
nodes.summary: Theodor Zachariae (1851–1934) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Göttingen (~1874) and his Habilitation at Greifswald (~1879), studying under Sauppe, Curtius, Brockhaus, and Benfey. He held professorships at Greifswald (1883) and Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

nodes.label: Hermann Beckh
nodes.summary: Hermann Beckh was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, Berlin State Library, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Theodor Bloch
nodes.summary: Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and continued his studies under Georg Bühler (~1892–1895).

nodes.label: Hermann von Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Hermann von Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1844-1848). A researcher in history and archaeology, he held a teaching assignment at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851-1854) and was a member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1862-1882) and Leopoldina.

nodes.label: Emil Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under tutor Franz Joseph Lauth. In 1864, he became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Georg Morgenstierne
variants: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.dewiki: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.summary: Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) studied Indology and Iranian linguistics at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Konow, Lüders, and Schulze. He served as a professor at the University of Gothenburg (1930–1937) and the University of Oslo (1937–1962).

nodes.label: Sten Konow
nodes.summary: Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo and Halle-Wittenberg under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel, holding professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Hamburg (1914–1919).

nodes.label: Frederick William Thomas
nodes.summary: Indologist and Tibetologist Frederick William Thomas studied at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Librarian at the India Office Records (1898–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

nodes.label: Tukaram Krishna Laddu
nodes.summary: Tukaram Krishna Laddu worked in Indology. He studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg until 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.

nodes.label: Edward Denison Ross
variants: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.image: Edward Denison Ross by John Lavery (1856-1941).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.summary: Edward Denison Ross studied at University College London and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. A scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the British Museum, and SOAS (1916-1937).

nodes.label: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan
nodes.summary: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sarat Chandra Das and earning a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He was Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Ganganatha Jha
nodes.summary: Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, and Allahabad, he was Professor of Sanskrit at Muir Central College, Principal of Sanskrit College and University, and Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

nodes.label: Edward Washburn Hopkins
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia University (~1874–1878) and Leipzig University under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch (~1880–1881, Ph.D.). He held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895), and Yale University (1895–1926).

nodes.label: Arthur Coke Burnell
nodes.summary: Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bedford School and King's College London, learning under Michael Viggo Fausbøll, Theodor Goldstücker, and Heinrich August Jäschke. He worked in the Indian Civil Service from ~1860 to 1880.

nodes.label: Peter von Bradke
nodes.summary: Peter von Bradke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dorpat/Tartu under Leo Meyer, at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and at Leipzig, Jena, and Giessen, later becoming an außerordentlicher Professor at Giessen (1886–1896).

nodes.label: Prafulla Chandra Ray
nodes.jawiki: プラフラ・チャンドラ・レイ
nodes.description: Bengali chemist, educationist, poet, historian, industrialist and philanthropist (1861–1944)
nodes.summary: Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Vidyasagar College, Presidency College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Presidency College, the University College of Science, and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: George Melville Bolling
variants: ジョージ・M・ボーリング
nodes.summary: George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins University (doctorate ~1891–1897). He held posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).

nodes.label: Bapu Deva Sastri
nodes.description: Indian scholar in Sanskrit and mathematics and translator
nodes.summary: Bapu Deva Sastri (1821–1900) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundhiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

nodes.label: S. M. Natesa Sastri
nodes.summary: S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. From circa 1883 to 1888, he served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Debendranath Tagore
variants: デヴェンドラナート・タゴール

nodes.label: Rabindranath Tagore
variants: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.jawiki: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.summary: Rabindranath Tagore worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London, and founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

nodes.label: Arthur Anthony Macdonell
variants: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Oxford, and Leipzig (PhD ~1883) under Benfey, Roth, and Müller. He served at Oxford as Deputy Professor and later Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1888/1899–1926).

nodes.label: LeRoy Carr Barret
nodes.summary: LeRoy Carr Barret (1877-1960) was an Indologist. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895-1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899-1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

nodes.label: Franklin Edgerton
variants: フランクリン・エジャトン
フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.jawiki: フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.summary: Franklin Edgerton (1885–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held professorships at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953), also visiting Harvard and Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Bernhard Geiger
nodes.summary: Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology and Iranian studies. He studied at Vienna, Bonn, Charles, Göttingen, and Heidelberg, learning under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn. He taught at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

nodes.label: Willibald Kirfel
nodes.summary: Indologist Willibald Kirfel studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, completing his PhD and habilitation. He worked as a librarian at Bonn University Library before becoming Bibliothekar, Privatdozent (1920), and ordentlicher Professor (1922) at Bonn.

nodes.label: Alfons Fürst
nodes.summary: Alfons Fürst specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Universities of Tübingen and Regensburg (habilitating under Norbert Brox). He held a post at Bamberg and became Professor and Dean of Catholic Theology at Münster.

nodes.label: Robert Zimmermann
nodes.summary: Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930), and as Leiter at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Leiden University
variants: Leiden University, Department of Indo-European Comparative Linguistics (VIET)

nodes.label: Friedrich Otto Schrader
nodes.summary: Friedrich Otto Schrader specialized in Indology and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from the University of Strasbourg (~1899-1902), served as Leiter of the Adyar Library (1905-1916), and was Professor of Indology at Kiel University from 1921.

nodes.label: Heinrich Lüders
variants: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.summary: Heinrich Lüders was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and taught at Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935).

nodes.label: Edward Joseph Thomas
nodes.summary: Edward Joseph Thomas, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a master's at St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge. From ~1909 to 1939, he served at Cambridge University Library and as departmental dean at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Shwe Zan Aung
nodes.summary: Shwe Zan Aung worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Yangon (~1887–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.

nodes.label: Pe Maung Tin
nodes.native: ဖေမောင်တင်
nodes.summary: Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Yangon, University of Calcutta, and University of Oxford, and later served as professor and principal at Yangon, principal at the University of Adult Education, and Burma Historical Commission chairman.

nodes.label: Benimadhab Barua
nodes.description: Bengali Writer, Indologist, and pundit of Pali and Buddhism (1888-1948)
nodes.summary: Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Calcutta and a D.Litt. from the University of London (~1914–1917). He was headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution (1912) and a professor at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

nodes.label: Hakuju Ui
nodes.image: Recent portrait of Dr. Hakuju Ui.jpg
nodes.summary: Hakuju Ui studied at Tokyo under Junjiro Takakusu, and at Oxford, Cambridge, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Tokyo and Tohoku universities and became president of Komazawa University in 1941.

nodes.label: Frank Lee Woodward
nodes.summary: Frank Lee Woodward (1871–1952) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College under Caroline Rhys Davids, and later served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translator for the Pali Text Society (circa 1919).

nodes.label: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy
variants: フョードル・シチェルバツコイ
フョードル・イポリトビッチ・シチェルバツコイ
nodes.jawiki: フョードル・イポリトビッチ・シチェルバツコイ
nodes.summary: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and Sergey Oldenburg, as well as under Georg Bühler and Hermann Jacobi, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg (~1909–1941).

nodes.label: Chimanlal Dahyabhai Dalal
nodes.description: Sanskrit scholar and librarian of the Central Library in Baroda

nodes.label: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Ramesh Chandra Majumdar studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served as professor, provost, and vice chancellor at the University of Dhaka, principal at BHU and RTM Nagpur University, and president of the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: A. B. Gajendragadkar
nodes.summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist. He held positions as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.

nodes.label: S. Kuppuswami Sastri
nodes.summary: S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher educated at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and held professorships at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

nodes.label: Amrith Krishna
nodes.summary: Amrith Krishna works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).

nodes.summary: Luca Brigada Villa works in the fields of linguistics and computational linguistics. He has held academic posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

nodes.label: Erica Biagetti
nodes.summary: Erica Biagetti specializes in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pavia in 2021, where she also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Amba Kulkarni
nodes.summary: Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Hyderabad by 2009, where she has served as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

nodes.label: Gérard Huet
nodes.summary: Active in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics, Gérard Huet studied under George Ernst (ca. 1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (ca. 1972–1976). He was appointed a professor at Inria around 1972.

nodes.summary: Sachin Kathale specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University by 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.

nodes.label: Sriram Krishnan
nodes.summary: Sriram Krishnan is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of Hyderabad, Central Sanskrit University, and the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad.

nodes.summary: Di Jiang is a scholar in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

nodes.label: Nathan W. Hill
nodes.summary: Nathan W. Hill specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and computational studies. After studying at Harvard (~2001-2009) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff, he held positions at SOAS, UC Berkeley, Oxford, and Trinity College Dublin.

nodes.label: Cameron David Warner
nodes.summary: Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu and has held posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

nodes.summary: Laxmidhar Behera is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

nodes.label: Tanuja Ajotikar
nodes.summary: Tanuja Ajotikar is a scholar in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. She has held posts at Harvard University, The Sanskrit Library (attested 2024–2025), and Maharishi Vedic University.

nodes.label: Hrishikesh Terdalkar
nodes.summary: Hrishikesh Terdalkar is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology who earned his PhD at IIT Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, Pralay Manna, and Sowmya Krishnapur. He was affiliated with IIT Kanpur around 2023–2024.

nodes.label: Anil Kumar
nodes.summary: Anil Kumar is a scholar working in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hyderabad by 2012 and subsequently held a post there.

nodes.label: Peter M. Scharf
nodes.summary: Peter M. Scharf is a scholar of Indology, computational studies, and linguistics who earned his doctorate under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Brown University (2006–2009) and serves as President of The Sanskrit Library.

nodes.label: Mark Pedersen
nodes.summary: Mark Pedersen is a scholar of computational linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Queensland by 2001 and held a post at the same institution.

nodes.summary: Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology, having studied at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at IIT Kanpur, IIIT Hyderabad (including as professor from 2002 to 2013), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi.

nodes.label: Gopal Lal Meena
nodes.summary: Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, he held posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Harunaga Isaacson
variants: ハルナガ・アイザクソン
nodes.jawiki: ハルナガ・アイザクソン
nodes.summary: Harunaga Isaacson specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker, Tilmann Vetter, and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hamburg.

Abteilung für Kultur und Geschichte Indiens und Tibets

nodes.label: Dorji Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. He has taught and held a professorship at the University of Hamburg since 1998.

nodes.label: Orna Almogi
nodes.summary: Orna Almogi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Almogi studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at Hamburg, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe

nodes.label: Jeffrey Hopkins

nodes.label: Kenichi Kuranishi

nodes.label: Toru Tomabechi
nodes.summary: Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and computational fields. nodes.label: Diwakar Acharya

nodes.label: Masao Shizutani

nodes.label: Yoshito S. Hakeda

nodes.label: Alf Hiltebeitel
variants: アルフ・ヒルテバイテル
nodes.summary: Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oakwood Friends School, Haverford College, and the University of Chicago and its Divinity School, before serving on the faculty at George Washington University from 1968 onward.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Clark Ruff
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Clark Ruff specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, later holding posts at UC Berkeley (2001–2002) and Marshall University (assistant professor from 2002).

nodes.label: Barbara A. Holdrege
nodes.summary: Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She served at the University of California, Santa Barbara, as Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and later as Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: William F. Powell
nodes.summary: William F. Powell is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held a career at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 1986, 2026).

nodes.label: Masaaki Hattori
nodes.summary: Masaaki Hattori worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, holding posts at Kyoto University from 1955 and 1961 to 1988, and later at Osaka Gakuin University in 1989.

nodes.label: Shinjo Suguro
nodes.summary: Shinjo Suguro (1925–2002) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948, doctorate 1987). He was vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and professor at Rissho University (~1965–1996, emeritus ~1996–2002).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Yoshimoto
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki, later serving at Otani University as an assistant (1976), lecturer (1986), and Buddhist studies laboratory appointee (~1990–2011).

nodes.label: Hidenori Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was attested as a professor at Nagoya University from 1968 to 1969.

nodes.label: Jonathan A. Silk
nodes.summary: Jonathan A. Silk studied at Oberlin, Kyoto, Ryukoku, and Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis O. Gómez). A scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and tibetology, he held posts at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, Leiden, Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and Minobusan University.

nodes.label: George Frederick Baumann

nodes.label: Lance S. Cousins
nodes.summary: Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–1998) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and was president of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).

nodes.label: Kate Crosby
nodes.summary: Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute (2003), SOAS University of London, and King's College London, where she is attested as Visiting Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2026.

nodes.label: Dragomir Dimitrov
nodes.summary: Dragomir Dimitrov is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and held posts at Marburg, the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Lars Martin Fosse
nodes.summary: Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Bonn, and the University of Oslo (~1974–1997). He also taught at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Jürgen Hanneder
nodes.summary: Jürgen Hanneder specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and Alexis Sanderson, later working as an assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (circa 2000–2007) and becoming a professor at Marburg in 2007.

nodes.label: George L. Hart
nodes.summary: George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD in Sanskrit from Harvard University in 1971. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Peter Harvey
nodes.summary: Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).

nodes.label: Craig Jamieson
nodes.summary: Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, and held posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 2002), including curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Matthew T. Kapstein
nodes.summary: Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at Brown University (1980–1987). He held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989–1996), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002–2018).

nodes.label: Birgit Kellner
nodes.summary: Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctoral degree at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. Her career includes posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Susanne Mrozik
nodes.summary: Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an MTS at Harvard, supervised by Charles Hallisey. She held academic posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Taku Fukuda
nodes.summary: Taku Fukuda (born 1963) works in Buddhist studies and studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed lecturer at Doho University in 1995, and his affiliations with the Eastern Institute, Doho University, and Nagoya University were attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Samuels
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2002) under Karen Christina Lang and studied under W. S. Karunatillake, later serving as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

nodes.label: Karen Christina Lang
nodes.summary: Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg (PhD 1983) and has held a long-term professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2026).

nodes.label: W. S. Karunatillake
nodes.summary: W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

nodes.label: Yukari Kimura
nodes.summary: Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having completed doctoral studies under Kenyo Mitomo. Kimura holds posts affiliated with the Eastern Institute and as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kenyo Mitomo
nodes.summary: Kenyo Mitomo studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held appointments including Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015) and visiting professor at UC Berkeley (1987).

nodes.label: Minori Nishimura
nodes.summary: Minori Nishimura (b. 1947), a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD at Taisho University (~1970–1976), where Nishimura taught (~1993–2018). Nishimura also held researcher roles at Sanko Research Institute and Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Shunkyo Katsumata
nodes.summary: Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1932–1935). He held positions at Toyo University and Taisho University, where he served from around 1957 to 1980 as professor and emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Koun Kajiyoshi
nodes.summary: Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929) and held a post at Taisho University (~1949–1974).

nodes.label: Shindai Sekiguchi
nodes.summary: Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1931). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1959–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1983).

nodes.label: Seiren Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seiren Matsunami worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1939). He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1952–1967) and Rissho University (~1967–1974).

nodes.label: Yasuhiko Nagano
nodes.summary: Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley (~1978-1983). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology, National Institutes for the Humanities, and Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: Soshu Nishioka
nodes.summary: Soshu Nishioka works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

nodes.label: Satoru Harada
nodes.summary: Satoru Harada (born 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973). He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Toho Gakuin, and as professor at Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

nodes.label: Hajime Kitamura
nodes.summary: Kitamura studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. Working in linguistics and Tibetology, he held posts at the National Institute for Japanese Language, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Reitaku University as president, and served as Toyo Bunko's board chairman.

nodes.label: Tokan Tada
nodes.summary: Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).

nodes.label: Noriyuki Kudo

He served as director of the Nepal Research Centre (2002) and became a professor and director at Hamburg.

nodes.label: Yusho Wakahara

nodes.label: Reimon Yuki
nodes.summary: Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daijo Tokiwa at the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1927). He served at the Eastern Cultural Institute, University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, and Kyoto Women's University.

nodes.label: Katsumi Mimaki
nodes.summary: Katsumi Mimaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the University of Paris under Gadjin M. Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

nodes.label: Masaaki Nohnin
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Masaaki Nohnin studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as associate professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Osamu Hayashima

nodes.label: Akifumi Naito

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Sakurai
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and later served there as a part-time lecturer and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Zensho Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Zensho Kitagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught at Rissho University, where he served as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026), and also held an affiliation with the Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Kaji
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Kaji is a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. His career includes posts at Koyasan, Nagoya, and Tamkang universities, as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College, and director at Ritsumeikan University.

nodes.label: Kōshō Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kōshō Kawamura, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Toyo University. He held positions at Toyo University (attested 1963–1984), Hamamatsu University, Minobusan University, and served as an honorary professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Kosho Mizutani
nodes.summary: Kosho Mizutani (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Ryukoku and Bukkyo universities. He served at Bukkyo University as associate professor (~1956–1974) and president (~1979–1995), and led Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen (~1995–2011) and Tokai Gakuen (~1998–2011).

nodes.label: Ichijo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and held academic posts at Otani University Junior College (~1967–1969) and Otani University (~1969–2007).

nodes.label: Hiroo Kashiwagi
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kashiwagi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Mie Chukyo University, president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College, and taught Wasō Harada.

nodes.label: Jason Birch
nodes.summary: Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney (BA Honours, 2005) and the University of Oxford (DPhil, 2013) under Alexis Sanderson and Peter Oldmeadow. He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Gareth Sparham
nodes.summary: Gareth Sparham (b. 1948) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, he was Lecturer in Tibetan Language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

nodes.label: Mayumi Nasu
nodes.summary: Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She held a lecturer post at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and was attested as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University in 2026.

nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Étienne Lamotte studied at KU Leuven, Sapienza, EPHE, and the Sorbonne under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at KU Leuven and Catholic University of Louvain (1932–1974).

nodes.label: Hubert Durt
nodes.summary: Hubert Durt was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He served as professor and editor-in-chief at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, director of the Hōbōgirin Institute, and held professorships at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and IIBS.

nodes.label: Mitsuji Fukunaga
nodes.summary: Mitsuji Fukunaga, a specialist in sinology and philosophy, studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University (1982–1986), and the University of Kitakyushu (1986–1989).

nodes.label: Yoshitaka Iriya
nodes.summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He later held posts at Kyoto University, as Chinese literature department head at Nagoya University (1955–1977), and at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1979–1986).

nodes.label: Shinjō Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Shinjō Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Hajime Nakamura and Dale Maurice Riepe, among others, and at Columbia University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Toyo Bunko, and University of Tsukuba.

nodes.label: Kangei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris. He later held an appointment at the Tokyo National Museum.

nodes.label: Takamatsu Yoshie
nodes.summary: Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Waseda University, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Matsumoto Fukashi High School, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne. He founded Waseda University, where he served as a lecturer and Dean of the Faculty of Letters (1930).

nodes.label: Satoshi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, Luis O. Gómez, and Gregory Schopen. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, later becoming Professor and President of Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Honjo
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kobe Women's University (1989–2004), Bukkyo University (1980, 2004, 2010, 2014), and Otani University (~1999–2017).

nodes.label: Shizuka Sasaki
nodes.summary: Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Jikido Takasaki, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, and was appointed professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University in 2002.

nodes.label: Stephen Jenkins
nodes.summary: Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

nodes.label: Malcolm David Eckel
nodes.summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Harvard and Oxford, completing his doctorate under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held positions at Middlebury College, Harvard University (1980–1991), and Boston University (1990–2024).

nodes.label: Donald S. Lopez Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held faculty posts at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (from 1990).

nodes.label: Charles Hallisey
nodes.summary: Charles Hallisey (b. 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Seiji Kimura
nodes.summary: Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University. He later held posts at Komazawa University and Komazawa Junior College.

nodes.label: Ernst Steinkellner
variants: エルンスト・シュタインケルナー
nodes.summary: Ernst Steinkellner, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his doctorate at Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He served as professor at Pennsylvania (1971) and directed the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and institutes at Vienna.

nodes.label: Helmut Krasser
nodes.summary: Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences, directing its Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History.

nodes.label: Gerhard Oberhammer
variants: G. オーバーハンマー
nodes.summary: Gerhard Oberhammer, specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studied at Innsbruck, Paris, and under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna, serving as professor from 1964 to 1997.

nodes.label: Yōhei Kawashiri
nodes.summary: Yōhei Kawashiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Lilian Silburn
nodes.summary: Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and traditional teacher Swami Lakshman Joo (1948), and worked at the CNRS / National Centre for Scientific Research from circa 1948 to 1978.

nodes.label: Swami Lakshman Joo
nodes.summary: Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991), working in Indology and philosophy, studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933). He founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991 and taught scholars including Lilian Silburn, André Padoux, and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: André Padoux
nodes.summary: André Padoux was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the Institut de civilisation indienne and under teachers including Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe. He directed the Institut français de Francfort (~1953-1959) and held research posts at the CNRS/NCSR.

nodes.label: Bettina Bäumer
nodes.summary: Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied across Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, and Munich. Her career includes posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

nodes.label: Jaideva Singh
nodes.summary: Jaideva Singh was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Srikrishna Harihirlekar, Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He served as chief producer at All India Radio and chairman of Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi.

nodes.label: Alexis Sanderson
nodes.summary: Alexis Sanderson is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held fellowships at Merton and Brasenose, served as Lecturer and Professor at Oxford, and was an All Souls Fellow.

nodes.label: Dominic Goodall
nodes.summary: Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied with S. A. Srinivasan. He has held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient since 2000 and lectured at EPHE in 2005.

nodes.label: Judit Torzsok
nodes.summary: Judit Torzsok is an Indologist who completed her DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She was an associate professor at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III in 2001 and became a professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

nodes.label: Alex Watson
nodes.summary: Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Wolfson College, Oxford, Preceptor in Sanskrit at Harvard, and Professor of Indian Philosophy at Ashoka University.

nodes.label: Isabelle Ratié
nodes.summary: Isabelle Ratié (born 1976) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

nodes.label: Kei Kataoka
nodes.summary: Kei Kataoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui and studied at National Sanskrit University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Wolfson College, Oxford, and Kyushu University.

nodes.label: Shigeo Kamata
nodes.summary: Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Edward Winslow Bastian
nodes.summary: Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied as a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under traditional teachers Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

nodes.label: Samdong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Samdong Rinpoche (born 1939) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as principal (attested 1980) and later as director (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenzin
variants: Gyurme Kensur Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Drepung Monastery. He led Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970) and served as principal and director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971; 1988–2001).

nodes.label: Sera Monastery
variants: Byes College of Se ra Monastery

nodes.label: Seitatsu Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seitatsu Matsunami specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Norio Koyama
nodes.summary: Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: David P. Jackson
variants: ディヴィッド・ポール・ジャクソン
nodes.summary: David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington, the latter under David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a C-3 professorship at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.

nodes.label: John E. Cort
nodes.summary: An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Cort completed a BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and an AM at Harvard University (~1982–1984). He became a Professor at Denison University starting around 1992.

nodes.label: Paul Dundas
nodes.summary: Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2017) and served as head of the Pali Text Society (~1993–2023).

nodes.label: Christoph Emmrich
nodes.summary: Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels by 2004, held an attested post at Heidelberg in 2001, and is attested as an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto in 2026.

nodes.label: Shubhachandra
nodes.summary: Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held posts as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Jayandra Soni
nodes.summary: Jayandra Soni specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed doctorates at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, later serving as a lecturer at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and holding a post at the University of Innsbruck (~2012).

nodes.label: Royce Wiles
nodes.summary: Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Derek F. Maher
nodes.summary: Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, later serving as co-director of East Carolina University's Religious Studies Program (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Georges B. J. Dreyfus

nodes.label: William A. Magee
nodes.summary: William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Virginia (attested 1992), Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and Chung-Hwa Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Jules Brooks Levinson

nodes.label: Richard B. Martin

nodes.label: Charles D. Orzech

nodes.summary: Daishun Ueyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University, serving as associate professor, professor, and president from 1999 to 2003.

nodes.label: Akira Fujieda

nodes.label: Paul B. Donnelly
nodes.summary: Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who holds a post at Northern Arizona University. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa, attested in 1997, as well as traditional teachers including Yeshe Thapkay.

nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery and served as director of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics until 1997.

nodes.label: Shoshin Fukihara
nodes.summary: Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Horyuji Kangakuin under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Otani University and Otani University Junior College, and assistant professor at Doho University.

nodes.label: Hoyo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Hoyo Watanabe (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1952 to 1961. He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor, dean of Buddhist studies, and special honorary professor.

nodes.label: Yosho Nomura
nodes.summary: Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University (~1935–1939), where he later served as professor (~1968–1986), and directed the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1977–1987).

nodes.label: Koken Sasaki
nodes.summary: Koken Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from 1950 to 1960. He had a long career at Rissho University, serving as an assistant professor, department chair, director, professor, and professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Senkyo Sakawa
nodes.summary: Senkyo Sakawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Rissho University (completing studies in 1965) and served there as a professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and later professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Enshu Kurumiya
nodes.summary: Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Australian National University in 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University in the 1980s.

nodes.label: Yinshun
nodes.summary: Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes and held leadership posts at Shandao Temple and the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Steven Collins
nodes.summary: Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Bristol, Indiana University Bloomington, and the University of Chicago, among others.
