nodes.label: Zenno Ishigami
nodes.summary: Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University. He served as professor at Taisho University, president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014), and director of the Jodo Shu Research Institute (~2004–2007).

nodes.label: Susumu Otake
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies and sinology scholar Susumu Otake studied at the University of Tsukuba under Makio Takemura (~1993–2002). He served as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (~2008), Kyoto University (~2008), and Bukkyo University (~2012).

nodes.label: Daniel A. Arnold
nodes.summary: Daniel A. Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago, later serving on the faculties of McGill University and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Barbara Stoler Miller
nodes.summary: Barbara Stoler Miller (1940–1993) was an Indologist educated at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch. She served as a professor at Barnard College and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

nodes.label: Theodore Riccardi Jr.
nodes.summary: Theodore Riccardi Jr. (1937–) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University (attested 2014), where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Robert A. F. Thurman
nodes.summary: Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as professor at Amherst College (1973–1988) and director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

nodes.label: José Ignacio Cabezón
nodes.summary: José Ignacio Cabezón specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Caltech, UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Sera Monastery. He held posts at Iliff School of Theology and UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Albrecht Wezler
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェッツラー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Wezler was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme and served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and Director of the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

nodes.label: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg (~1960-1967), where he later served as Privatdozent for Indology from 1973 to 1997.

nodes.label: Satoru Noriyama
nodes.summary: Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).

nodes.label: Kyoto Koka Women's University
variants: 京都光華女子大学真宗文化研究所
京都光華女子大学・同短期大学部

nodes.label: Silvio Vita
nodes.summary: Silvio Vita was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. He held posts at L'Orientale (1992–2001) and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023).

nodes.label: Shōshin Ichishima
nodes.summary: Shōshin Ichishima worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Taisho University as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014), and was a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: David B. Gray
nodes.summary: David B. Gray earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Rice University and held an associate professorship at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

nodes.label: Ryuichi Abe
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, SAIS/Johns Hopkins, Taisho, and Columbia. He taught at Columbia (1991–2004) before becoming Edwin O. Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard (~2003).

nodes.label: Ryushin Uryuzu
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryushin Uryuzu studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1951 to 1955. His career included posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Kyoto Sangyo University
variants: 京都産業大学外国語学部
京都産業大学国際言語科学研究所
京都産業大学文化学部

nodes.label: Fernando Tola
nodes.summary: Fernando Tola (1915–2017) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the National University of San Marcos, was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989), and directed the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2017).

nodes.label: Carmen Dragonetti
nodes.summary: Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at San Marcos, she was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and vice-director of the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (circa 1989–2018).

nodes.label: Tsugunari Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University (PhD, 1985), he taught at Rissho and served as President of Reiyukai (~1975–1996) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: International Institute for Buddhist Studies
variants: The International Institute for Buddhist Studies
International Institute for Buddhist Studies, Tokyo

nodes.label: Tarthang Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tarthang Monastery and under teachers including Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, later holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Nyingma Institute (~1972).

nodes.label: Yeshe De Project
variants: Yeshe De Buddhist Research and Translation Project

nodes.label: Yohei Furukawa
nodes.summary: Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Ryuji Hayashi and served as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryuji Hayashi
nodes.summary: Ryuji Hayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi. He has held posts at Tohoku University, NIT Sendai College, Eastern Institute, and Kodomo Kyoiku Hosen College, where he was professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Takao Kagawa
nodes.summary: Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Shoju Inaba
nodes.summary: Shoju Inaba was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Otani University from around 1949 to 1981 and held a part-time lecturer post at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Michitoshi Baraida
nodes.summary: Michitoshi Baraida is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University, Toho Gakuin, Toho Kenkyukai, and the Eastern Institute as chief priest of Ganshō-ji.

nodes.label: V. Raghavan
nodes.summary: V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught at Madras (1934–1968), founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was its secretary (~1944–1979).

nodes.label: Juro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Juro Watanabe studied Indology and philosophy under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested between 1989 and 1990.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1980–1987) and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1987–1989), and served as assistant professor at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004) and professor at Tohoku University (~2004–2019).

nodes.label: Atsushi Uno
nodes.summary: Atsushi Uno is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under T. R. V. Murti and others. He held academic posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima, and Kindai universities.

nodes.label: Raghunath Giri
nodes.summary: Raghunath Giri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Bama Charan Bhattacharya. He taught Atsushi Uno and held the position of department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: Keisho Tsukamoto
nodes.summary: Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Tohoku University. He served as dean of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, professor at Tohoku University, and president of Hosen Gakuen College.

nodes.label: Endo Asai
nodes.summary: Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held academic posts at Minobusan College, Nihon Fukushi University, and Rissho University, eventually becoming president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).

nodes.label: Noriaki Inoue
nodes.summary: Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Ensho Kanakura
nodes.summary: Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University and Rissho University, and served as president of Miyagi University of Education.

nodes.label: Shuyu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Shuyu Sakurai (born 1916) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from circa 1940 to 1943. He held a post at Komazawa University from around 1956 to 1987, where he became emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Takushu Sugimoto
variants: すぎもと・たくしゅう
nodes.summary: Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935), a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others. He taught at Kanazawa University (~1976–1999) and held professorships at Komazawa and Kinjo universities.

nodes.label: Yutaka Takagi
nodes.summary: Yutaka Takagi (b. 1928) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and was a professor at Rissho University (~1973–1999).

nodes.id: I:Tokyo University of Literature and Science
nodes.label: Tokyo University of Literature and Science
Tsuguhito Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD under Christopher I. Beckwith), later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

nodes.label: Hisashi Sato
nodes.summary: Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1934–1937). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (circa 1963–1977), Bukkyo University (circa 1977–1987), Toyo University, and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Tatsuo Nishida
nodes.summary: Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Kyoto University and at the National Center for Science Information Systems (1992–1994).

nodes.label: Helmut Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Helmut Hoffmann was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Freiburg, Berlin (under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg, he held posts at the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

nodes.label: Christopher I. Beckwith
variants: クリストファー・I・ベックウィズ
nodes.jawiki: クリストファー・ベックウィズ
nodes.summary: Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, joining Indiana University's faculty in ~1978 and becoming Professor in 1982.

nodes.label: Shindo Kusumoto
nodes.summary: Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Hiroshima University by 2001, studying under Shoryu Katsura, Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

nodes.label: Hideyo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hiroshima University as associate professor (~1988-1997) and professor of Indian Philosophy (~1997-2019, attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yoshihito Muroji
nodes.summary: Yoshihito Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, was an assistant at Kyoto University, an associate professor at Koyasan University (1995–2012), and a professor at Shiga University of Medical Science (2014–2015).

nodes.label: Robert Kritzer
nodes.summary: Robert Kritzer works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini and served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

nodes.label: Kyoto Notre Dame University
variants: 京都ノートルダム女子大学
ノートルダム女子大学

nodes.label: Kazufumi Oki
nodes.summary: Kazufumi Oki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught Shindo Kusumoto and served as assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

nodes.label: Hiromi Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Ryukoku University as a full-time lecturer (専任講師, attested 1987) and faculty member (attested 2006). During his career, he also taught Shindo Kusumoto.

nodes.label: Toshihiko Kimura
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He served as an assistant professor at Tokai Gakuin University (~1980) and professor emeritus at Shitennoji University (~2011).

nodes.label: Toshihide Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi. He held an appointment as a professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Sengaku Mayeda
nodes.summary: Sengaku Mayeda was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, and University of Münster. He held faculty posts at Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Musashino University, and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

nodes.label: Hideto Ono
nodes.summary: Hideto Ono specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1964-1973) and served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1987-1994).

nodes.label: Dongguk University
variants: 東国大学校印度哲学科
京城私立恵化専門学校

nodes.label: Masaaki Nitta
nodes.summary: Masaaki Nitta studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1968). He held professorial posts at Fukui Prefectural College (~1975–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Kobe University
variants: 神戸大学大学院人文学研究科
神戸大学文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Taiken Tanaka
nodes.summary: Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Johannes Bronkhorst
nodes.summary: Johannes Bronkhorst studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Rajasthan, Pune under S. D. Joshi, and Leiden. Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2011 (and circa 1987–2025).

nodes.label: Karin Preisendanz
nodes.summary: Karin Preisendanz (born 1958) is an Indologist and philosopher. She studied at the University of Hamburg (Dr. phil., Habilitation), and held posts at the Free University of Berlin (1987–1990), University of British Columbia (1990–1993), and University of Vienna (1999).

nodes.label: Konrad Klaus
nodes.summary: Konrad Klaus specializes in Indology and Tibetology, having studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. Between 1999 and 2001, he held deputy professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn.

nodes.label: Shujun Motegi
nodes.summary: Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and earned an MA from Kyoto University in 1977, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 1998, 2010).

nodes.label: Beatrix Pfleiderer
nodes.summary: Beatrix Pfleiderer (1941–2011) was an Indology scholar who studied at Heidelberg University. She taught at the University of Maryland (1971–1975) and held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Hamburg (1982), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1989–1991).

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer and professor at Otani University (attested 1984–2002) and held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2015.

nodes.label: Paul Demiéville
variants: ポール・ドミエヴィル
nodes.jawiki: ポール・ドミエヴィル
nodes.summary: Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held the Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at the Collège de France (1946–1964) and taught at EPHE and INALCO.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Kimura
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Tokyo, where he taught (1983–2001), and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University (~2001–2011).

nodes.label: Fumihiko Sueki
variants: Fumihiko Sueki (末木 文美士, Sueki Fumihiko)
nodes.summary: Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura, later serving as professor at Tokyo, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and SOKENDAI.

nodes.label: Hajime Okayama
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and bhikku
nodes.summary: Hajime Okayama studied at Kyoto University, University of Tokyo, CASS, and Peking University under Xianlin Ji. A specialist in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, he was a professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

nodes.label: Koyu Tamura
nodes.summary: Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees including a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University (1965) and Toyo University (1972; professor emeritus 1977–2000), and taught Shigeki Moro.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Misaki
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and later served there as professor emeritus (attested 1988–2000).

nodes.label: Katsumi Okimoto
nodes.summary: Katsumi Okimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1988–2014) and as director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Takao Maruyama
nodes.summary: Takao Maruyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University until 1962. He held professorships at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; emeritus 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Kato
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Otani University (1927–1931) under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji Kobe Betsuin (1935) and Kōjō Girls' Vocational School (1938).

nodes.label: Ryuzan Nishimoto
nodes.summary: Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and traditional teacher Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.

nodes.label: Weizhong Huang
nodes.summary: Weizhong Huang (1969–) is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ariane Macdonald
nodes.summary: Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.

nodes.label: Yoshiro Imaeda
nodes.summary: Yoshiro Imaeda (b. 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Shoju Inaba. His career includes posts at CNRS and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Xuezhu Li
nodes.summary: Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and indology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li held a fellowship at Ryukoku University (2011) and posts at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017, 2026).

nodes.label: Zhao Luo
nodes.summary: Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Futoshi Takehashi
nodes.summary: Futoshi Takehashi works in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.

variants: 真宗大谷派真宗教学研究所
真宗大谷派教学研究所

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Shimokawabe
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He later held posts at Rissho University (attested 1990, 2001) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Takayuki Hirosawa
nodes.summary: Takayuki Hirosawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held positions at Taisho University, where he was a group member until 1991 and attested as professor in 2014.

nodes.label: Noboru Ueda
nodes.summary: Noboru Ueda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and later served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shoko Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shoko Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969), and an associate professorship at Kyushu University (1948–1953).

nodes.label: Eli Franco
nodes.summary: Eli Franco (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Charles Malamoud and habilitated at Hamburg. He held the chair of Indology at Leipzig University (2004–2021) along with posts at Vienna and La Trobe.

nodes.label: Xinchuan Huang
nodes.summary: Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Peking University (~1954–1958). Huang later served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1979) and taught Jiang Yili.

nodes.label: Robert DeCaroli
nodes.summary: Robert DeCaroli specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA, studying under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount before joining George Mason University's faculty (~2002).

nodes.label: Robert L. Brown
nodes.summary: Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1986–2014).

nodes.label: Ravindra Singh Bisht
nodes.summary: Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Lucknow, Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He worked at the Institute of Archaeology (1986–1997) and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India until 2004.

nodes.label: Michiya Ito
nodes.summary: Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held an academic post there (attested 2001–2004).

nodes.label: Eishu Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Miyazaki studied at Rissho University under Gyōō Kageyama and later held posts at Rissho University and Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Gyoko Iotani
nodes.summary: Gyoko Iotani studied at Rissho University and worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor (~1984–1993), professor (~1993–2015), and professor emeritus (~2015), and was a former specially appointed professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Taijo Iwata
nodes.summary: Taijo Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), a professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gen'ichi Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1965–1974) and as a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.

nodes.label: Kokugakuin University
variants: Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics at Kokugakuin University
國學院大學文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Hisao Takahashi
nodes.summary: Hisao Takahashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Ryukai Mano at Taisho University, where he also spent his career as an assistant, lecturer, and professor (circa 2002–2015).

nodes.label: Ippei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Ippei Okamoto works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kaiun Shirodate
nodes.summary: Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Otani University, where he served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).

nodes.label: Taido Kitamura
nodes.summary: Taido Kitamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Kitamura held positions at Shuchiin University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and on staff (attested 1994–1999).

nodes.label: Koichi Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Koichi Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his MA at the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa and Gyoin Hashimoto. He was an assistant professor at Rikkyo University from circa 1974 to 2005.

立教大学アジア地域研究所

nodes.label: Gyoin Hashimoto
nodes.summary: Gyoin Hashimoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1921–1925) and under Join Saeki. He served as chief abbot at Yakushi-ji from 1939 to 1967.

nodes.label: Shoshin Kuwayama
nodes.summary: Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1957 to 1966 and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1966 to 2002.

nodes.label: Akira Miyaji
nodes.summary: Akira Miyaji specializes in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and held posts at Hirosaki University (~1974–1978), Nagoya University (~1978–2007), Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art (~2007–2013), and Ryukoku University (2013).

nodes.label: Ryujo Yamada
nodes.summary: Ryujo Yamada worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sylvain Lévi. He served as professor (attested 1953) and professor emeritus (attested 1972–1973) at Tohoku University, and as head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

nodes.label: Jiro Sugiyama
nodes.summary: Jiro Sugiyama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953) in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1979), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1979–1994), Bukkyo University (~1994–1996), and ICPBS (~1996–2004).

nodes.label: Tetsujiro Inoue
nodes.summary: Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, and Leipzig, he served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, and as president of Daito Bunka University.

nodes.label: Ryōkei Kaginushi

nodes.label: Takashi Ogawa
nodes.summary: Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo. He was appointed associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.

nodes.label: Kenji Kinugawa
nodes.summary: Kenji Kinugawa (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971-1980) and under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida (~1975-1985), later teaching Eric M. Greene.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Matsumoto works in the field of history and archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Waseda University under Shinya Hoshiyama and served as a researcher at the Kuboso Memorial Museum of Arts, Izumi (attested 1986).

nodes.summary: Kyoko Fujii, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977). She served as a professor at Hokkaido University (~1997–2013) and has held roles at ICPBS, Eastern Institute, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Kenryo Minowa
nodes.summary: Kenryo Minowa (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000-2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (2025).

nodes.label: Shogo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shogo Watanabe, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University and taught there from circa 1991 to 2024, becoming professor around 1996. He held posts at the Eastern Institute around 2024 and Taisho University around 2026.

nodes.label: Ikuro Hattori
nodes.summary: Ikuro Hattori works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Pune and held posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2003), the Eastern Institute (attested 2026), and Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Takayoku Kimura
nodes.summary: Takayoku Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University. He worked as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (c. 1973–1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichō-ji (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Michihiko Yajima
nodes.summary: Michihiko Yajima works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A former graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981), he held a post there (attested 1992) and later served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Gyoei Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyoei Takahashi works in Buddhist studies. Takahashi has been affiliated with Rissho University as an assistant professor (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2026), and served as a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Shunei Mori
nodes.summary: Shunei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Mori held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Kaiten Nukariya
nodes.description: Religious scholar and ordained Zen Buddhist monk
nodes.summary: Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa and Keio universities. He lectured at Harvard University (circa 1913–1915) and served as the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).

nodes.label: Gustav Roth
nodes.summary: Gustav Roth was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Munich. He held a post at the University of Göttingen from 1965 to 1981 and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from 1982 to 1985.

nodes.label: Reinhold Grünendahl
nodes.summary: Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Petra Kieffer-Pülz
nodes.summary: Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (ca. 2000), and the Pali Text Society (ca. 2018).

nodes.label: Sen Wang
nodes.summary: Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1932–1936), he served as a professor at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1964.

nodes.label: Syed Hasan Askari
nodes.summary: Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University. He later served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.

nodes.label: Tilmann Vetter
variants: ティルマン・フェッター
nodes.summary: Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He later served as a professor at Leiden University from 1974 until ~2002.

nodes.label: Minoru Kiyota
nodes.summary: Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees after studying at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1966 to 1994.

nodes.label: John P. Keenan
nodes.summary: John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota and with Noriaki Hakamaya, later serving at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture and Middlebury College.

nodes.label: Paul L. Swanson
nodes.summary: Paul L. Swanson (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a professor at Nanzan University and directed the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture.

nodes.label: Horst Lasic
nodes.summary: Horst Lasic, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999. He became a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995 and a lecturer at Vienna in 1999.

nodes.label: Taiken Kyuma

nodes.label: Yumi Nakamoto
nodes.summary: Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies. Nakamoto studied at Ryukoku University and held a research post there in 2012.

nodes.label: Jokai Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Jokai Hiraoka, a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1947–1953). He held academic posts at Shuchiin University and served as professor at Otemae University (~1966–1988).

nodes.label: Ryosei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Ryosei Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1956–1965, PhD 1993). He was appointed professor at Taisho University in 1973 (emeritus 2007) and visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2012, while also directing institutes including Kawasaki Daishi (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ryojin Soga
nodes.summary: Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and held multiple professorships and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1991) was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (1930). He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar
nodes.summary: Indologist and philosopher Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar served as principal of Sir Parashurambhau College. He was also Professor and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Hajime Nakamura
nodes.summary: Hajime Nakamura studied at the University of Tokyo, specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He became a professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1973), founded Toho Gakuin and the Eastern Institute, and served as director of both institutions.

nodes.label: Antonio Gargano
nodes.summary: Antonio Gargano worked in Indology and other fields. He held a position as professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1966) and served as a curator and editor for Serie Orientale Roma (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Champa Thupten Zongtse
nodes.summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Göttingen, where he is attested from 1991 and worked as a lecturer (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Erich Heintel
nodes.summary: Erich Heintel (1912–2000) was a philosopher who earned his doctorate (1931–1936) and habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He served Vienna as extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982), and joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held an appointment as a special researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Tomohiro Manabe

nodes.label: Shinya Yasutomi
nodes.summary: Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held positions at Otani University, the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute, and the Eastern Buddhist Society.

nodes.summary: Kōgi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and held an editorial post at the Ryukoku Buddhist Studies Association (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Ryoichi Kondo
nodes.summary: Ryoichi Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Lobsang Gyatso
nodes.summary: Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso and served as head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics from ~1973 to 1997.

nodes.label: Christian Lindtner
nodes.summary: Christian Lindtner was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

nodes.label: Migmar Tsering
nodes.summary: Migmar Tsering was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and served as head of Sakya College.

nodes.label: Joseph Hackin
nodes.summary: Joseph Hackin worked in history/archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, earned a doctorate from the University of Paris, and held posts at the Musée Guimet, École du Louvre, and DAFA.

nodes.label: René Grousset
nodes.summary: René Grousset worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and sinology after studying at the University of Montpellier. He held posts at the Musée Guimet, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, Louvre Museum, and École Libre des Sciences Politiques.

nodes.label: Bunzaburo Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University, serving as Kyoto's second president (1908–1915).

nodes.label: Shoson Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Shoson Miyamoto (1893–1983) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa, Toyo, and Waseda, and founded the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Giei Honda
nodes.summary: Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. After graduating from Kyoto University in 1914, he served there as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1935–1948), and later as professor at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.

nodes.label: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya

nodes.label: Shuntaro Matsuyama
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, later lecturing at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, and Tama Art University, and serving as professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1988–1996).

nodes.label: Masashi Nagai

nodes.label: Ichiro Katayama

nodes.label: Tatsugen Sato
nodes.summary: Tatsugen Sato (1924–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University. He served as professor at Komazawa University (~1974–1995) and lectured at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Mauro Maggi
nodes.summary: Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Naples "L'Orientale," served as Director of the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and joined Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Toshio Sako
nodes.summary: Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under his doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Anna-Pya Sjödin
nodes.summary: Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Uppsala University in 2007, where her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, with additional instruction from Barbro Eriksson.

nodes.label: Gunilla Gren-Eklund
nodes.summary: Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1970 to 2003.

nodes.label: Jonardon Ganeri
nodes.summary: Jonardon Ganeri studied at Cambridge, King's College London, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. Specializing in philosophy and indology, he held appointments at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU, and became Bimal K. Matilal Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at Toronto.

nodes.label: K. Venugopalan
variants: K・ヴェーヌゴーパラン

nodes.label: Toshihiro Wada
nodes.summary: Toshihiro Wada is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under V. N. Jha in 1981. He held an academic post, including as an assistant professor, at Nagoya University from ~1989 to 2019.

nodes.label: Tadashi Tani
nodes.summary: Tadashi Tani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1972–1977), studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, and served as professor at Kochi College (~1989–2006).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
variants: 高知工業高等専門学校

nodes.label: Ryudo Fujii
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Ryudo Fujii studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. His career includes posts at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kosuke Nakazawa
nodes.summary: Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts at Rissho University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and was a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: Karl Jettmar
nodes.summary: Karl Jettmar was an archaeologist and historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna. He held positions at the University of Vienna, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and served as director at Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

nodes.label: Gérard Fussman
nodes.summary: Gérard Fussman studied at the École Normale Supérieure from around 1961 to 1965, working in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. In 1984, he became a professor at the Collège de France, succeeding Jean Filliozat.

nodes.label: Ahmad Hasan Dani
nodes.description: Pakistani intellectual, archaeologist, historian, and linguist (1920–2009)
nodes.summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam University, where he became Dean in 1971.

nodes.label: Jan Van Bragt
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヴァン・ブラフト
nodes.summary: Jan Van Bragt (1928–2007) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After studying at KU Leuven, he served as a professor at Nanzan University (~1967–1998) and as Director of the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (~1976–1990).

nodes.label: Gessho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. At Otani University, he served as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

nodes.label: Koichi Hokazono
nodes.summary: Koichi Hokazono, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held positions at Kyushu University and The International University of Kagoshima.

nodes.label: Ryuken Sato
nodes.summary: Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Akitoshi Saito
nodes.summary: Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as an adviser at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kotetsu Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kotetsu Yoshida (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has served as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ryushin Kitao
nodes.summary: Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2014 and 2026).

nodes.label: Institute for Zen Studies
variants: Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zen Bunka Kenkyūsho)
Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zenbunka kenkyujo)

nodes.label: Zhejiang University
variants: 浙江省立甲種工業学校

nodes.label: Yumi Katayama
nodes.summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama studied at Hiroshima University and under Kenyo Mitomo.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his education at Sera Monastery (Lharampa Geshe, 1953) and Gyume Tantric College.

nodes.label: Meiji Yamada
nodes.summary: Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962) and served there as a professor (attested 1963 and 2007).

nodes.label: Frank-Richard Hamm
nodes.summary: Frank-Richard Hamm (1920–1973) specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later lecturing there (1948–1952, 1957–1964) before becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

nodes.label: Daniel Cozort
nodes.summary: Daniel Cozort (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding positions at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2020).

nodes.label: Kensur Yeshe Thupten
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kensur Yeshe Thupten served in 1982 as a visiting Tibetan scholar at the University of Virginia and held a post at Middlebury College that same year. He taught numerous scholars, including Donald S. Lopez Jr.

nodes.label: Geshe Palden Drakpa
nodes.summary: Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Librarian at Tibet House New Delhi (attested 1987–1992, 2004) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987.

nodes.label: Shaoyong Ye
nodes.summary: Shaoyong Ye works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan, Ye held faculty appointments at Peking University as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Qing Duan
nodes.description: Chinese scholar of Indian and Iranian languages; Professor of Indo-Iranian Studies and Boya Chair Professor of Peking University
nodes.summary: Qing Duan was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University and the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1986 under Ronald Eric Emmerick), she served as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

nodes.label: Zhaohua Yang
nodes.summary: Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and as a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Shinsho Hanayama
nodes.summary: Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Naoshiro Tsuji
nodes.summary: Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford under Takakusu, Macdonell, Geldner, and Lévi. He became Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and directed Toyo Bunko (1974).

nodes.label: Paul Hacker
nodes.summary: Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin, he held the chair for Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and at the University of Münster (1963–1978).

nodes.label: Catholic University of Louvain
variants: Institut Orientaliste de l'Université Catholique de Louvain

nodes.id: I:Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
nodes.label: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
variants: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde

nodes.label: Michael Friedrich
nodes.summary: Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich. He served on the faculty at the University of Munich and was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

nodes.label: Jowita Kramer
nodes.summary: Jowita Kramer works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, held posts at Munich, Heidelberg, and Göttingen, and became a professor at Leipzig University in 2021.

nodes.label: Masaru Akimoto
nodes.summary: Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002 and 2015).

nodes.label: George Robert Elder
nodes.summary: George Robert Elder worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Columbia University, where he was attested in 1978 as having Alex Wayman as his doctoral supervisor.

nodes.label: Ikuhisa Takigawa
nodes.summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Angelika Krebs
nodes.summary: Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel, where she took the chair for practical philosophy in 2001.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Tweed
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Tweed (1954–) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~1981–1989) under William R. Hutchison, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

nodes.label: William A. Clebsch
nodes.description: American church historian, developer of religious studies, and university professor (1923-1984)

nodes.label: Robert E. Buswell Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Kusan Sunim and completed his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. He held a professorship at UCLA (~1986–1993), later becoming Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Luis O. Gómez
variants: Luis O. GÓMEZ ルイス・ゴメス
nodes.description: Puerto Rican buddhologist, translator and psychologist
nodes.summary: Luis O. Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler, served as department chair and professor at the University of Michigan, and was Academic Director at the Mangalam Research Center (c. 2010–2017).

nodes.label: Van Austin Harvey
nodes.image: Van A. Harvey and a dog.jpg
nodes.summary: Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Occidental, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale, he held posts at Princeton, Southern Methodist, Pennsylvania, and Stanford, where he was George Edwin Burnell Professor (~1978–1996).

nodes.label: Lee Yearley
nodes.summary: Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a professorship at Stanford University (attested 1989-1992), where he is currently attested as Emeritus (2026).

nodes.label: Gordon Dester Kaufman
nodes.summary: Gordon Dester Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University, held posts at Pomona College and Vanderbilt University, and served as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University from 1963.

nodes.label: Carl Bielefeldt
nodes.summary: Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, and earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley. He served at Stanford University from around 1980 to 2012, becoming emeritus in 2012.

nodes.label: William R. Hutchison
nodes.summary: A religious studies and history scholar, Hutchison earned degrees from Oxford and Yale (PhD 1956). He held posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, Wisconsin-Madison, and taught at Harvard University beginning in 1968.

nodes.label: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned an MA at the University of Washington and a PhD at Harvard (~1995–2000). He held posts at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and the University of Virginia (2005).

nodes.label: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (Karabchampa, 1990) and Harvard University (PhD, ~1997–2004 under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Thomas Burke, and Khenchen Trinley Paljor).

nodes.label: Jagdish Kashyap
nodes.summary: Jagdish Kashyap was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and in Sri Lanka under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught at BHU and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

nodes.label: Satkari Mookerjee
variants: サトカリ・ムカージー
サトカーリ・ムケルジー
nodes.summary: Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1955) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

nodes.label: John Brough
nodes.summary: John Brough, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. He held chairs as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1948–1967) and professor at the University of Cambridge (1967–1984).

nodes.label: Chitai Takenaka
nodes.summary: Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University (circa 1966–1968). He held posts as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (1979–1983) and professor at Tokoha University (1989).

nodes.label: Hideki Kiyoshima
nodes.summary: Hideki Kiyoshima works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University around 1989.

nodes.label: Jun Takashima
nodes.summary: Jun Takashima specializes in Indology, religious studies, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

nodes.label: Muneo Tokunaga
variants: Muneo Tokunaga (徳永 宗雄, Tokunaga Muneo)
nodes.summary: Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD from Harvard University. He taught at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1982–1988) and Kyoto University as assistant professor (~1988–1990) and professor (~1990–2008).

nodes.label: Yasumasa Sekine
nodes.summary: Yasumasa Sekine is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His academic posts include positions at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Watase
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University (~1989–2007) and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Katsuhiko Kamimura
nodes.summary: Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. His career included posts at the University of Tokyo and Kokugakuin University, among other institutions.

nodes.label: Michio Yano
nodes.summary: Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1996) under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and at Brown University under David Pingree (~1978–1979). From 1973 to 2015, he was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University.

nodes.label: Issei Suzuki
nodes.summary: Issei Suzuki (1863–1943) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served there as a professor.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Michihata
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Michihata worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Otani University, he held a post there from circa 1934 to 1969, and later served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from circa 1969 to 1978.

nodes.label: Mizumaro Ishida
nodes.summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who held a professorship at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Fuchs
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Fuchs (b. 1950) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Tenzin Dorjee
nodes.summary: Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel and Geshe Sonam Rinchen. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery.

nodes.label: Allen Wright Thrasher
nodes.summary: Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He later worked at the Library of Congress from circa 1985 to 2016.

nodes.label: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
variants: ダニエル・インゴールス
nodes.summary: Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1916–1999) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Harvard University under Walter Eugene Clark and W. V. O. Quine, as well as under Kalipada Tarkacharya. He was appointed professor at Harvard University in 1939.

nodes.label: T. Shrinivas Shastri
nodes.summary: T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar affiliated with the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he is attested as Pandit in 1993 and as Professor in 2026.

nodes.label: Stefan Anacker
nodes.summary: Stefan Anacker worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Alex Wayman from ~1965 to 1970.

nodes.label: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry
nodes.description: Kannada writer, lexicographer, grammar expert, critic and editor
nodes.summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak. He held lecturing posts before becoming Professor at Mysore (1984–1994).

nodes.label: University of Mysore
variants: Institute of Kannada Studies, University of Mysore
Department of Jainology and Prakrits, University of Mysore
Kuvempu Institute of Kannada Studies at the university

nodes.label: Jacques May
nodes.summary: Jacques May worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1981) and as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1968–1992).

nodes.label: Richard Hugh Robinson
nodes.summary: Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Alberta, SOAS, and London under supervisors Arthur Waley and David Friedman, served on the Toronto faculty, and became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

nodes.label: Kyojun Shimizudani
nodes.summary: Kyojun Shimizudani studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and was chief abbot (kanju) of Sensō-ji from around 1952 to 1979.

nodes.label: Manabendu Banerjee
nodes.summary: Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and as Secretary of the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: John D. Dunne
nodes.summary: Dunne works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, having studied at Amherst, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University (~2005–2016), as well as Antioch College and CIHTS.

nodes.label: Margaret R. Miles
nodes.summary: Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history. After earning her PhD from the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and returned to GTU as dean (1996–2001).

nodes.label: Gary A. Tubb
nodes.summary: Gary A. Tubb (b. 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011, 2026).

nodes.label: James W. Benson
nodes.summary: James W. Benson is an Indologist who held an Assistant Professorship in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

nodes.label: National Institute of Japanese Literature
variants: 国文学研究資料館文献資料部

nodes.label: Tokyo Woman's Christian University
variants: 東京女子大学文理学部

nodes.label: Leela Aditi Wood
nodes.summary: Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (completed by 2005) under Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Walter M. Spink
nodes.summary: Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD) and served on the faculty at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

nodes.label: Thomas E. Crow
nodes.summary: Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) is an art historian educated at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and joined NYU as professor in 2007.

nodes.label: Marvin Eisenberg
nodes.summary: Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held an academic post at the University of Michigan from ~1949 to 1990.

nodes.label: Cyrus Stearns
nodes.summary: Cyrus Stearns is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

nodes.label: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima
variants: Sde gzhung Rin po che, Kun dga' bstan pa'i nyi ma
デシュン・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Buddhist scholars - Dezhung Rinpoche III seated on a stool, Chris Wilkinson, student seated at the feet of his lama, wearing Buddhist robes, malas, likely Seattle, Washington, USA (16134833232) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche
variants: Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che, Ngag dbang legs bshad rgya mtsho
Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kunga Chöphel, Geshe Tshechok, and Zimwok Rinpoche. In 1928, he became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery.

nodes.label: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche
variants: Dil mgo Mkhyen brtse Rin po che, Rab gsal zla ba
キャブジェ・ディルゴ・ケンツェ・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Buddhist Vajrayana master, scholar, poet, and teacher (1910–1991)
nodes.summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Khenpo Thubga.

nodes.label: Jong-Nam Choi
nodes.summary: Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under the supervision of Lambert Schmithausen.

nodes.label: David Seyfort Ruegg
nodes.summary: David Seyfort Ruegg was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. After studies at the EPHE and the University of Paris, he held chairs and professorships at Leiden (1966–1972), the University of Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1989–2000).

nodes.label: Edward Garrett
nodes.summary: Edward Garrett works in computational linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at UCLA (~1995-2001) under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Carson T. Schütze
nodes.summary: Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who earned his degree at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1992–1997). In 1997, he held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Dominique Sportiche
nodes.summary: Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1978–1984). He has held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles since around 1987.

nodes.label: Anna Szabolcsi
nodes.summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She worked at the Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics (~1976–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and became professor of linguistics at NYU (~1998).

nodes.label: Naomi Appleton
nodes.summary: Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist, Indological, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under supervisors Christopher Minkowski and David N. Gellner, and later became a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff and a professor at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Lancaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies in Lancaster
The Institute for Philosophy and Public Policy, Lancaster University

nodes.label: Laurie L. Patton
nodes.summary: Laurie L. Patton (born 1961) works in Indology and religious studies, holding degrees from Harvard and the University of Chicago. She served as Professor and Dean at Duke, President of Middlebury College (2015-2024), and became President of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2024).

nodes.label: Anna Aurelia Esposito
nodes.summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Würzburg, and Tübingen (MA, 1998). She served as an assistant professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and later joined the University of Zurich as PD Dr. (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Geen
nodes.summary: Jonathan Geen, a scholar of indology and religious studies, completed his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching positions at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

nodes.label: Phyllis Granoff
nodes.summary: Phyllis Granoff (born 1947), an Indologist and scholar of Buddhism and religion, earned degrees from Radcliffe College and Harvard University. She served as Professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) before becoming Lex Hixon Professor Emeritus at Yale University in 2004.

nodes.label: McMaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies at McMaster

nodes.label: Shoshin Higuchi
nodes.summary: Shoshin Higuchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Otani University (attested in 1998) and as a committee member of the Otani Society (attested in 2000).

nodes.label: Myoshin Fujitake
nodes.summary: Myoshin Fujitake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a committee member for the Otani Society (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Ryusei Keira
nodes.summary: Ryusei Keira is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, completing his thesis in 2003.

nodes.label: Koichi Shinohara
nodes.summary: Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He served as a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004) and as a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2018).

nodes.id: I:The Okura Institute for the Study of Cultural Science
nodes.label: The Okura Institute for the Study of Cultural Science
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held several posts at Taisho University, attested as a researcher (1998), research student (2006), lecturer (2008), and chief research fellow (2017).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Toda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1975–2000) and was a special member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: University of Texas at Austin
variants: The University of Texas at Austin
テキサス大学オースティン校

nodes.label: Hiroko Matsuoka
nodes.summary: Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006). She held an affiliation at Leipzig University (attested 2016) and served as faculty at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Sueki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied briefly at Tübingen University Library under George Baumann and held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996-2012).

nodes.label: Michael Torsten Much
nodes.summary: Michael Torsten Much is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He was a fellow at the University of Hamburg and studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Helmut Tauscher
nodes.summary: Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held faculty posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1983–2026) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Zeff Bjerken
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Zeff Bjerken studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed a PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. in 2001. That year, he held a post at the College of Charleston.

nodes.label: T. Griffith Foulk
nodes.summary: T. Griffith Foulk works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1978–1987) under Luis O. Gómez, later serving there as assistant professor (1987–1995) and at Sarah Lawrence College (1995–2005).

nodes.label: Lopon Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Lopon Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries. He served as lopön at Menri Monastery (1953–1959, 1978) and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.

nodes.label: Ryoken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryoken Nawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Makoto Nagai
nodes.summary: Makoto Nagai was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942) and served as president of Chuo Shoka Junior College in 1951.

nodes.label: Shun Hidaka
nodes.summary: Shun Hidaka works in Buddhist studies. Hidaka served as a researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Rajendra Chandra Hazra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka under Sushil Kumar De. He taught at Jagannath University and the University of Dhaka, and was Associate Professor of Smṛti and Purāṇa at Sanskrit College.

nodes.label: Sushil Kumar De
nodes.summary: Indologist Sushil Kumar De studied at Presidency College, Calcutta, SOAS, and Bonn. He taught English at Presidency and Calcutta (~1913–1923), was professor of Sanskrit and Bengali at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and led Jadavpur's Bengali department from 1947.

nodes.label: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar
nodes.summary: Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar earned degrees from Mumbai University and Heidelberg University. He served as professor and Dean of Arts at Savitribai Phule Pune University and was the longtime Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1939 to 2001.

nodes.label: Izumi Hoshi
nodes.summary: Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1987–1997). At Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, she was an assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023).

nodes.label: Michiyo Hoshi
nodes.summary: Michiyo Hoshi is a researcher in Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts as a joint researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
