variants: ガワン・トゥンドゥプ

nodes.label: Tenpa Gyaltsen
variants: テンバ・ギェンツェン

nodes.label: Jitsuaki Oshika
nodes.summary: Jitsuaki Oshika is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1941–1944) and later served as a professor at Toyo University (~1968–1989).

nodes.label: Yasuo Goto
nodes.summary: Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who has served as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ronald Y. Nakasone
nodes.summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Isoda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Isoda (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966). He taught at Tohoku University as lecturer (~1968–1973) and associate professor (~1973–2002), and became professor emeritus at Shimane University.

nodes.label: Werner Abraham
nodes.summary: Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1965. His academic career included posts at the University of Groningen from 1971, the University of Tübingen, and several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Tarab Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–1998) and at the University of Copenhagen (~1970–1998).

nodes.label: Hartmut Buescher
nodes.summary: Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhāl Tripāṭhī and held positions at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Burkhard Quessel
nodes.summary: Burkhard Quessel specializes in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member (attested 1997), and worked as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

nodes.label: British Library
variants: British Library’s Oriental and India Office Collections

nodes.label: Kenneth G. Zysk
nodes.summary: Kenneth G. Zysk (born 1951) is an Indologist and historian who earned an MA at UC Santa Barbara and a PhD at ANU. He held posts at Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen, among other institutions.

nodes.label: Christian K. Wedemeyer
nodes.summary: Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Wesleyan and Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, he held positions at Antioch, Columbia, the University of Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

nodes.label: Ole Holten Pind
nodes.summary: Ole Holten Pind was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 2004 to 2009 under doctoral supervisor Ernst Steinkellner, receiving his Dr.phil.

nodes.label: John Ronald Newman
nodes.summary: John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and later served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida.

variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派教学伝道研究センター

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Ueno
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies. He conducted doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003-2004) and held a research post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Eric David Mortensen
nodes.summary: Eric David Mortensen specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, also studying under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and Xuewen He.

nodes.label: Kimberley C. Patton
nodes.summary: Kimberley C. Patton is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992), where she later served as Assistant Professor (~1993–1999) and Professor (~2005).

nodes.label: Yoshiki Motoaki
nodes.summary: Yoshiki Motoaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic appointments at Otani University, attested in 2013 and 2026.

nodes.label: Christopher S. George
nodes.summary: Christopher S. George is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Padma Gyaltsan. He founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972) and taught at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.

nodes.label: Geshe Wangyal
nodes.summary: Geshe Wangyal worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1921–1938) and Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Agvan Dorjiev. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1972) and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).

nodes.label: Joe Bransford Wilson
nodes.summary: Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 1984. He held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

nodes.label: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin
nodes.summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indology, archaeology, and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich. He held long-term posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences and Moscow State University.

nodes.summary: Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, she held long-term positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

nodes.label: Ryojun Mitomo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and served as a professor of social welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Raghu Vira
nodes.summary: Raghu Vira was an Indology, Iranian, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of the Punjab, University of London, and Leiden University, he founded the International Academy of Indian Culture and headed Sanskrit at Sanatan Dharma College.

nodes.label: Lokesh Chandra
nodes.jawiki: ローケーシュ・チャンドラ
nodes.summary: Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University, he led the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1950–1963) and chaired the Indian Council of Historical Research (~2014–2017).

nodes.label: Richard F. Nance
nodes.summary: Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago by 2004 and held assistant (attested 2013) and associate (attested 2026) professorships in religious studies at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Toshio Horiuchi
nodes.summary: Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (circa 2003–2008). He was a visiting researcher at Toyo University (circa 2014–2018) and a postdoctoral researcher at Zhejiang University (circa 2019).

nodes.label: Atsushi Ibuki
nodes.summary: Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989). He serves as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Japanese Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies
Tomoyuki Komine
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and was attested as a part-time lecturer there in 2015.

nodes.label: Ruriko Sakuma
nodes.summary: Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University (~1981–1991). She held posts at the Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daiki Sasaki
nodes.summary: Daiki Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He held posts as an instructor at Taisho University (attested 2015, 2026) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Fumio Shoji
nodes.summary: Fumio Shoji is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Rissho University. He served there as an assistant professor from ~2013 to 2016 and became an associate professor in ~2016.

nodes.label: Kenta Suzuki
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kenta Suzuki studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2004). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2013.

nodes.label: Kimiaki Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kimiaki Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, and at the University of Oxford (1993). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, and Keio University.

variants: 一般財団法人人文情報学研究所

nodes.label: Tensho Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Tensho Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2009–2012) and the University of Tokyo (~2012–2016).

nodes.label: Masahide Mori
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Masahide Mori studied at Nagoya University and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Nagoya University (~1996–2000) and Kanazawa University as associate professor and professor from ~2000.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hokkaido University and held posts at the Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Hotta
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He served as director at the Tokyo University Buddhist Association (attested 2007) and term assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Steven Weinberger
nodes.summary: Steven Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA at Amherst College and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding an affiliation there (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Sakya Trizin
nodes.summary: Sakya Trizin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Appey Rinpoche and Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and has taught numerous students, including Steven Weinberger and Sam van Schaik.

nodes.label: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Dudjom Rinpoche, Kangyour Rinpoché, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Jé Kar Lama Gönpo Sam Drub, teaching at Tokyo, Kyoto, and Virginia.

nodes.label: Ralf Kramer
nodes.summary: Ralf Kramer studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. Between approximately 2004 and 2011, he served as the Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

nodes.label: Achim Bayer
nodes.summary: Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD 2005) under Lambert Schmithausen, David P. Jackson, and others. He was a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006) and a Research Fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Lore Sander
nodes.summary: Lore Sander worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (c. 1961–1967). She served as Curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and lectured at the Free University of Berlin (1994).

nodes.summary: Hoshu Mitsuhara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he was recorded as professor in 1982 and professor emeritus in 2004.

nodes.label: Hans T. Bakker
nodes.description: b. 1948; teaches Sanskrit, Philosophy, and Indian Religions, U. of Groningen
nodes.summary: Hans T. Bakker (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held a post at the University of Groningen (ca. 1996–2013) and served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).

nodes.label: Arjo Vanderjagt
nodes.summary: Arjo Vanderjagt studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). Working in philosophy and history/archaeology, he held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

nodes.label: Seiji Kumagai
nodes.summary: Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (circa 2005–2008), where he later served as an associate professor from circa 2013.

nodes.label: Seizan Yanagida
nodes.summary: Seizan Yanagida was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Kaiten Nukariya, he held professorships at Hanazono, Kyoto, and Chubu universities, and directed the IRIZ.

nodes.label: Yoshio Kawakatsu
nodes.summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a sinology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and under Paul Demiéville (~1957–1959), later serving as an assistant librarian at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1984.

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami, earning a doctorate at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard in 1958.

nodes.label: Serinity Young
nodes.summary: Serinity Young was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University in 2000.

nodes.label: Carole McGranahan
nodes.summary: Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, and held a post as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at CU Boulder (~2001–2008).

nodes.label: Nicholas Dirks
nodes.summary: Nicholas Dirks (b. 1950) studied at Wesleyan and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at Caltech (~1986–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

nodes.label: Ann Laura Stoler
nodes.summary: Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who earned degrees at Barnard College and Columbia University. She held teaching positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Michigan before becoming founding director at The New School in 2004.

nodes.label: Samuel M. Grupper
nodes.summary: Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Central Asian, Sinological, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West (attested 1980).

nodes.label: Join Saeki
nodes.summary: Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Jocho Chihaya. He held posts at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy, and served as chief abbot (管主) of Horyu-ji from 1903 to 1950.

nodes.label: Shoko Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. Takeuchi later served at Ryukoku University, where an appointment as professor emeritus was attested between 1987 and 1995.

nodes.label: Yasutoshi Murakami
nodes.summary: Yasutoshi Murakami (b. 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University. He held positions at Yamaguchi University, Koyasan University (~1989–2007), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takatoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Takatoshi Ito is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.

nodes.label: Guangchang Fang
nodes.summary: Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1986 to 2000 and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2005.

nodes.label: Michael J. Walsh
nodes.summary: Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he completed his doctorate under William F. Powell.

nodes.summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Doshisha and Kyoto universities under Ryosaburo Sakaki, later serving as professor at Kyoto University and Tokai University, and president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies.

nodes.label: T. R. Chintamani
nodes.summary: T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (~1930–1944) and as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research.

nodes.label: T. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

nodes.label: Kunio Mugitani
nodes.summary: Kunio Mugitani works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga around 1970–1977 and served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1992 to 2012.

nodes.label: Niigata University

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Okano
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Okano works in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as assistant professor (attested 2002) and as professor in Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Pāsādika
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, holding degrees from Magadh and Punjabi universities. He held academic posts at Punjabi, Marburg, and Würzburg universities, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and was rector at the Frankfurt Buddhist Academy (2022).

nodes.label: Sherab Gyatso
nodes.summary: Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries under teachers including Gungthang Lodrö Gyatso. He served as president of the Buddhist Association of China and dean at the Buddhist Academy of China.

nodes.summary: Ho-chin Yang, a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology, earned a PhD at the University of Washington (completed by 1994) under the doctoral supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Susumu Shimazono
nodes.summary: Susumu Shimazono studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as professor of religious studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013), later holding posts at Sophia University (~2013–2018) and directing its Grief Care Institute (~2017–2021).

nodes.label: James A. Matisoff
nodes.summary: James A. Matisoff is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) and is Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Donald Phillip Verene
nodes.summary: Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who earned a bachelor's at Knox College (~1955–1959) and a doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis (~1960–1964). nodes.summary: Henk Blezer studied at Leiden University (Doctoraal 1987–1997). A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he worked at Leiden University (postdoctoral researcher 1993–1997; lecturer 2002–2008) and the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

nodes.label: Toni Huber
nodes.summary: Toni Huber is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Canterbury in 1993 under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

nodes.summary: Sensho Kimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1962–1971) and later served as a professor there from around 1989 to 2009.

nodes.label: John Stratton Hawley
nodes.summary: Hawley works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1970–1974). He held a post at Bowdoin College (~1974–1976) and became a professor at Columbia University around 1986.

nodes.label: Charles Ramble
nodes.summary: Charles Ramble (b. 1957) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies educated at Durham University under Michael Aris. He has held professorships at the University of Oxford (2002–2005) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2009).

nodes.summary: Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima, attended the University of Tsukuba and the University of Vienna, and served as an associate professor at Tsukuba (circa 2004).

nodes.label: W. Norman Brown
nodes.summary: W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton, he taught at Johns Hopkins and SPM Rajput College before serving as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).

nodes.summary: Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught Latin at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

nodes.label: Thomas Burrow
nodes.summary: Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai, studying under E. J. Rapson and P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri. He held posts at the British Museum and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1944–1976).

nodes.label: Hanns Oertel
nodes.summary: Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Marburg (1922), and held a chair at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

nodes.label: Yudru Tsomu

nodes.label: Yutaka Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He has held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mai Mishiro
nodes.summary: Mai Mishiro is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Junko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Junko Matsumura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an MA at the Australian National University and completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen. Matsumura held a professorship at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Henk Bodewitz
nodes.summary: Henk Bodewitz earned classical, Indo-Iranian, and doctoral degrees at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He held posts at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966; chair of Sanskrit 1976–1992) and Leiden University (associate professor ~1973–1976; professor 1992–2002).

nodes.label: Yusho Miyasaka
nodes.summary: Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chizan Senmon Gakko, under Shoko Watanabe, and at Tohoku University. His career included professorships at Koyasan University and Nagoya University, as well as roles at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

nodes.label: John R. McRae
nodes.description: born:1947-04-28|died:2011|; McRae, John R., 1947-2011; McRae, John R.
nodes.summary: John R. McRae worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Yale (~1975–1983) under Stanley Weinstein and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He taught at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2005–2008).

nodes.label: Ryosho Tanaka
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Ryosho Tanaka held several roles there, including professor (2002–2003) and president (2009). He also served as professor at Ryukoku University and director of the Sōtō Zen Center for Advanced Studies (2005).

nodes.label: Chishō Namai
nodes.summary: Chishō Namai (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chikyo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and later as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).

nodes.label: Shintei Hinonishi
nodes.summary: Shintei Hinonishi (1924–2016) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeru Gorai and served as an assistant professor at Koyasan University in 1980.

Akira Mukai
nodes.summary: Akira Mukai works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (attested 1978), and later became a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Klaus Wille
nodes.summary: Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with manuscript cataloguing at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and served as a research associate at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2026).

nodes.label: Kongozyushinkai
variants: 社会福祉法人金剛樹心会

nodes.label: Takanori Fukita
nodes.summary: Takanori Fukita is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017). He held a post at Bukkyo University and served as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mohan G. Dhadphale
nodes.summary: Mohan G. Dhadphale is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and as editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Suhasini D. Laddu
nodes.summary: Suhasini D. Laddu (born 1926) is an Indologist and linguist. She was affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and served as Editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Saroja Bhate
nodes.summary: Saroja Bhate is an Indologist and linguist who served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1978–2002) and Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~2002–2007).

nodes.label: Amrit Madhav Ghatage
nodes.summary: Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961–1978) and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).

nodes.label: Yūto Kawamura
nodes.summary: Yūto Kawamura is an Indologist who completed a postdoc at Kyoto University (2015–2018). Kawamura held positions at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tokyo University of Education
variants: 東京教育大学文学部倫理学科
東京教育大学大学院文学研究科

nodes.label: Laura Harrington
nodes.summary: Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Geshe Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

nodes.label: Gregory Hillis
nodes.summary: Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia (-1993), where he also held a post (attested 2002), and is a continuing lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Satoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Satoshi Ito (born 1961) works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (~2005).

nodes.label: Mio Shinma
nodes.summary: Mio Shinma (b. 1949) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies, serving as a professor (attested 2007) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Osamu Izumoji
nodes.summary: Osamu Izumoji (born 1948) is a scholar in sinology who held posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Charles Goodman
nodes.summary: Charles Goodman specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard in 2002 and served as an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Allan Gibbard
nodes.description: American philosopher and social choice theorist
nodes.summary: Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).

nodes.label: Stephen F. Teiser
nodes.summary: Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned degrees at Oberlin College and Princeton University under Alan Sponberg, Denis Twitchett, and Daniel L. Overmyer, later teaching at Middlebury College and Princeton.

nodes.label: Franciscus Verellen
nodes.summary: Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Hamburg, Oxford, and the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at Columbia University (1987–1991) and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

nodes.label: Monica Esposito
nodes.description: Italian translator and historian of Chinese Religion, Daoism (1962-2011)
nodes.summary: Monica Esposito worked in sinology and religious studies. She earned a PhD at Paris Diderot University and completed postdoctoral studies at Ca' Foscari, Paris, and Kansai Universities before serving as an associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

nodes.label: Michael Puett
nodes.summary: Michael Puett is a sinologist, historian, and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. He has held professorships in humanities, Chinese history, and anthropology at Harvard University since approximately 1994.

nodes.label: Jean-Noël Robert
nodes.summary: Jean-Noël Robert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at INALCO and under Bernard Frank, later holding posts at CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and Collège de France as professor (2011–2022).

nodes.label: Eikan Taki
nodes.summary: Eikan Taki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Taisho University. He served as a lecturer at its Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Koda
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Koda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Satoshi Kono
nodes.summary: Satoshi Kono (born 1954) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

nodes.label: Nobukatsu Komai
nodes.summary: Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed research student training at Taisho University and held an appointment as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Paul G. Hackett
nodes.summary: Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan Collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later held research and lecturing posts at Columbia University (attested 2003–2016).

nodes.label: Masaaki Chikusa
nodes.summary: Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history who completed his degrees, including a doctorate (1980), at Kyoto University. He served as a Kyoto University professor (1981–1993) before becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

nodes.label: Yeshe Thubten
nodes.summary: Yeshe Thubten (1935–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Zong Rinpoche. He founded several Buddhist organizations and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

nodes.label: University of California, Santa Cruz
variants: Oakes College, University of California at Santa Cruz

nodes.label: Jean Filliozat
nodes.summary: Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He was a professor at EPHE and Collège de France, and directed the EFEO and French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Thomas F. Yarnall
nodes.summary: Thomas F. Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman and others, later serving as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Wayne Proudfoot
nodes.summary: Wayne Proudfoot (1939–) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (MTh ~1966–1969, PhD ~1969–1972), later teaching at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and Columbia University (~1972).

nodes.label: G. Thomas Tanselle
nodes.summary: G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978–2004), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation from 1978 to 2006.

nodes.label: E. Gene Smith
nodes.summary: E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, Utah, and Washington under Turrell V. Wylie, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held posts at the Library of Congress and the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: 14th Dalai Lama
variants: His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama
nodes.description: 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual and temporal leader of Tibetans
nodes.summary: The 14th Dalai Lama (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Khunu Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, and Trulshik Rinpoche, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989).

nodes.label: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya
nodes.summary: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

nodes.label: Mario D'Amato
nodes.summary: Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College.

nodes.label: Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue
variants: ヴァチカンの非キリスト教宗教研究部門

nodes.label: Bunkyo Aoki
nodes.summary: Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University, was a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1909–1914), and was appointed as a lecturer in Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951.

nodes.label: Ekai Kawaguchi
variants: Ekai Kawaguchi (河口慧海, Kawaguchi Ekai)
nodes.summary: Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under teachers including Sarat Chandra Das. He served as a professor at Toyo University in 1916.

nodes.label: Johan Elverskog
nodes.summary: Johan Elverskog is a Buddhist, Iranian and Central Asian, and history scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington, later holding posts at UC Santa Barbara, Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences, and Southern Methodist University.

nodes.label: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences
variants: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences

nodes.label: Eun Hino
nodes.summary: Eun Hino is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~2006–2008). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and Musashino University (~2014–2018; ~2018).

nodes.label: Hiromi Habata
nodes.summary: Hiromi Habata (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg (~1993–2000). She was a researcher at the University of Munich (~2000–2018) and later professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takayasu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1993). Around 2008, he served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University.

nodes.label: Yamaguchi Prefectural University
variants: 山口県立大学国際文化学部

nodes.label: Shinten Sakai
nodes.summary: Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University in 1959.

nodes.label: Günter Schweiger
nodes.summary: Günter Schweiger studied at Vienna University of Economics and Business and under Gert Klingenschmitt. A scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he was an assistant at Linz and served as a full university professor at WU Vienna (1974–2009).

nodes.label: Gert Klingenschmitt
nodes.summary: Gert Klingenschmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he also worked as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent (~1968–1976). Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held the Indogermanistik chair at Regensburg (1983–2006).

nodes.label: Rosemarie Lühr
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Lühr (b. 1946) is a linguist and Indologist. After earning her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg and habilitating at Regensburg, she held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and served as Indogermanische Gesellschaft president (2004–2016).

nodes.label: Michael Janda
nodes.summary: Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna and his Habilitation at the University of Zurich. He held an assistant post at Zurich in 1995 and a chair at Münster in 2002.

nodes.label: Chlodwig H. Werba
nodes.summary: Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, attested between 1997 and 2022.

nodes.label: Harumi Hirano Ziegler
nodes.summary: Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed both her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Tairyo Makita
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, Makita studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He was a Kyoto University professor (1949–1976), president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997), and professor at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.

nodes.label: Rolf Alfred Stein
nodes.summary: Rolf Alfred Stein was a Sinologist and Tibetologist who studied under scholars including Marcel Granet and Paul Pelliot. He was a directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1951–1975) and a professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).

nodes.label: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay
nodes.summary: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay (born 1936) works in Tibetology and religious studies. After earning a PhD at the University of London under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, CNRS (Director of Research 1980), and was IATS President (1995–2000).

nodes.label: Klemens Karlsson
nodes.summary: Klemens Karlsson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk and received his Doctor of Philosophy from Uppsala University in 2000.

nodes.label: Stockholm University
variants: Institutionen for Orientaliska Språk, Universitet i Stockholm

nodes.label: Susan L. Huntington
nodes.summary: Susan L. Huntington (1943–) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1972 to 2012.

nodes.label: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan
nodes.summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (-2003) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

nodes.label: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal
nodes.summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal studied at the University of Allahabad, University of Oxford (Jesus College), and Lincoln's Inn. Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he was Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1937).

nodes.label: Masako Keta
nodes.summary: Masako Keta studied philosophy and religious studies at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi and Shōtō Hase. She served as professor at Kanazawa University in 1998 and later as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).

nodes.label: Keiji Nishitani
nodes.summary: Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Hajime Tanabe, and Martin Heidegger. He taught at Otani University and served as a professor at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Kitaro Nishida
nodes.summary: Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He taught at the Fourth Higher School and served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

nodes.label: Om Prakash
nodes.summary: Om Prakash is a scholar in history, archaeology, and indology who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. Prakash taught at the University of Delhi, Kirori Mal College (attested 1961), and the Delhi School of Economics (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Dasharatha Sharma
nodes.summary: Dasharatha Sharma studied at the University of Delhi and taught history and Indology. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi (~1959–1966), Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1966–1976).

nodes.label: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala
nodes.summary: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow, he served as curator of Mathura Museum, director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and head of Indology at BHU.

nodes.label: Bahadur Chand Chhabra
nodes.summary: Bahadur Chand Chhabra (1908–1990) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his doctorate from Leiden University. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), as Government Epigraphist (~1949–1953), and as professor at Panjab University (~1965–1973).

nodes.label: Leah Zahler
nodes.summary: Leah Zahler (1937-2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Harvey B. Aronson, and Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.label: University of North Carolina Wilmington
variants: University of North Carolina at Wilmington

nodes.label: Lati Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Ganden and Gyuto monasteries. He served as abbot of Ganden Monastery (~1976–1985), taught at Namgyal Monastery (1976), and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1976).

nodes.label: Geshe Gedün Lodrö
nodes.summary: Geshe Gedün Lodrö was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and under Khensur Ngawang Lekden, later holding posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Mikisaburo Mori
nodes.summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He earned degrees from Kyoto University and Osaka University, and held posts at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Osaka High School, Osaka University, and Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Tou-hui Fok
nodes.summary: Tou-hui Fok was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (until 1966) and Otani University (1969). He was attested as a lecturer at The Chinese University of Hong Kong in 1981.

nodes.label: Jérôme Ducor
nodes.summary: Jérôme Ducor specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May from circa 1978 to 1992, and held a position at the University of Lausanne from circa 1996 to 2020.

nodes.label: Egaku Maeda
nodes.summary: Egaku Maeda specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen University Junior College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

nodes.label: Fumimaro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Fumimaro Watanabe worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Hammalawa Saddhatissa and A. K. Warder, later holding posts at Kindai University (1972–1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

nodes.label: Genryu Kagamishima
nodes.summary: Genryu Kagamishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served as a professor there from circa 1959 to 1983.

nodes.label: Chaesong Kim
nodes.summary: Chaesong Kim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima.

nodes.label: Eshun Otsuka
nodes.summary: Eshun Otsuka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied as a research student at Taisho University, where he also held a research student post attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Piotr Balcerowicz
nodes.summary: Piotr Balcerowicz specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Warsaw, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He held professorships at the University of Warsaw and SWPS University.

nodes.label: Marek Mejor
nodes.summary: Marek Mejor is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and was a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

nodes.label: Yoshinari Fuji
nodes.summary: Yoshinari Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University in 1986. He held posts at Daegu University, the Institute of Religious Culture, Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Rupert Gethin
nodes.summary: Rupert Gethin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held positions at the University of Bristol from 1987, the Pali Text Society, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Peter Ebbatson
nodes.summary: Peter Ebbatson is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford, where he conducted his research under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

nodes.label: Hu Shi
nodes.summary: Hu Shi was a philosopher, sinologist, and historian. He studied at Cornell University and earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor John Dewey, also learning under Kaiten Nukariya. He was president of Peking University in 1946 and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

nodes.label: John Dewey
nodes.description: American philosopher, psychologist, and educational reformer (1859–1952)
nodes.summary: A philosopher who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University, Dewey held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1884–1894), University of Minnesota (~1888–1889), University of Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).
