nodes.label: Noriaki Hosoda
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hosoda is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He held assistant and associate professor posts at Hokkaido University (attested 1986, 2003) and served as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Haruhiko Masaki
nodes.summary: Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He held a professorship at Nagasaki University (~1978–2003).

nodes.label: Shokin Furuta
nodes.summary: Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido University (~1951–1966) and Nihon University (~1966–1982).

nodes.label: Shōkō Kabutogi
nodes.summary: Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University from ~1932 to 1936 and later served as a professor there from ~1968 to 1980.

nodes.label: Taion Satomi
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Taion Satomi studied at Rissho University (~1930–1933) and served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Nobumasa Hibi
nodes.summary: Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to 1959 and later held a post there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Taishun Mibu
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Taishun Mibu studied at Taisho University (~1933–1937) and later served as its library director (~1950–1983).

nodes.label: Senchu Murano
nodes.summary: Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1935–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from approximately 1954 to 1978.

nodes.label: Michihiro Ikeda
nodes.summary: Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Natalie Maxwell
nodes.summary: Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1975) under Stephan Beyer, also studying with Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

nodes.label: Stephan Beyer
nodes.summary: Stephan Beyer specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).

nodes.label: David M. Knipe
nodes.summary: David M. Knipe is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor and Chair of Religious Studies, and later as Professor Emeritus in the Department of Languages and Cultures of Asia.

nodes.label: Robert J. Miller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Miller was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and as a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Awadh Kishore Narain
nodes.summary: Awadh Kishore Narain worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS. He held major chairs and directorships at Banaras Hindu University and was professor at Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

nodes.label: Jun Fujii
nodes.summary: Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2009 to 2013.

nodes.label: John W. Schroeder
nodes.summary: Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Don Levi, he held posts at Oregon (1993–1994), The College of Wooster (1994–1995), and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Rau
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Rau studied Indology at Leipzig under Weller and Marburg under Nobel. He held professorships at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955) and Marburg (1958–1987, succeeding Nobel), and later taught at Leipzig (1992–1993).

nodes.label: Sheng Yen
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist monk, religious scholar, and writer (1931–2009)
nodes.summary: Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Jing'an Buddhist Academy and Rissho University (~1969–1975), and under Dongchu and Lingyuan. He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Kondo
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa
nodes.summary: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and lecturer (attested 2015), and is attested at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (2026).

nodes.label: Douglas S. Duckworth
nodes.summary: Douglas S. Duckworth is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He earned his BA at James Madison University and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later teaching at East Tennessee State University.

nodes.label: Sallie B. King
nodes.summary: Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served at James Madison University as professor (circa 1992–2008) and professor emerita (circa 2008–2017).

nodes.label: Rangjung Yeshe Institute
variants: Rangjung Yeshe Institute, the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Kathmandu University
Kathmandu University - Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute
Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute
Kathmandu University's Center for Buddhist Studies
Rangjung Yeshe Institute for Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Thomas Doctor
nodes.summary: Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Christian K. Wedemeyer, and Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, and at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling. He held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Erik Pema Kunsang
nodes.summary: Erik Pema Kunsang (born 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

nodes.label: Gendün Chöphel
nodes.summary: Gendün Chöphel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung Monasteries, under teachers including Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso. In 1941, he was associated with the Maha Bodhi Society.

nodes.label: George de Roerich
variants: ユーリー・ニコラエーヴィチ
ユーリイ・リョーリフ
nodes.summary: George de Roerich specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later directing the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942).

nodes.label: Anagarika Dharmapala
variants: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.jawiki: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist revivalist and writer (1864-1933)
nodes.summary: Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Educated at S. Thomas' College (~1876–1878) and Royal College, Colombo (~1878–1883), he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

nodes.label: Albion Moonlight Butters
nodes.summary: Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he earned a PhD by 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Ngawang Samten
nodes.summary: Ngawang Samten (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at CIHTS and Ganden Monastery, he directed CIHTS (attested 1990–2019), served as Principal Teacher at the Vajrayana Institute, and held visiting posts at Smith, Hampshire, Amherst, and Tasmania.

nodes.label: Alexander von Rospatt
nodes.summary: Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at Leipzig University and serves as Professor at UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Shintaro Kitano
nodes.summary: Shintaro Kitano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda. He held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 2005) and Kyushu University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yönten Gyatso
nodes.summary: Yönten Gyatso (1932–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He obtained a Geshé degree from Drepung Gomang Dratsang, earned a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served as a research advisor there (~1981–1997).

nodes.label: Gelek Rimpoche
nodes.summary: Gelek Rimpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Monastery, the Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University, and under teachers including Ling Rinpoche and Trijang Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House New Delhi.

nodes.label: Per Kværne
nodes.summary: Per Kværne (b. 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. After earning his degrees at the University of Oslo (~1965–1973), he taught at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as professor at Oslo (1975–2007).

nodes.label: Anne-Marie Blondeau
nodes.summary: Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai
variants: Translation Committee of the English Tripiṭaka
Translation Committee of the BDK English Tripitaka
Translation Committee of the English Tripitaka
Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai, the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism
Editorial Committee of the BDK English Tripitaka

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Inada
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Inada (1923-2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983-1999) and served as chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

nodes.label: Todd A. Gibson
nodes.summary: Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Jong Cheol Lee
nodes.summary: Jong Cheol Lee studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. Active in Buddhist studies and indology, he held posts at the University of Mysore and the Academy of Korean Studies.

nodes.label: Academy of Korean Studies
variants: 韓国精神文化研究院 韓国学大学院

nodes.label: Oriental Research Institute, Mysore
variants: Mysore大学付設東方学研究所

nodes.label: Thomas A. Forsthoefel
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. under Paul J. Griffiths), and served as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Katherine Janiec Jones
nodes.summary: Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

nodes.label: W. Randolph Kloetzli
variants: W・ランドルフ・クレツリ
nodes.summary: W. Randolph Kloetzli is an Indology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Chicago in 1964 under multiple teachers. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Milton Kleintop
variants: ミルトン・クライントップ

nodes.label: Joseph Haroutunian
variants: ジョセフ・ハロウトゥニアン
nodes.summary: Joseph Haroutunian was a religious studies scholar who studied at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University (PhD ~1930-1932), and Union Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Wellesley College (1932-1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940-1962), and the University of Chicago (1962-1968).

nodes.label: Frank E. Reynolds
variants: フランク・レイノルド
nodes.description: American historian of religion and Buddhist studies scholar (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Frank E. Reynolds (1930–2019) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from circa 1967 until 2019.

nodes.label: Dartmouth College
variants: Department of Religion at Dartmouth College

nodes.label: Akira Unete
nodes.summary: Akira Unete is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career includes appointments at Otani University, where he served as an associate professor (attested 2010) and faculty member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Eiichi Yamaguchi
variants: やまぐち えいいち
nodes.summary: Eiichi Yamaguchi studied Indology and philosophy as a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990). He also held a post there as a research assistant (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Gyosho Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Toshiya Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshiya Unebe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. In 2009, he was attested as an Associate Professor in the Department of Indian Studies at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Chizuko Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earned a doctorate from the University of Vienna (1994). She advanced from lecturer to professor at the University of Tsukuba (2003–2011) and joined Toyo Bunko in 2019.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Nemoto
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Nemoto works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Hiroshima University, where he served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Kino
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Kino was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who graduated from the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).

nodes.label: Hogetsu
nodes.summary: Hogetsu (1737–1805) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Tsugen and Zuihe. He succeeded Tsugen and taught Hōkai.

nodes.label: Tanso Hirose
nodes.summary: Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and went on to found Kangien in 1801.

nodes.label: Hōkai
nodes.summary: Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.

nodes.label: Masao Abe
variants: Masao Abe (阿部 正雄, Abe Masao)
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist, professor in religious studies
nodes.summary: Masao Abe studied at Kyoto, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary under Hajime Tanabe and Daisetsu Suzuki. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Kyoto, Hanazono, and Nara universities, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Siglinde Dietz
nodes.summary: Siglinde Dietz worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn by 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar
nodes.description: Indian historian and scholar of Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) studied Indology and philosophy under K. B. Pathak. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1907–1927), honorary secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, and general secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

nodes.label: Alberto Todeschini
nodes.summary: Alberto Todeschini works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a guest post at Kyoto University and is attested at the Italian School of East Asian Studies in 2010.

nodes.label: Sojo Hirano
nodes.summary: Sojo Hirano (1930–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann. He was an associate professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and shika at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Soto Zen Buddhism
nodes.label: Research Institute of Soto Zen Buddhism
Xuesong Zhang
nodes.summary: Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and became an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hsing Yun
nodes.summary: Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Temple, Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy, and under Yinshun. He founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as its abbot from ~1967 to 1985, and taught at Tunghai University.

nodes.label: Fo Guang Shan
variants: Fo Guang Shan Buddhist monastic order

nodes.label: Taixu
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Taixu studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Wenhui Yang at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927), served at Bilu Temple, and founded multiple institutes and associations.

nodes.id: I:Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
nodes.label: Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
Takao Yamagata
nodes.summary: Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1969–1998) and served as president of the Society for Indian Philosophy and Religion (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Carlo Formichi
nodes.summary: Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kerbaker, Deussen, Oldenberg, and Bühler, and at Kiel University. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

nodes.label: Institut de civilisation indienne
variants: Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the University of Paris
Institut de Civilisation Indienne du Collège de France

nodes.label: Alfred Foucher
variants: アルフレッド・フーシェ
アルフレッド・A・フーシェ
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・フーシェ
nodes.summary: Alfred Foucher worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at EFEO, EPHE, Columbia University, Sorbonne University, and the Maison Franco-Japonaise.

nodes.label: Marcelle Lalou
nodes.summary: Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at the EPHE (1938–1963).

nodes.label: Jean Przyluski
nodes.description: French linguist and scholar of religion
nodes.summary: Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss, later holding posts at INALCO (1923–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

nodes.label: Velcheru Narayana Rao
nodes.description: Indian author, critic, and literary translator
nodes.summary: Velcheru Narayana Rao (born 1933) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University, and served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Shingo Einoo
nodes.summary: Shingo Einoo (b. 1948) specializes in indology and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1974–1980) and held a post at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1989–2013).

nodes.label: Takanobu Takahashi
nodes.summary: Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor at Shitennoji University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996; 1999–2016).

nodes.label: Tadashi Toda
nodes.summary: Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

nodes.label: Kevin Alan Vose
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Kevin Alan Vose studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD in 2005 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He also studied under traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa.

nodes.label: Ngawang Jinpa
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jinpa studied at Drepung Loseling College and worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995), and taught Kevin Alan Vose and Lobsang Tendzin.

nodes.label: National Taiwan University
variants: Department of Philosophy, National Taiwan University
台灣大學音樂學研究所

nodes.label: University of Warsaw
variants: Institute of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw

nodes.label: Maria Krzysztof Byrski
nodes.summary: Maria Krzysztof Byrski is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1955–1960). He later served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw (~1990–1996) and held a post at Civitas University.

nodes.label: Helmut Eimer
nodes.summary: Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Berlin, Hamburg, and Bonn, completing his doctorate at Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, and held a post at the University of Bonn from around 1975 to 2001.

nodes.label: Esho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at Osaka University (circa 1971–1982) and held a post at Ritsumeikan University (circa 1982–1989).

nodes.label: Norio Harada
nodes.summary: Norio Harada is a sinologist who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1964).

nodes.label: Taichiro Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Taichiro Kobayashi (1901–1963) studied Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Sentaro Sawamura and others. He worked at the Eastern Cultural Institute, Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts, and as professor at Kobe University (1950).

nodes.label: Sentaro Sawamura
nodes.summary: Sentaro Sawamura was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1907 to 1910 and later held a post there from approximately 1920 to 1930.

nodes.label: Naoki Kano
nodes.image: Mr. Naoki Kano, Advisor of the Education Association of Kyoto Prefecture.jpg
nodes.summary: Naoki Kano (1868–1947) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893). He held a post at Kyoto University beginning in 1906.

nodes.label: Kosaku Hamada
nodes.summary: Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) specialized in archaeology, history, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1905), he held posts at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1913–1938), teaching Taichiro Kobayashi and Seiichi Mizuno.

nodes.label: Konan Naito
nodes.summary: Konan Naito was a Sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Akita Normal School from 1881 to 1885. He held an academic post at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1926.

nodes.label: Kazuo Osumi
nodes.summary: Kazuo Osumi is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was an assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and a professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).

nodes.label: Chandrabhāl Tripāṭhī
nodes.summary: Chandrabhāl Tripāṭhī was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen and the University of Cologne, and served as Professor of Indology at Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Romila Thapar
nodes.summary: Romila Thapar is a historian of ancient India who completed her doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1955–1958). She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).

nodes.label: Arthur Llewellyn Basham
nodes.summary: Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He served as professor at SOAS (1957–1965) and head of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

nodes.label: Masatoshi Konishi
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at ICU, University of Calcutta, University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, holding posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

nodes.label: Toshio Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (circa 1953–1965), the University of Tokyo (circa 1965–1977), Chuo University (circa 1977–1987), and Hannan University.

nodes.label: Keinin Hayashi
nodes.summary: Keinin Hayashi is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who formerly lectured at Waseda University and has served as a full-time researcher at the Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Myles Dillon
nodes.description: Irish academic, historian, philologist and celticist (1900–1972)
nodes.summary: Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was a Celticist and Indologist who studied at University College Dublin and in Europe. He held positions at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Chicago, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: James Kenneth Powell II
nodes.summary: James Kenneth Powell II specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1998) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Ichiro Numata
nodes.summary: Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. By 2026, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Tomomichi Nitta
nodes.summary: Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 2012 and as a professor in 2026.

nodes.label: Chang-geun Hwang
nodes.summary: Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

nodes.label: Luo Changpei
nodes.summary: Luo Changpei was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held academic posts at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1944).

nodes.label: Hugh B. Urban
nodes.summary: Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wendy Doniger, and in 1998 held a post as Associate Professor in Comparative Studies at Ohio State University.

nodes.label: Wendy Doniger
nodes.summary: Wendy Doniger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an MA and PhD from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and a D.Phil. from Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, before joining the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.

nodes.label: Bruce Lincoln
nodes.summary: Bruce Lincoln is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and Chicago (~1993).

nodes.label: Clinton B. Seely
nodes.summary: Clinton B. Seely is an Indology scholar who held an academic appointment at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007 and attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

nodes.label: Jeffrey J. Kripal
nodes.summary: Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago, later holding the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (~2002).

nodes.label: Tony K. Stewart
nodes.summary: Tony K. Stewart is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and held a post at Vanderbilt University (~2011).

nodes.label: Joachim Prandstetter
nodes.summary: Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna in 1994, having studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Lessing
nodes.image: Professor Ferdinand Deiderich Lessing, Univ. of California, Berkeley. 1952.jpg
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Lessing (1882–1961) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1905). He taught at Peking University (1919–1921), Humboldt University (~1925–1938), and UC Berkeley beginning in 1938.

nodes.label: Ronald M. Davidson
nodes.summary: Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist, Tibetan, and Indic studies. He earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley in 1985, studied under numerous academic and traditional teachers, and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

nodes.label: Gil Fronsdal
nodes.summary: Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a PhD from Stanford University (~1991–1998), where he studied under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others. He served as a teacher at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997).

nodes.label: Bernard Faure
nodes.jawiki: ベルナール・フォール
nodes.summary: Bernard Faure (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who earned a Doctorat d'État from Paris Diderot University. He held professorships at Cornell (~1983–1989), Stanford (~1990–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

nodes.label: Vesna Wallace
nodes.summary: Vesna Wallace works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley and held posts at the University of Oxford (-2010) and UC Santa Barbara, where she is attested as Professor, Department Chair, and Distinguished University Professor.

nodes.label: Peter Skilling
variants: ピーター・スキリング
nodes.summary: Peter Skilling specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub by 2004. He founded and directed the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held positions at EFEO, Chulalongkorn, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Kunio Harikai
nodes.summary: Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, and later served as an Associate Professor at Saga University (~1976–1993).

nodes.label: Futoshi Omae
nodes.summary: Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Yasuke Ikari

Educated at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, he served at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), was president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

nodes.label: Satoshi Naiki
nodes.summary: Satoshi Naiki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Kyoto University, where he also served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

nodes.summary: Chijo Akamatsu was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto and at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial, Koyasan, Hanazono, Ryukoku, and Yamaguchi universities.

nodes.label: Kazuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: A scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Kazuhiko Yoshida studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~2004–2021) and Nagoya City University (2021–2024).

nodes.label: Tokuno Oda
nodes.summary: Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjiro Takakusu. He held teaching posts at Fukui Normal School, Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Mokurai Shimaji
nodes.summary: Mokurai Shimaji, a figure in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as managing director at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870), founded Chiyoda Jogakuen (1888), and was the 25th head priest of Gankyo-ji (1892–1905).

nodes.label: Enryo Inoue
nodes.summary: Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and Toyo University, serving as its lecturer and manager.

nodes.label: Teun Goudriaan
nodes.summary: Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. His academic career includes an appointment at Utrecht University, where he is attested as having served as Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Sanjukta Gupta
variants: サンジェクタ・グプタ
nodes.summary: Indology and religious studies scholar Sanjukta Gupta earned degrees from Visva-Bharati University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, University of Calcutta, Jadavpur University (~1962–1967), Utrecht University (~1968–1986), and University of Oxford (~1986–2000).

nodes.label: Kojun Fukui
nodes.summary: Kojun Fukui was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Waseda University, studying under Sokichi Tsuda. He served as a professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and as president of Taisho University.

nodes.label: Joen Imai
nodes.summary: Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University, with posts attested in 2010 and 2026.

nodes.label: Takudo Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Takudo Ishikawa works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career includes serving as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and holding teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

nodes.label: Kengo Harimoto
nodes.summary: Kengo Harimoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyushu University and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass. Harimoto has held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

nodes.label: Kenji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop, also studying at Leiden University (2015-2016). He held a fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.

nodes.label: Peter Bisschop
nodes.summary: Peter Bisschop specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, later serving as Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Editor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Andrey Klebanov
nodes.summary: Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist who completed his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg, studying under Harunaga Isaacson, among others. He was appointed Professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: James L. Fitzgerald
nodes.summary: James L. Fitzgerald specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as Professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Ryosaburo Sakaki
nodes.summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895). He lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and held professorships at Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

nodes.label: Gikyo Ito
nodes.summary: Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University (-1935, 1953) under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, and was a professor there (1968–1972) and at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

nodes.label: Koji Kamioka
nodes.summary: Koji Kamioka was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara. He was a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University in 1969 and a staff member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

nodes.label: Norihiko Uchida
nodes.summary: Norihiko Uchida is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).

nodes.label: Shingo Enomoto
nodes.summary: Shingo Enomoto (b. 1948) is an indologist who earned a PhD from the University of Marburg (~1974–1980). From circa 1982 to 1989, he held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology.

nodes.label: Takao Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takao Hayashi is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. His academic career includes posts at Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Doshisha University (1986–2015).

nodes.label: Mizuho Okita
nodes.summary: Mizuho Okita works in religious studies and Indology, having studied at Tokai University, Gakushuin University, under Katsuhiko Kamimura, and with doctoral supervisor Atsuhiko Yoshida. Okita was attested as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University in 2008.

nodes.label: Atsuhiko Yoshida

nodes.label: Anand Venkatkrishnan

nodes.label: David Pingree
nodes.summary: David Pingree was a scholar of Indology and history. He earned his bachelor's and doctorate from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (from 1971).

nodes.label: Sonja Glauch
nodes.summary: Sonja Glauch (born 1967) is a linguist who completed her Magister, doctorate, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1986–2005). She held posts at Heidelberg University Library, Erlangen-Nuremberg (2007), Vienna (visiting professor, 2008), and Munich (deputy professor, 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Karl Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

nodes.label: Eva Tichy
nodes.summary: Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1974–1981) and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg (~1982–1989). She held a chair at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

nodes.label: Yoshitsugu Sawai
nodes.summary: Yoshitsugu Sawai (b. 1951) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman. He was a professor and dean of human studies at Tenri University (~1984–2017).

nodes.label: Arindam Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Arindam Chakrabarti earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford and works in philosophy and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Delhi and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later holding the Mattoo Endowed Chair at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gösta Liebert
nodes.summary: Gösta Liebert studied at Lund and Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. An Indology and linguistics scholar, he held posts at Lund University, Uppsala University (1951–1953), and as professor at Gothenburg University (1955–1982).

nodes.jawiki: スティグ・ヴィカンデル
nodes.description: Swedish historian of religion and iranologist (1908–1983)
nodes.summary: Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was an Indology and Iranian studies scholar. Educated at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and at Copenhagen, he held posts at Lund University and served as chair of Sanskrit at Uppsala (1953–1974).

nodes.label: Hugh Edward Richardson
nodes.summary: Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Keble College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1930–1950) and was later an Honorary Fellow at the British Academy (1952) and Keble College (1981).

nodes.label: Keishin Okamura
nodes.summary: Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught as an associate and visiting professor at Koyasan University and served as a professor at Kochi University.

nodes.label: Miki Ujiie
nodes.summary: Miki Ujiie is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Tribhuvan University. He held an instructional post at Koyasan University (attested 1970).

nodes.label: Naoji Okuyama
nodes.summary: Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He served as an assistant and lecturer at Tohoku University (~1985–1993) before becoming a professor at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).

nodes.label: Munenobu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1986–1989), later serving as assistant professor at Iwate University and professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

nodes.label: Kōken Unno
nodes.summary: Kōken Unno, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earned master's and doctoral degrees at Nagoya University. He held positions at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (attested 2002).

Ikko Arai
nodes.summary: Ikko Arai is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Komazawa University. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

nodes.label: Tetsuhiko Shibata
nodes.summary: Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued his education at Taisho University. During his studies, he was taught by Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

nodes.label: Takeshi Fujii
nodes.summary: Takeshi Fujii is a historian and Indologist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, serving as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus (2021).

nodes.label: Takashi Yamada
nodes.summary: Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He held a post as assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Toru Kumeji
nodes.summary: Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held positions at the Institute of Humanities Informatics and as a senior researcher at the Institute of Digital Humanities (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hidenaka Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hidenaka Tanaka was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920-1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1951-1974).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Broughton
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Kozui Otani

nodes.label: Yuko Kamishima
nodes.summary: Yuko Kamishima works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Kamishima studied at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and Ritsumeikan University (2016).

nodes.label: Koji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Bukkyo University, earning a doctorate in literature in 1991. He served as an assistant professor and professor at Bukkyo University between circa 1969 and 2005.

nodes.label: Eva K. Neumaier

nodes.label: Eduard Hermann

nodes.label: G. P. Malalasekera
nodes.summary: G. P. Malalasekera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He held senior posts at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, later serving as a visiting professor there and teaching philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1974).

nodes.label: Mrinal Kanti Gangopadhyay

nodes.summary: François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Lyon from circa 1950 to 1955 and later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1977 to 2002.

nodes.label: Csaba Kiss
nodes.summary: Csaba Kiss is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed a D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2003–2009) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Libbie Mills
nodes.summary: Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She held a post teaching Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Thanon Chitkament
nodes.summary: Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under guide V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Eugen Hultzsch
nodes.summary: Eugen Hultzsch studied at Leipzig and under Georg Bühler in Vienna. Specializing in Indology, he served as Government Epigraphist in India (1886–1903) and held the chair of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg from 1903 to 1925.

nodes.label: Hosakote Krishna Sastri
nodes.summary: Hosakote Krishna Sastri (1870–1928) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He served as an epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1904 to 1925 and as Government Epigraphist for India from circa 1920 to 1925.

nodes.label: Georg von Simson
nodes.summary: Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1953–1956) and completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1956–1965), later working at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

nodes.label: Thích Minh Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He was a lecturer at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1961) and Vice Chancellor of Van Hanh University (~1964–1975).

nodes.label: Ashok Narhar Aklujkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Narhar Aklujkar is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

nodes.label: Tatiana Oranskaia
nodes.summary: Tatiana Oranskaia (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

nodes.label: Arthur William Ryder
nodes.summary: Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD 1901) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as instructor at Harvard (1902–1906) and professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1906–1938).

nodes.label: Vempati Kutumba Sastry
nodes.summary: Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

nodes.label: Mamata Dash

nodes.label: Krishna Venkateswara Sarma

nodes.label: Mark Singleton
nodes.summary: Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Elizabeth De Michelis. He held a post as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Eivind Kahrs
nodes.summary: Eivind Kahrs is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. Kahrs taught Aleix Ruiz-Falqués, held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010), and is attested as a Council Member of the Pali Text Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Elizabeth De Michelis
nodes.summary: Elizabeth De Michelis studied at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1998–2002). Working in Indology and religious studies, she directed the Dharam Hinduja Institute of Indic Research (2000) and held posts at the Universities of Cambridge and Oxford.

nodes.label: Suzanne Newcombe

nodes.summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He served as a professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

nodes.label: Ernst Johann Eitel
nodes.summary: Ernst Johann Eitel, a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earned his MA and PhD at the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and taught German language and literature at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

nodes.label: Raffaele Torella
nodes.summary: Indologist and philosopher Raffaele Torella studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1970–1974). He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from ~1976 to 2020.

nodes.label: August Fischer
nodes.summary: August Fischer worked in linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from c. 1884 to 1889. He held a post at Leipzig University from c. 1900 to 1930 and was a board member of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft in 1910.

nodes.label: Anant Sadashiv Altekar
nodes.description: historian, archaeologist, and numismatist from Maharashtra, India
nodes.summary: Anant Sadashiv Altekar was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), the Numismatic Society of India (1947), Patna University (~1949–1957), and the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

nodes.label: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington
nodes.image: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, negative, 1927 (Lafayette; NPG x41720).png
nodes.summary: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington (1899-1986) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, and held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1931-1948) and the University of London (~1948-1966).

nodes.label: Cyril Henry Philips
nodes.summary: Historian and indologist Cyril Henry Philips studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS. He succeeded Ralph Lilley Turner as Director of SOAS in 1957 and later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London from 1972 to 1976.

nodes.label: Ying-shih Yü
nodes.summary: Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a sinologist and historian educated at Yenching, New Asia College, and Harvard. He held major posts at Michigan, Harvard, New Asia College, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton (1987–2001).

nodes.label: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani
nodes.summary: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai (PhD) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt and at MS University of Baroda, where he taught Sanskrit (~1951–1980) and directed the Oriental Institute (1975–1981).

nodes.label: Parashuram Krishna Gode
nodes.image: Dr. Parshuram Krishna Gode, M.A., D. Litt.jpg

nodes.label: K. R. Norman
nodes.summary: K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned his M.A. at Downing College, Cambridge. He taught at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

nodes.label: Frank Raymond Allchin
nodes.summary: Frank Raymond Allchin (1923–2010) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He earned his BA at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959–1989), and was affiliated with the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

nodes.label: David Roy Shackleton Bailey
nodes.summary: David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge (Litt.D. 1958), he held appointments at Cambridge, Harvard University as Pope Professor of Latin (1975–1988), and the University of Michigan (1988–2002).

nodes.label: Paul Mus
nodes.summary: Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology educated at Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EFEO, Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University.

nodes.label: Kun Chang
nodes.summary: Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist. Educated at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang, he held positions at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington (from 1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Samuel Beal
nodes.summary: Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Durham. He served as headmaster at Bramham College (1848–1850) and as Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877; University of London ~1877–1889).

nodes.label: Trinity College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Cornelis Petrus Tiele
nodes.jawiki: コルネーリス・ティーレ
nodes.summary: Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Remonstrant Seminary and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts as a Remonstrant pastor and professor, and as professor of the history of religions at Leiden University (1873, 1877–1901).

nodes.label: Teruji Ishizu
nodes.summary: Teruji Ishizu (1903–1972) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as dean and president (1963–1966), and later served as president of Miyagi University of Education.

nodes.label: Ichiro Hori
nodes.summary: Ichiro Hori was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he also studied under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
nodes.description: Indian archeologist and historian from Bihar
nodes.summary: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of London (SOAS) under Lionel David Barnett. His posts included Patna College (~1942), Patna University department head (1958), and K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.

nodes.label: Patna University
variants: Department of History and Archaeology at Patna University

nodes.label: Thomas Oberlies
nodes.summary: Thomas Oberlies (born 1960) is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001) and an Arbeitsstellenleiter post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Peter Schreiner
nodes.summary: Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who earned his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (~1970–1972) and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).

nodes.label: Zumo Zhou
nodes.summary: Zumo Zhou (1914–1995) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Peking University under Luo Changpei. He held appointments at Academia Sinica, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1940–1952), and Peking University as associate professor (1947) and professor (1950).

nodes.label: August Hjalmar Edgren
nodes.summary: August Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

nodes.label: Per Kjeld Sørensen
nodes.summary: Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Copenhagen (1971–~1990) under Erik Haarh, he held posts at Copenhagen (1982–1989), Leipzig University (1994–2017), and UC Berkeley (2017).

nodes.label: Sangye Tenzin
nodes.summary: Sangye Tenzin (1904–1978) worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, serving as Abbot of Menri Monastery and studying as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia (attested 2026). He taught Matthew T. Kapstein and Lopon Tenzin Namdak.

nodes.label: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Geshe degree from Menri Monastery and the Dialectic School, where he served as director (~1986–1989), and later founded Ligmincha Institute and Ligmincha International.

nodes.label: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima
variants: H. H. Menri Khen Rinpoche Lungdog Denpa Nyima
nodes.summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery (~1943–1953) under Horwa Drungrampa Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot beginning in 1969.

nodes.label: Anne C. Klein
nodes.summary: Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), she founded Dawn Mountain (~1996) and became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University (~1987).

nodes.label: Namkhai Norbu
nodes.summary: Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Derge Gonchen and under several traditional masters, and served as Professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1962–1992) and University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

nodes.label: Geshe Tsondru Kongpel
nodes.summary: Geshe Tsondru Kongpel is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Rice University
variants: Center for Cultural Studies, Rice University
Center for Cultural Studies at Rice University

nodes.label: Gergely Hidas
nodes.summary: Gergely Hidas is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2002–2008). He was a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum (2014).

nodes.label: Hermann Hirt
nodes.summary: Hermann Hirt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University, subsequently holding posts at Leipzig University (1891-1912) and as professor at the University of Giessen (1912-1936).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Streitberg
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Streitberg studied linguistics and Indology at Münster, Leipzig (under Brugmann and Windisch), and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1899), Münster (1899), Munich (1909–1920), and Leipzig (1898; 1920–1925, succeeding Brugmann).

nodes.label: Donald R. Davis Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle, and held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Richard W. Lariviere
nodes.summary: Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at the University of Iowa and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean and professor emeritus at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, and president of the Field Museum.

nodes.label: Patrick Olivelle
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Indologist and Sanskrit scholar (born 1942)
nodes.summary: Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford and earned his Ph.D. under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Timothy Lubin
nodes.summary: Timothy Lubin (born 1964) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1994. He held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Louis Dumont
nodes.summary: Louis Dumont specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying under Marcel Mauss and Walther Schubring. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, the University of Oxford (1951–1955), and the EPHE/EHESS (1955).

nodes.id: I:Directorate of Archaeology, Archives and Museums, Madhya Pradesh
nodes.label: Directorate of Archaeology, Archives and Museums, Madhya Pradesh
variants: Department of Archaeology, Museums and Archives in Madhya Pradesh

nodes.label: Anne Casile
nodes.summary: Anne Casile is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2005–2009) and joined the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2012).

nodes.label: Karl Benedikt Hase
nodes.summary: Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied at Jena and Helmstedt, and later held long-term posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1805–1864), École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

nodes.label: Helga Uebach
nodes.summary: Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (c. 1960–1967) and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a scientific collaborator in 1964.

nodes.id: I:Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities

nodes.label: Jampa Losang Panglung
nodes.summary: Jampa Losang Panglung worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery (-1958) and the University of Munich (~1968–1979), later serving as a research staff member at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–2004).

nodes.label: Erich Haenisch
variants: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.jawiki: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.summary: Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a Sinologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Göttingen (1925), Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

nodes.label: C. R. Lama
nodes.summary: C. R. Lama specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, held a post at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1997), and taught James Low and Andreas Ruft.

nodes.label: Tatsushi Tamai
nodes.summary: Tatsushi Tamai specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a visiting researcher at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (attested 2010–2016).

nodes.label: Saraju Rath
nodes.summary: Saraju Rath is an Indologist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies (attested 2012 and 2022).

nodes.label: Max Sparreboom
nodes.image: 2015 Erasmus Prize - 25 November 2015 - Stichting Praemium Erasmianum (4).JPG

nodes.label: Christopher Minkowski
nodes.summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist who studied at Harvard College, the University of Delhi, and Harvard University. He held positions at Brown University, the University of Iowa, Cornell University (1989–2006), and Oxford University as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

nodes.label: Gérard Colas
nodes.summary: Gérard Colas specializes in Indology and religious studies. He has served as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS, attested in 2004 and 2009, as well as at the Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud in 2012.

nodes.id: I:Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud

variants: Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud, École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales
Centre d’Études de l’Inde et de l’Asie du Sud, École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales
Centre for Indian and South Asian Studies (Paris)
Centre for Indian and Southern Asian Studies

variants: Institute for the Study of Religions
Institute of English Studies Jagiellonian University

nodes.label: Heike Oberlin
nodes.summary: Heike Oberlin is an Indology scholar who studied at Kerala Kalamandalam and Tübingen, completing her PhD at Würzburg (~2001–2004) and Habilitation at Tübingen (~2005–2013). She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

nodes.label: Saraswathi Mahal Library
variants: Thanjavur Maharaja Serfoji's Saraswathi Mahal Library

nodes.label: Kim Plofker
nodes.summary: Kim Plofker (born 1964) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford and Brown under David Pingree, and held posts at Brown, Dibner Institute, Utrecht, MIT, and Union College, where she became associate professor in 2019.

nodes.label: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma
nodes.description: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma, Dept. of Sanskrit, Aligarh Muslim U., Aligarh-202002
nodes.summary: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD 1963-1966), later serving as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1976-1997).

nodes.label: Jack Goody
nodes.summary: Jack Goody, who worked in history and archaeology, studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He spent his academic career at the University of Cambridge (~1954–1984).

nodes.label: S. N. Savadi
nodes.summary: S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

nodes.label: Sao Htun Hmat Win
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Sao Htun Hmat Win studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at the University of Yangon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).

nodes.label: University of Yangon
variants: Pāli and Abhidhamma Department of the University of Yangon

variants: International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies at Kaba-Aye

nodes.label: Ministry of Religious Affairs and Culture
variants: Ministry of Religious Affairs, Union of Myanmar

nodes.label: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar
nodes.summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and later as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

nodes.label: Subhash Kak
nodes.image: Subhash Kak at Single Photon Workshop, Geneva, July 2015.jpg
nodes.summary: Subhash Kak (born 1947) works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan. His career includes professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

nodes.label: Albert Debrunner
nodes.summary: Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer, Alfred Körte, Friedrich Leo, and Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships and teaching posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, Bern, and Basel.

nodes.label: Robert B. Ekvall
nodes.description: missionary, explorer, ethnographer, curator of Asian ethnology (1898-1983)
nodes.summary: Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetology and history scholar. He served as a research fellow at the University of Washington (1958), a research associate at the University of Chicago (1958–1960), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (1963–1983).

nodes.label: Csaba Dezső
nodes.summary: Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2004.

nodes.label: R. Sathyanarayana
nodes.summary: R. Sathyanarayana was an Indologist who completed a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College from 1949 to 1984 and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

nodes.label: Surendranath Dasgupta
variants: スレンドラナート・ダスグプタ
nodes.description: Bengali scholar of Sanskrit and philosophy (1887-1952)
nodes.summary: Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Calcutta and Cambridge (PhD ~1920–1922). He held posts at Chittagong College, Presidency College, Cambridge, Sanskrit College (Principal ~1931–1942), and the University of Calcutta (Chair of Philosophy ~1942–1945).

nodes.label: Mircea Eliade
variants: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.jawiki: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.description: Romanian-American historian, writer, philosopher and professor at the University of Chicago (1907–1986)
nodes.summary: Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Universities of Bucharest and Calcutta, and held posts at Bucharest, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Christopher Wallis
nodes.summary: Christopher Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from the University of Rochester, the University of Oxford (studying under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as a guest lecturer at Naropa University.

nodes.label: Robert P. Goldman
nodes.summary: Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and S. D. Joshi. He has held a professorship at UC Berkeley from ~1971.

nodes.label: M. Seshagiri Sastri
nodes.summary: M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar who served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Kolkata, both attested in 1899.

nodes.label: K. Kunjunni Raja
nodes.summary: K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned PhDs from the University of Madras and University of London (under John Brough), and held posts at Madras, the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

nodes.label: Harald Hauptmann
nodes.description: German praehistorian and near eastern archaeologist
nodes.summary: Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) was a scholar of archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin, he held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, Heidelberg University, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Shivram Dattatray Joshi
nodes.summary: Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and department head at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Peri Sarveswara Sharma
nodes.summary: Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Rau from around 1968 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Marburg from circa 1971 to 1991.

nodes.label: Karl Richard Lepsius
nodes.jawiki: カール・リヒャルト・レプシウス
nodes.summary: Karl Richard Lepsius was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1846–1884) and served as Chief Librarian at Berlin State Library.

nodes.label: Florinda De Simini
nodes.summary: Florinda De Simini is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2017).

nodes.label: Nirajan Kafle
nodes.summary: Nirajan Kafle specializes in Indology. He studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane, completing his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter Bisschop in 2015. He held posts at the University of Naples (2019) and Leiden (2021).

nodes.label: A. N. Krishna Aiyangar
nodes.summary: A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist. He held posts as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin (attested 1942) and at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1942).

nodes.label: John Myrdhin Reynolds
nodes.summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lopon Tenzin Namdak, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Namkhai Norbu.

nodes.label: Megumu Honda
nodes.summary: Megumu Honda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells, and later served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Johannes Rahder
nodes.summary: Johannes Rahder was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University. He held chairs at Utrecht (1930–1931) and Leiden (1931–1946) before serving as a professor at Yale University (1947–1965).

nodes.label: Paul Tedesco
nodes.summary: Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, held a research post at Princeton, and later became a professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at Yale University.

nodes.label: Rulon Wells
nodes.summary: Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology who studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942). He held an academic post at Yale University from ~1945 to 1989.

nodes.label: Eng Jin Ooi
nodes.summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Mahidol University under the supervision of Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

nodes.label: Walter Clawiter
nodes.description: born:1923|died:1970|; Clawiter, Walter 1923-1970; Clawiter; Clawiter, Walter ....-1970; Clawiter, Walter, m. 1970

nodes.label: Zhihua Yao
nodes.summary: Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002) and held positions at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).

nodes.label: Dipesh Chakrabarty
variants: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.jawiki: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.summary: Dipesh Chakrabarty works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University under Donald Anthony Low. He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago (1995).

nodes.label: Ronald Inden
nodes.summary: Ronald Inden (b. 1940) is an Indologist and historian. He served at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

nodes.label: John D. Kelly
nodes.summary: Kelly is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held appointments at the University of Chicago, serving as the Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Christopher Pinney
nodes.image: The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Shri Award to Prof. Christopher Pinney, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 20, 2013.jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Pinney works in Indology and history/archaeology. His career includes posts at the Australian National University (~1993–1995), University College London (professor from ~1995), the University of Chicago (~2000–2001), Northwestern University (~2008), the University of Cape Town, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.label: Donald Anthony Low
nodes.summary: Donald Anthony Low was a historian and Indologist who studied at Exeter College and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Australian National University (~1959–1982), the University of Sussex (~1964–1972), and the University of Cambridge (~1983–1994).

nodes.label: Siniruddha Dash
nodes.summary: Siniruddha Dash works in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras from 2000 to 2014 and became director at the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

nodes.label: Godabarish Mishra
nodes.summary: Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: N. Veezhinathan
nodes.summary: N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. He studied under A. Sankaran, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and T. M. P. Mahadevan, and was appointed Lecturer at Madras in 1964.

nodes.label: Elisa Freschi
nodes.summary: Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2006). She held positions at the University of Vienna (~2012–2017), the IKGA (~2017–2022), and became Associate Professor at the University of Toronto (~2022).

nodes.label: John Taber

nodes.label: Andrew Huxley

nodes.label: Peter Koret

nodes.label: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi
