nodes.label: Navalpakkam Ramanuja Tatacharya
nodes.summary: Navalpakkam Ramanuja Tatacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry and served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University from 1989 to 1994.

nodes.label: Stewart McFarlane

nodes.label: Bret W. Davis
nodes.summary: Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, held research and teaching posts at Otani, Shiga, Kwansei Gakuin, and Kyoto universities, and taught philosophy at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).

nodes.label: Jake H. Davis
nodes.summary: Jake H. Davis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and CUNY, and with several traditional teachers. He held posts at Brown University, NYU, City College of New York, and BCBS.

nodes.label: William Edelglass
nodes.summary: William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics as a visiting professor.

nodes.label: Alan Fox

nodes.label: Richard P. Hayes
nodes.summary: Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya, holding posts at Toronto, McGill University, and the University of New Mexico.

He headed Calcutta's Pali Department (~1930–1958) and presided over the Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

nodes.label: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya

nodes.label: Shaman Hatley

nodes.label: Stanley Wolpert

nodes.label: Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Calcutta, Presidency College, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand under Ganganatha Jha, he served as a lecturer, reader, and professor at Allahabad, and as Director of Sampurnanand's Research Institute.

nodes.label: Sheldon Pollock
nodes.summary: Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard University (~1971–1975). His career includes professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University (~2005).

nodes.label: David N. Lorenzen
nodes.summary: David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he served as a professor and research scholar at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010 (emeritus 2019).

nodes.label: Sonam Kachru
nodes.summary: Sonam Kachru works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago under Daniel A. Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and the Max Planck Institute, later becoming Assistant Professor at Yale (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Mohanty
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, and Emory, and served as professor at Temple University (~1986–2011).

nodes.label: Edward C. Dimock Jr.
nodes.summary: Edward C. Dimock Jr., an Indologist and scholar of religion, studied at Harvard (Ph.D. ~1954-1959) and Yale. He served as assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972-1986).

nodes.label: Kashinath Trimbak Telang
nodes.description: Indian judge, Indologist, writer and translator (1850–1893)
nodes.summary: Kashinath Trimbak Telang studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. In Indology, he held posts at Elphinstone College, served as syndic (1881) and vice-chancellor (1892–1893) of the University of Mumbai, and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1892–1893).

nodes.label: Mahesh A. Deokar
nodes.summary: Mahesh A. Deokar specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.id: I:Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
nodes.label: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
variants: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies

nodes.label: David Drewes
nodes.summary: David Drewes studied at Lawrence University, UW-Madison, and UVA (PhD 2006 under Karen Christina Lang). He taught at UVA, Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh
nodes.summary: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College. He worked at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Professor of Sanskrit & Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

nodes.label: Ramchandra B. Athavale
nodes.summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at S.L.D. Arts College (attested in 1938) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith.

nodes.label: James McHugh
nodes.summary: James McHugh works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, his teachers included Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Lawrence J. McCrea
nodes.summary: Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a professor at Cornell University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Anne E. Monius
nodes.summary: Anne E. Monius was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) before returning to Harvard University as professor of South Asian Religions in 2002.

nodes.label: Parimal G. Patil
nodes.summary: Parimal G. Patil is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University (c. 1991–1993) and the University of Chicago (c. 1993–2002). Around 2004, he became a Professor at Harvard University.

nodes.label: University of Southern California
variants: USC Shinso Ito Center for Japanese Religions and Culture
南カリフォルニア大学

nodes.label: Jayashree Sathe
nodes.summary: Jayashree Sathe specializes in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as editor in chief (attested 2011) and later as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Pondicherry University
variants: Subramania Bharathi School of Tamil Language and Literature, Pondicherry University

nodes.label: K. A. Subramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist who taught D. N. Shukla. He served as Professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972 and 1987) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Department of Oriental Manuscripts Publications
variants: Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum

nodes.label: Victor Turner
variants: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.summary: Victor Turner worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester, holding posts at Manchester (~1955–1963), Cornell (1963), the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

nodes.label: Lawrence E. Sullivan
nodes.summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000) and the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2004), and as Professor of Theology at Notre Dame (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Joseph Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Joseph Kitagawa was a religious studies, Japanology, and history scholar. He studied at Rikkyo University, CDSP, Seabury-Western, and Chicago under Joachim Wach (PhD ~1951). He spent his career at the University of Chicago (1951-1987), serving as dean of the Divinity School.

nodes.id: I:Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing
nodes.label: Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing
variants: 島根県立国際短期大学

nodes.label: Alexandra van der Geer
nodes.summary: Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Y. Sondaar.

nodes.label: Kern Institute
variants: Kern Institute, Leiden University, the Netherlands
Kern Institute of Indology, Leiden University
Kern-Institut für Indische Archäologie und Geschichte der Universität Leiden
Kern Institute for Archaeology and Indian History, Leiden University

nodes.label: Shoshun Hayashidera
nodes.summary: Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and was a professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hirotomo Teranishi
variants: Teranishi Hirotomo 寺西 宏友
nodes.summary: Hirotomo Teranishi served as a professor and assistant vice-president at Soka University in 2010. He succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 as Director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, holding the role into the 2010s.

nodes.label: Herbert Härtel
nodes.summary: Herbert Härtel worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, directed the Museum of Asian Art, and held professorships at Humboldt and Free universities.

nodes.label: Oliver Philipp Frey
nodes.summary: Oliver Philipp Frey is a scholar in indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Yasutaka Muroya
nodes.summary: Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He has been affiliated as a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and Leipzig University (attested 2015), and at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Elena Mucciarelli
nodes.summary: Elena Mucciarelli is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held posts at Tübingen and was appointed Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition at the University of Groningen in 2020.

nodes.label: Annette L. Heitmann
nodes.summary: Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg, and attended the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) before earning her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna by 2002.

nodes.label: Eshin Nishimura
nodes.summary: Eshin Nishimura studied at Hanazono and Kyoto universities, Pendle Hill, and under Zenkei Shibayama. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Carleton College and served as director of the IRIZ and president of Hanazono University (2002–2005).

nodes.label: Ensho Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor and later professor emeritus at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Paul Pelliot
variants: ポール・ユジェーヌ・ペリオ
nodes.summary: Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) specialized in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying under Émile Senart, Sylvain Lévi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as a professor at the EFEO and held the Central Asian chair at the Collège de France (1911–1945).

nodes.label: Henri Cordier
nodes.image: Gustave Caillebotte - Henri Cordier - Google Art Project.jpg
nodes.description: French linguist, historian, ethnographer, author, editor and Orientalist (1849–1925)
nodes.summary: Henri Cordier, who studied at Lycée Chaptal, worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and at Sciences Po (~1885–1925).

nodes.label: Noël Péri
nodes.summary: Noël Péri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar. He taught Western music at Tokyo Fine Arts School (1896–1906), founded Tenchijin and Mélanges japonais, and served as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911) at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

nodes.id: I:Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises
nodes.label: Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: ベルギー中國學高等研究所
Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises

nodes.label: Gaston Renondeau
variants: ガストン・ルノンドー
nodes.image: Major Gaston Renondeau - Allied missions at Vladivostock LCCN2014708663 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gaston Renondeau was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1898 to 1900.

nodes.label: Henri Maspero
nodes.image: 201230 camp de Buchenwald dessins de prisonniers par Léon Mazeaud Henri Maspéro Bloc 61 1944 JB (2) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Henri Maspero studied under Édouard Chavannes and at INALCO and EFEO. He worked at EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930), and held chairs in Sinology at the Collège de France (1918–1945), University of Paris, and Sorbonne University.

nodes.label: Marcel Granet
nodes.summary: Marcel Granet was a Sinologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held professorships at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.

nodes.label: Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: パリ大學中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Étienne Balazs
variants: エティエンヌ・バラ―シュ
エティエンヌ・バラーシュ
nodes.summary: A scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology, Étienne Balazs earned his doctorate under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later worked as a CNRS senior researcher (1949) and held a professorship at the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1955–1963).

nodes.label: Otto Franke
nodes.summary: Otto Franke was a sinologist and indologist who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut and University of Hamburg (1910–1923) and was professor of sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

nodes.label: Jacques Gernet
nodes.summary: Jacques Gernet, a scholar of sinology and history, studied at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at EPHE/EHESS (1955–1976), the University of Paris (1957–1968), Paris Diderot University (~1968–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

nodes.label: André Bareau
nodes.summary: André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, later holding professorships at EPHE (1956-1973) and the Collège de France (1971-1991).

nodes.label: Bernard Frank
variants: ベルナール・フランク
nodes.summary: Bernard Frank (1927–1996) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies and studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1976) and held the chair of Japanese Civilisation at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

nodes.label: Michel Soymié
nodes.summary: Michel Soymié (1924–2002) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO (-1952) and held positions at the CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1953–1966), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1957–1960), and EPHE (~1966–1992).

nodes.id: I:Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali
nodes.label: Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali
Kenji Shimada
nodes.summary: Kenji Shimada (1917-2000) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1938 to 1941 and worked there as a researcher from circa 1954 to 1981.

nodes.label: Annette Schmiedchen
nodes.summary: Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where she was a faculty member (around 1999–2014) before researching at Humboldt around 2014.

nodes.label: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson
nodes.summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1858–1861), served as President of the Asiatic Society (1886–1887), and was Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

nodes.label: Atsushi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indologist who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Joseph E. Schwartzberg
nodes.summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, University of Paris, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne (PhD 1960). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, JNU, and University of Minnesota (1964-2000).

nodes.label: Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Russische Akademie der Wissenschaften in Sankt Petersburg
russische kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften in St. Petersburg
Russische Akademie der Wissenschaften in St. Petersburg
ロシア科学アカデミー
Imperial Academy of Sciences at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Adam Bowles
nodes.summary: Adam Bowles is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate under Greg Bailey. He served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

nodes.label: Greg Bailey
nodes.summary: Greg Bailey (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He served as a professor at La Trobe University, where his posts were attested in 1994 and 2004.

nodes.label: Julia Leslie
nodes.summary: Julia Leslie worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies, and held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1993 to 2004.

nodes.label: Palmira Brummett
nodes.summary: Palmira Brummett is a historian and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Chicago (1975) and an MPH from the University of Illinois (1981). She held posts at the University of Tennessee (c. 1987–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Robin Coningham
nodes.summary: Robin Coningham is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1989–1994) and held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).

nodes.label: Ryuo
nodes.summary: Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (Tō-ji Sōgaku) and at Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Hirth
nodes.summary: Friedrich Hirth worked in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald, and served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870-1897) before becoming Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University in 1902.

nodes.label: William Woodville Rockhill
variants: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Rockhill studied at Lycée Condorcet and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873). He was taught by Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux.

nodes.label: Prayoon Mererk
nodes.native: ประยูร ธมฺมจิตฺโต
nodes.summary: Prayoon Mererk is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010–2011) and chairperson of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (attested 2010).

nodes.id: I:Educational Department of the Bombay Presidency
nodes.label: Educational Department of the Bombay Presidency
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate
nodes.summary: Abaji Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist who succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. He held the post of Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Andrew J. Nicholson
nodes.summary: Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, and studied under Shree Narayan Mishra. He is an Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.summary: John Marshall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Cambridge, the British School at Athens, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.

nodes.label: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit
nodes.summary: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944.

nodes.label: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917).

nodes.label: George Abraham Grierson
variants: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.description: Irish linguistic scholar and civil servant (1851–1941)
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist George Abraham Grierson was educated at St Bees School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1873–1903), directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and was a governor of SOAS (1917–1925).

nodes.label: M. H. Krishna
nodes.image: Portrait photograph of M. H. Krishna.jpg
nodes.summary: M. H. Krishna was a historian and Indologist who studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He was Professor of History, department head, and dean at the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Charles Duroiselle
nodes.summary: Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught Pali at the University of Yangon (~1906–1919) and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940).

nodes.label: Madeleine Biardeau
nodes.summary: Madeleine Biardeau was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied at the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (~1943–1946) and the University of Kerala (~1953–1954), and was an enseignante at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Samuel
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach, later holding professorships at Lancaster, Newcastle, and Cardiff universities.

nodes.label: University of Newcastle
variants: University of Newcastle, New South Wales

nodes.label: Sandra Bell
nodes.summary: Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and subsequently held a post there.

nodes.label: Jules Oppert
variants: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.jawiki: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.summary: Jules Oppert was a linguist and historian who earned his PhD from Kiel University (1847) after studies at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Berlin. He taught at INALCO (1857) and was a professor at the Collège de France (1874-1905).

nodes.label: R. Venkatraman
nodes.summary: R. Venkatraman works in Indology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, later serving there as Reader, attested in 1990.

nodes.label: Madurai Kamaraj University
variants: Department of Art History, M.K. University, Madurai

nodes.label: Kamil Václav Zvelebil
nodes.summary: Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from Charles University in 1952. He worked at the Oriental Institute (1952–1970) and was a professor of Dravidian studies at Utrecht University (~1976–1992).

nodes.label: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat
nodes.summary: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and positions at EHESS, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: V. Kameswari
nodes.summary: V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as a supervisor and guide (attested 2026).

nodes.label: K. S. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: K. S. Balasubramanian is an Indologist and philosopher. He has held posts at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

nodes.label: T. V. Vasudeva
nodes.summary: T. V. Vasudeva is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. His career includes serving at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Deputy Director (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ralph Lilley Turner
nodes.description: Indic languages philologist and university administrator (1888–1983)
nodes.summary: Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Christ's College, Cambridge. He held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University and was a professor at the University of London and director of SOAS from 1922 to 1957.

nodes.label: Harold Walter Bailey
variants: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.jawiki: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.summary: Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and the University of Oxford under Frederick William Thomas. He held posts at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

nodes.label: Jules Bloch
nodes.summary: Jules Bloch studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at INALCO (1921-1937), EPHE (1919-1951), and the Collège de France (1936-1951).

nodes.label: Bernhard Breloer
nodes.summary: Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist who served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1945), where he succeeded Heinrich Lüders.

nodes.label: Friedrich Weller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at Leipzig University, studying under August Conrady, and later held teaching posts there (~1922-1928, 1938-1958) and membership in the Saxon Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Paul Thieme
nodes.summary: Paul Thieme (1905–2001) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale University (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

nodes.label: Herbert Niel Randle
nodes.summary: Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He was professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (circa 1910–1927) and served as Librarian at the India Office and India Office Records (1927–1949).

nodes.label: Minobusan University
variants: 身延山大学東洋文化研究所

nodes.label: Gensho Imanari
nodes.summary: Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD in 1983, from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1965–1972) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).

nodes.label: Gyoshu Nakajo
nodes.summary: Gyoshu Nakajo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Masumi Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Masumi Mochizuki works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Mochizuki held posts at Minobusan University as lecturer (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and special appointment professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kanji Tamura
nodes.summary: Kanji Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has taught at Rissho University, serving as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yukio Kotani
nodes.summary: Yukio Kotani (born 1931) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Having studied under Hanjiro Tominaga, Kotani held a position at Rissho University from around 1970 to 2002.

nodes.label: Annie Besant
nodes.description: British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer and orator (1847-1933)
nodes.summary: Annie Besant worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Birkbeck, University of London around 1879–1883. She founded Banaras Hindu University in 1898, serving as its President, and served as President of the Theosophical Society from around 1907 to 1933.

nodes.label: Theosophical Society
variants: Kyoto branch of the Theosophical Society

nodes.label: Surama Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Surama Dasgupta (1907–1988) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earning degrees from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge (PhD, 1948). She served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.

nodes.label: Elizabeth A. Cecil
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, religious studies, and archaeology, Elizabeth A. Cecil earned degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University (PhD 2008). She taught at Leiden University (~2016–2018) before joining Florida State University as Assistant Professor (~2018).

nodes.label: Sam van Schaik
nodes.summary: Sam van Schaik (born 1972) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester (~2000). He held posts at the British Library, heading the Endangered Archives Programme (1999), and SOAS.

nodes.label: Lewis Doney
nodes.summary: Lewis Doney, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history, studied under Ulrich Pagel and earned a PhD from SOAS University of London. He held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Dániel Balogh
nodes.summary: Dániel Balogh is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Charles DiSimone
nodes.summary: Charles DiSimone works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and serves as co-director and permanent member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Anna Filigenzi
nodes.summary: Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of IsMEO from 1984, she directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Naples Federico II (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art
variants: Department of Asian Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

nodes.label: Jason Neelis
nodes.summary: Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned degrees from UT Austin and the University of Washington (PhD, 2001) under Richard G. Salomon, later serving as Associate Professor and Chair at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2013–2021).

nodes.label: Richard Payne
nodes.summary: Richard Payne works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held affiliations with the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Rijksmuseum
variants: Museum of Asiatic Art in Amsterdam

nodes.label: Max Deeg
nodes.summary: Max Deeg is an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of School at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021) and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Goethe University Frankfurt
variants: Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: Hofstra University
variants: Department of Philosophy at Hofstra University

nodes.label: University of Luxembourg
variants: Department of Philosophy at the University of Luxembourg

nodes.label: Lhagpa Phuntshogs
nodes.summary: Tibetology scholar Lhagpa Phuntshogs served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983-1991), secretary-general of the China Society of the Tibet Plateau (1991-2000), and director general of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

nodes.id: I:Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region
nodes.label: Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region
variants: Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region

nodes.label: Dramdul
nodes.summary: Dramdul is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He was Director at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2007) and editor-in-chief for Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
nodes.summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø, a specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies, studied at the University of Paris, University of Oslo (PhD 1981), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (Dr. habil. ~1984). He held professorships at Mainz and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, attested in 1882 and 1914.

nodes.label: Rama Misra Shastri
nodes.summary: Rama Misra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He held the post of assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in both 1882 and 1914.

nodes.label: Vitus Angermeier
nodes.summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz (completing his MA in 2007), Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. By 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Thomas Edward Colebrooke
nodes.summary: Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.label: Pascale Hugon
nodes.summary: Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Friedhelm Hardy
nodes.summary: Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987) and Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004).

nodes.label: A. N. Narasimhia
nodes.summary: A. N. Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933) and held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hettrich
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hettrich was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich, later holding posts at Saarland, Munich, Zurich, Marburg, and as chair of comparative linguistics at Würzburg from 1889.

nodes.label: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis
nodes.summary: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (circa 1934–1939) and held posts at SOAS University of London (circa 1965–1978) and as a professor at Leiden University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Nalini Balbir
nodes.summary: Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (Professor from 1988), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (Directeur d'Études from 2000).

nodes.label: Sylvain Brocquet
nodes.summary: Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1996), and later held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Aix-Marseille University
variants: エクス＝マルセイユ大学

nodes.label: Whitney Cox
nodes.summary: Whitney Cox is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Virginia and University of Chicago. Cox held academic posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2003 and becoming a professor around 2013.

nodes.label: Bard College
variants: Institute of Advanced Theology, Bard College

nodes.label: Albert Lutz
nodes.description: Swiss art historian, director Museum Rietberg
nodes.summary: Albert Lutz is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker at the University of Zurich (~1974–1983). He worked at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019).

nodes.label: Michael Jansen
nodes.summary: Michael Jansen (1947–2022) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Bonn, Sapienza, Delhi, the Archaeological Survey of India, and RWTH Aachen. He served as dean of architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector at GUtech (2007–2008).

nodes.label: Department of Archaeology and Museums
variants: Federal Department of Archaeology and Museums, Islamabad

nodes.label: Christoph Cüppers
nodes.summary: Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. From ~1993 to 2013, he served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute.

nodes.label: Christopher Key Chapple
nodes.summary: Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

nodes.label: Bloomfield College
variants: Bloomfield College of Montclair State University

nodes.label: Ramesh Shankar Gupte
nodes.summary: Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology and archaeology. In 1967, he was attested as Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and as a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State.

nodes.label: Radha Krishna Choudhary
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Radha Krishna Choudhary studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He held positions at Ganesh Dutt College, Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University, and founded Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Archaeological Museum.

nodes.label: Dineschandra Sircar
nodes.summary: Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and was Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from 1962.

nodes.label: Ram Sharan Sharma
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna University and earned a PhD from SOAS under A. L. Basham. He headed history departments at Patna University and Delhi University, and was founding president of the Indian Council of Historical Research.

nodes.label: Madhav M. Deshpande
nodes.summary: Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with his position attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.

nodes.label: Pandurang Vaman Kane
nodes.image: Pandurang Vaman Kane 2022 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indologist who studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He taught at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and Government Law College, later serving as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

nodes.label: Amalananda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1968 and was later a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
variants: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.image: Photograph of Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan presented to First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy in 1962.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.description: 2nd President and 1st Vice President of India, Indian philosopher and politician (1888–1975)
nodes.summary: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studying at Madras Christian College under Alfred George Hogg and William Meston. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu universities.

nodes.label: Edwin Whitfield Fay
nodes.summary: Edwin Whitfield Fay was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins University (Ph.D.), and Leipzig University under Maurice Bloomfield and others. He held professorships at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas.

nodes.label: Rhodes College
variants: South-Western Presbyterian University of Clarksville, Tennessee

nodes.label: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve
nodes.summary: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve (1831–1924) studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen (Dr. phil.). A scholar of linguistics, he served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

nodes.label: John Henry Wright
nodes.image: John Henry Wright young age photo.jpg
nodes.summary: John Henry Wright was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College and Leipzig University under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard University (~1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

nodes.label: Herbert Weir Smyth
nodes.summary: Herbert Weir Smyth was a scholar in linguistics and classics. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe, later holding posts at Williams College, Johns Hopkins, Bryn Mawr College, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Minton Warren
nodes.summary: Linguist Minton Warren (1850–1907) studied at Tufts, Yale, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He taught Latin at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899) and Harvard (from 1899), and headed the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899).

nodes.label: James Wilson Bright
nodes.summary: James Wilson Bright specialized in linguistics. After studying at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882), he taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

nodes.label: Yukio Yamanaka
nodes.summary: Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology and philosophy. Yamanaka studied at Kyoto University and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Nao Kasamatsu
nodes.summary: Nao Kasamatsu is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Kasamatsu served as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 2015) and as a part-time lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jin Kyoung Choi
nodes.summary: Jin Kyoung Choi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich and Ghent University. Attested in 2026, Choi held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Ghent University.

nodes.label: Eisaku Okada
nodes.summary: Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). Okada held positions at Koyasan University, Kyoto University, and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

nodes.label: Huanhuan He
nodes.summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo, and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hisataka Ishida
nodes.summary: Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna in 2011 under Helmut Krasser, having also studied under Akira Saitō. He served as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yukihiko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University, where an affiliation as a special researcher is attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Chizan Denbo-in
variants: 真言宗智山派智山伝法院

nodes.label: Hiroshi Tokushige
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Davaadorj Purevdorj
variants: ダワードルジ・プルプドルジ

nodes.label: Kaie Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Kaie Mochizuki (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has held academic posts at Minobusan University, serving as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tomoko Makidono
nodes.summary: Tomoko Makidono is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held a research post at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and was a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jianming Hu
nodes.summary: Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and held a researcher position at Komazawa University (both attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shigeki Moro
nodes.summary: Shigeki Moro (born 1972) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and computational fields. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities, studying under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, and held posts at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and Waseda University (2025).

nodes.id: I:Sōtō Zen Center for Advanced Studies
nodes.label: Sōtō Zen Center for Advanced Studies
variants: 曹洞宗総合研究センター

nodes.label: Hideyuki Matsumori
nodes.summary: Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006). He later held posts there as an assistant professor (助教, attested 2015) and professor (教授, attested 2026).

nodes.label: Isshin Teshima
nodes.summary: Isshin Teshima is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

nodes.label: Shinran Buddhist Center
variants: 真宗大谷派親鸞仏教センター

nodes.label: Hirotaka Kato
nodes.summary: Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派学院

nodes.label: Zijie Li
nodes.summary: Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015). In 2015, Li held a DC special researcher position at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

nodes.label: Siegfried Lienhard
nodes.summary: Siegfried Lienhard was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at Stockholm University. He was professor of Indology at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990).

nodes.label: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar
nodes.summary: Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin (PhD 1921), working under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1925).

nodes.label: Paul Fredericq
nodes.description: historian, teacher, professor and rector from Belgium (1850-1920)
nodes.summary: Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a history and archaeology scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of Liège (~1871–1875). He served as a professor at the University of Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University, where he became rector in 1919.

nodes.label: Henri Pirenne
nodes.summary: Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège (~1879–1883). He served as Professor of History at Ghent University from 1886 to 1931.

nodes.label: Edward James Rapson
nodes.summary: Edward James Rapson studied at Hereford Cathedral School and St John's College, Cambridge. A scholar of Indology, history, and linguistics, he held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1906-1936).

nodes.label: Kisari Mohan Ganguli
nodes.summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indology scholar who completed his studies at Presidency College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency College, Kolkata (~1857–1860), later holding posts at Presidency College (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

nodes.label: Michael Hutt
nodes.description: Professor of Nepali and Himalayan Studies
nodes.summary: Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his BA and doctorate at the University of London. He held several posts at SOAS, including Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) works in Indology and linguistics. He graduated from Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1986–1992) and associate professor at TUFS (2000–2024).

nodes.label: Francis V. Tiso
nodes.summary: Francis V. Tiso works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, and has taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University alongside visiting roles in Rome and San Francisco.

nodes.label: Lobsang Shastri
nodes.summary: Lobsang Shastri works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Albrecht Hanisch
nodes.summary: Albrecht Hanisch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg by 2000 under Michael Hahn, later serving as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

nodes.label: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri
nodes.summary: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. At the University of Madras, he held posts as reader in Indian philosophy (attested 1929) and reader and head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

nodes.label: R. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: R. Balasubramanian was an Indian scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. From around 1980 to 1990, he served as Director at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Harold G. Coward
nodes.summary: Harold G. Coward (born 1936) is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate from McMaster University in 1973. He held posts as professor at the University of Calgary and director at the University of Victoria.

nodes.label: Claus Vogel
nodes.summary: Claus Vogel worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Marburg and Deccan College under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau, among others. He held posts at the University of Marburg, University of Göttingen, and University of Bonn (1976–1998).

nodes.label: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala
nodes.summary: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard. He was Director General of the Department of Archaeology from circa 1992 to 2001.

nodes.label: Tse-fu Kuan
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Tse-fu Kuan completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He held a postdoctoral research post at National Cheng Kung University and was affiliated with Yuan Ze University in 2015.

nodes.label: Alexander Yiannopoulos
nodes.summary: Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under supervisor Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017) as well as traditional teachers Khenpo Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje.

nodes.label: John J. Makransky
nodes.summary: John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and several traditional teachers. He held posts at Boston College, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Jay L. Garfield
nodes.summary: Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Ngawang Samten, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Robert Thurman, holding posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, and the University of Melbourne.

nodes.label: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri
variants: シュリーニヴァーサ・シャーストリー
nodes.summary: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1972 and later as Professor between 1984 and 1992.

nodes.label: Umakant Premanand Shah
nodes.summary: Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. His career was based at the Oriental Institute, Baroda, where he became deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

nodes.label: Wang Yao
nodes.summary: Wang Yao (1928–2015) was a Tibetologist who studied under the traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and later taught Qingying Chen. He served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Tibet Academy of Social Sciences
variants: チベット社会科学アカデミー

nodes.label: China Society of the Tibet Plateau
variants: Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

nodes.label: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski
nodes.summary: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (1951–2025) studied Indology at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford (PhD ~1975–1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), as well as with traditional teachers in India.

nodes.label: Susan J. Rosenfield
nodes.summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under teachers including Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, and James W. Benson.

nodes.label: Bhagavan Das
nodes.summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indian scholar in philosophy and Indology who graduated with an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1921) and headmaster at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).

nodes.label: Raniero Gnoli
nodes.summary: Raniero Gnoli was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1950–1954) and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: John W. Spellman
nodes.summary: John W. Spellman worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Washington from around 1964 to 1967 and as a professor at the University of Windsor from around 1967 to 1999.

nodes.label: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri
nodes.summary: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri worked in linguistics and Indology, holding a professorship at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

nodes.label: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi
nodes.summary: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib. He worked in Indology and history, holding posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, AMU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).

nodes.label: Thomas R. Trautmann
nodes.summary: Thomas R. Trautmann (born 1940) is an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Bala Sahai Shastri
nodes.summary: Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist who worked at Panjab University, where he was attested as an Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1941.

nodes.label: Wolfgang Morgenroth
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Morgenroth, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Jena under Richard Hauschild and at Greifswald. He held academic posts at Jena, Greifswald, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Indology chair 1972–1994), alongside a guest professorship at Pune.

nodes.label: Richard Hauschild
nodes.summary: Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena, where he completed his doctorate (1926) and Habilitation (1948). He taught at the University of Jena as Lektor (1938) and Professor (1951–1967).

nodes.label: Karl Ammer
nodes.summary: Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1930–1935) and served as Director of the Institute of Indology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1954–1970).

variants: Institute of Tibetan Cultural Heritage, Palace Museum, Beijing

Jinhua Jia
nodes.summary: Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll and held posts at Harvard, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and CU Boulder.

nodes.label: International Christian University
variants: Institute for Asian Cultural Studies at International Christian University
国際基督教大学教養学部人文学科

nodes.label: Needham Research Institute
variants: Needham Institute for the History of Science and Technology in East Asia

nodes.label: Mary Shepherd Slusser
nodes.description: American anthropologist, archaeologist and art historian (1918 - 2017)
nodes.summary: Mary Shepherd Slusser worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Michigan, Columbia (PhD ~1950), NYU, and Harvard. She worked for the U.S. State Department (1951–1958) and held posts at the National Museums of African and Asian Art.

nodes.label: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under multiple teachers, including Madhusudana Nyayacharya, Gopinath Bhattacharyya, and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Dipak Ranjan Das
nodes.summary: Dipak Ranjan Das worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Dineschandra Sircar and held a post in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Ram Karan Sharma
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned an MA from Patna University and a PhD from UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He was vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga and Sampurnanand Sanskrit Universities, alongside holding several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Arvind Sharma
nodes.summary: Arvind Sharma is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Syracuse University, and Harvard Divinity School, and held posts at the University of Queensland, University of Sydney, and McGill University (Birks Chair, 1994).

nodes.label: Gyatsho Tshering
nodes.summary: Gyatsho Tshering studied at the University of Calcutta and worked in Tibetology. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, where he served as Acting Director (1972) and Director (1974–1998).

nodes.label: Hans Harder
nodes.summary: Hans Harder (born 1966) is an Indologist who studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das. He served as Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and joined the Heidelberg University editorial board in 2007.

nodes.label: Ellen M. Raven
nodes.summary: Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. Her career includes posts at the Kern Institute (attested 2003) and on an editorial board at Leiden University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Corrado Pensa
nodes.summary: Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci, taught Cristina Pecchia and Filippo Marsili, and served as professor at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Sarva Daman Singh
nodes.summary: Sarva Daman Singh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. His career included holding a post at the University of Queensland, where he was attested as Professor of History in 1958 and attested again in 1987.

nodes.label: Govind Chandra Pande
nodes.image: The Vice President Shri Bhairon Singh Shekhawat presenting 13th "Saraswati Samman" award to Prof. G.C. Pande on his book 'Bhagirathi' at a function organised by K.K. Birla foundation in New Delhi on September 6, 2004.jpg
nodes.summary: Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya, held professorships and Vice-Chancellorships at the Universities of Allahabad and Rajasthan, and chaired the Allahabad Museum and Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

nodes.label: K. V. Ramesh
nodes.summary: K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Panjab University
variants: Visvesvaranand Institute of Sanskrit and Indological Studies der University of the Punjab

nodes.label: Gudrun Melzer
nodes.summary: Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate under Jens-Uwe Hartmann at the University of Munich. In 2026, her positions were attested at the University of Munich, Göttingen Academy, and IIBS.

nodes.label: Bruce B. Lawrence
nodes.summary: Bruce B. Lawrence specializes in religious studies and indology. Educated at Fay School, Episcopal Divinity School, and Princeton University, he was a professor at Duke University from approximately 1971 to 2011, later becoming professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Duke University
variants: Duke University at Durham, North Carolina

nodes.label: Annemarie Schimmel
nodes.summary: Annemarie Schimmel worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning doctorates at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Ellenberg, Hans Heinrich Schaeder, and Friedrich Heiler. She held professorships at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

nodes.label: B. N. K. Sharma
nodes.summary: B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha and at the University of Madras. He served as principal of Rajah's College (1938–1948) and professor of Sanskrit at Ramnarain Ruia College (1953–1969).

nodes.label: Arinde L. Jonker
nodes.summary: Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology scholar who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied under Jonathan A. Silk and MA supervisor Peter Bisschop.

nodes.label: Daniele Cuneo
nodes.summary: Daniele Cuneo works in Indology and philosophy. He held a post at the University of Paris (attested 2018) and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

nodes.label: Katrin Querl
nodes.summary: Katrin Querl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna. As of 2026, she is attested as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin and lecturer for Tibetan at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Hermann Goetz
nodes.summary: Hermann Goetz worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Munich and under mentor Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as curator at the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery (1939-1953) and director at Heidelberg University (1961-1976).

nodes.label: Ibrahim Shah
nodes.summary: Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati. He has served as Associate Professor and Chairman of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.

nodes.label: Ihsan Ali
nodes.summary: Ihsan Ali is an archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts as professor at the University of Peshawar (~1998), director of KP Archaeology and Museums (~2002–2006), and vice chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).

nodes.label: Pratapaditya Pal
nodes.summary: Pratapaditya Pal works in history/archaeology, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge, holding curatorial posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Gouriswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Gouriswar Bhattacharya (1924–2013) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin, serving there from circa 1974 to 2005, including as Lehrbeauftragter from circa 1975 to 2005.

nodes.label: Adam Hardy
nodes.summary: Adam Hardy (born 1953) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2000), Director of PRASADA, and editor of South Asian Studies (~2004–2011).

nodes.label: Joe Cribb
nodes.summary: Joe Cribb is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Queen Mary University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).

nodes.label: Hari Damodar Velankar
nodes.summary: Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indologist who studied under H. M. Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

nodes.label: Charles Burnett
nodes.summary: Charles Burnett is a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held posts at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and notably the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999.

nodes.label: Jan P. Hogendijk
nodes.summary: Jan P. Hogendijk (b. 1955) specializes in the history of science and Central Asian studies. After completing his doctorate at Utrecht University, he held posts as Professor of the History of Mathematics at Utrecht University and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Toke Lindegaard Knudsen
nodes.summary: Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and under doctoral supervisor David Pingree in 2008.

nodes.label: Warburg Institute
variants: ヴァールブルク研究所

nodes.label: Edwin Gerow
nodes.summary: Edwin Gerow was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1997) and as Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1993–1997).

nodes.label: Shlomo Pines
nodes.description: Israeli scholar of Jewish and Islamic philosophy (1908–1990)
nodes.summary: Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt universities, and held positions at the University of Paris and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Rosane Rocher
nodes.summary: Rosane Rocher (b. 1937) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles under Ludo Rocher. She was a Research Fellow at the FNRS (1961–1970) and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1970.

nodes.label: Sang-Kyun Sun
nodes.summary: Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under Sanghasena Singh (attested 1995). Sun held a post as Lecturer at Uiduk University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Nicolas Morrissey

Jinah Kim
nodes.summary: Jinah Kim, a scholar of South Asian art, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (attested 2007). She held appointments at Vanderbilt University and the Institute for Advanced Study, and is a professor at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Kurt A. Behrendt
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Kurt A. Behrendt earned his PhD from UCLA in 1997. Around 2006, he served as assistant curator of Asian art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Lionel David Barnett
nodes.summary: Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Liverpool and Cambridge, held keeper positions at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), and taught at UCL (1906–1917) and SOAS (1917–1948).

nodes.label: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch
nodes.summary: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche, and held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006), Hamburg, and Munich.

nodes.label: Gustaaf Houtman
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart. He was attested in 2014 as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

nodes.label: Pyi Phyo Kyaw
nodes.summary: Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at King's College London in 2014 and was attested there as a postdoctoral research fellow in 2017.

nodes.label: Asatoshi Kamiya
nodes.summary: Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Gail Hinich Sutherland
nodes.summary: Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

nodes.label: Narayan Hemandas Samtani
nodes.summary: Narayan Hemandas Samtani (1924–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD as a research fellow at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).

nodes.label: Prahlad Pradhan
nodes.summary: Prahlad Pradhan worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. His posts included research fellow at Visva-Bharati, principal at Gangadhar Meher University, and professor at Utkal University (~1963–1975).

nodes.label: N. Aiyaswami Sastri
nodes.summary: N. Aiyaswami Sastri worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and later as a professor at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Vidya Niwas Mishra
nodes.image: Dr. Vidhyanivas Mishra with Dr. Archana Dwivedi.jpg
nodes.summary: Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya and earned degrees from Allahabad and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1977), K. M. Institute (~1977–1986), and as vice-chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).

nodes.label: Richard Peter Hottelet
nodes.summary: Richard Peter Hottelet was active in Buddhist studies, studying under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and holding an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1971.

nodes.label: Marie G. Wanek
nodes.summary: Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where she was taught by Sengaku Mayeda.

nodes.label: Giacomella Orofino
nodes.summary: Giacomella Orofino works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985) under Raniero Gnoli, later teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2000–2007).

nodes.label: Roger R. Jackson
nodes.summary: Roger R. Jackson was a Buddhist and Tibetan studies scholar. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (~1974–1983) and taught religion at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

nodes.label: John S. Strong
nodes.summary: Strong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He was a professor at Bates College and held visiting professorships at Chicago, Harvard, Princeton, and Stanford.

nodes.label: Geshe Kelsang Gyatso
variants: dGe bshes sKal bzang rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Geshe Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Chambaling, Tashilhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery (~1945–1973) under Trijang Rinpoche. He served as a teacher at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977.

nodes.label: Martin Baumann
nodes.description: German university teacher in religious studies at university of Lucerne (Switzerland)
nodes.summary: Martin Baumann (b. 1960) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1990–1993) and a Habilitation at Leipzig University (~1994–1999) before becoming professor of religious studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

nodes.label: J. Gordon Melton
nodes.summary: J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar who studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).

nodes.label: George D. Bond
nodes.summary: George D. Bond works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD from Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he served as Professor of Religion (~1974–2012).

nodes.label: Richard Kieckhefer
nodes.summary: Richard Kieckhefer, a scholar of religious studies and history, earned his undergraduate degree at Saint Louis University and his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin. He joined Northwestern University in 1975 and served as president of Societas Magica and ASCH.

nodes.label: Gavin Flood
nodes.summary: Gavin Flood is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held positions at the University of Wales Lampeter, University of Stirling, University of Oxford, and Yale-NUS College.

nodes.label: Carola Roloff
nodes.summary: Carola Roloff works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang. Her posts include the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and visiting professor at Hamburg (2018–2025).

nodes.label: Erling von Mende
nodes.summary: Erling von Mende (born 1940) is a Sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, and Bonn, completing his PhD (1964–1969) and habilitation (~1972–1979) at the University of Cologne. He served as Professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin (1983–2007).

nodes.label: Lutz Bieg
nodes.summary: Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University (~1964–1971) and his Habilitation at the Free University of Berlin (1986). From 1989 to 2008, he served as a professor at the University of Cologne.

nodes.label: Monika Zin
nodes.summary: Monika Zin works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich, where she taught (circa 1994–2015), later leading research projects in Leipzig.

nodes.label: Dalsukh Malvania
nodes.summary: Dalsukh Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1956), served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (~1957–1973), and held posts at the University of Toronto and MS University of Baroda.
