nodes.label: Douglas Osto
nodes.summary: Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD under Ulrich Pagel at SOAS University of London (~1999–2004). In 2005, he became a Senior Lecturer at Massey University.

nodes.label: Dan Lusthaus
nodes.summary: Dan Lusthaus is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Temple University. He held teaching posts at Grinnell College, Bates College, the University of Georgia, and served as a research associate at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Gunapala Dharmasiri
nodes.summary: Gunapala Dharmasiri was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.

nodes.label: Ulrich Pagel
nodes.summary: Ulrich Pagel specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip T. Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme (attested 1995), and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Carola S. Carstens
nodes.summary: Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg by 2006 and held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999.

nodes.label: Ratna Basu
nodes.summary: Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. Attested in 2026, she holds the post of Professor (Special Invitee) at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Michael Balk
nodes.summary: Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff
nodes.summary: Scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology Friedrich Alexander Bischoff completed PhDs at the University of Paris, supervised by Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1964–1982) and the University of Hamburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: William C. Kirby
nodes.summary: William C. Kirby works in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth and at Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn, later holding posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1979-1992), Harvard University (1992), and the Fairbank Center (~2006-2013).

nodes.label: Philip A. Kuhn
nodes.summary: Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown, and served as Associate Professor at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) before becoming Francis Lee Higginson Professor and Fairbank Center director at Harvard.

nodes.label: Nicola Di Cosmo
nodes.summary: Nicola Di Cosmo is a historian of Sinology and Central Asia who studied at Indiana State and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD 1991). He held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, Canterbury, Columbia, and as Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the IAS (~2003).

nodes.label: Arthur Waley
variants: アーサー・デイヴィッド・ウェイリー
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・ウェイリー
nodes.summary: Arthur Waley was a scholar of sinology and japanology. Educated at Rugby School and King's College, Cambridge, he studied under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi, and worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

nodes.label: Wm. Theodore de Bary
nodes.summary: Wm. Theodore de Bary worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Columbia and studying at Harvard. He served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017) and president of the AAS (1969–1970).

nodes.label: Charles A. Moore
nodes.summary: Charles A. Moore was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his AB and PhD at Yale University, where he also taught. He conducted postdoctoral work at Banaras Hindu University and was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967).

nodes.summary: A philosopher and religious studies scholar, James studied at Plymouth College and Harvard University (MD 1864–1869). He spent his academic career at Harvard, serving as physiology lecturer (1872), assistant professor (1876, 1880), and professor (1885).

nodes.label: Maurice Walshe
nodes.summary: Maurice Walshe worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held an academic post attested at the University of London in 2009.

nodes.label: Ann Heirman
nodes.summary: Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research from 1995 to 2009 and at Ghent University as a permanent member and director from 2003 to 2012.

nodes.label: Lisa N. Owen
nodes.summary: Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

nodes.label: Janice Leoshko
nodes.summary: Janice Leoshko works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daud Ali
nodes.summary: Daud Ali studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1996–2009) and became associate professor of South Asian history at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

nodes.label: Harold Hargreaves

nodes.summary: Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an archaeologist and Indologist. After serving as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar, he held positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

nodes.label: Frederick M. Asher
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, where he served as a professor from around 1971 to 2021.

nodes.label: Shailendra Bhandare
nodes.summary: Shailendra Bhandare specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has held positions at the British Museum, the Fitzwilliam Museum, the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), and St Cross College (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Dilip K. Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Calcutta (1965–1977), Delhi (1977–1990), and Cambridge (1990–2008), where he became Professor Emeritus of South Asian Archaeology.

nodes.label: Suryakumar Bhuyan
nodes.summary: Suryakumar Bhuyan (1892–1964) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency College, Calcutta, and SOAS (PhD 1936). He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University.

nodes.label: Banikanta Kakati
nodes.summary: Banikanta Kakati (1894–1952) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cotton University, Presidency College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

nodes.label: Cathy Cantwell
nodes.summary: Cathy Cantwell is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Kent (~1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Robert Mayer
nodes.summary: Robert Mayer works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bristol and Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. He joined the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Eshō Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Eshō Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of the Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo (attested 1999) and president of the Kyushu Ryukoku Society (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Fang-Kuei Li
nodes.summary: Fang-Kuei Li (1902–1987) worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan (BA), Chicago (PhD under Edward Sapir), and Harvard, later teaching at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).

nodes.label: Hellmut Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin under Otto Franke. He served as assistant at Frankfurt, taught German at Peking University (1933–1948), and held the sinology chair at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

nodes.label: Joseph Rock
variants: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.summary: Joseph Rock was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He held positions at Mills College (~1908), Mid-Pacific Institute, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908-1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920-1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

nodes.label: Qian Lin
nodes.summary: Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding degrees from Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD under Collett Cox). In 2026, Lin was attested at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Fudan University
variants: National Institute for Advanced Humanistic Studies at Fudan University

nodes.label: Amy Snyder Ohta
nodes.summary: Amy Snyder Ohta works in linguistics and Japanology. She completed studies at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and became a professor at the University of Washington in ~1995.

nodes.label: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami
nodes.summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in Japanology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, taught Qian Lin, and is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

nodes.label: Itsuko Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who studied at Teachers College and taught Qian Lin. She is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

nodes.label: Chi-chiang Huang
nodes.summary: Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history who completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: John Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After completing his MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, he held academic posts at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Miriam Levering
nodes.summary: Miriam Levering was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 1978. She later served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee, attested between 2007 and 2010.

nodes.label: Whalen Lai
nodes.summary: Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard (~1969–1975) and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1973–1976) and University of California, Davis (~1976–2009).

nodes.label: Taigen Dan Leighton
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Leighton earned a bachelor's from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from the Graduate Theological Union. He trained under numerous teachers, became Adjunct Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994), and taught at Loyola University Chicago.

nodes.label: Shohaku Okumura
nodes.summary: Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Kōshō Uchiyama. He founded Pioneer Valley Zendo and Sanshin Zen Community, taught at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

nodes.label: Ruth Fuller Sasaki
variants: ルース・フラー・エヴェレット
nodes.summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (1927–1929) and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Mukai Kono, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, and Zuigan Goto. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

nodes.label: Ashin Nandamālābhivaṃsa
nodes.native: နန္ဒမာလာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: Wilhelm Halbfass
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Halbfass was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Vienna and Göttingen. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1968–1971), the University of Pennsylvania (1982–2000), and as a visiting teacher at Hamburg (~1989–1990).

nodes.label: Harogadde Manappa Nayak
nodes.summary: Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was a linguist who served as Director at the University of Mysore (circa 1961–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

nodes.label: Patrick de Silva Kularatne
nodes.summary: Patrick de Silva Kularatne (1893–1976) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at University College London and the University of London around 1913 to 1918, later serving as Principal of Ananda College from circa 1918 to 1943.

nodes.label: Ryosho Nakamura
nodes.summary: Ryosho Nakamura is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Seventh Higher School Zoshikan, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from circa 1970 to 1998.

nodes.label: Masanori Nakagawa
nodes.summary: Masanori Nakagawa worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty at Chikushi Jogakuen University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1991 and as an associate professor of literature in 2002.

nodes.label: M. Shinoda
nodes.image: Linkin Park - From Zero Lead Press Photo - James Minchin III (Mike Shinoda).jpg
nodes.description: American musician, rapper, singer and songwriter
nodes.summary: M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami, as well as attending Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design.

nodes.label: Mun-keat Choong
nodes.summary: Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland (MA and PhD), where Roderick S. Bucknell supervised his MA.

nodes.label: Roderick S. Bucknell
nodes.summary: Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Queensland from ~1976 to 2002, where he was an Associate Professor (attested 1999–2000).

nodes.label: Asim Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.description: indologist; writer; taught at Dept. of Ancient Hist. and Culture, Calcutta U., India
nodes.summary: Asim Kumar Chatterjee is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta (~1962–1967) under D. Mukherjee. He served as a senior research fellow at the University of Calcutta and lectured at Jangipur College.

nodes.label: Lobsang Dargyay
nodes.summary: Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

nodes.label: K. V. Raman
nodes.summary: K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India and was Professor and Head at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Elisa Ganser
nodes.summary: Elisa Ganser works in Indology and philosophy. Her appointments include serving as Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026) and as a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vincenzo Vergiani
nodes.summary: Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Raffaele Torella from circa 1995 to 2001 and became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge around 2010.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson
nodes.image: Jeffrey Masson appearing on "After Dark", 23 September 1989.jpg
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later teaching at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and serving as professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

nodes.label: Antonello Palumbo
nodes.summary: Antonello Palumbo is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He held posts at SOAS University of London, attested in 2005 and 2010, where he taught Brian J. Nichols and Aristotle C. Dy.

nodes.label: Anukul Chandra Banerjee
nodes.summary: Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He served as assistant lecturer in Pali at Calcutta (attested 1943) and director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Richard D. Mann
nodes.summary: Richard D. Mann is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Errington
nodes.description: specialist on the archaeology of Gandhara and the collections of Charles Masson, and a numismatist specialising in Asian coins
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Errington studied at SOAS and completed graduate work under Adrian David Hugh Bivar. Specializing in archaeology and Buddhist studies, she served as curator of pre-Islamic coins of South and Central Asia at the British Museum from 1993.

nodes.label: Dorji Banzarov
nodes.summary: Dorji Banzarov was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and completed his doctoral dissertation at Kazan Imperial University under Józef Kowalewski (~1842–1846).

nodes.label: Galsan Gomboev
nodes.summary: Galsan Gomboev (1818–1863) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Józef Kowalewski. He taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

nodes.label: Gombojab Tsybikov
nodes.summary: Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (circa 1902–1917).

nodes.label: Bazar Baradiin
nodes.summary: Bazar Baradiin (1878–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and was appointed head of the Buryat Scientific Committee in 1922.

nodes.label: Tsyben Zhamtsarano
nodes.summary: Tsyben Zhamtsarano worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Mongolian Academy of Sciences
variants: Scientific Committee of the Mongolian People's Republic
Akademie der Wissenschaften der Mongolischen Volksrepublik

nodes.label: Buryat Scientific Committee
variants: Scientific Committee of the Buriat Mongolian ASSR

nodes.label: Sachindra Kumar Maity
nodes.summary: Sachindra Kumar Maity was an Indian historian and Indologist. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from circa 1953 to 1956 and held a post at Jadavpur University from circa 1958 to 1986.

nodes.label: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, Kendriya Hindi Shikshan Mandal, and Sandhaan (1991).

nodes.label: Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya
variants: グルクル・カングリ大学

nodes.label: Kendriya Hindi Sansthan
variants: 中央ヒンディー語研究所

nodes.label: Kendriya Hindi Shikshan Mandal
variants: 中央ヒンディー語理事会

nodes.label: Anil Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Anil Vidyalankar is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director.

nodes.label: Iwao Nakajima
nodes.summary: Iwao Nakajima studied under Nichiki Kimura and earned a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as editor-in-chief at Sandhaan (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Hitotsubashi University
variants: 一橋大学大学院社会学研究科

nodes.label: Ernst Fürlinger
nodes.summary: Ernst Fürlinger, a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He was study director at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), lectured at Vienna (2006–2016), and held research and leadership roles at Krems from 2007.

nodes.label: Lodrö Sangpo
nodes.summary: Lodrö Sangpo (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Robert M. Gimello
nodes.summary: Robert M. Gimello is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1968–1976) and held faculty positions at the University of Arizona (~1981–2000) and Harvard University (~2000–2006).

nodes.id: I:Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
nodes.label: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
Bruce Matthews
nodes.summary: Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. A graduate alumnus of McMaster University, he was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon and served as C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

nodes.label: Mathieu Boisvert
nodes.summary: Mathieu Boisvert (born 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who studied under A. K. Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992.

nodes.id: I:Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux
nodes.label: Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux
variants: Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux

nodes.label: Victor Chan
nodes.image: The Dalai Lama @ The Vancouver Peace Summit.jpg
nodes.summary: Victor Chan is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at the University of Chicago. In 2005, he founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and was attested as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Larry DeVries
nodes.summary: Larry DeVries is a religious studies and Indology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Washington, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, held a research post at Chicago, and was at Langara College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Mavis L. Fenn
nodes.summary: Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen. She served as Assistant Professor at United College (attested 2005–2006) and Professor and Department Chair at the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: United College, University of Waterloo
variants: St Paul's College, University of Waterloo

nodes.label: James G. Mullens
nodes.summary: James G. Mullens specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

nodes.label: Robert Florida
nodes.summary: Robert Florida is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later held an appointment as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: University of Victoria
variants: Centre for the Study of Religion and Society at the University of Victoria
University of Victoria's Centre for Studies in Religion and Society

nodes.label: Baihui Wu
nodes.summary: Baihui Wu (1919–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

nodes.label: Robert Gardner
nodes.summary: Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (~1943–1947), worked at the Harvard Art Museums, and taught medieval art and history at the University of Puget Sound (~1951–1953). He later served as a professor at Harvard University from 1956 to 1997.

nodes.label: R. Gordon Wasson
variants: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.summary: R. Gordon Wasson was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, later serving in the American Expeditionary Forces, at various newspapers, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.

nodes.label: Ernest Bender
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Ernest Bender earned his B.A. at Temple University and studied at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig S. Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He taught at Penn from 1950 to 1989, becoming professor in 1967.

nodes.label: David Webster
nodes.summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Thibaut d'Hubert
nodes.summary: Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago and is attested as Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Manan Ahmed Asif
nodes.description: historian and professor at Columbia University

nodes.label: Yigal Bronner
nodes.summary: Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and under Sheldon Pollock at the University of Chicago (~1994–1999). He later served as an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2008).

nodes.label: Kiel University
variants: Historisches Seminar, Asiatische Geschichte, Universität Kiel

nodes.label: George C. O. Haas
nodes.summary: George C. O. Haas was an Indologist. He served as the recording secretary of the American Oriental Society (~1913–1918) and worked as an editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Kanai Lal Hazra
nodes.summary: Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune (~1964–1968), later lecturing at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Paul Fuller
nodes.summary: Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Paul Dundas and completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin. As of 2026, he is attested at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: John Dowson
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist who studied under Edwin Norris, Dowson served as a tutor at East India Company College (~1855–1858) and as Professor of Hindustani at both Staff College, Camberley, and University College London (1855–1877).

nodes.label: Krishna Mohan Banerjee
nodes.summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Hare School, Presidency College, under Alexander Duff, and at Bishop's College, he later served at Hare School (~1828–1831) and as Second Professor at Bishop's College (1852).

nodes.label: Edward Backhouse Eastwick
nodes.summary: Edward Backhouse Eastwick (1814–1883) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Charterhouse, Merton College, and Oxford. He served as Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and held a post at the Foreign Office.

nodes.label: K. N. Jayatilleke
nodes.summary: K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge, and served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ヨーゼフ・ヨーハン・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge, earning his PhD at Cambridge in 1929. He was a fellow and lecturer at Trinity College and professor of philosophy at Cambridge (1930–1947).

nodes.label: Simo Parpola
nodes.summary: Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics and Assyriology who earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968). He held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and served as professor at the University of Helsinki beginning in 1978.

nodes.label: Pentti Aalto
nodes.summary: Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt (~1936–1950) and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

nodes.label: Kimmo Koskenniemi
nodes.summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi is a computational linguistics scholar who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and as director of the BAULT research community (~2008–2013).

nodes.label: Frank Ernest Keay
nodes.birth_place: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

nodes.label: Thomas Zehnder
nodes.summary: Thomas Zehnder is an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Alexander Lubotsky
nodes.summary: Alexander Lubotsky is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD ~1979–1987 under Robert S. P. Beekes), becoming Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.

nodes.label: Kristen De Joseph
nodes.summary: Kristen De Joseph is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied under Arlo Griffiths and is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop (attested 2026).

nodes.label: M. S. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: M. S. Nagaraja Rao was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under Madhukar Narhar Deshpande and at the Universities of Mysore and Pune. He served at Karnatak University, Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and as Director General of the ASI (1984–1987).

nodes.id: I:Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Karnataka
nodes.label: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Karnataka
Govind Swamirao Gai
nodes.summary: Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1966), Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and consultant for epigraphy at AIIS (attested 1986).

nodes.id: I:Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
nodes.label: Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
Wei-jen Teng
nodes.summary: Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD attested 2011), he has held posts at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Dylan Esler
nodes.summary: Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and completed his PhD in 2018 at the Catholic University of Louvain, where he also served as a research scholar.

nodes.label: University of Zagreb
variants: Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb

nodes.label: Chen-kuo Lin
nodes.summary: Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Temple University. He served as a professor and distinguished professor at National Chengchi University, with visiting positions at Leiden University and IIAS.

nodes.label: Andrea Schlosser
nodes.summary: Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch, earning degrees from the Free University of Berlin, and holds posts attested in 2026 at Göttingen Academy and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Yao-ming Tsai
nodes.summary: Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1997), Tsai became a Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Cristina Pecchia
nodes.summary: Cristina Pecchia is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at Sapienza University of Rome under Gnoli, Torella, and Pensa, and studied at Vienna under Steinkellner. She has held posts at IKGA and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Sanne Dokter-Mersch
nodes.summary: Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: K. Meenakshi
nodes.summary: K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist. She earned her PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under Madhukar Anant Mehendale, and held an attested post at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1983.

nodes.label: Madhukar Anant Mehendale
nodes.summary: Madhukar Anant Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and held professor roles at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1970, 1983, and 2026.

nodes.label: Jiryo Masuda
nodes.summary: Jiryo Masuda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Unrai Wogihara and held a post as professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Adyar Library and Research Centre
variants: The Adyar Library and Research Centre
Adyar Library of Theosophical Society Adyar

nodes.label: James Haughton Woods
nodes.summary: James Haughton Woods worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Strasbourg, he studied under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman before serving on Harvard University's faculty (~1903–1934).

nodes.label: Arthur Venis
nodes.summary: Arthur Venis was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Professor of English (1881) and Principal (1885) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1888–1914).

nodes.label: University College, Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学ユニヴァーシティ・カレッジ
ユニバーシティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Corpus Christi College, Oxford
variants: Corpus Christi College Centre for the Study of Greek and Roman Antiquity
オックスフォード大学のコーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Charles Henry Tawney
nodes.summary: Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He taught at Trinity College, led Presidency College in Kolkata (1875–1892), and served as Librarian of the India Office (1892/1893–1903).

nodes.label: Robert Ford Campany
nodes.summary: Robert Ford Campany specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He served as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), worked at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and joined the faculty of Vanderbilt University in 2010.

nodes.label: D. N. Shukla
nodes.summary: Indologist D. N. Shukla earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Banerjea
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

nodes.label: Tiziana Pontillo
nodes.summary: Tiziana Pontillo (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

nodes.label: David Burton
nodes.summary: David Burton, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). In 2010, he was attested as Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University.

nodes.label: Kodai Akino
nodes.summary: Kodai Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple administrative and leadership positions at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909 and lectured at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Nyoten Jimbo
nodes.summary: Nyoten Jimbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and served as a professor at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kodo Yamada
nodes.summary: Kodo Yamada was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held teaching posts at both Komazawa University and Keio University.

nodes.label: Totsudo Kato
nodes.summary: Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Enryo Inoue, Seiran Ouchi, and Bankon Shimada, attending Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University. He later taught at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

nodes.label: Seiran Ouchi
nodes.summary: Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Totsudo Kato. He served as a lecturer (侍講) at Nishi Hongan-ji and was president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

nodes.label: Hakuun Yasutani
nodes.summary: Hakuun Yasutani (1885–1973) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He graduated from Tokyo Prefectural Toshima Normal School and studied under teachers including Daiun Sogaku Harada, Bokusan Nishiari, and Genpo Tsuyama. He founded the Sanbo Kyodan in 1954.

nodes.label: Daiun Sogaku Harada
nodes.summary: Daiun Sogaku Harada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, and under Dokutan Sōsan and Sotan Oka, among others. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.

nodes.label: Tetsuo Otani
nodes.summary: Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple leadership positions at Komazawa University, including president (2002–2006), and later served as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

nodes.label: Sokuo Eto
nodes.summary: Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Komazawa, Kyoto, and Tokyo universities. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (circa 1950–1957) and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

nodes.label: John Firminger Duthie
nodes.summary: Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from ~1876 to 1903 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from ~1891 to 1903.

nodes.label: George Watt
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ワット (植物学者)
nodes.summary: George Watt worked in Indology and other fields. After studying at Aberdeen and Glasgow (~1868–1873), he held posts at Glasgow, Presidency College Kolkata (1873–1874), the University of Calcutta (~1873–1884), the Indian Museum (~1894–1903), and Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Moodeen Sheriff
nodes.description: Indian surgeon and practitioner of native medicine
nodes.summary: Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist and medical professional who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

nodes.label: Penor Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Palyul Monastery, under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1960–1991), and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

nodes.label: G. V. Devasthali
nodes.summary: G. V. Devasthali (1906–1993) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (attested 1944) and as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

nodes.label: Ram Niwas Pandey
nodes.summary: Ram Niwas Pandey is an archaeologist and Indologist. He pursued his education at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Institute of Archaeology, completing his doctoral studies under the supervision of Hit Narayan Jha.

nodes.label: Institute of Archaeology
variants: School of Archaeology at New Delhi

nodes.label: Francis X. Clooney
nodes.summary: Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and comparative theology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1978–1984), he taught at Boston College (1984–2005) and joined Harvard University as Parkman Professor of Divinity in 2005.

nodes.label: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Jacqueline Suthren Hirst completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has held posts at the University of Manchester, including as Honorary Research Fellow.

nodes.label: Julius Lipner
nodes.summary: Julius Lipner studied under Hywel David Lewis at King's College London, as well as at Jadavpur and Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth. He served as Professor of Hinduism and the Comparative Study of Religion at the University of Cambridge (1975-2013).

nodes.label: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar
nodes.summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

nodes.id: I:Cultural Relics Bureau of Tibet Autonomous Region
nodes.label: Cultural Relics Bureau of Tibet Autonomous Region
variants: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet

nodes.label: Peter Gaeffke
nodes.summary: Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Mainz in 1952, studying under Ernst Schwarz. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).

nodes.label: James Morison
nodes.summary: James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

nodes.label: Kenneth Somerled Macdonald
nodes.image: Kenneth S. Macdonald, M.A., D.D. (page 8 crop).jpg

nodes.label: Erik Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik Zürcher (1928–2008) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959), studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak. He served as Director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

nodes.label: John Powers
nodes.summary: Powers specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied at College of the Holy Cross, McMaster University, and University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, among others. He held posts at ANU, USF, Deakin University (2016–2022), and University of Melbourne (2022).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as principal at Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was honorary professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

nodes.label: Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University
variants: College of Indology of Nagpur University

nodes.label: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz
nodes.summary: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz studied at the University of Bonn (PhD, Habilitation). A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, she was a professor (appointed 1999), faculty dean (2007–2010), and emerita (~2023) at the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Youru Wang
nodes.summary: Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and later taught at Rowan University (attested 2007, 2018).

nodes.label: Charles Wei-hsun Fu
nodes.summary: Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1956) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969). He held a post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

nodes.label: Marc Aurel Stein
variants: マーク・オーレル・スタイン
nodes.summary: Marc Aurel Stein was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College, Principal of Aliah University, and officer positions in the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Mithilesh Chaturvedi
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, Mithilesh Chaturvedi has been affiliated with the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi, attested as faculty in 2009 and as Professor emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: P. K. Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: P. K. Mukhopadhyay is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Andrew Glass
nodes.summary: Andrew Glass specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA, PhD), supervised by Richard G. Salomon and taught by Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Wanggyal Sonam, and Gudrun Melzer.

nodes.label: Mark Allon
nodes.summary: Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning a PhD from Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1989–1994). He served at SOAS (~1995–1998) and the University of Sydney, becoming an Associate Professor (~2010).

nodes.label: Timothy Lenz
nodes.summary: Timothy Lenz is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox at the University of Washington, where he later served as a faculty member and professor.

nodes.label: Embar Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), as Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library, and at Baroda Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Noémie Verdon
nodes.summary: Noémie Verdon is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2015 under supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.

nodes.label: John Faithfull Fleet
nodes.summary: An Indologist and historian educated at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London, Fleet served in the Indian Civil Service and Bombay Civil Service, as Epigraphist to the Government of India (1883–1886), and as Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Robert Sewell
nodes.summary: Robert Sewell was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and was the Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.

nodes.label: Masato Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Masato Kobayashi (born 1970) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1990–1995) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000) under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at TUFS (~2000–2004).

nodes.label: Junglan Bang
nodes.summary: Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Dongguk University and under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn before completing a PhD at Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson (2012). Bang served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Karma Lekshe Tsomo
nodes.description: Buddhist nun, scholar and social activist
nodes.summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as a professor at the University of San Diego and held a professorship at Hawaiʻi in 2023.

nodes.id: I:Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
nodes.label: Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
variants: Sakyadhita: International Association of Buddhist Women
Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women

nodes.label: Michael Alram
nodes.summary: Michael Alram is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer, and served as Vice President of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Kunsthistorisches Museum
variants: Münzkabinett des Kunsthistorischen Museums in Wien
Vienna Coin Cabinet at the Kunsthistorisches Museum

nodes.label: Deborah Klimburg-Salter
nodes.description: Austrian art historian and professor for non-European art history
nodes.summary: Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist. She completed her PhD under Oleg Grabar at Harvard and habilitated at the University of Vienna. Her career includes posts at UCLA and the University of Vienna's Asian art history chair (1994–2015).

nodes.label: Durga Prasad Dikshit
nodes.summary: Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under teachers R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and completed his doctoral studies under Baij Nath Puri.

nodes.label: Baij Nath Puri
nodes.summary: Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976).

nodes.label: S. S. Misra
nodes.summary: S. S. Misra worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as professor and head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as professor of Indology and linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Akira Hataya
nodes.summary: Akira Hataya works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Reiner Wiehl
nodes.summary: Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

nodes.label: R. N. Gadre
nodes.summary: R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: R. P. Paranjpye
nodes.summary: R. P. Paranjpye studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1959.

nodes.label: Klaus Rüping
nodes.summary: Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker. He held a post as Dozent at the University of Münster (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Volker Caumanns
nodes.summary: Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and a PhD at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has held teaching and research posts at Munich, Hamburg, Leipzig, Bern, and the Lumbini International Research Institute.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wackernagel
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wackernagel studied linguistics at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh (1824–1827). He taught at Pädagogium Basel (~1833–1835) and held a professorship at the University of Basel (1833; 1835–1869).

nodes.label: Haruka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1980–1994) and the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Yamashita
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University, attested from 1996 to 1999.

nodes.label: Nobuhiro Ota
nodes.summary: Nobuhiro Ota is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1988–2001). After serving as a Research Fellow at Tokyo, he became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2021.

nodes.label: Akio Tanabe
nodes.summary: Akio Tanabe works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor, 2015).

nodes.label: Nicolas Tournadre
variants: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.jawiki: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.summary: Nicolas Tournadre is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle under Claude Hagège. He held posts at CNRS, INALCO, Paris 8, University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University, alongside affiliations with Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and LACITO.

nodes.label: Khenpo Appey Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Appey Rinpoche studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Dragyab Lodrö. Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985 and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and Young Lamas Home School under numerous traditional teachers. He founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981 and became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976.

nodes.label: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Karsé Kongtrul, Dzongsar Khyentse 02, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: John Clifford Holt
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Holt studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, the Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–1988), the University of Calgary (2006), and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: P. D. Premasiri
nodes.summary: P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under David J. Kalupahana and Eliot Deutsch, and served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Peradeniya (1997–2004).

nodes.label: Asanga Tilakaratne
nodes.summary: Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (University of Kelaniya) and as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Alvappillai Veluppillai
nodes.summary: Indologist Alvappillai Veluppillai earned doctorates from the University of Ceylon under K. Kanapathypillai and Oxford under Thomas Burrow. He held academic posts at Ceylon, Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University, among others.

nodes.label: Mahinda Deegalle
nodes.image: Mahinda Deegalle in the video 'Imagine a Buddhist AI...'.png
nodes.summary: Mahinda Deegalle studied at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Diana L. Eck. He was a lecturer at Bath Spa University (~2002–2021) and held visiting roles at McGill, Harvard, and Colgate.

nodes.label: Abdur Rehman
nodes.summary: Abdur Rehman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani. In 1988, he held a post at the University of Peshawar.

nodes.label: Luise Hercus
nodes.summary: Luise Hercus was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at St Anne's College and Australian National University. She taught at St Anne's College (1948–1954), was a research fellow at Adelaide (1965–1969), and worked at ANU (~1969–1991).

nodes.label: Pamela Gutman
nodes.summary: Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna and conducted research at the Australian National University from circa 1972 to 1976.

nodes.label: Sakda Hemthep
nodes.summary: Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.Phil. at Cardiff University under Max Deeg and Peter Harvey by 2014. As of 2026, he is a PhD researcher at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Radhika Herzberger
nodes.summary: Radhika Herzberger works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal and served as Director of the Rishi Valley School from ~1982 to 2012.

nodes.label: Alois Anton Führer
nodes.summary: Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD at Würzburg and studied with Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Lucknow State Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Jean Dantinne
nodes.summary: Jean Dantinne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

nodes.id: I:Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
nodes.label: Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
variants: Académie royale des Sciences, des Lettres et des Beaux-Arts de Belgique
Königliche Akademie der Wissenschaften, Literatur und Schönen Künste Belgiens

nodes.label: Michael Carrithers
nodes.summary: Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, and served as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University, along with posts at Oxford and LSE.

nodes.label: Caroline Humphrey
nodes.summary: Caroline Humphrey works in Iranian/Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds, she held fellowships at Girton and King's, and served as a university lecturer/professor at the University of Cambridge from 1978 to 2010.

nodes.label: Klaus Bruhn
nodes.summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who earned his doctorate (~1949–1955) and completed his Habilitation (~1959–1964) at the University of Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as Ordinarius für Indische Philologie at the Free University of Berlin (1966–1991).

nodes.label: Mary Jaksch
nodes.summary: Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez
nodes.summary: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Jane Caple
nodes.summary: Jane Caple is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and at the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

nodes.label: Vanderbilt University
variants: ヴァンダービルト大学

nodes.label: Sanjay Subrahmanyam
nodes.summary: Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and Delhi School of Economics. His posts include the University of Oxford (1993–1995, 2002), EHESS (1995–2002), UCLA (founding director 2005–2011; endowed chair 2014), and Collège de France (2013–2021).

nodes.label: Calambur Sivaramamurti
nodes.summary: Calambur Sivaramamurti studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India (~1946–1955), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

nodes.label: Mortimer Wheeler
nodes.summary: Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at UCL. He directed the National Museum Cardiff and the London Museum, founded the UCL Institute of Archaeology, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948).

nodes.label: Hermann Beythan
nodes.summary: Hermann Beythan was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai.

nodes.label: Sibani Das Gupta
nodes.summary: Sibani Das Gupta worked in Indology. She studied at the University of Dhaka, under teacher Rajendra Chandra Hazra, and completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta under Sushil Kumar De by 1954.

nodes.label: Ram Chandra Kak
nodes.summary: Ram Chandra Kak was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall. He served as curator of Sri Pratap Singh Museum, Archaeological Survey of India superintendent, and Kashmir's Director of Archæology and Research.

nodes.label: John Collinson Nesfield
nodes.summary: Nesfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Highgate School and Merton College, Oxford. He taught at Highgate School (1859–1864) and held posts at Presidency College, Krishnagar Government College, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (principal, 1878), and the University of Allahabad.

nodes.label: Thupten Jinpa
nodes.image: HH the Dalai Lama enlightened translator, Dr. Thupten Jinpa.jpg
nodes.summary: Thupten Jinpa (born 1958) is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Monastery, Zongkar Choede Monastery, and the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Ganden Monastery, Girton College, Stanford University, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

nodes.label: Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Tashi Tsering (born 1960) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Central School for Tibetans and under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, he held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1984–1992) and Amnye Machen Institute (~1992).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Napper
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Napper completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Rory Mackenzie
nodes.summary: Rory Mackenzie is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and served as a teacher at International Christian College.

nodes.label: Institute of Oriental Philosophy
variants: 公益財団法人東洋哲学研究所

nodes.label: Kōdō Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kōdō Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He later held a post as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1994.

nodes.id: I:Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada
nodes.label: Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada
variants: Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada

nodes.label: Kurunegoda Piyatissa
nodes.summary: Kurunegoda Piyatissa worked in Buddhist studies and served as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998, 2009).

nodes.label: Sarasvati Bhavan Library
variants: Sarasvati Bhavan Library, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University
Sarasvati Bhavan Library of the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi

nodes.label: Rajendra Mishra
nodes.summary: Indologist Rajendra Mishra studied under traditional teacher Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Pascale Haag
nodes.summary: Pascale Haag is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University and under Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre University. She held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 2003.

nodes.label: David L. Haberman
nodes.description: American indologist and historian of religion
nodes.summary: David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington (~1993–2021), where he became Professor Emeritus in 2021.

nodes.id: I:Jammu and Kashmir Research and Publication Department
nodes.label: Jammu and Kashmir Research and Publication Department
variants: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, Srinagar

nodes.id: I:Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
nodes.label: Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer
nodes.summary: K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer worked in the field of Indology. He served as the Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and as Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).

nodes.label: Norvin J. Hein
nodes.summary: Norvin J. Hein was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He held a post at Yale Divinity School as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion, attested in 1965.

nodes.label: John James Jones
nodes.summary: John James Jones was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912–1916). He served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales from around 1926 to 1957.

nodes.label: St John's College
variants: ケンブリッジ大学セント・ジョンズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Betty Heimann
nodes.summary: Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle under teachers including Simmel, Deussen, Sieg, and Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle, Hamburg (1931–1933), London, Oxford, and Colombo (1945–1949).

nodes.label: Ivo Fišer
nodes.summary: Ivo Fišer (1929–2004) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Charles University (attested 1960) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology (attested 1970).

nodes.label: Herbert V. Guenther
nodes.summary: Herbert V. Guenther studied Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Walther Wüst, alongside traditional teachers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and headed Far Eastern Studies at the University of Saskatchewan.

nodes.label: Ananda W. P. Guruge
nodes.summary: Ananda W. P. Guruge worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Ceylon and University of London. He held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
nodes.label: National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
Ratna Handurukande
nodes.summary: Ratna Handurukande is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who held lecturer posts at the University of Ceylon, in the Department of Sanskrit (attested 1970), and at the University of Peradeniya.

nodes.label: Carmen Meinert
nodes.summary: Carmen Meinert is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001 and held posts at the University of Hamburg, Ruhr University Bochum, and Käte Hamburger Kolleg.

nodes.label: Christoph Anderl
nodes.summary: Christoph Anderl works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed an MA at the University of Vienna (~1989–1995) and a PhD under Christoph Harbsmeier at the University of Oslo (~1997–2004), becoming a permanent member at Ghent University around 2012.

nodes.label: N. Venkataramanayya
nodes.summary: N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy at Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums.

nodes.label: Evan Thompson
nodes.summary: Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst under Robert Thurman and at the University of Toronto under Francisco Varela. His main posts include York University (2002–2005), University of Toronto (~2005–2013), and University of British Columbia (from 2013).

nodes.label: Dan Zahavi
nodes.summary: Dan Zahavi is a philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and his habilitation from the University of Copenhagen. He has held directorships at Copenhagen and the Center for Subjectivity Research, and a professorship at Oxford.

nodes.label: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
nodes.summary: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate in philosophy from Oxford, held research fellowships at Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Trinity College, Oxford, taught at NUS, and became a Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

nodes.summary: Francisco J. Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive neuroscience. He earned degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard (PhD 1968–1970), holding posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, École Polytechnique, and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

nodes.label: Eleanor Rosch
nodes.summary: Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her Ph.D. at Harvard University under Roger Brown (~1963–1969) and became a professor of cognitive psychology at the University of California, Berkeley in 1971.

nodes.label: Karen O'Brien-Kop
nodes.summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After completing her PhD at SOAS University of London, she held posts at SOAS, the University of Roehampton (attested 2020), and King's College London (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daniela Bevilacqua
nodes.summary: Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.

nodes.label: Sravana Borkataky-Varma
nodes.summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD). Working in Indology and religious studies, she taught at Rice, UNC Wilmington, University of Houston, University of Montana, Harvard, and held a fellowship at CSWR (~2021-2023).

nodes.label: Mikel Burley
nodes.summary: Mikel Burley is a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the University of Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, at the University of Bristol under John Peacock, and also under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr. He joined the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Philip Deslippe
nodes.summary: Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student (attested 2020–2026) and teaching associate (attested 2020) at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Carl W. Ernst
nodes.summary: Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Stanford (A.B.) and Harvard (Ph.D.), he taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

nodes.label: Gordon Hannington Luce
nodes.summary: Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (circa 1908–1911) and served as a professor at the University of Yangon from circa 1912 to 1964.

nodes.label: John Alexander Stewart
nodes.summary: John Alexander Stewart, an Aberdeen graduate who worked in linguistics, served in the Indian Civil Service from ca. 1905 to 1933. From ca. 1933 to 1948, he held posts as Reader in Burmese at the University of London and SOAS.

nodes.label: O. M. Moneer
nodes.summary: O. M. Moneer was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He served as Curator at the Central Asian Antiquities Museum and was attested in 1939 as Assistant Superintendent, Western Circle, for the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Nanigopal Majumdar
nodes.summary: Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He became a Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and served as Superintendent of the Arch&aelogic&al Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Daya Ram Sahni
nodes.summary: Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab, he held museum and archaeology posts in Lucknow, Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935).

nodes.label: Sydney Frank Markham
nodes.summary: Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College (~1919–1923) and served as Secretary, then President, of the Museums Association between circa 1929 and 1942.

nodes.label: Ghulam Yazdani
nodes.summary: Ghulam Yazdani was an indologist and archaeologist. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (B.A. 1905) under J. Godfrey F. Day, C. F. Andrews, M. Ishaq, and N. A. Dehlvi. He directed the Archaeological Department of Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

nodes.label: Hirananda Sastri
nodes.summary: Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College and University of the Punjab. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, as Jammu and Kashmir's Superintendent of Archaeology, and Baroda State's Director of Archaeology (1934–1942).

nodes.label: Ramaprasad Chanda
nodes.summary: Ramaprasad Chanda worked in Indology and archaeology, studying at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served as Superintendent of the Indian Museum's Archaeological Section (1921–1932) and president of the Indian Anthropological Institute (1938–1942), which he also founded.

nodes.label: Richard K. Payne
nodes.summary: Richard K. Payne works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata, served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1993–2017), and held posts at the Graduate Theological Union and Numata Center.

nodes.label: Jeffrey S. Lidke
nodes.summary: Jeffrey S. Lidke specializes in religious studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of Virginia (visiting assistant professor of religion, attested 2003) and Berry College.

nodes.label: Anna Andreeva
nodes.summary: Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is attested as a permanent member in 2026.

nodes.label: Georgios T. Halkias
nodes.summary: Georgios T. Halkias, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Oxford under Charles Ramble (DPhil, ~2001–2006). He held research posts at SOAS, Warburg, and Bochum, and became associate professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2013).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Kotyk
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Judith Simmer-Brown
nodes.summary: Judith Simmer-Brown works in Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa and earned degrees from Cornell College, Florida State, and Walden University. She has been on the faculty of Naropa University since 1977.

nodes.label: Eric Haruki Swanson
nodes.summary: Eric Haruki Swanson works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held a post at Loyola Marymount University and served at Stanford University as a Senior Visiting Scholar (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sthaneshwar Timalsina
nodes.summary: Sthaneshwar Timalsina works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, he has held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University, and Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: John Chadwick
variants: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.summary: John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at the University of Oxford (ca. 1946–1952) and Cambridge, where he served as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics from 1969 to 1984.

nodes.label: Bridget Allchin
nodes.description: English archaeologist, specializing in South Asian archaeology
nodes.summary: Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) worked in history, archaeology, and indology. She studied at the University of Cape Town and UCL Institute of Archaeology under Frederick Zeuner, and was later a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978–2017).
