nodes.label: D. C. Sarasvati
nodes.summary: D. C. Sarasvati was an indologist who studied under V. Raghavan. From 1964 to 1965, she served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Seema Alavi
nodes.summary: Seema Alavi is a historian who completed her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held teaching and professorship posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia, the University of Delhi, and Ashoka University.

nodes.label: Ali S. Asani
nodes.description: Chair:Near Eastern Languages/Civilizations Department/Director:Prince Alwaleed bin Talal Islamic Studies Program/Harvard University
nodes.summary: Ali S. Asani specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and graduate education at Harvard College and Harvard University between circa 1973 and 1984, subsequently becoming a professor of Middle Eastern and Indo-Muslim studies there from 1983.

nodes.label: Emmie te Nijenhuis
nodes.summary: Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning a PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University and held a post at Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Alex McKay
nodes.summary: Alex McKay is a historian, archaeologist, and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London by 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

nodes.label: Shek-Wing Tam
nodes.description: Hong Kong Buddhist scholar, writer, and fortune-teller
nodes.summary: Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau. He held posts at Renmin University of China (~2007) and Tsinghua University.

nodes.label: Weirong Shen
nodes.summary: Weirong Shen (1962–) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has taught Penghao Sun and held academic appointments at Renmin University of China (~2006–2020) and the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Henry C. H. Shiu
nodes.summary: Henry C. H. Shiu works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto (completed by 2006), having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David B. Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

nodes.label: Kapila Vatsyayan
nodes.summary: Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu universities. She founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, serving as its trustee, Academic Director, and chairperson.

nodes.label: David J. Kalupahana
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist scholar and philosopher (1936–2014)
nodes.summary: David J. Kalupahana was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS/University of London (PhD ~1966). He taught at Ceylon (~1959–1972) and chaired the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from 1972.

nodes.label: N. A. Jayawickrama
nodes.summary: N. A. Jayawickrama (born 1920) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1976) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens

nodes.label: Clare Carlisle
nodes.summary: Clare Carlisle is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She held posts as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and professor at King's College London (~2020).

nodes.label: Washington and Lee University
variants: Department of Religion at Washington and Lee University

nodes.label: Edward Vernon Arnold
nodes.summary: Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1875–1879) and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (~1881–1882). He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1880–1886) and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

variants: University College of North Wales in Bangor

nodes.label: Carl Darling Buck
nodes.summary: Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University and Leipzig University before serving as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

nodes.label: Lawrence Heyworth Mills
nodes.summary: Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837-1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford (attested 1903).

nodes.label: George Foot Moore
nodes.summary: George Foot Moore was a scholar of religious studies. He studied at Yale (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877), and held professorships at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Harvard University (1902–1928), along with a guest professorship in Berlin (1909–1910).

nodes.label: Pulinbihari Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Pulinbihari Chakravarti was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. In 1951, he was attested as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Bhāgīratha Prasāda Tripāṭhī
nodes.summary: Bhāgīratha Prasāda Tripāṭhī was an Indologist and linguist who held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1976 and attested in 1989 as head of the Research Department.

nodes.label: Donald Eric Capps
nodes.summary: Donald Eric Capps was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, North Carolina at Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

nodes.label: Helen Hardacre
nodes.summary: Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard University from 1992.

nodes.label: James L. Taylor
nodes.summary: James L. Taylor works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Syed Nawab Ali
nodes.description: Persian-English translator who worked as a professor in Baroda
nodes.summary: Syed Nawab Ali worked in linguistics and religious studies. Attested in 1932, he served as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.

nodes.label: Catherine Prueitt
nodes.summary: Catherine Prueitt is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Yoshio Nishiguchi
nodes.summary: Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

nodes.label: Ester Bianchi
nodes.summary: Ester Bianchi, a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earned her PhD from Ca' Foscari and EPHE under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna. She has taught at the University of Perugia since circa 2007.

nodes.label: Karl Debreczeny
nodes.summary: Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he studied under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Fabienne Jagou
nodes.summary: Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. She earned her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the EHESS (~1994–1999) and was appointed Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~2001).

nodes.label: Rob Linrothe
nodes.summary: Rob Linrothe is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and art history scholar. He studied at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago (PhD 1992). He held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College, Rubin Museum, and Northwestern University.

nodes.label: Paul K. Nietupski
nodes.summary: Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Abraham Zablocki
nodes.summary: Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College in 2008.

nodes.label: Bal Krishen Thapar
nodes.summary: Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Punjab and Heidelberg universities and under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of CCRT (1982–1992).

nodes.label: Richard King
nodes.summary: Richard King specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster universities (PhD under Daniel Mariau), and held posts at the University of Stirling (~1993–2002), Vanderbilt University (~2002–2009), and the University of Glasgow (~2009–2011).

nodes.label: Klaus Karttunen
nodes.description: Finnish ethnologist, indologist and university teacher
nodes.summary: Klaus Karttunen works in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his BA at the University of Helsinki, studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, among others. His career includes multiple research and teaching appointments at Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

nodes.label: Henrik Zilliacus
nodes.summary: Henrik Zilliacus, a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology, studied at the University of Helsinki (~1926–1936) and later held an academic post there (~1944–1974).

nodes.label: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz
nodes.summary: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz (1934–2001) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Graz from circa 1953 to 1958 and later served there as a professor from circa 1976 to 1999.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Vasilkov
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1962-1967). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1978, ~1996).

nodes.label: Katsutoshi Ono
nodes.summary: Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University, later working at Kyoto University (1933–1943), the Eastern Cultural Institute's Beijing Branch (~1938–1945), Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and Ryukoku University (~1970–1980).

nodes.label: Rita Langer
nodes.summary: Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004) under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at the University of Bristol.

nodes.label: Alexander Piatigorsky
variants: アレクサンデル・モイシェイェヴィチ・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンデル・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.summary: Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Moscow State University (~1946–1951), he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and taught at SOAS University of London, serving as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia (1990–2001).

nodes.label: J. B. Disanayaka
nodes.summary: J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 1996, he was attested as a professor at the University of Colombo and held an attested post at SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Robert Alan Goodding
nodes.summary: Robert Alan Goodding is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

nodes.label: Frederick M. Smith
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held positions at the University of Iowa as professor (attested 2006–2008) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Philip Lutgendorf
nodes.summary: Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (ca. 1967–1987), joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985, and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

nodes.summary: Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich (1876–1883) and had a career at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881, serving as Director (1904–1921).

nodes.label: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi
nodes.summary: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

nodes.label: Elliot M. Stern
nodes.summary: Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, earning PhD degrees attested in 1988 and 1998.

nodes.label: Michael C. Shapiro
nodes.summary: Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a Professor at the University of Washington from circa 1970 to 2013, later becoming Professor Emeritus of Hindi.

nodes.label: Satya Vrat Shastri

nodes.description: Jnanpith Award recipient in Sanskrit. Indian academic
nodes.summary: Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma at Punjab, Banaras Hindu, and Punjabi universities. He held professorships at Delhi and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

nodes.label: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam
nodes.summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his dissertation and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1967.

nodes.label: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld
nodes.summary: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld, an Indologist, studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1946–1974). He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

nodes.label: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
nodes.summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Muni Jinavijaya. He held academic positions at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the International School of Dravidian Linguistics, and directed the L.D. Institute of Indology.

nodes.label: Fabrizia Baldissera
nodes.summary: Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Florence (~2000) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

nodes.label: Yun Ji
nodes.summary: Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at Fudan University by 2006. Ji served as a librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Eun-su Cho
nodes.summary: Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini (attested 1997). She taught at the University of Michigan (until 2004) and Seoul National University (from 2004).

nodes.label: Georges-Jean Pinault
nodes.summary: Georges-Jean Pinault studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry (~1975–1980). Active in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, he taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1980–1986), Clermont Auvergne University (~1987–1996), and became professor at EPHE in 1999.

nodes.label: Jason Protass
nodes.summary: Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016) and held posts at Ryukoku University and Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Nathan Sivin
nodes.summary: Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian educated at DLI, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977, was Professor Emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006), and was Honorary Professor at CAS (~2014-2022).

nodes.label: Joseph Needham
nodes.summary: Joseph Needham was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Oundle School, Gonville and Caius College, and the University of Cambridge (~1918-1925), later holding posts at Cambridge (~1924-1966), Gonville and Caius, and the Needham Research Institute (~1987-1990).

nodes.label: Sean D. Gaffney
nodes.summary: Sean D. Gaffney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, also studying under Philip T. Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a post there.

nodes.label: Bulcsu Siklós
nodes.summary: Bulcsu Siklós is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles Roskelly Bawden, and later held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Yang-Gyu An
nodes.summary: Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies and indology. An completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (attested 1998) and also studied under Hojin (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Chikafumi Watanabe
nodes.summary: Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia (under Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Narhar Aklujkar) and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura.

nodes.label: Catherine Ludvik
nodes.summary: Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Toronto under David B. Waterhouse, later holding positions at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Akio Donohashi
nodes.summary: Akio Donohashi works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1974) and served as a professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

nodes.id: I:Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Forschungsstelle »Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway« der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Forschungsstelle „Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway“ an der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, University of Heidelberg

nodes.label: University of Cologne
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Cologne
Centre for Advanced Study of Humanities, University of Cologne

nodes.label: Robert E. Morrell
nodes.summary: Robert E. Morrell was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic appointment at Washington University in St. Louis (attested in 1985 and 2006).

nodes.label: Washington University in St. Louis
variants: Washington University in St. Louis Missouri

nodes.label: James W. Heisig
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・ハイジック
nodes.summary: James W. Heisig works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge, he was a longtime Permanent Research Fellow at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1976; 1978; 1991–2001).

nodes.label: Presidency College, Chennai
variants: プレジデンシー・カレッジ

nodes.label: Barbra R. Clayton
nodes.summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from McGill University, where she was supervised by Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and later held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Katherine K. Young
nodes.summary: Katherine K. Young studied at the University of Chicago and McGill University. Working in Indology and religious studies, she served as a professor at McGill University from ~1978 to 2016.

nodes.label: Damien Keown
nodes.summary: Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He served as Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London.

nodes.label: Horst Brinkhaus
nodes.summary: Horst Brinkhaus (born 1945) is an Indologist. He held positions at the University of Münster from around 1978 to 1988 and at Kiel University from circa 1993 to 2011.

nodes.label: Sarah J. Horton
nodes.summary: Sarah J. Horton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Gopinath Kaviraj
nodes.summary: Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at University Maharani College and University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis and others, he served as librarian at Sarasvati Bhavan Library (1914–1920) and Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1923–1937).

nodes.label: Klaus-Dieter Mathes
nodes.summary: Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Marburg and habilitated at Hamburg under Michael Hahn and Klaus Sagaster. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and served as professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Melvyn C. Goldstein
nodes.summary: Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at the University of Michigan and earned his PhD at the University of Washington (~1968), later serving as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

nodes.label: Jay M. Bernstein
nodes.summary: Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Essex (~1975–1996), Vanderbilt University (~1996–2001), and The New School (~2001).

nodes.label: The New School
variants: The New School for Social Research, New York
The New School for Social Research

nodes.label: Osmund Bopearachchi
nodes.summary: Osmund Bopearachchi (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, Panthéon-Sorbonne, and Paris-Sorbonne, and held posts at the CNRS and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Deborah Carlson
nodes.summary: Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Department of Archaeology
variants: Archaeological Survey Department of the Government of Sri Lanka

nodes.label: Paul Bernard
nodes.summary: Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne, he directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1965–1980) and taught at EPHE (1981).

nodes.label: Doris Meth Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Doris Meth Srinivasan specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning degrees from Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington University, George Mason University, the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, and Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: Axel Michaels
nodes.summary: Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg and Kiel, and under Laxmi Nath Shrestha. He held posts at Kiel, Bern (1992–1996), and became professor of Classical Indology at Heidelberg University in 1996.

nodes.label: Hans Hartog
nodes.summary: Hans Hartog (born 1912) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Wuppertal/Bethel, and Munich before earning his PhD at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under doctoral supervisor Friedrich Heiler.

nodes.label: Friedrich Heiler
nodes.summary: Friedrich Heiler was a religious studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Munich (~1912-1917). He held teaching assignments at Munich in 1918 and served as Leiter at the University of Marburg beginning in 1920.

nodes.label: Walther Wüst
nodes.description: Rector of the University of Munich and SS member (1901-1993)
nodes.summary: Walther Wüst (1901–1993) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich as professor and Dean, led a section at Ahnenerbe, and served as president of Deutsche Akademie.

nodes.label: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer
nodes.image: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-2004-0413-501, Prof. Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.jpg
nodes.summary: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

nodes.label: Kurt Huber
nodes.description: German folk song researcher, professor at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in Munich, member of the White Rose (1893-1943)
nodes.summary: Philosopher Kurt Huber earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He remained there for his academic career, serving as extraordinary professor in 1926 and full professor in 1938.

nodes.label: Erich Rudolf Jaensch
nodes.summary: Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a philosopher. After studying at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD 1905–1908), and Strasbourg, he served as Ordinarius for philosophy at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and as ordinary professor at the University of Marburg from 1913.

nodes.label: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen
nodes.summary: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at Bonn (1934), Munich (1936-1941), and Mainz (~1947-1969), alongside visiting posts at Córdoba, UCLA, Tokyo, and Chicago.

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schultz
nodes.description: German philosopher, historian and art historian (1881-1936)
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Schultz worked in philosophy and history/archaeology, receiving his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He was administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and held the Chair of Philosophy at Munich (1934).

nodes.label: Ferdinand Sommer
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Sommer (1875–1962) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen (1896) and completed his habilitation at Leipzig, subsequently holding professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

nodes.label: Giovanni Vacca
nodes.summary: Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence, taught at Florence (1910), and held chairs in East Asian language, literature, history, and geography at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

nodes.id: I:Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
nodes.label: Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
Sakkottai Krishnaswami Aiyangar
nodes.summary: Sakkottai Krishnaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Madras. He lectured at Central College, Bangalore (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.

nodes.label: John Kieschnick
nodes.summary: John Kieschnick is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Bristol from around 2005 to 2011 before becoming a professor of Buddhist studies at Stanford University in 2011.

nodes.label: Hellmuth Hecker
nodes.summary: Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948) and under Paul Debes in 1945. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1952 to 1988.

nodes.label: Rudrapatna Shamasastry
nodes.summary: Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist educated at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Pathashala (1912–1918) and Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

nodes.label: Indologica Taurinensia
variants: Indologica Taurinensia, The Journal of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies

nodes.label: Richard A. Rosengarten
nodes.summary: Richard A. Rosengarten is a scholar in religious studies. He has served at the University of Chicago as Dean (attested 2008–2012) and as Associate Professor of Religion and Literature, including in the College (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daniel Dubuisson
nodes.summary: Daniel Dubuisson (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held appointments as director of research at the CNRS / National Centre for Scientific Research (~1980–2015) and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III (~1989–2015).

nodes.label: Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III
variants: Charles-de-Gaulle University of Arts and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Elaine Fisher
nodes.summary: Elaine Fisher is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010). She holds a faculty post at Stanford University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Z. Smith
variants: ジョナサン・Z・スミス
nodes.summary: Jonathan Z. Smith studied at Haverford, Yale, and Yale Divinity School. A religious studies scholar, he held posts at Dartmouth, UC Santa Barbara, served as president of the Society of Biblical Literature, and was Dean of the College at Chicago.

nodes.label: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Meinrad Scheller
nodes.summary: Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, and at Paris. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).

nodes.label: Gregory Max Seton
nodes.summary: Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara (-2008), and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (-2015), where he was supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Martin Joachim Kümmel
nodes.summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel (b. 1970) is a linguist and Indologist. He earned his master's, doctorate, and Habilitation at the University of Freiburg, where he was an assistant and academic councillor (~1999–2007) before taking a chair at the University of Jena in 2013.

nodes.label: Helmut Rix
nodes.summary: Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen. He held posts at Neuendettelsau, Tübingen, the University of Regensburg, and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: Jinzhang Peng
nodes.summary: Jinzhang Peng was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He served as deputy director of the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1976–1986) and as a research professor at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2020).

nodes.label: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng
nodes.summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn. Tseng has served on the faculty at Fo Guang University.

nodes.label: Fo Guang University
variants: 佛光人文社會學院宗教學系

nodes.label: Peter Moran
nodes.summary: Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Charles Keyes and teachers including Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Thomas Watters
nodes.description: British diplomat in China and Korea, sinologist
nodes.summary: Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Queen's University Belfast, Queen's University of Ireland, and Queen's University at Kingston, earning B.A. degrees circa 1861.

nodes.label: Willem van der Molen
nodes.summary: Willem van der Molen worked in linguistics and Sinology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971-1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1983-2017) and the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Zarawar Khan
nodes.summary: Zarawar Khan specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

nodes.label: Jessie Pons
nodes.summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and served as Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Max Walleser
nodes.summary: Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD). He taught at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936), founding the Heidelberg Institute for Buddhology in 1928.

nodes.label: Michael Comans
nodes.summary: Michael Comans is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong, as well as under Dayananda Saraswati and R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and taught at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.summary: Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit College, Chamrajpet, and under teachers including P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.

nodes.label: Rahul Peter Das
nodes.description: German professor of South Asian studies (born 1954)
nodes.summary: Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler. He served as Chair and Professor of South Asian Studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Nagin J. Shah
nodes.summary: Nagin J. Shah is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He succeeded Dalsukh Malvania as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968) and taught Maria Heim.

nodes.label: Ernest John Henry Mackay
nodes.summary: Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. From 1919 to 1922, he served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine.

nodes.label: Rakhal Das Banerji
nodes.summary: Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served as an officer in the Archaeological Survey of India and held the Manindra Chandra Nandy professorship at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Grove
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Grove specializes in Tibetology and computational fields. He held affiliations at the University of Virginia, where he is attested in 2006 and as a Research Associate in 2026.

nodes.label: Stephen Wootton Bushell
nodes.summary: Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a Sinology and history scholar. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London, and held medical posts at Guy's Hospital (1866) and Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

nodes.label: Alexander Rogers
nodes.summary: Alexander Rogers was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).

nodes.label: Henry Beveridge
nodes.description: British linguist and Indian Civil Service officer
nodes.summary: Henry Beveridge studied at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast. He worked in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and served as President of the Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

nodes.label: Edgar Howard Sturtevant
variants: エドガー・H・スターティヴァント
エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.jawiki: エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.summary: Edgar Howard Sturtevant (1875–1952) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Illinois College and Indiana University Bloomington, later holding academic posts at Columbia University (circa 1907–1920) and Yale University (circa 1923–1943).

nodes.label: Joanna Jurewicz
nodes.summary: Joanna Jurewicz is an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She holds academic posts as a professor at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2006 and 2026.

nodes.label: University of Western Australia
variants: 西オーストラリア大学

nodes.label: Peterhouse, Cambridge
variants: Peterhouse College of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Klaus Ludwig Janert
nodes.description: born:1922|died:1994|; Janert, Klaus Ludwig, 1922-1994; Janert, Klaus L.
nodes.summary: Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Frankfurt (1946–1954), and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He was an assistant at Göttingen (~1954–1957) and held a full professorship at Cologne (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Christophe Vielle
nodes.summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He held a professorship at the Catholic University of Louvain (attested 2009–2013) and is attested as an Associate member at Ghent University in 2026.

nodes.label: Robert Deliège
nodes.summary: Robert Deliège is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1981–1984). He has held academic posts at the University of Kerala and as a professor at the Catholic University of Louvain (~1988).

nodes.label: Jacques Scheuer
nodes.summary: Jacques Scheuer was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the Catholic University of Louvain and under Madeleine Biardeau at Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1972–1978). He held posts at Centre Sèvres and the Catholic University of Louvain (~1978–2007).

nodes.label: Utz Podzeit
nodes.image: Venia Legendi 1997- Dr. Utz Podzeit mit Mechthild.jpg
nodes.summary: Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at the University of Vienna starting in 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

nodes.label: Roderick M. Chisholm
nodes.summary: Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown University and earned his PhD at Harvard (~1938–1942). He held professorships at the Barnes Foundation (~1945–1946) and Brown University (~1947–1986), also serving as Metaphysical Society of America president (1973).

nodes.label: Philip L. Quinn
nodes.summary: Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (ca. 1976–1985), served as John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at Notre Dame from 1985, and presided over the APA (1994–1995).

nodes.label: Ernest Sosa
nodes.summary: Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and as Board of Governors Professor at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

nodes.label: Antoine Cabaton
nodes.summary: Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales and the École du Louvre, and later held a post at the Bibliothèque nationale de France from around 1899 to 1928.

nodes.label: Karunesh Shukla
nodes.summary: Karunesh Shukla is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Eduard Müller-Hess
nodes.summary: Eduard Müller-Hess (1853–1923) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed an Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University in 1874 and was attested as a professor at the University of Bern in 1897–1898.

nodes.label: Mabel Haynes Bode
nodes.summary: Mabel Haynes Bode was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a PhD from Bern and studied under T.W. Rhys Davids, Cecil Bendall, and Sylvain Lévi, later lecturing at UCL (1909–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

nodes.label: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff
nodes.jawiki: ウルリヒ・フォン・ヴィラモーヴィッツ＝メレンドルフ
nodes.summary: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, and under Johannes Schmidt, Otto Jahn, and Moriz Haupt. He was a professor at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

nodes.label: David Ludden
nodes.summary: David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. Educated at Yale and Penn, he held posts at Virginia (1979–1980), Penn (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and NYU (starting 2007 as professor of political economy and globalization).

nodes.label: Allison Busch
nodes.summary: Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University, attested for 2026.

nodes.label: James B. Apple
nodes.summary: James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under John D. Dunne and studied with numerous academic and traditional teachers, including Jan Nattier, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and the 14th Dalai Lama.

nodes.label: Henepola Gunaratana
nodes.summary: Henepola Gunaratana studied at Kelaniya, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (BA and PhD). He led the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur (~1958–1968) and held posts at the Buddhist Vihara Society, American University, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenzin Negi
variants: Lobsang Tenzin Negi (legal name Satya Dev Negi)

nodes.label: Glenn H. Mullin
nodes.image: Visit of Telo Tulku to Roerich House, U.B. (3861963599).jpg
nodes.summary: Glenn H. Mullin (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous traditional masters, including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.

nodes.label: 14th Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso
variants: His Holiness the Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso
nodes.summary: 14th Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Heinrich Harrer, Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Tagdrag Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and founded the Mind and Life Institute in 1990.

nodes.label: Luciano Petech
nodes.summary: Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at Allahabad, held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and served as IATS President (c. 1989–1995).

nodes.label: Mel Weitsman
variants: ソウジュン・メル・ウェイツマン

nodes.label: Reb Anderson
nodes.summary: Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from circa 1986 to 1995.

nodes.label: Elena De Rossi Filibeck
nodes.summary: Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history at Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech until 1971. In 1980, she became an associate professor at Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Stefan M. Maul
nodes.summary: Stefan M. Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Free University of Berlin, later holding posts as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University (1995) and research unit head at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2004).

nodes.label: Søren Sørensen
nodes.summary: Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indologist. He held posts at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 to 1902.

nodes.label: Vilhelm Thomsen
variants: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
ヴィルヘルム・ルズヴィ・ペーター・トムセン
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
nodes.summary: Vilhelm Thomsen was a Danish linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (PhD 1859–1869). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1869), associate professor (1875), and professor (1887–1913), later serving as President of the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters (1909).

nodes.label: Karl Verner
variants: カール・アドルフ・ヴェルナー
nodes.summary: Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Copenhagen and under August Leskien. He worked as a librarian at Halle (~1876–1883) and became a docent in Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.

nodes.label: Rosina Pastore
nodes.summary: Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She worked as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne and is an Affiliated Researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Marianne Winder
nodes.summary: Marianne Winder (1918–2001) studied at London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served as Assistant Librarian and Curator at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine.

nodes.label: Nigel Allan
nodes.summary: Nigel Allan is a scholar of history and archaeology who succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Charles Edmund Godakumbura
nodes.summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977), an Indologist and archaeologist, earned multiple degrees at the University of London, where he later taught (~1953–1959). He served as Sri Lanka's Commissioner of Archaeology (1956–1967) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1963–1970).

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary
variants: Union Theological Seminary in New York City
Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York

nodes.label: Anne MacDonald
nodes.summary: Anne MacDonald is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012) and the University of Vienna (attested 2008, 2026).

nodes.label: Bhagwan Dash
nodes.summary: Bhagwan Dash was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (~1971–1978). He worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer for the Library of Congress.

nodes.label: Vaibhav Singh
nodes.summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Reading by 2017, where he also held a post attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Richard Carnac Temple
nodes.summary: Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1931), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society (~1928–1931).

nodes.label: Himanshu Prabha Ray
nodes.summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) works in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Panjab University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Cambridge. She served as Associate Professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

nodes.label: Kuvempu University

nodes.label: Geoff Childs
nodes.summary: Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

variants: 財団法人西蔵大蔵経研究会

nodes.label: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
nodes.summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian who studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928. He became a lecturer in Chinese at Leiden in 1946 and served as Professor from 1956 to 1975.

nodes.label: Robert H. Brower
nodes.description: Professor of far east language and literature (1923–1988)
nodes.summary: Robert H. Brower was a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Minnesota, Stanford, and the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Wright
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Wright was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He served on the faculty at Stanford from 1947 (professor in 1958) before becoming Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

nodes.label: Steven Lukes
nodes.jawiki: スティーヴン・ルークス
nodes.summary: Steven Lukes is a scholar of philosophy who studied at Oxford. He held academic appointments at Balliol College, Florence, Siena, the European University Institute, the London School of Economics, and New York University.

nodes.label: Soonil Hwang
nodes.summary: Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich. He later held a post at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Fawad Khan
nodes.summary: Fawad Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, serving as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Kirby Flower Smith
nodes.description: American classical philologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Kirby Flower Smith was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Anālayo
nodes.description: German Buddhist monk, scholar, and meditation teacher (born 1962)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Peradeniya (~1997–2000) and completed his habilitation at the University of Marburg (~2000–2006). He held posts at Hamburg, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and Barre Center.

nodes.label: Wataru Ryose
nodes.summary: Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

nodes.label: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé
variants: Kong sprul Blo gros mtha’ yas

nodes.jawiki: ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.summary: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, and Pema Nyinche Wangpo, and also taught several prominent figures.

nodes.label: David Higgins
nodes.summary: David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala
nodes.summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He was Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955).

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.image: Sukumar Sen linguist 2020 cover of India cr.jpg
nodes.summary: Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. He served as lecturer and Khaira Professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: David Kopf
nodes.summary: David Kopf was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1958–1964) and spent his academic career at the University of Minnesota (~1967–2003).

nodes.label: Phra Brahmapundit
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), and President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004).

nodes.label: Willard Van Orman Quine

nodes.summary: Willard Van Orman Quine worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University, where he served as Junior Fellow (1933-1936), Assistant Professor (1940), and Edgar Pierce Chair of Philosophy (1948-1978).

nodes.label: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri
nodes.summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras. He served at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University as Sanskrit department head (1942–1947).

nodes.label: Charles Cutler Torrey
nodes.summary: Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and served as a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

nodes.label: Alexander W. Macdonald
nodes.summary: Alexander W. Macdonald was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He was a professor at Paris Nanterre University (~1970–1991) and was affiliated with the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Rasmus Rask
variants: ラスムス・クリスチャン・ラスク
nodes.summary: Rasmus Rask was a Danish scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen. He held multiple posts at the University of Copenhagen, including professor of Eastern languages (1831).

nodes.label: Stella Kramrisch
nodes.summary: Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held faculty positions at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993), and NYU (1964–1982).

nodes.label: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati
nodes.summary: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served as Librarian at the Asiatic Society (1943) and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: H. G. Narahari
nodes.summary: Indologist H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, completing an MA under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he was attested as a Research Fellow at Madras and a Research Assistant at the Adyar Library.

nodes.label: Charles Philip Brown
nodes.summary: Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884), an Indologist and linguist, studied at East India Company College and under traditional teachers in India. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1855–1879).

nodes.label: Frank F. Conlon
nodes.summary: Frank F. Conlon (1938–2021) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and was Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington from circa 2002 to 2021.

nodes.label: Daniel Clarke Waugh
nodes.summary: Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He studied at Yale University (B.A. 1963) and Harvard University (Master's 1965, 1972), joining the faculty of the University of Washington in 1972.

nodes.label: Katia Buffetrille
nodes.summary: Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald, later holding posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002) and the Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale.

nodes.label: Baliram Shukla
nodes.summary: Baliram Shukla is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.image: Shunryu Suzuki at Zen Mountain Center (cropped).png
nodes.summary: Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji under several traditional teachers. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara.

nodes.label: Richard Baker
variants: ゼンテツ・リチャード・ベーカー
nodes.summary: Richard Baker (born 1936) is a religious and Buddhist studies figure. He studied at UC Berkeley and Harvard, and under Shunryu Suzuki from 1961, whom he succeeded in 1971 as Abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center until 1984.

nodes.label: Huston Smith
nodes.summary: Huston Smith (1919–2016) worked in religious studies and philosophy, earning degrees from Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Denver, Washington University in St. Louis, MIT, Syracuse University, and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Johanna Narten
nodes.description: Professor of Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistics (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Saarland under Ernst Zinn and at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann, where she earned a PhD and habilitation, later serving as an assistant there (1973–1977).

nodes.label: Ngawang Jorden
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ngawang Jorden has held posts at Harvard University (attested 1999) and Sakya College, and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Jadunath Sarkar
nodes.summary: Jadunath Sarkar was a historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Ripon, Vidyasagar, Ravenshaw, and Patna colleges, and served as dean at Banaras Hindu University and vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

nodes.label: George Vladimir Bobrinskoy
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist George Vladimir Bobrinskoy studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary (BA 1926) and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago (1927–1966), becoming chairman of the linguistics department in 1951.

nodes.label: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy
nodes.summary: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy was an Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Wycliffe College, University College London, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed Ceylon's Geological Survey and held posts at the Boston MFA and the Smithsonian.

nodes.label: Peter Masefield
nodes.summary: Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Karel Werner
nodes.summary: Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate from Palacký University. He taught Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990) and later served as a professor at Masaryk University (1993–1998).

nodes.label: Ninian Smart
nodes.summary: Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher educated at Glasgow and Oxford. He held chairs and posts at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University (1967–1982), UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998), and UC Berkeley (1976–1998).

nodes.label: Denis Sinor
nodes.summary: Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

nodes.label: Herbert Franke
nodes.summary: Herbert Franke studied sinology and Central Asian studies at Bonn, Berlin, and Cologne under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer. He held posts at the University of Cologne, University of Munich, and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: S. N. Balagangadhara
nodes.summary: S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch, later serving as director at Ghent University and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion.

nodes.label: Kazu Uehara

nodes.summary: Christoph Harbsmeier works in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Merton College, Oxford (~1966–1973) and the University of Copenhagen (~1973–1981). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia (1973–1976) and the University of Oslo, where he became Professor in 1980.

nodes.label: Shu-Fen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-Fen Chen specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and Hans Henrich Hock, and later served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

nodes.summary: Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. nodes.label: Todd T. Lewis
nodes.summary: Todd T. Lewis (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Columbia University, he was attested at the College of the Holy Cross from 1996, serving as a named professor by 2016–2017.

nodes.label: Lothar Ledderose
nodes.summary: Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne, and served as a professor at Heidelberg University (c. 1976–2010) and president of DMG (1978–1990).

nodes.label: David Faure
nodes.summary: David Faure is a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD from Princeton University. He taught at Indiana University, lectured at St Antony's College (1990), and served as director at CUHK.

nodes.label: Michel Strickmann
nodes.summary: Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot University (PhD 1979) under teachers including Anthony Hulsewé, Kristofer Schipper, and Max Kaltenmark. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Dodrupchen Rinpoche

nodes.label: Alf Sommerfelt

nodes.label: Olivier Lacombe
