nodes.summary: Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Karam Tej Singh Sarao
nodes.summary: Karam Tej Singh Sarao (b. 1955) is an Indian historian and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman in 1989 and became a professor at the University of Delhi in 1995.

nodes.label: David Ownby
nodes.summary: David Ownby is a historian and sinologist. After earning his B.A. from Vanderbilt and a Ph.D. from Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993) and was Professor of History at the University of Montreal from 1994 to 2023.

nodes.label: Vincent Goossaert
nodes.summary: Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He worked at the CNRS (~1998–2012) before becoming Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

nodes.label: Zhe Ji
nodes.summary: Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and served as an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).

nodes.label: Benjamin A. Elman
variants: ベンジャミン・エルマン
ベンジャミン・A・エルマン
nodes.image: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) at the lecture 'The Role of Shanghai in Building Modern Science in China in the 19th Century'.png
nodes.jawiki: ベンジャミン・エルマン
nodes.summary: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a Sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He taught at UCLA (1986–2002) and became Director of the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton (2002).

nodes.label: William M. Bodiford
variants: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Bodiford studied at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale (PhD under Stanley Weinstein). He taught at Davidson and Iowa before serving as professor at UCLA (~1992–2021; emeritus ~2021).

nodes.label: Vasudha Narayanan
nodes.summary: Vasudha Narayanan (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology with degrees from Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She served as Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982) and was president of the American Academy of Religion.

nodes.label: Sumit Ganguly
nodes.summary: Sumit Ganguly works in Indology. He held the Rabindranath Tagore Chair and directed the India Studies Program at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus (attested 2026), and is a Senior Fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mark Juergensmeyer
nodes.summary: Mark Juergensmeyer (born 1940) studied at Illinois, Union Theological Seminary, Columbia, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1974). A religious studies and Indology scholar, he held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2017).

nodes.label: Friederike Assandri
nodes.summary: Friederike Assandri works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Heidelberg University under Rudolf G. Wagner, Günther Debon, and Günther-Dietz Sontheimer (PhD attested 2002), and held a post there attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Tufts University
variants: Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine

nodes.label: Karen Nelson Villanueva
nodes.summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar in religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teacher Geshe Ngawang Dakpa.

nodes.label: Stefan Larsson
nodes.summary: Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, also studying under David Germano, and was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Marta Sernesi
nodes.summary: Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007 and was attested as a visiting professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Shayne Clarke
nodes.summary: Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later holding posts at McMaster University and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Sonya S. Lee
nodes.summary: Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under Hung Wu. She taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004) and held posts at Stanford and USC (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Hung Wu
nodes.summary: Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard University. He taught at Harvard before joining the University of Chicago in 1994, with appointments also at NYU, Oxford, and the Smart Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Jerome Silbergeld
nodes.summary: Jerome Silbergeld is a sinologist and art historian who completed his BA and PhD at Stanford University. He served as Chair of Art History at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Professor of Chinese Art History at Princeton (~2001–2018).

nodes.label: William L. Ames
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Ames studied at Caltech (MS) and the University of Washington (PhD) under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University (librarian, 2006).

nodes.id: I:University of North Carolina at Charlotte
nodes.label: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
variants: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

nodes.label: Richard A. Hutch
nodes.summary: Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2011).

nodes.label: Southern Illinois University Carbondale
variants: Morris Library, Southern Illinois University at Carbondale

nodes.label: William R. LaFleur
variants: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.summary: A Japanologist and Buddhist studies scholar, LaFleur studied at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago (PhD 1973). He held posts at Princeton, UCLA, UC Berkeley, and served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

nodes.label: Sibaraj Chetry
nodes.summary: Sibaraj Chetry works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and several teachers, and served as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Huiwen Zhuang
nodes.summary: Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar. Zhuang earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher
nodes.summary: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an art historian and Indologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota, where she also served as an assistant professor from circa 1984 to 2021.

nodes.label: Aaron P. Proffitt
nodes.summary: Aaron P. Proffitt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback and became an assistant professor of Japanese Studies at the University at Albany, SUNY, around 2015.

nodes.label: Valdo H. Viglielmo
variants: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.summary: Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. Educated at Pennsylvania, Harvard, Tokyo, Gakushuin, and Meiji Gakuin, he taught at Meiji Gakuin, Harvard, and Princeton before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

nodes.label: Dan Smyer Yü
nodes.summary: Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

nodes.label: University of California, Davis
variants: カリフォルニア大学デービス校

nodes.label: David L. McMahan
nodes.summary: David L. McMahan specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at UCSB and the University of Vermont, he served at Franklin & Marshall College as assistant professor (attested 2002) and professor of religious studies (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Hugh Gray
nodes.summary: Hugh Gray was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he served as a lecturer at SOAS University of London and the University of London from circa 1964 to 1982.

nodes.label: Drolma
nodes.summary: Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Oslo (attested 2008), completing an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik.

nodes.label: Hanna Havnevik
variants: ハンナ・ハヴネヴィク
nodes.summary: Hanna Havnevik works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at the University of Oslo, serving as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

nodes.label: J. Thomas Rimer
nodes.summary: J. Thomas Rimer, a scholar of Japanese studies, was educated at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held positions at UCLA (~1965–1971), Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland (~1985–1988), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1988–2010).

nodes.label: Tomoko Masuzawa
nodes.summary: Tomoko Masuzawa is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara, and held faculty appointments at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999).

nodes.label: James Robson
nodes.image: James Robson (academic) on Filled with Meaning.png
nodes.summary: James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford University, and held faculty positions at Williams College, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University, later directing the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

nodes.label: Lori Meeks
nodes.summary: Lori Meeks specializes in Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies. Educated at Columbia University and Princeton University (PhD c. 1998–2003 under Jacqueline I. Stone), she held posts at Stanford University (c. 2003–2004) and the University of Southern California (c. 2004).

nodes.label: Masayuki Taira
nodes.summary: Masayuki Taira (born 1951) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held posts at Osaka University (~1987–2017), Kansai University (~2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University.

nodes.label: Shunsho Manabe
nodes.summary: Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (circa 1960–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, where he was a professor circa 1999–2010.

nodes.label: Shenpen Hookham
nodes.summary: Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading and earned a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido (~1981–1986), alongside training with several traditional Buddhist masters.

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche
variants: mKhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
Mkhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Zopa Tarchin, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Lama Zolpa Trinlé, later serving as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

nodes.label: Wilfred Cantwell Smith
variants: ウィルフレッド・キャントウェル・スミス
nodes.summary: Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from Princeton (-1948). He held major positions at Forman Christian College (1940–1946), McGill University (1948–1951), and Harvard University (1964–1973, 1978–1985).

nodes.label: Lama Kunga Rinpoche
nodes.description: Buddhist Lama of the Sakya school
nodes.summary: Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

nodes.label: Brian Cutillo
nodes.summary: Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.label: Sorbonne
variants: Institute de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne

nodes.label: Supree Kanjanapisarn
nodes.summary: Supree Kanjanapisarn works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Assumption University under doctoral supervisor Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Veerachart Nimanong
nodes.native: วีรชาติ นิมะนงค์

nodes.label: Kemu Jin
nodes.summary: Kemu Jin was an Indology and linguistics scholar who held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

nodes.label: Fabio Rambelli
variants: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.jawiki: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.summary: Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro across Venice, Tokyo, and Naples. He held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (from ~2009).

nodes.label: Gregory P. A. Levine
nodes.summary: Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University, and became an Associate Professor of Art History at the University of California, Berkeley (~2003).

nodes.label: Lin Heng
nodes.summary: Lin Heng is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Roger T. Ames
nodes.summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and Sinologist who earned his PhD from SOAS under D. C. Lau (1975–1978). He spent his primary career at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016) and served as Fulbright Professor at Peking University (~2016).

nodes.label: Steve Odin
nodes.summary: Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Stony Brook University under Robert Cummings Neville and David A. Dilworth. He became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1982.

nodes.label: Jason M. Wirth
nodes.image: Jason Martin Wirth (born 1963) in the video 'Everybody's Climate 2025 – Jason Wirth on Humanity in the Anthropocene'.png
nodes.summary: Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and became a professor of philosophy at Seattle University around 2005.

nodes.label: Graham Priest
variants: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.jawiki: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.summary: Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell, he held posts at the University of Melbourne (~2000–2009), University of St Andrews (~2007–2018), and CUNY Graduate Center (~2009).

nodes.label: Jan Westerhoff
nodes.summary: Jan Westerhoff (b. 1976) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Cambridge and SOAS University of London, and serves as Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Lili Zheng
nodes.summary: Lili Zheng is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Uma Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her master's at Banaras Hindu University and her doctorate at the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti (~1975–1981). She was an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

nodes.label: D. Devahuti
nodes.description: D. Devahuti, 1929-1988; taught at universities of Malaya, Queensland, and Delhi

nodes.label: Ron Garry
nodes.summary: Ron Garry works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and teacher Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Stuart Ray Sarbacker
nodes.summary: Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001, where he studied under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Usha Nilsson
nodes.summary: Usha Nilsson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She spent her career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she was a faculty member (attested 2001) and later Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia (attested 2026).

nodes.label: B. Alan Wallace
nodes.description: American author, translator, teacher, researcher, interpreter, and Buddhist practitioner
nodes.summary: B. Alan Wallace is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from Amherst College and a PhD from Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He taught at Rabten Choeling (1975–1979), UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001), and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (2003).

nodes.label: Berthe Jansen
nodes.description: Assistant Professor of Tibetan Studies at Leiden University
nodes.summary: Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk in 2010. She held posts at Heidelberg University (~2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

nodes.label: Vincent Michaël Nicolaas Breugem
nodes.summary: Vincent Michaël Nicolaas Breugem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA (1996) and PhD (2012) from Leiden University, studied at Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono universities under Lucia Dolce, and was a Leiden research fellow in 2012.

nodes.label: Tulku Thondup
nodes.summary: Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

nodes.label: David E. Cooper
nodes.summary: David E. Cooper studied at St Edmund Hall and lectured in philosophy at Oxford (1967). He was Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008) and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

nodes.label: Purushottama Bilimoria
nodes.summary: Purushottama Bilimoria, a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed a PhD at La Trobe University. He has held appointments at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, Stony Brook, Columbia, and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Simon P. James
nodes.summary: Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point
variants: University of Wisconsin at Stevens Point

nodes.label: Latika Lahiri
nodes.summary: Latika Lahiri is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 as an Indian Government scholar and held a post at the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Tan Chung
nodes.summary: Tan Chung (1929–2024), a scholar of Sinology and history, earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He taught at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and chaired Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

nodes.label: Michael Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

nodes.label: Sonam Chhoki
nodes.summary: Sonam Chhoki works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Tibetology. She earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

nodes.label: Thierry Mathou
nodes.summary: Thierry Mathou (1963–) is a political scientist and Tibetology scholar. Educated at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, he held posts at the National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) as an Associated Political Scientist.

nodes.label: Françoise Pommaret
variants: フランソワーズ・ポマレ
nodes.summary: Françoise Pommaret is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at INALCO and the University of Paris. Her career includes lecturing at INALCO and positions at the CNRS (~1993, 2002) and the Royal University of Bhutan (~2005).

nodes.label: Karma Ura
nodes.summary: Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

nodes.label: Ronald E. Purser
nodes.summary: Ronald E. Purser (b. 1956) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

nodes.label: San Francisco State University
variants: School of Business der San Francisco State University
サンフランシスコ州立大学

nodes.label: David R. Loy
nodes.summary: David R. Loy is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Carleton, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, he taught at Singapore (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: David Forbes
nodes.summary: David Forbes held academic posts at Brooklyn College as faculty and at the Graduate Center, CUNY, as affiliate faculty, both attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Pamela D. Winfield
nodes.summary: Pamela D. Winfield is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She was affiliated with Temple University in 2001 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Paula Arai
nodes.summary: Paula Arai works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Waseda, Kalamazoo, and Harvard under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith, she has held posts at Vanderbilt (1994–2002), LSU, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

nodes.label: Patricia Fister
variants: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.jawiki: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.summary: Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas. She held positions at the Spencer Museum of Art, University of Kansas, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Michaela Mross
nodes.summary: Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich (2014). She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and taught at the University of Göttingen and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Diane Elizabeth Riggs
nodes.summary: Diane Elizabeth Riggs is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College (attested 2010), and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Daniel Timothy Aitken
nodes.summary: Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under teachers Parimal G. Patil, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

nodes.label: University of Tasmania
variants: Centre for Applied Philosophy and Ethics

nodes.label: Chan Ju Mun
nodes.summary: Chan Ju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda. He also studied at the University of Tokyo and with John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Valerie Hansen
nodes.summary: Valerie Hansen (born 1958) is a historian and sinologist who studied under Victor H. Mair. She taught at East China Normal University (2005) and held posts at Yale University, including Professor of History attested between 1993 and 2018.

nodes.label: Yifa
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist nun, scholar and writer
nodes.summary: Yifa (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at University of the West, Harvard University, and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.

nodes.label: Reginald A. Ray
nodes.summary: Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under mentors including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University, attested between 2001 and 2006.

nodes.label: Dainin Katagiri
nodes.summary: Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, and under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Thích Nhất Hạnh
variants: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.summary: Thích Nhất Hạnh (1926–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Saigon, Columbia, and Princeton universities. He held academic posts at Columbia, Princeton, Van Hanh, and Cornell universities, and founded several Buddhist institutions.

nodes.label: Shōdō Harada
nodes.summary: Shōdō Harada is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Shofuku-ji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982), whom he succeeded, became Abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982, and founded the Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

nodes.label: John Daido Loori
nodes.image: Daido Roshi in the Buddha Hall.jpeg
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Loori studied at Rutgers and under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Soen Nakagawa. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from ~1980 to 2009.

nodes.label: Dagfinn Føllesdal
variants: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
ダグフィン・フォレスダール
nodes.jawiki: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
nodes.summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine. In philosophy and linguistics, he taught at Harvard, became Professor Emeritus at the University of Oslo, and held an endowed chair at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Jiang Wu
nodes.summary: Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Harvard University (attested 2002) under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello, he became a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).

nodes.label: Yonsei University
variants: Institute of East and West Studies at Yonsei University

nodes.label: Gregory Adam Scott
nodes.summary: Gregory Adam Scott is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history who studied at Columbia University. His posts include Dr at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026) and Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Thierry Meynard
nodes.summary: Thierry Meynard (1963–) is a philosopher and sinologist. He earned his PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003), became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006), and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

nodes.id: I:The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
nodes.label: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
variants: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Scott Pacey
nodes.summary: Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the Australian National University. He has held posts at ANU, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the University of Manchester.

nodes.label: Ken McLeod
nodes.summary: Ken McLeod is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology specialist who earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia and trained under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche. He was resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling and founded Unfettered Mind.

nodes.label: Kalu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied at Palpung Monastery under Drupon Norbu Dondrup, served there as Vajra Master (circa 1943–1955), became abbot of Jangchub Choeling Monastery in 1957, and founded Samdrup Thargye Ling.

nodes.label: Stephen H. Phillips
nodes.summary: Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held positions in philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, attested as professor in 1999 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Tomy Augustine
nodes.summary: Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned a master's at the University of Madras studying under C. S. Sundaram, and a PhD from Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Michela Clemente
nodes.summary: Michela Clemente specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015) as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny
nodes.description: Polish bibliologist, paper historian, conservator of monuments.
nodes.summary: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University. She held affiliations with Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

nodes.label: Field Museum of Natural History
variants: フィールド自然史博物館

nodes.label: Thomas Cleary
nodes.summary: Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jonathan Christopher Cleary
nodes.summary: Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Kazuaki Tanahashi
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Tanahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

nodes.label: Mary Clabaugh Wright
nodes.summary: Mary Clabaugh Wright was a Sinologist and historian educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1951). She served as curator of Stanford's China collection (1947) and later became an associate professor (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale.

nodes.label: Torkel Brekke
nodes.summary: Torkel Brekke studied at the University of Oslo (MPhil ~1991–1995) and the University of Oxford (PhD 1996–1999 under Richard Gombrich). Working in religious studies, Indology, and history, he held posts at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

nodes.label: Kenryu T. Tsuji
nodes.summary: Kenryu T. Tsuji worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and also studied at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Gerd J. R. Mevissen
nodes.summary: Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who served as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Free University of Berlin, with affiliations attested in 2017 and 2026.

nodes.label: University of California, Irvine
variants: University of California, Irvine Seminar in Experimental Critical Theory
カリフォルニア大学アーバイン校

nodes.label: Edward S. Casey
nodes.summary: Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and Paris under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale, and Stony Brook University, where he was dean of philosophy, and served as president of the APA.

nodes.label: Rebecca Redwood French
nodes.summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Washington and Yale University. She held legal academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Rafal Stepien
nodes.summary: Rafal Stepien specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and Bernard Faure, and held posts at Wadham College and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Chun-fang Yu
nodes.summary: Chun-fang Yu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Columbia University, as well as under traditional teachers Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (attested 2000) and Columbia University (professor, attested 2007–2015; emerita attested 2026).

nodes.label: École Normale Supérieure
variants: Husserl Archives at the École normale supérieure (ENS/CNRS)

nodes.label: University of Sussex
variants: University of Sussex's School of African & Asian Studies

nodes.label: Philippe Turenne
nodes.summary: Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD from McGill University, supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori alongside several other teachers.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Komarovski
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Komarovski studied at Tibetan monastic institutes under teachers including Lobsang Gyatso, and at the University of Virginia. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University and a post at University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011-2015).

nodes.label: Peter Schwieger
nodes.summary: Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who earned his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Bonn under Dieter Schuh. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy, Humboldt University of Berlin, and was appointed to Bonn's chair of Tibetology in 2001.

nodes.label: Dieter Schuh
nodes.summary: Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christian Wittern
nodes.summary: Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational humanities, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2011) and Kyoto University, where he was attested as professor in 1993 and affiliated in 2008.

nodes.label: Eliot Deutsch
nodes.summary: Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Thittila
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Thittila worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University, later serving as a librarian at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the Buddhist Society, and as a lecturer at the University of Yangon.

nodes.label: Reiho Masunaga
nodes.summary: Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He was attested as a teacher at Komazawa University in 1956.

nodes.label: Kamala Tiyavanich
nodes.summary: Kamala Tiyavanich is a historian of Buddhism who studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg. She also held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at Cornell from 1993 to 1994.

nodes.label: David K. Wyatt
variants: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.jawiki: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.summary: David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell (PhD ~1966). He held posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell (1969–2002), where he chaired the history department, later serving as AAS president (1993).

nodes.label: Richard Polenberg
nodes.summary: Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (PhD). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1974–1975).

nodes.label: Trung Huynh
nodes.summary: Trung Huynh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long, attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Lama Jampa Thaye
nodes.summary: Lama Jampa Thaye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester (~1986–1990) and studied under several traditional teachers, later joining the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

nodes.label: Susan Whitfield
nodes.summary: Susan Whitfield, working in Central Asian studies, history, and sinology, completed her PhD at SOAS (~1990–1995). She directed the British Library's International Dunhuang Project (~1994–2017) and held posts at UCL (~2017) and the Sainsbury Institute (~2020).

nodes.label: Imre Galambos
nodes.description: Scholar of medieval Chinese and Tangut manuscripts
nodes.summary: Imre Galambos is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai University, and UC Berkeley (PhD), he held posts at the British Library, the University of Cambridge (2012–2023), and Zhejiang University (~2023).

nodes.label: Joseph Zalman Margolis
nodes.summary: Joseph Zalman Margolis was a philosopher who earned an M.A. from Columbia University by 1950. He taught Youru Wang and held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University in 1991.

nodes.label: Sandra A. Wawrytko
nodes.summary: Sandra A. Wawrytko specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She has held posts at San Diego State University, serving as Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Megan Bryson
nodes.summary: Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Rachelle M. Scott
nodes.summary: Rachelle M. Scott specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee, attested between 2009 and 2017.
