nodes.label: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
variants: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Eastern Asiatic Art

nodes.label: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
variants: Oriental Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Oriental Collection, Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Institut für Altaische Forschungen an der Ungarischen Akademie der Wissenschaften

nodes.label: Zsóka Gelle
nodes.description: Hungarian Tibetologist, translator, writer, filmmaker and guide
nodes.summary: Zsóka Gelle (b. 1967) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna, and held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College and Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016).

nodes.label: Benjamin Bogin
nodes.summary: Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr.

nodes.label: John J. Holder
nodes.summary: John J. Holder is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006–2018).

nodes.label: Eric Huntington
nodes.summary: Eric Huntington is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

nodes.label: Dina Bangdel
nodes.summary: Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held academic posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Virginia Commonwealth University
variants: Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine

nodes.label: Andy Rotman
nodes.summary: Andy Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, later holding posts at Smith College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
variants: ジャムヤン・キェンツェ・ワンポ
nodes.summary: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Minling Khenchen Rigdzin Zangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and taught Jamgön Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamgön Kongtrul, and others.

nodes.label: Peter Alan Roberts
nodes.summary: Peter Alan Roberts is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche
nodes.image: Thrangu Rinpoche on 24 May 2016 face detail, from- 17th Karmapa performs Long Life Offering to Kenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche studied under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1960), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).

nodes.label: Somphong Santacitto
nodes.summary: Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master's Degree in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Watchara Ngamchitcharoen
nodes.native: วัชระ งามจิตรเจริญ

nodes.id: I:Centre national de la recherche scientifique
nodes.label: Centre national de la recherche scientifique
variants: Center National de la recherche scientifique

nodes.label: Brian D. Ruppert
nodes.summary: Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under mentor Willis Stoesz (~1982–1986). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018).

nodes.label: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani
nodes.summary: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. She pursued graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of Perry Link.

nodes.label: Perry Link
nodes.summary: Perry Link (b. 1944) is a sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and UC Riverside (~2008) as Chancellorial Chair Professor.

nodes.label: James Ishmael Ford
nodes.summary: James Ishmael Ford works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sonoma State University and the Pacific School of Religion (~1988–1991), and trained under Mel Weitsman, Hōun Jiyu-Kennett (~1970–1975), and John Tarrant.

nodes.label: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
nodes.summary: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Sōji-ji. She was head priest at Unpukuji, founded Shasta Abbey in 1969, and served as its abbess until 1996.

nodes.label: Jonathan C. Gold
nodes.summary: Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and tibetology. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Michael Eido Luetchford
nodes.summary: Michael Eido Luetchford is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford, studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima, and founded Windbell Publications.

nodes.label: Gudo Wafu Nishijima
nodes.summary: Gudo Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who earned a law degree at the University of Tokyo and studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at the Tokyo University Buddhist Association and Toho Gakuin.

nodes.label: Noranit Setabutr
nodes.native: นรนิติ เศรษฐบุตร

nodes.label: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dudjom Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

nodes.label: Anna Balikci-Denjongpa
nodes.summary: Anna Balikci-Denjongpa works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS under Lionel Caplan, also studying with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku, and became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in 2002.

nodes.label: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson
nodes.summary: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and studied with traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.

nodes.label: Alexander Macmillan
nodes.summary: Alexander Macmillan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Morrison
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and Sinology, having completed her doctorate under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She held an instructor post at Amherst College (1998–1999) and an appointment at Middlebury College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chögyam Trungpa
variants: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
チョギャム トゥルンパ
チューギャム・ドゥンパ
nodes.image: Trungpa from Khenpo gangshar2 cropped image.jpg
nodes.jawiki: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
nodes.summary: Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies figure who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, Shechen Kongtrul, and at Oxford. He was a spiritual advisor at Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Naropa University (1973).

nodes.label: Aruna Haldar
nodes.summary: Aruna Haldar was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kedar Nath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and taught at Patna University.

nodes.label: Girindrasekhar Bose
nodes.summary: Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency College, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and was president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

nodes.label: Joachim Gentz
nodes.summary: Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Junior Professor at the University of Göttingen and Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Perry Schmidt-Leukel
nodes.summary: Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) studied at the University of Munich (~1974–1996), where he also held a post (~1988–1998). He served as professor at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

nodes.label: Adam Yuet Chau
nodes.summary: Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Williams College and Stanford University (PhD 2001). After a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard, he served as lecturer (attested 2011–2015) and later professor (attested 2026) at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Philip Clart
nodes.description: German Sinologist, Professor of Chinese Studies at Leipzig University, Germany
nodes.summary: Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from ca. 1990 to 1996 and was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at Leipzig University in ca. 2008.

nodes.label: Michael Stanley-Baker
nodes.summary: Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA under Stephen R. Bokenkamp at Indiana University Bloomington. He has held posts at the MPIWG, Leipzig University, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.

nodes.label: Harold Stewart
nodes.summary: Harold Stewart (1916–1995) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney (circa 1939–1941).

nodes.label: David Tracy
nodes.summary: David Tracy is a religious studies scholar and philosopher. Educated at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, he lectured at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and was a professor at the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

nodes.label: Douglas L. Berger
nodes.summary: Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He has held positions at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007–2014) and Leiden University (attested 2026), and served as General Editor for Dimensions of Asian Spirituality (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Peter Schwabland
nodes.summary: Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Michael L. Walter
nodes.summary: Michael L. Walter is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He served as a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute and as a cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Akimichi Eda
nodes.summary: Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.

nodes.label: Lita Peipina
nodes.summary: Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008), where she was supervised by Jens Braarvig in 2003.

nodes.label: Stephen Prothero
nodes.summary: Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale University and Harvard University under William R. Hutchison. Around 1996, he joined Boston University, where he became C. Allyn and Elizabeth V. Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America.

nodes.label: Duncan Ryūken Williams
nodes.summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later holding posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Tanaka (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Stanford, Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He held faculty posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University, and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

nodes.label: Kōshō Uchiyama
nodes.summary: Kōshō Uchiyama studied Western philosophy at Waseda University and trained under Kodo Sawaki. A scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary and served as abbot of Antai-ji from 1965 to 1975.

nodes.label: Kodo Sawaki
nodes.summary: Kodo Sawaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Koho Sawada, Sotan Oka, and Join Saeki at institutions including Horyuji Kangakuin. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).

nodes.label: Sotan Oka
nodes.summary: Sotan Oka was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

nodes.label: Ian Kishizawa
nodes.summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Yasutani.

nodes.label: See Mui Yian
nodes.summary: See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Warren Lee Todd
nodes.summary: Warren Lee Todd works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and the traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Alison Denton Jones
nodes.summary: Alison Denton Jones works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, as well as instructors Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

nodes.label: Martin King Whyte
nodes.summary: Martin King Whyte (b. 1942) is a sociologist of China. Educated at Cornell and Harvard (PhD 1971), he held faculty appointments at the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University (from 2000).

nodes.label: Allan H. Barr
nodes.summary: Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Margaret H. Dornish
nodes.summary: Margaret H. Dornish specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Daniela Berti
nodes.summary: Daniela Berti is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena. She was a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya (attested 2004).

nodes.id: I:Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
nodes.label: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
variants: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, Paris

nodes.label: Gilles Tarabout
nodes.summary: Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. His posts include senior fellow at the CNRS and director of the Indo-French exchange program at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme (both attested 2004).

nodes.id: I:Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
nodes.label: Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
variants: Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris

nodes.label: Cortland Dahl
nodes.summary: Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and was mentored by Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

nodes.label: Khunu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khunu Rinpoche (1894–1977) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das and Dev Narayan Tripathi, and he taught at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa.

nodes.label: Myosei Tatsuguchi
nodes.summary: Myosei Tatsuguchi (born 1932) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Robert Charles Zaehner
nodes.image: Internationaal Theologisch Congres toekomst van de religie, religie van de toeko, Bestanddeelnr 925-4729.jpg
nodes.description: British spy and academic on Eastern religions (1913–1974)
nodes.summary: Robert Charles Zaehner worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, he worked with the SIS (~1943–1952) and served as Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics (1952).

nodes.label: Stephen Harris
nodes.summary: Stephen Harris is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of New Mexico in 2014 and became a University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Channa Li
nodes.summary: Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015). Li is attested in 2026 as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: James A. Benn
nodes.summary: James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

nodes.label: Kyoko Tokuno
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Kyoko Tokuno taught Douglas Ober and held academic posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

nodes.label: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje
variants: ドゥジョム・ジグドラル・イェシェ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein and Alexander Berzin.

nodes.label: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley
nodes.summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied under A. K. Warder and F. E. L. Priestley. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Julia Ching
nodes.summary: Julia Ching studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University (PhD ~1968-1971). Active in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, she became a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

nodes.label: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby
nodes.summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, and held posts at McGill (1960-1964), Yale (1966-1971), and the University of Toronto and Trinity College (1971-1999).

nodes.label: Jacob Holubeck
nodes.summary: Jacob Holubeck works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Eric Stephen Goodell
nodes.summary: Eric Stephen Goodell specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned master's degrees from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Kristin Johnston Largen
nodes.summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

nodes.label: Brandon Dotson
nodes.summary: Brandon Dotson (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and a habilitation at Munich (~2010–2013), holding posts at SOAS (~2006–2010) and the University of Munich (~2010–2017).

nodes.label: Marcus Bingenheimer
nodes.summary: Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Nagoya University under Yasuhisa Matsumura and at the University of Würzburg, later holding posts at Chung-Hwa Institute, Dharma Drum institutions, and Temple University (2012–2015).

nodes.label: Jongmyung Kim
nodes.summary: Jongmyung Kim studied at Yonsei, Seoul National University, and UCLA (under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). Focusing on Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies, he served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

nodes.label: Roderick Whitfield
nodes.summary: Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was an emeritus professor (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Central Academy of Fine Arts
variants: Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing
Chongqing National College of Fine Arts
国立北平芸術専科学校

nodes.label: Eugene Y. Wang
nodes.summary: Eugene Y. Wang studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. Specializing in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, he held posts at the University of Chicago and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Kristofer Schipper
nodes.summary: Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied in Paris and at Academia Sinica. He held appointments at EFEO, EPHE, CNRS, Collège de France, and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Erik Haarh
nodes.summary: Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a Tibetologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He held positions at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and served as a department head and theology professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

nodes.label: Helen Josephine Baroni
nodes.summary: Helen Josephine Baroni is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Paul B. Watt at Columbia University and held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Shou-chien Shih
nodes.summary: Shou-chien Shih (born 1951) works in sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University from circa 1987 to 2004 and was director of the National Palace Museum from circa 2004 to 2006.

nodes.label: Alice Y. Tseng
nodes.summary: Alice Y. Tseng, a scholar of Japanology and history and archaeology, studied as a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang. She is attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

nodes.label: Gesellschaft für Mahāyāna-Buddhismus
variants: an active society for the study of Mahāyāna
society for the study of Mahāyāna

nodes.label: Brian J. Nichols
nodes.summary: Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and completed his PhD at Rice University under Anne C. Klein (attested 2011).

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Program for Chinese language studies at Tsinghua University
Inter-University Board of Chinese Language Studies

nodes.label: Tansen Sen
nodes.summary: Tansen Sen works in history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later teaching at Baruch College (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Takeshi Umehara
nodes.summary: Takeshi Umehara studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi and Michitaro Tanaka. Active in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and directed the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

nodes.label: Derge Gonchen
variants: sDe dge dbon stod slob grwa at sDe dge dgon chen Monastery

nodes.label: Kuse Serjong Shedra
variants: sDe dge Ku se gSer ljongs bshad grwa

nodes.label: Dragyab Lodrö
variants: mKhan Rinpoche Brag gyab Blos gros

nodes.label: Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro (1893–1959) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo.

nodes.label: Sarah Aoife Richardson
nodes.summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (completed by 2016) under doctoral supervisor Jenny Purtle and studied with several scholars, including John C. and Susan L. Huntington.

nodes.label: Julia F. Andrews
nodes.summary: Working in Sinology and art history/archaeology, Julia F. Andrews studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley. She joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

nodes.label: Frank J. Hoffman
nodes.summary: Frank J. Hoffman works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Stewart R. Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and K. N. Upadhyaya.

nodes.label: Trent Walker
nodes.summary: Trent Walker is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

nodes.label: Olivier de Bernon
nodes.summary: Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He has held a post as professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Pa-Auk Sayadaw
nodes.native: ဖားအောက်တောရဆရာတော်

nodes.label: Jan Chozen Bays
nodes.summary: Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Swarthmore College, UC San Diego, and under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Shōdō Harada. She taught at Zen Community of Oregon and became abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.

nodes.label: Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi
nodes.summary: Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and San Francisco State University under teachers including Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Yasutani. A priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956), he founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Neal Donner
nodes.summary: Neal Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Wenjie Qin
nodes.summary: Wenjie Qin is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu.

nodes.label: Wei-ming Tu
nodes.summary: Wei-ming Tu (1940–) is a philosopher and sinologist. He studied at Tunghai University and Harvard (PhD ~1962–1968), and held positions at Princeton, UC Berkeley, the East-West Center, Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008), Harvard University (1999–2010), and Peking University (~2010).

nodes.label: Bing Chen
nodes.summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He has held positions as Professor at Sichuan University (from ~1987) and at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Yun-hua Jan
nodes.summary: Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Jan was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

nodes.label: Lhakpa Tsering
nodes.summary: Lhakpa Tsering, working in Tibetology and linguistics, has served as a professor at Tibet University and an assistant professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Stephanie Roemer
nodes.summary: Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

nodes.label: Eberhard Sandschneider
nodes.summary: Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who completed his education and PhD at Saarland University (~1976–1986). He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

nodes.label: German Council on Foreign Relations
variants: Forschungsinstitut der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik

nodes.label: Naoki Nabeshima
nodes.summary: Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2004 as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, an institution he founded.

nodes.label: David Matsumoto
nodes.summary: David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and is President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jing-shen Tao
nodes.summary: Jing-shen Tao is a sinologist and historian. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. ~1964–1967), and he served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).

nodes.label: Christian Coseru
nodes.description: American philosopher and scholar of Buddhist philosophy
nodes.summary: Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University, and held posts including Associate Professor at the College of Charleston and Numata Visiting Professor at UC Berkeley (~2022).

nodes.label: C. W. Huntington, Jr.
nodes.summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).

nodes.label: Kevin Buckelew
nodes.summary: Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, with doctoral supervision by Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

nodes.label: Chao-heng Liao
nodes.summary: Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He has been affiliated with Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Valeria Gazizova
nodes.summary: Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis under the supervision of Per Kværne, and was also taught by Hanna Havnevik.

nodes.label: Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche (born 1940) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche, he directed Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966), worked at the University of Bonn (1966), and founded Tibet House Germany (2005).

nodes.label: Pema Tsering
nodes.summary: Pema Tsering, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied under Shenphen Nangwa, taught Ruth Gamble, and held a post at the University of Bonn (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Martin Brauen
nodes.summary: Martin Brauen (b. 1948) specializes in Tibetology, art history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Delhi and Zurich (doctoral degree), he served as curator and department head at the University of Zurich's Ethnographic Museum (from 1975) and chief curator at the Rubin Museum (2008–2012).

nodes.label: Michael Jay Sweet
nodes.summary: Michael Jay Sweet (d. 2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD under Geshe Lhundub Sopa at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was attested as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry in 1996 and 2006.

nodes.label: Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche
variants: Thub bstan bzod pa rin po che
nodes.image: Kyabje Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche December 2008 Kopan monastery Nepal.jpg
nodes.summary: Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dungkar Monastery and under numerous teachers, founded Kopan Monastery and the FPMT, and served as spiritual director of the FPMT from 1984.

nodes.label: John Ross Carter
nodes.summary: John Ross Carter specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under Wilfred Cantwell Smith (~1965–1972), later spending his career as a professor at Colgate University (~1972–2006).

nodes.label: Amita Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Amita Chatterjee (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She held a post as professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, where she is attested in 1999 and 2009.

nodes.label: Catholic University of America
variants: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)

nodes.label: Knut A. Jacobsen
nodes.summary: Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He received his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1989–1994) and served as a professor at the University of Bergen (1996) and the University of Oslo (~1996–1999).

nodes.label: John M. Koller
nodes.summary: John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, and George T. Artola, and served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

nodes.label: Daya Krishna
nodes.summary: Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1960–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Shigenori Nagatomo
nodes.summary: Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology who served as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999, 2017).

nodes.id: I:Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Philosophy, Academy of Sciences USSR

nodes.label: Michiko Yusa
nodes.summary: Michiko Yusa works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar (~1979–1983) and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2020).

nodes.label: Diego Loukota
nodes.summary: Diego Loukota is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

nodes.label: Susan Andrews
nodes.summary: Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu.

nodes.label: Michael Como
nodes.summary: Michael Como is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang, and is the Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Brian Kensho Nagata
nodes.summary: Brian Kensho Nagata works in Buddhist studies. He has served as Director of BDK America (attested 2004, 2013), President of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research, and Director at Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Karma Thinley Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling (1973) and Tekchen Lekshay Ling (1988), and served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School (~1962) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling (~1976).

nodes.label: Gendun Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Gendun Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling and served as its abbot and retreat master from circa 1977 to 1997.

nodes.label: Bokar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989). He served at Bokar Monastery (~1984–2004) and taught Shenpen Hookham, Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö.

nodes.label: Michael M. Broido
nodes.summary: Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held a post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Geshe Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, later teaching at Kopan Monastery (~1992–1994) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (from 1994).

nodes.label: Qiwen Xiao
nodes.summary: Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi in 2013.

nodes.label: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda
nodes.summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and was a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies in 2011.

nodes.id: I:Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
variants: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute for Asian Studies

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Saksena
nodes.summary: Shri Krishna Saksena (born 1897) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: East-West Center
variants: ハワイ東西センター文化・コミュニケーション研究所

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Malhotra
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1966). He founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

nodes.label: Gregory Forgues
nodes.summary: Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) under Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Pema Bhum
nodes.summary: Pema Bhum is a scholar of Tibetology. He previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and directed the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

nodes.label: Morton Klass
nodes.summary: Morton Klass was a scholar of religion and Indology who studied at Columbia University under Conrad M. Arensberg. He taught at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Margaret Mead
variants: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.jawiki: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.summary: Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, The New School, and Fordham, and founded the Institute for Intercultural Studies.

nodes.label: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヤーコプ・マリア・デ・ホロート
nodes.summary: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as a professor at Leiden University and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Xiaoting Wei
nodes.summary: Xiaoting Wei focuses on sinology and Buddhist studies. Wei earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng Mei Ku (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Jinshi Fan
nodes.summary: Jinshi Fan works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Bai Su (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and part-time professor at Lanzhou University (~2004).

nodes.label: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan
nodes.summary: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under traditional teacher A. P. Lama and under Mrinal Kanti Gangopadhyay (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Bhajagovinda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Bhajagovinda Ghosh was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1994, he served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Martin Collcutt
nodes.jawiki: マーティン・コルカット
nodes.summary: Martin Collcutt (b. 1939) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975), he taught at Yokohama National and Tokyo universities before serving as professor and East Asian Studies director at Princeton (1975–2015).

nodes.label: Luangpor Teean Jittasubho
nodes.native: หลวงพ่อเทียน จิตฺตสุโภ

nodes.label: Andrew Quintman
nodes.summary: Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He has served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

nodes.label: Masaharu Imai
nodes.summary: Masaharu Imai studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1970–1977), working in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He was an associate professor at Ibaraki University (1977) and later became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba (2006).

nodes.label: Juhn Y. Ahn
nodes.summary: Juhn Y. Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He served as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan, attested in 2019.

nodes.id: P:Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
Lobsang Yongdan
nodes.summary: Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and University of Bonn.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
variants: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin

nodes.label: Fernando Jose Benetti
nodes.summary: Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, where his doctoral supervisor was Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

nodes.label: William H. Nienhauser, Jr.
nodes.summary: William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Bonn under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He held posts at Indiana University (~1972-1973) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1983).

nodes.label: Kristina Myrvold
nodes.summary: Kristina Myrvold is an Indology and religious studies scholar who was a Ph.D. candidate and editor at Lund University. By 2014, she held a post as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University.

nodes.label: Olle Qvarnström
nodes.summary: Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen, supervised by Tord Olsson and taught by Karl Harrington Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund University.

nodes.label: Gurinder Singh Mann
nodes.summary: Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He taught religion at Columbia from 1988 to 1999 and held the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair at UC Santa Barbara from 1999 to 2015.

nodes.label: University of Bergen
variants: Department of Social Anthropology, University of Bergen

nodes.label: Anne Hardgrove
nodes.summary: Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1991–1999), and joined the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

nodes.id: I:University of Texas at San Antonio
nodes.label: University of Texas at San Antonio
variants: University of Texas at San Antonio

nodes.label: Paul Copp
nodes.summary: Paul Copp is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser. He held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago, attested as Associate Professor in 2026.

nodes.label: Ching-mao Cheng
nodes.summary: Ching-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a Sinologist and Japanologist who earned his PhD from Princeton (circa 1965–1970). He taught at UC Berkeley, chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst (circa 1976–1996), and was Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University.

nodes.label: Donald E. Gjertson
nodes.summary: Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John C. Y. Wang and Akira Takeda, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Stephen Batchelor
nodes.summary: Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied with Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He was a translator at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (1979), director of Sharpham College (~1992–2000), and core faculty at Bodhi College (~2015).

nodes.label: Mohan Wijayaratna
nodes.description: Sinhalese anthropologist and translator specializing in Buddhism

nodes.label: Kosai Fukushima
nodes.summary: Kosai Fukushima (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Paul L. Swanson. He held posts at Otani University, including Dean of Students (attested 1985) and professor (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Royall Tyler
nodes.summary: Royall Tyler is a Japanologist who earned his B.A. from Harvard and his master's and PhD from Columbia under Donald Keene (~1966–1977). He held teaching posts at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, Harvard, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).

nodes.label: Huai-Chin Nan
nodes.summary: Huai-Chin Nan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and the University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. His career included teaching at the ROC Military Academy, National Chengchi University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Chinese Culture University.

nodes.label: Chinese Culture University
variants: College of Chinese Culture Graduate School in Taipei
Institute of Chinese Culture in Taipei
中国文化大学印度研究所

nodes.label: Huynh Kim Lan
nodes.summary: Huynh Kim Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.

nodes.label: Phra Sithawatchamethi
nodes.native: พระศรีวัชรเมธี

nodes.label: Gareth Fisher
nodes.summary: Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (ended 2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Nirupam Chakma
nodes.summary: Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where he studied under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

nodes.label: Tilak Kariyawasam
nodes.summary: Tilak Kariyawasam (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Fa Qing
nodes.summary: Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary (attested 2001) under Leslie S. Kawamura, A. W. Barber, and X. Jie Yang.

nodes.label: Wei Wu
nodes.summary: Wei Wu (1949–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who founded the International Buddhist College. Attested in 2026, he serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

nodes.label: Ki-yong Rhi
nodes.summary: Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he was attested in 1983 and attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

nodes.label: Martin Willson
nodes.summary: Martin Willson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Michael Weiers
nodes.summary: Michael Weiers (1937–2025) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), where he was a professor (1972–2003), and was an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1993).

nodes.label: Geshe Jampa Tegchok
nodes.summary: Geshe Jampa Tegchok, a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar, studied at Sera Monastery. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1982), Nalanda Monastery as abbot (~1982–1993), and the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1995–2001).

nodes.label: Daniel L. Overmyer
nodes.description: Scholar of the history of Chinese popular religions
nodes.summary: Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) specialized in Sinology and religious studies, earning degrees from Westmar, Evangelical Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

nodes.label: Klaus Mylius
nodes.summary: Klaus Mylius was an Indologist who earned degrees at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University. He held positions at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig University (1970–1991), the University of Bayreuth, and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).

nodes.label: Dieter B. Kapp
nodes.summary: Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Hermann Berger at Heidelberg University. He taught at Heidelberg and served as Director of the Institut für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).

nodes.label: Peter James Gilks
nodes.summary: Peter James Gilks specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (attested 2010), alongside training under several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués
nodes.summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Cambridge by 2016 under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at Shan State Buddhist University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Di Luo
nodes.summary: Di Luo is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Southern California under the supervision of Sonya S. Lee (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Richard von Glahn
nodes.summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

nodes.label: Jeff Watt
nodes.summary: Jeff Watt specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Justin Shimeld
nodes.summary: Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where his doctoral supervisors were Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Jeff Malpas
nodes.summary: Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. His career includes posts at Murdoch University (~1992–1999) and the University of Tasmania, where he became professor in 1999.

nodes.label: Sonam Thakchoe
nodes.summary: Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD (~1999–2002) at the University of Tasmania under mentors Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, subsequently holding a post there around 2003.

nodes.label: Barry Kerzin
nodes.image: Barry Kerzin, American Professor of Medicine and Buddhist monk.gif
nodes.summary: Barry Kerzin studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Southern California (MD). Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he held posts at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and the University of Hong Kong (2014–2015, 2021–2022).

nodes.label: Chun-i Tang
nodes.image: Tang Chun-i - New Asia College and Yale-China Association Cooperation 1954 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and National Central University under Shuming Liang, Shili Xiong, and Thomé H. Fang. He held posts at National Central University (1944–1949), the New Asia Institute (~1953–1978), and CUHK (~1963–1974).

nodes.label: Shili Xiong
nodes.summary: Shili Xiong (1885–1968) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology, studying under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Boone University (~1919–1920), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1944–1946).

nodes.label: Mou Zongsan
nodes.summary: Mou Zongsan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He held posts at National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, the University of Hong Kong, and New Asia College.

nodes.label: Philip Whalen
nodes.summary: Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984), resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

nodes.label: Karen L. Brock
nodes.summary: Karen L. Brock works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Princeton University and held assistant professorships in Japanese art at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1988) and the University of Michigan (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Noboru Miyata
nodes.summary: Noboru Miyata was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history who studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba. He held professorships at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1970–1979), Tsukuba (~1979–1999), and Kanagawa University (~1999–2000).

nodes.label: Oleg Grabar
nodes.summary: Oleg Grabar was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, and held posts at the Albright Institute (1953), University of Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and IAS (1990–1998).

nodes.label: Jörg Heimbel
nodes.summary: Jörg Heimbel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg (completed 2014) and studying at Tibet University, he held posts at Hamburg, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Elizabeth English
nodes.summary: Elizabeth English is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 1999 under the doctoral supervision of Alexis Sanderson, having also studied under Harunaga Isaacson.

nodes.label: Sung Bae Park
nodes.summary: Sung Bae Park (1934–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctorate under Lewis R. Lancaster. He taught at Dongguk University and became Professor Emeritus at Stony Brook University, which he joined in 1977.

nodes.label: Alfred Bloom
variants: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.summary: Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held faculty posts at the University of Oregon, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: University at Albany, SUNY

University at Albany, State University of New York

nodes.label: Ruben L. F. Habito
nodes.summary: Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, later holding posts at Sophia (~1978–1989), Southern Methodist University (1989), and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Yutai Ikeda
nodes.summary: Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he served as emeritus professor (~1970–2005).

nodes.label: Kenshi Kusano
nodes.summary: Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1975 and later served as a professor there from circa 1996 to 2018.

nodes.label: Ryoen Minamoto
nodes.summary: Ryoen Minamoto (1920–2020) specialized in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1942–1952). He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1964–1972), Tohoku University (Emeritus Professor ~1984), and International Christian University (~1984–1992).

nodes.label: Shunsho Terakawa
nodes.summary: Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post at Otani University from circa 1964 to 2000, where he became emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Thomas Yūhō Kirchner
nodes.summary: Thomas Yūhō Kirchner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held a professorship at Hanazono University (attested 2001) and a post at the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Michael Jerryson
nodes.summary: Michael Jerryson (1974–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and earned his PhD under Mark Juergensmeyer at UC Santa Barbara, later holding professorial posts at Eckerd College and Youngstown State University.

nodes.label: Daniel W. Kent
nodes.summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia. He held instructor positions at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Brian Daizen Victoria
variants: ブライアン・アンドレー・ヴィクトリア
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ヴィクトリア
nodes.summary: Brian Daizen Victoria works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities and Eihei-ji, he held posts at Auckland, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Adelaide (~2004–2015), Antioch (2005–2013), and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (2013).

nodes.label: Nebraska Wesleyan University
variants: ネブラスカ・ウェズリアン大学

nodes.label: Xue Yu
nodes.summary: Xue Yu works in Buddhist and religious studies. Yu held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nancy S. Steinhardt
nodes.image: Nancy Steinhardt Keynote for Whitworth University Library.jpg
nodes.summary: Nancy S. Steinhardt is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She became a professor of East Asian art at the University of Pennsylvania and curator of Chinese art at the Penn Museum circa 1982.

nodes.label: Baruch College
variants: Baruch College, City University of New York

nodes.label: Franz-Karl Ehrhard
nodes.summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and Professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).

nodes.label: Navina Lamminger
nodes.summary: Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Stacey Van Vleet
nodes.summary: Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, sinology, and history. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and Columbia University (PhD, attested 2006) under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and held a post at Columbia (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Barstow
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and earned degrees from Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia before joining Oregon State University around 2013.

nodes.label: Takao Moriyasu
nodes.summary: Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) was a Central Asian and Iranian studies historian who studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He held faculty posts at Kanazawa University, Osaka University (1984–2012), Kindai University (2012–2015), Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Tokio Takata
nodes.summary: Tokio Takata (born 1949) is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, later holding professorships at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022).

nodes.label: Yutaka Yoshida
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yoshida (b. 1954) specializes in history, Japanology, and linguistics. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo, he taught at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018; emeritus 2018) and held posts at Kyoto University and other research centers.

nodes.label: James Burnell Robinson
nodes.summary: James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975).

nodes.label: Cuong T. Mai
nodes.summary: Cuong T. Mai specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, and served as adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Reiko Ohnuma
nodes.summary: Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and completed her PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. She held posts at Texas, Alabama, and Dartmouth.

nodes.label: Gereon Kopf
nodes.summary: Gereon Kopf, working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at Temple University (~1991–1996) and under Yasuo Yuasa. He conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan, taught at Hong Kong, and joined Luther College (~1998).

nodes.label: John C. Maraldo
nodes.summary: John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served on the faculty at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

nodes.label: Seijun Ishii
nodes.summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1986). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from approximately 2005 to 2024.

nodes.label: Stephen G. Covell
nodes.description: professor of world religions and cultures
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Covell works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone around 1995–2001 and held a post at Western Michigan University around 2003.

nodes.label: Wendi L. Adamek
nodes.summary: Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Adamek earned a PhD at Stanford University by 1998, held a post at Barnard College in 2008, and served as Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Sadajiro Sugiura
nodes.summary: Sadajiro Sugiura was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at Rikkyo, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School, he held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus in 1931–1932.

nodes.label: Bo Jiang
nodes.summary: Bo Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Soochow University
variants: School of Foreign Languages, Soochow University

nodes.label: Mary Evelyn Tucker
nodes.summary: Mary Evelyn Tucker works in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at SUNY, Sophia, Fordham, and Columbia (PhD ~1985), she held posts at Bucknell (Professor ~1989–2006), Harvard (~1995–2006), and Yale (Professor ~2006).

nodes.label: Zhiru Shi
nodes.summary: Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello and held appointments at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Donald Harper
nodes.summary: Donald Harper works in Sinology and religious studies. He taught Zhiru Shi and held posts at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryoshun Okubo
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University, Ryoshun Okubo served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there (circa 2005). He also held posts at Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007), ICPBS (attested 2026), and IIBS (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Phanindra Nath Bose
nodes.description: Bengali historian, writer and professor at Santiniketan

nodes.label: Shashibhusan Dasgupta
nodes.description: Scholar in philosophy, languages and literature, particularly Bengali literature, literary critic, author, theologian
nodes.summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned an MA and PhD and served as Lecturer from circa 1939 to 1964.

nodes.label: Dung Ngoc Duong
nodes.summary: Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel.

nodes.label: Dudjom Rinpoche
nodes.image: Dudjom Rinpoche with Prince Paljor Namgyal and Maharani Kunzang Dechen Tshomo Namgyal.jpg
nodes.summary: Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jampal Delek Nyima and others, and taught Keith Dowman, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, and numerous other students.

nodes.label: Antoine Lutz
nodes.summary: Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco J. Varela.

nodes.label: Christine Mollier
nodes.summary: Christine Mollier specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié (1989–1995), served as a CNRS researcher (1989–1995; attested 2006, 2014 as Director), and was Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jacques Giès
nodes.summary: Jacques Giès was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Beaux-Arts de Paris and Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and served as curator and president (2008–2011) at the Musée Guimet.

Dzongsar Institute of Advanced Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: James Leibold
nodes.summary: James Leibold specializes in sinology and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Southern California under Charlotte Furth, and held posts at the University of Melbourne and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Charlotte Furth
nodes.summary: Charlotte Furth was a scholar of sinology and history. She served as a professor at California State University (~1966–1989) and held a post at the University of Southern California (~1989–2008).

nodes.label: Kumbum Monastery

nodes.label: Dhivan Thomas Jones
nodes.summary: Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He has held teaching posts at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).

nodes.label: Shan Shan Zhao
nodes.summary: Shan Shan Zhao specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Zhao earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Mark Rowe
nodes.summary: Mark Rowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who has held academic posts at McMaster University, including Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: St Edmund's College, Cambridge
variants: St. Edmunds College, University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Margaret Gouin
nodes.summary: Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Thinh Canh Quang
nodes.summary: Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis R. Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

nodes.label: Noa Ronkin
nodes.summary: Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and completed a D.Phil. at Wolfson College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich in 2003. She later served as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Patricia Buckley Ebrey
nodes.summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

nodes.label: Kate Wharton
nodes.summary: Kate Wharton, a scholar of philosophy and Indology, completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008. She held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Peter Fenner
nodes.summary: Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Advised by Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, he also studied under Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and held a post at Deakin University.

nodes.label: Lindsay G. McCune
nodes.summary: Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kathleen M. Erndl, John Corrigan, and MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas.

nodes.label: Nancy G. Lin
nodes.summary: Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She completed graduate work at Columbia and earned a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, later serving as professor at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hermann Kulke
nodes.summary: Hermann Kulke worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Freiburg, Madras, and Heidelberg under Hermann Goetz. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967-1988) and as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988-2003).

nodes.label: Emanuel Sarkisyanz
nodes.summary: Emanuel Sarkisyanz studied at the University of Tehran (~1943–1945) and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1948–1952). A scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he became Head at Heidelberg University in 1967.

nodes.label: Werner Sundermann
nodes.summary: Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), Humboldt University of Berlin, and Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

nodes.summary: Yanling Chen focuses on Buddhist studies. Chen earned an MA at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Agehananda Bharati
nodes.summary: Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Vienna. He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu University, Tokyo, and Kyoto, and served as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

nodes.label: Ron Leifer
nodes.summary: Ron Leifer (1932–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under teacher Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching at Rumtek Monastery and serving as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra.

nodes.label: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz
nodes.summary: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz (1958–2001) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Florida State University and the University of Virginia (PhD), later teaching at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis and Florida State University.

nodes.label: Krishnanath Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheswar Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: Ramaranjan Mukherji
nodes.summary: Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji held degrees from the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur University, vice chancellor at the University of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati University, and chancellor of the National Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: J. P. Mallory
nodes.summary: Specializing in archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, J. P. Mallory studied at Occidental College (~1963–1967) and UCLA (~1970–1975). He held posts at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2010) and Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

nodes.label: James Matthew Baskind
nodes.summary: James Matthew Baskind specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Yale University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein.

nodes.label: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Tsuneki Nishiwaki
nodes.summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Kyoto University from ~1996 to 2007.

nodes.label: Tom De Rauw
nodes.summary: Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Ann Heirman. By 2026, he held an AAP post at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Anthony Cerulli
nodes.summary: Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 2000 to 2007 and served at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 2014 as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies.

nodes.label: C. Pierce Salguero
nodes.description: professor of Asian history and religious studies
nodes.summary: C. Pierce Salguero studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (PhD ~2005–2010). Working in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, he held posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010), the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012), and Asian Medicine (2016).

nodes.label: Christoph Kleine
nodes.description: German japanologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Christoph Kleine specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held professorships at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and Leipzig University (appointed 2008).

nodes.label: Mervin Viggo Hanson
nodes.summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980), and also studied under Kathryn A. Cissell.

nodes.label: Kendall R. Marchman
nodes.summary: Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

nodes.label: Si Ti La
nodes.summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). They also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra.

nodes.label: Osvald Sirén
nodes.summary: Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) worked in sinology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), the Guimet Museum (1924–1925), and as keeper at the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

nodes.label: Erik-Jan Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik-Jan Zürcher (born 1953) is a historian and linguist educated at Leiden University (BA ~1971–1974, PhD ~1977–1984). He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and Leiden University (1997).

nodes.label: Soko Morinaga
nodes.summary: Soko Morinaga (1925–1995) studied at Toyama High School, Daitoku-ji, and under Zuigan Goto and Sesso Oda. He served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and abbot of Daishu-in.
