variants: College of the City of New York
City College in New York City

nodes.label: Joseph Loizzo
nodes.summary: Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He founded the Nalanda Institute and served as a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science
variants: Nalanda Institute for Meditation and Healing

nodes.label: Kennard Lipman
nodes.summary: Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979) and held an appointment as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Ji Hao
nodes.summary: Ji Hao is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Minnesota under the supervision of Paul Rouzer. He held an academic post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Paul Rouzer
nodes.summary: Paul Rouzer is a scholar in the fields of Sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2007, he was attested holding posts at both Harvard University and the University of Minnesota.

nodes.label: Namgyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Toronto Baptist Seminary, Michigan, and under Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

nodes.label: Sun-Ah Choi
nodes.summary: Sun-Ah Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying with teachers Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

nodes.label: Robert S. Nelson
nodes.summary: Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist. He completed his studies at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978), later holding professorships at the University of Chicago (~1977–2005) and Yale University (~2005).

nodes.label: Jaś Elsner
nodes.summary: Jaś Elsner works in religious studies and history/archaeology. After degrees at Cambridge and the Courtauld Institute, he held posts at Cambridge, the Courtauld Institute (~1991–1999), Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and the University of Oxford (2014).

nodes.label: Aden Kumler
nodes.summary: Aden Kumler (born 1974) is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, and Harvard University (PhD ~2007). She taught at the University of Chicago (2007) and became professor at the University of Basel in 2020.

nodes.label: Katherine R. Tsiang
nodes.summary: Katherine R. Tsiang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held a faculty post at the University of Chicago (attested in 2012 and 2026).

nodes.label: Carl Gustav Jung
nodes.jawiki: カール・グスタフ・ユング
nodes.summary: Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. After earning a medical degree at the University of Basel, he held posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

nodes.label: Erwin Rousselle
nodes.summary: Erwin Rousselle studied in Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and TU Darmstadt under Krause, Walleser, and von Staël-Holstein. He held posts at Peking University (1924–1929), Goethe University Frankfurt (from 1931), Tsinghua, and Yenching, working in sinology and Buddhist studies.

nodes.label: Richard Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Sinologist Richard Wilhelm studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen. He served as a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

nodes.label: David L. Gosling
nodes.summary: David L. Gosling specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall in 1992 and was attested at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

Academy of Social Science of Shanghai

nodes.label: Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Achard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who was educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the CNRS.

nodes.label: Ramin Etesami
nodes.summary: Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Geshe Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Richard J. Davidson
nodes.image: Rajesh Kasturirangan at Mind and Life.jpg
nodes.summary: Richard J. Davidson studied at Midwood High School, New York University (~1968–1972), and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987, 1996, and from 2001 to 2017 as a psychology professor.

nodes.label: Benjamin Brose
nodes.description: American cultural historian of religion in China
nodes.summary: Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2004–2011) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2011–2017).

nodes.label: Erik J. Hammerstrom
nodes.summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Randy J. LaPolla
nodes.summary: Linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist Randy J. LaPolla earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley under James A. Matisoff. He served as a professor at the City University of Hong Kong (c. 1996–2004) and joined Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai in 2021.

nodes.label: Tak Pui Sze
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Tak Pui Sze completed a Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia under supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh
nodes.summary: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Brigitte Marschall
nodes.summary: Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna (~1980–1984), where she earned her doctorate. She later served as an extraordinary university professor at the University of Vienna from around 1999 to 2022.

nodes.label: Guo Jun
nodes.summary: Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney. His traditional teachers included Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, and he was abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.

nodes.label: George Lakoff
variants: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
nodes.summary: George Lakoff works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at MIT (~1958–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1962–1966). He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1972 to 2016.

nodes.label: Mark Johnson
nodes.jawiki: マーク・ジョンソン (哲学者)

nodes.label: Alexander Berzin
nodes.summary: Alexander Berzin is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his B.A. from Rutgers and Princeton (~1961–1965) and a doctoral degree from Harvard (~1965–1972) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later serving at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1979).

nodes.label: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Monastery, where he also held a post.

nodes.label: Men-Tsee-Khang
variants: Tibetan Institute of Medicine and Astrology

International Council for Day of Vesak
International Organizing Committee for the UN Day of Vesak

nodes.label: Kamal K. Sridhar
nodes.summary: Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. Her academic posts at Stony Brook University include director (attested 2007) and Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shikaripur N. Sridhar
nodes.summary: Shikaripur N. Sridhar works in linguistics and indology. At Stony Brook University, he is attested as Chair in 2007 and as Director of the Center for India Studies in 2026.

nodes.label: Akira Takeda
nodes.summary: Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University, served as assistant (1961) and professor (1965–1991) at the University of Tokyo, and became professor emeritus at Meikai University.

nodes.label: Charles Taliaferro
nodes.summary: Charles Taliaferro (b. 1952) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, he served as a professor at St. Olaf College from ~1985 to 2022.

nodes.label: Charlene Makley
nodes.summary: Charlene Makley is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and later became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

nodes.label: Roy Rappaport
nodes.summary: Roy Rappaport was an anthropologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his doctorate from Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

nodes.label: Marco Walther
nodes.summary: Marco Walther works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the doctoral supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Jamie Hubbard
nodes.summary: Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Kazuo Okabe and Minoru Kiyota. He held named professorships in Buddhist, religious, and East Asian studies at Smith College (attested 2016, 2026).

nodes.label: St Hugh's College
variants: Becket Institute, St Hugh's College, Oxford
Becket Institute at St. Hugh's College, Oxford
Becket Institute, St. Hugh's College, Oxford

nodes.label: Takayasu Higuchi
nodes.summary: Takayasu Higuchi studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), working in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1967–1983) and director at Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, and Research Centre for Silk Roadology.

nodes.label: P. R. Srinivasan
nodes.description: Indian epigraphist, archaeologist and art historian

nodes.label: John Woodroffe
nodes.summary: An indologist and religious studies scholar, John Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford. He served as a Judge at the Calcutta High Court, Fellow and Tagore Law Professor at the University of Calcutta, and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford.

nodes.label: Eishō-ji
variants: Eishoji Zen training and practice facility

nodes.label: Bingtao Ma
nodes.summary: Bingtao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed an MA at Peking University (-2008) and a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Cécile Ducher
nodes.summary: Cécile Ducher works in tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein and served as a research fellow there.

nodes.label: Nicholas Justin Allen
nodes.summary: Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Oxford under Rodney Needham, he lectured at Durham (1972–1976) and served at Oxford as Lecturer (1976) and Reader (1997) in the Social Anthropology of South Asia.

nodes.label: Charles Taylor
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・マーグレイヴ・テイラー
nodes.summary: Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1948–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961). He taught at McGill University (~1961–1997), Northwestern University (~2002), and the University of Montreal.

nodes.label: Zhiru Ng
nodes.summary: Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Bryan W. Van Norden
nodes.summary: Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and held a professorship in philosophy and Chinese & Japanese at Vassar College starting around 1996.

nodes.label: Harjit Singh
nodes.summary: Harjit Singh is a Tibetologist who held a professorship at Jawaharlal Nehru University, attested in 1997 and 2016.

nodes.label: Chi-wah Chan
nodes.summary: Chi-wah Chan works in sinology and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from UCLA in 1993 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and previously served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Patrice Ladwig
nodes.summary: Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
variants: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
Max Planck Institute of Social Anthropology

nodes.label: Ingmar Heise
nodes.summary: Ingmar Heise is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University in 2005 and later pursued doctoral studies at the University of Bristol (attested 2012).

nodes.label: G. C. Nayak
nodes.summary: G. C. Nayak is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held appointments as a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1994–1997) and senior fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (1996).

nodes.label: D. P. Chattopadhyaya
nodes.image: D. P. Chattopadhyaya Rajya Sabha photo.jpg

nodes.label: Peter D. Hershock
nodes.summary: Peter D. Hershock (b. 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. A Yale University graduate, he studied under Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, and directed the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center.

nodes.label: Stephen J. Laumakis
nodes.summary: Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe. He served at the University of St. Thomas as Professor of Philosophy, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: British Academy
variants: British Academy Committee for Southeast Asian Studies

nodes.label: Christopher Ives
nodes.summary: Christopher Ives specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and later became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

nodes.label: Sharon J. Roe
nodes.summary: Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and held a post as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, attested in 2015.

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College
variants: 舞鶴工業高等専門学校人文科学部門

nodes.label: Yozo Taniyama
nodes.summary: Yozo Taniyama (b. 1972) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University (~1991–1996), he held positions at Sophia University (~2000–2004), St. Thomas University, Japan (~2004–2007), Shitennoji University (~2007–2012), and Tohoku University (~2012).

nodes.label: Dickwela Piyananda
nodes.summary: Dickwela Piyananda was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Catholic University of America, studying under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Christian Bernert
nodes.summary: Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, earning a Mag. phil. under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with additional instruction from Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

nodes.label: Hugh J. Silverman
nodes.summary: Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Stanford University. He was a longtime professor at Stony Brook University from 1974, executive director of the IAPL, and held visiting chairs and appointments at the University of Vienna, AFA Vienna, Stanford, Klagenfurt, and Turin.

nodes.label: Heeraman Tiwari
nodes.summary: Heeraman Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Heidelberg University (2011–2012), and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: Lang Chen
nodes.summary: Lang Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Yale University, studying under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Matthew Orsborn
nodes.summary: Matthew Orsborn works in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. By 2026, he was attested as professor and Head of International Affairs at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Fred Porta
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Fred Porta held posts at Stanford University as a professor (attested 2012) and as a lecturer in the Stanford Language Center and Department of Classics (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sogyal Rinpoche
variants: ソギャル・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Tibetan Dzogchen lama of the Nyingma tradition
nodes.summary: Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Tibetan Buddhist teacher who studied at the universities of Delhi and Cambridge, as well as under Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

nodes.label: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje
nodes.summary: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Katok and Nyoshul Monasteries and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Penor Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam
nodes.summary: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

nodes.label: Erica Baffelli
nodes.summary: Erica Baffelli is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and serves as Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Manchester (attested 2016, 2026).

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Human Development
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
variants: Max Planck Institute for Human Development

nodes.label: Lara Braitstein
nodes.summary: Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and became Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism there (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Markus Viehbeck
nodes.summary: Markus Viehbeck is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD in 2012 at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later working as a Heidelberg University project researcher and Vienna faculty member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: David R. Kinsley
nodes.summary: David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, and spent his career at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

nodes.label: Bihani Sarkar
nodes.summary: Bihani Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held a post at the University of Hamburg and is attested in 2026 as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University.

nodes.label: Liang Cai
nodes.summary: Liang Cai, a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology, studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kenneth Doo Young Lee
nodes.summary: Kenneth Doo Young Lee works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe, and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: D. Phillip Stanley
nodes.summary: D. Phillip Stanley is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He served as director of the Nitartha Institute (~1996) and Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Lorne Ladner
nodes.summary: Lorne Ladner works in Buddhist studies and counseling. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and served as an adjunct faculty member at Argosy University, both attested in 2004.

nodes.label: W. F. Jayasuriya
nodes.summary: W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

nodes.label: Beata Grant
nodes.summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Stanford University (~1981–1987) and served as Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989–2018).

nodes.label: Weiru Guan
nodes.summary: Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where studies were supervised by Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Sīlānanda
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Sīlānanda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon University College, under U Paññāvanta, and under Mahasi Sayadaw. He held leadership and teaching posts at the University of Mandalay, Tathāgata Meditation Center, and Dhammananda Vihara, among other institutions.

nodes.label: Mahasi Sayadaw
nodes.native: မဟာစည်ဆရာတော်
nodes.summary: Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Aletawya Sayadaw, U Narada, and Thelon Sayadaw. He was abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung (1941), resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947), and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).

nodes.label: Atithokdayone Pali University
variants: Atithokdāyone Pali University in Shwegu Taik Monastery

nodes.label: Vishwanathan Venkatachalam
nodes.summary: Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He served as Director of the Scindia Oriental Research Institute, Professor at Vikram University, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, among other leadership roles.

nodes.label: Joanna Cook
nodes.summary: Joanna Cook is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under advisor James Laidlaw. She holds a post at Christ's College, University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Edo Shonin
nodes.summary: Edo Shonin works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: William Van Gordon
nodes.summary: Active in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and psychology, Van Gordon founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and was a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Nirbhay N. Singh
nodes.summary: Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious and Buddhist studies. He has served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).

nodes.id: I:Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
nodes.label: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
variants: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research

nodes.label: Mark D. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) earned a BSc at Bradford and a PhD at Exeter (1988–1990). He held posts at the Workers' Educational Association, the University of Plymouth (1990–1995), and Nottingham Trent University as Professor of Gambling Studies (1995–2025).

nodes.label: Charles Gabriel Seligman
nodes.summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). He held the chair of ethnology at the London School of Economics and Political Science and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

nodes.label: James C. Dobbins
nodes.summary: James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.

nodes.label: Francis Harold Cook
nodes.summary: Francis Harold Cook was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He served as a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1989) and chaired the Numata Center (1999).

nodes.label: Taitetsu Unno
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Unno earned degrees from UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo. From 1971 to 1998, he served as the Jill Ker Conway Professor of Religion at Smith College.

nodes.label: Joshua W. C. Cutler
nodes.summary: Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Anna Sawerthal
nodes.summary: Anna Sawerthal is a scholar of Tibetology. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with Johanna Buß, and later earned a PhD at Heidelberg University, studying under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

nodes.label: Lauran R. Hartley
nodes.summary: Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University Bloomington, taught at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and served as an Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ann Appleby Hazlewood
nodes.summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 1983, she completed a Master of Arts at the Australian National University under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

nodes.label: Nika Jovic
nodes.summary: Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Jovic studied under teacher Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008) and completed a Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Conor Roddy
nodes.summary: Conor Roddy is a philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011), having studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

nodes.label: John W. Pettit
nodes.summary: John W. Pettit works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Haverford College, completed doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

nodes.label: Haverford College
variants: Margaret Gest Center for the Cross-Cultural Study of Religion at Haverford

nodes.label: Ashok Gangadean
nodes.summary: Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD in philosophy at Brandeis University (~1965–1969). He was the Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College (~1968–2020) and founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

nodes.label: Lal Mani Joshi
nodes.summary: Lal Mani Joshi studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under G. C. Pande. Active in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, he held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Harvard, Amherst, Haverford, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri.

nodes.label: New College of Florida
variants: New College of the University of South Florida

nodes.label: Rongdao Lai
nodes.summary: Rongdao Lai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her Ph.D. at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and held posts at the Center for Chinese Studies and McGill University.

nodes.label: Robin D. S. Yates
nodes.summary: Robin D. S. Yates is a historian and Sinologist. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University from ~1993 to 2021.

nodes.label: Zhenhua
nodes.summary: Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Temple (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). He served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Robert Baker Aitken
nodes.summary: Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Ryutaku-ji, and UC Berkeley under D.T. Suzuki and Hakuun Yasutani, and held posts at Besant Hill School and the East-West Center.

nodes.label: Bruno Dagens
nodes.summary: Bruno Dagens (1935–2023) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Colette Caillat and held positions at EFEO, Catholic University of Louvain, French Institute of Pondicherry, KU Leuven (~1977–1986), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).

nodes.label: Constance Powell Chin
nodes.summary: Constance Powell Chin works in religious studies, history, and archaeology. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

nodes.label: Michael G. Morony
nodes.summary: Michael G. Morony is a historian and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.

nodes.label: Benjamin Wood
nodes.summary: Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto under the supervision of Frances Garrett.

nodes.label: Donald Keene
nodes.summary: Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University (~1947–1948). He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

nodes.label: Peipei Qiu
nodes.summary: Peipei Qiu specializes in Japanology and Sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where she completed her doctorate under Donald Keene and also studied under Paul Rouzer, before taking up a post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Erndl
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Erndl was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held academic posts at DePauw University (~1984–1986), the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1986–1987), Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

nodes.label: Dennis Hudson
nodes.summary: Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served on the faculty at Smith College, where he was Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies (attested 1987–1989) and taught religion (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Dominique-Sila Khan
nodes.summary: Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and held a post as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).

nodes.label: June McDaniel
nodes.summary: June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS from Emory University and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She held posts in philosophy, religion, and religious studies at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

nodes.label: Soraj Hongladarom
nodes.native: โสรัจจ์ หงศ์ลดารมภ์
nodes.summary: Soraj Hongladarom works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was an Erasmus Mundus exchange scholar at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (2008) and Linköping University, and held a post in philosophy at Chulalongkorn University (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Norwegian University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
variants: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

nodes.label: Yu-Chen Tsui
nodes.summary: Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Tsui completed master's studies at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and pursued doctoral research supervised by Natasha Heller, also studying under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Dermott Walsh
nodes.summary: Dermott Walsh is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (BA 2003), Leiden University (MA 2009), and completed his PhD in 2018 at the University of California, Los Angeles, under William M. Bodiford.

nodes.label: C. D. Sebastian
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, C. D. Sebastian earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University, studying under Ashok Kumar Chatterjee and Abhimanyu Singh, with postdoctoral mentoring by Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa. He taught at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Gavin D'Costa
nodes.summary: Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Birmingham under John Hick. His career includes posts at the West London Institute of Higher Education and the University of Bristol.

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and served as professor and head of philosophy at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Dennis A. Johnson
nodes.summary: Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he completed his MA under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Hiroko Kawanami
nodes.summary: Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and later taught Jiancheng Shi. Her career includes serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

nodes.label: Alfred Gell
nodes.summary: Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach and at the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex, the Australian National University, and the London School of Economics.

nodes.label: John Okell
nodes.summary: John Okell was a linguist who studied at the University of Oxford and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

nodes.label: Sunhee Kim
nodes.summary: Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under doctoral supervisor Phillip B. Zarrilli (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nancy McCagney
nodes.summary: Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Jeong-Eun Kim
nodes.summary: Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

nodes.label: Giovanni Verardi
nodes.summary: Giovanni Verardi is an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and indologist who studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur universities. He taught at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (1972–1987), the University of Bologna (1981–1987), and was professor at Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Aoyagi
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) is a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1993–1998), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (~1998).

nodes.label: Antonio Terrone
nodes.summary: Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University in 2010 under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and later served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.summary: Ramon Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources in 1999 and Pompeu Fabra University in 2017.

nodes.label: Nicolas Sihlé
nodes.summary: Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010; attested as former assistant professor in 2026).

nodes.label: Somboon Watana
nodes.summary: Somboon Watana specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and was an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tulku Sherdor
nodes.summary: Tulku Sherdor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, and his teachers included Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

nodes.label: Sharon Salzberg
nodes.summary: Sharon Salzberg is a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo and trained under teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Satya Narayan Goenka, and Dipa Ma. She co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (1989).

nodes.label: Yuko Matsuda
nodes.summary: Yuko Matsuda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Matsuda studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Natalie Gummer
nodes.summary: Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University in 2001 and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

nodes.label: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture
variants: Thomas Burke Memorial Washington State Museum, University of Washington

nodes.label: Barbara Gerke
nodes.summary: Barbara Gerke, a specialist in Tibetology and religious studies, completed her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.id: I:Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
nodes.label: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
variants: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies

nodes.label: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt
nodes.summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt (born 1955) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the Universities of Bonn, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Marburg, where she habilitated. She held posts as guest professor at the University of Vienna (~2004–2005) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

nodes.label: Huidi Zeng
nodes.summary: Huidi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Yi-hsun Huang
nodes.summary: Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Huang earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Alexander Kabanoff
nodes.summary: Alexander Kabanoff was a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies. By 2000, he was Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Phra Medhidhammaporn
nodes.summary: Phra Medhidhammaporn (born 1955) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis in 1985 at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

nodes.label: David Azzopardi
nodes.summary: David Azzopardi, an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

nodes.label: János Szerb
nodes.summary: János Szerb worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (circa 1974–1980), he became a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna in 1982 and a Buddhist studies researcher at the ISTB in 1986.

nodes.label: Kurt Tropper
nodes.summary: Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna (2001) under Ernst Steinkellner, and held posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ñāṇavīra Thera graduated from Magdalene College (1938) and served in the Royal Artillery and Intelligence Corps (1939–1945). He later studied under traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana.

nodes.label: Pelene Siri Vajiragnana
variants: Pälänē Siri Vajirañāņa Mahā Nāyaka Thera

nodes.label: Louis Komjathy
nodes.summary: Sinologist and religious studies scholar Louis Komjathy earned his PhD at Boston University under Paul Rouzer. In 2014, he was attested as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego.

nodes.label: Heng Sure
nodes.summary: Heng Sure studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), as well as under Hsuan Hua. He has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

nodes.label: Edmond Yee
nodes.summary: Edmond Yee (b. 1938) is a scholar in religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculties of both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1986 to 2006.

nodes.label: Niras Ruangsan
nodes.native: นิราศ เรืองแสน
nodes.summary: Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

nodes.label: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle
nodes.summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: G. Clinton Godart
nodes.summary: G. Clinton Godart specializes in Japanology, history, and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago under James Ketelaar, held posts at Needham Research Institute and the University of Southern California, and worked at Hokkaido University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Chien-hsing Ho
nodes.summary: Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho has held posts at Nanhua University as an associate professor of religious studies and at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Charles B. Jones
nodes.summary: Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.

nodes.label: Technical University of Berlin
variants: ベルリンのシャルロッテンブルク工科大学

nodes.label: Hürelbaatar Ujeed
nodes.summary: Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He received his PhD from the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (attested 2010) and Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

nodes.label: Ralph Abraham
nodes.summary: Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton before serving as associate professor (1968) and professor (1980) at the University of California, Santa Cruz.

nodes.label: Sisir Roy
nodes.summary: Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields, having studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts as Professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).

nodes.label: National Institute of Advanced Studies
variants: National Institute of Advanced Studies, Bangalore

nodes.label: Ajahn Brahm
nodes.summary: Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at the University of Cambridge who studied under Nai Boonman and Ajahn Chah. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1995.

nodes.label: Terese Tse Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

nodes.label: Ryan Anningson
nodes.summary: Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences

nodes.label: Amy Heller
nodes.summary: Amy Heller (born 1951) is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She held appointments at the CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Mireille Helffer
nodes.summary: Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology and held posts at the National Centre for Scientific Research as Chargé de Recherche and at Paris Nanterre University (both attested 1985).

nodes.label: Dawa Norbu
nodes.summary: Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) specialized in Tibetology and history. He studied at the University of Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and UC Berkeley. He taught at SFSU, USF, CIIS, and served as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2006).

nodes.label: Nawang Tsering
nodes.summary: Nawang Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a Lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Hsuan Hua
nodes.summary: Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Chang Chih and Hsu Yun. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, and was Abbot of Tathagata Monastery.

nodes.label: Hsu Yun
nodes.summary: Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He co-founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as its honorary president.

nodes.label: Drepung Gomang Dratsang
variants: Gomang College of the Gelugpa Drepung monastic university
Gomang College of Drepung Monastic University

nodes.label: Chien Y. Hsu
nodes.summary: Chien Y. Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed doctoral work under Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple, and also studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua.

nodes.label: Joseph D. Markowski
nodes.summary: Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at McGill University, where he studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Peter Francis Kornicki
nodes.summary: Peter Francis Kornicki (b. 1950) studied at Oxford (MSc, DPhil 1975–1979). Specializing in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and the University of Cambridge (~1985–2017).

nodes.label: Rosemary Radford Ruether
nodes.summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether (1936–2022) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

nodes.label: E. W. Adikaram
nodes.summary: E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

nodes.label: Arthur Philip McKeown
nodes.summary: Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

nodes.label: Ruth Denison
nodes.description: Western Theravada meditation teacher resided in USA (1922-2015)

nodes.label: Polly Young-Eisendrath
nodes.summary: Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied Zen under Philip Kapleau, attended Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, and became clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont in 1994.

nodes.label: Hayao Kawai
nodes.summary: Hayao Kawai was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1952). He held posts at Tenri University (~1959–1969), Kyoto University (~1992–2007), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1995–2001).

nodes.label: Moriya Okano
nodes.summary: Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has held positions at Musashino University and the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies (attested 2002).
