variants: Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies

nodes.label: Yasuo Deguchi
nodes.summary: Yasuo Deguchi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1987-1991). He served at Nagoya Institute of Technology, founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy, and became a professor and dean at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Constance Kassor
nodes.summary: Constance Kassor works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a BA from Smith College under Jay L. Garfield and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining Smith College's faculty (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Karin Meyers
nodes.summary: Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eyal Aviv
nodes.summary: Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett (attested 2008), and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

nodes.label: Annette Baier
nodes.summary: Annette Baier was a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Otago and a PhD at Somerville College, Oxford. She taught at Carnegie Mellon University (around 1969–1973) and in the philosophy department at the University of Pittsburgh (around 1973–1995).

nodes.label: Wilfrid Sellars
variants: ウィルフリド・ストーカー・セラーズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィルフリド・セラーズ
nodes.summary: Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He held teaching posts at Iowa (1938–1946), Minnesota (1947–1958), and Yale (1958–1963), before serving as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

nodes.label: Zuicho Tachibana
nodes.summary: Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1903–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908–1909).

nodes.label: Ines Konczak
nodes.summary: Ines Konczak specializes in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University (2012).

nodes.label: Angela Falco Howard
nodes.summary: Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and held a professorship at Rutgers University, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Giuseppe Vignato
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A doctoral student at Peking University, he studied under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Bai Su, and Shichang Ma, and was affiliated with Peking University in 2017.

nodes.label: Bai Su
nodes.summary: Bai Su (1922–2018) was a Chinese archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. He completed graduate studies at Peking University under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor at Peking University (1948–2004).

nodes.label: Shichang Ma
nodes.summary: Shichang Ma (born 1938) is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in Peking University's Archaeology Department beginning in 1982.

nodes.label: Max Oidtmann
nodes.summary: Max Oidtmann is a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott, later holding posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Gustav Haloun
nodes.summary: Gustav Haloun was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at Leipzig University. He directed at the University of Göttingen from 1931 to 1938 and held the Chair of Chinese Language and History at the University of Cambridge from 1938 to 1951.

nodes.label: Jotika Khur-Yearn
nodes.summary: Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the doctoral supervision of Kate Crosby, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Rangama Chandawimala
nodes.summary: Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha Thera. He was attested as Associate Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Gregory Price Grieve
nodes.summary: Gregory Price Grieve (born 1964), a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, earned his degrees from SFSU and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Department Head at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

nodes.label: Michael S. Drummond
nodes.summary: Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

nodes.label: Michel Bitbol
nodes.summary: Michel Bitbol (born 1954) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University (completed 1985) and under Pierre Mills. He held research director posts at the CNRS from ~1990 and positions at the University of Paris, Linacre College, and ENS.

nodes.label: Guy Claxton
nodes.summary: Guy Claxton worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He founded Sharpham College and served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol's Graduate School of Education (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Sharpham College
variants: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry

nodes.label: Owen Flanagan
nodes.summary: Owen Flanagan is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Fordham University and Boston University, and was appointed Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

nodes.label: Andrew Olendzki
nodes.summary: Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003-2014), and as senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Insight Meditation Society
variants: Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts

nodes.label: University of Warwick
variants: Centre for Translation & Comparative Cultural Studies, University of Warwick

nodes.label: Fazun
nodes.summary: Fazun (1902–1980) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Taixu and at Drepung Monastery, directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies from 1933, and became vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China in 1956.

nodes.label: Tzungkuen Wen
nodes.summary: Tzungkuen Wen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Queensland, taught at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005, and later headed the Counseling and Guidance Center at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Buddhadasa Bhikkhu
nodes.native: พุทธทาสภิกขุ

nodes.label: Robert A. Orsi
nodes.summary: Robert A. Orsi is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held academic posts at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard, Northwestern University, and the University of Notre Dame.

nodes.label: Clara Sue Kidwell
nodes.description: Native American academic scholar, historian, feminist
nodes.summary: Clara Sue Kidwell was a historian who earned her master's and PhD at the University of Oklahoma. She held positions at Haskell Indian Nations University, UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian, the University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Karen McCarthy Brown
nodes.summary: Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar. She studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University, and was a professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009) alongside posts at Temple and other institutions.

nodes.label: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri
nodes.summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri studied at London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, serving as its president (~2000), and held posts at the University of Toronto (attested 2001) and Ontario Tech University.

nodes.label: Christopher Hatchell
nodes.summary: Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

nodes.label: Jason Matthew McCombs
nodes.summary: Jason Matthew McCombs works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA (2014) under Gregory Schopen, later serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

nodes.label: Jigmeth Junu
nodes.summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, having also studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian.

nodes.label: Miri Albahari
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Miri Albahari earned an MA from the University of Otago and a PhD in 2005 from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker. Affiliations include the University of New South Wales and the University of Western Australia.

nodes.label: University of New South Wales
variants: The University of New South Wales

nodes.label: Martin Heidegger
variants: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.jawiki: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.summary: Martin Heidegger (1889–1976) was a German philosopher. He studied under Heinrich Rickert at the University of Freiburg, where he completed his studies in 1916 and later taught (1915–1923, 1936–1940), alongside a professorship at the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

nodes.label: Christian Parker Bardolph Haskett
nodes.summary: Christian Parker Bardolph Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having also studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, and held an affiliation at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Graeme MacQueen
nodes.summary: Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Harvard University (~1971–1979) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2003).

nodes.label: Linda Jean LaMacchia
nodes.summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Martin Straube
nodes.summary: Martin Straube is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2026, he was attested at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: China Institute of Inner Learning
variants: China Institute of Inner Learning (支那內學院)
China Inner Academy of Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Michael Sheehy
nodes.summary: Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at CIIS under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

nodes.label: Qingying Chen
nodes.summary: Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at Qinghai Minzu University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao, later directing the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center (~1986–2005).

nodes.label: Anagarika Govinda
nodes.image: Lama Govinda in an internment camp during World War II.jpg
nodes.summary: Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar with a doctorate from the University of Freiburg. He taught at Visva-Bharati University (1931–1935) and Patna University (1935–1936), and served as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).

nodes.label: Adeu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Adeu Rinpoche (1931–2007) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Zen Mountain Monastery
variants: Zen Mountain Monastery at Mt. Tremper

nodes.label: Hegoda Khemananda
nodes.summary: Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes serving as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena (attested 1993) and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Dewei Zhang
nodes.summary: Dewei Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Paul Crowe
nodes.summary: Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: King Pong Chiu
nodes.summary: King Pong Chiu is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Thomé H. Fang
nodes.summary: Thomé H. Fang (1899–1977) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, under John Dewey, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

nodes.label: Ilkka Pyysiäinen
nodes.description: Finnish cognitive science of religion scholar
nodes.summary: Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under Juha Pentikäinen, René Gothóni, and Simo Knuuttila. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki (1984) and visited Oxford (~2007–2008).

nodes.label: Juha Pentikäinen
nodes.summary: Juha Pentikäinen is a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki and the University of Turku. He served as Professor of Comparative Religion at the University of Helsinki from ~1972 to 2008.

nodes.label: Hiram W. Woodward
nodes.summary: Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Harvard (B.A.) and Yale (M.A.). He held faculty posts at Michigan (1972–1982) and Vermont (~1982–1986), and was curator of Asian art at Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

nodes.label: ISEAS–Yusof Ishak Institute
variants: Institute of Southeast Asian Studies, Singapore

nodes.label: Andrew B. Irvine
nodes.summary: Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. After completing a PhD at Boston University, he held a post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Brooke Schedneck
nodes.summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

nodes.label: Jacques Leider
nodes.summary: Jacques Leider works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne, the University of Luxembourg, and INALCO under Denise Bernot and Pierre L. Lamant. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the EFEO in 2001.

nodes.label: William Edward Soothill
nodes.summary: William Edward Soothill worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University (1911) and Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford (1920).

nodes.label: Lewis Hodous
nodes.summary: Lewis Hodous, who worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held leadership posts at Fukien Union Theological Seminary (1902-1917) and taught at Hartford Seminary (1917-1945).

nodes.label: Adrian Zenz
nodes.summary: Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology, having studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He lectured at the European School of Culture and Theology and became a Senior Fellow at the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation in 2019.

nodes.label: Xiuzhi Zeng
nodes.summary: Xiuzhi Zeng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Pompeu Fabra University
variants: Department of Humanities of the University Pompeu Fabra

nodes.label: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy
nodes.summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a scholar of Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, EPHE, and Harvard, under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert, and taught anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).

nodes.label: Tibet Arts Research Institute
variants: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau (Bod ljongs sgyu rtsal zhib 'jug khang)

nodes.label: James Whitehill
nodes.summary: James Whitehill is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

nodes.label: David Bubna-Litic
nodes.summary: David Bubna-Litic earned a PhD from Western Sydney University and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (both attested 2000).

nodes.label: University of Technology Sydney
variants: School of Management in the University of Technology, Sydney

nodes.label: Susan Naquin
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian Susan Naquin earned a BA from Stanford University (~1962–1966) and an MA and PhD from Yale University (~1966–1974). She served at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and as a professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

nodes.label: Jiyu Ren
nodes.summary: Jiyu Ren studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. He taught at Peking University (1942–1964) and directed the Institute of World Religions (~1964–1985) and the National Library of China (1987–2005).

nodes.label: Xiaoling Wu
nodes.summary: Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and indology. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1949), Peking University (~1949–1952), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).

nodes.label: Marion L. Matics
nodes.summary: Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral research under supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, having also studied under Robert A. Fowkes.

nodes.label: Horace L. Friess
nodes.summary: Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia and Heidelberg universities. He held posts at Johns Hopkins and Columbia, where he was Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations from 1962 to 1966.

nodes.label: Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center
variants: Soto Zen Education Center of North America
曹洞宗北アメリカ開教センター

nodes.label: Susan L. Beningson
nodes.summary: Susan L. Beningson works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist Jr. (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Robert E. Harrist Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Harrist Jr. is a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, where he is attested in 2009 and served as the Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Wayne Bass
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Wayne Bass works in Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of North Carolina Wilmington and University of Tennessee, he earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, subsequently teaching at UCLA and UC San Diego as a lecturer.

nodes.label: William P. Chu
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, Chu completed an MA in 2006 at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he was supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.id: I:International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
variants: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
IITB GmbH (International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies GmbH)

nodes.label: Dhirendra Sharma
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Sharma (1932–2022) was a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under Surendra Sharma and David Friedman.

nodes.label: John R. B. Campbell
nodes.summary: Campbell works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, and studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and Gyumed Khensur Lobsang Ngawang.

nodes.label: H. V. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He has held positions at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Geshe Karma Sonam
nodes.summary: Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Lang Eun Ra
nodes.summary: Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ra completed doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

nodes.label: Norbert M. Samuelson
nodes.summary: Norbert M. Samuelson was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines, later holding professorships at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Leonard Swidler
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Leonard Swidler studied at St. Norbert College, Saint Paul Seminary, Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, Tübingen, and Munich. He taught at Duquesne University (1960-1966) and served as professor at Temple University from 1966 to 2022.

nodes.label: Alan Gerard Wagner
nodes.summary: Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2008) under supervisor Parimal G. Patil, and also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Iselin Frydenlund
nodes.summary: Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She has held posts as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo (attested 2016) and as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Martin Lehnert
nodes.summary: Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: James Mark Shields
nodes.summary: James Mark Shields works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. His posts include Associate Professor at Bucknell University (attested 2016) and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Foundation for Buddhist Studies
variants: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg

nodes.label: Kim Gutschow
nodes.summary: Kim Gutschow, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Leiden University and Drepung Monastery (attested 1966–1995), serving as a Geshe of sGo-mang sgrva-tshang and Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

nodes.label: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Jenkuan Shih
nodes.summary: Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having previously studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Mark Csikszentmihalyi
nodes.summary: Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) is a sinologist and philosopher. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2007) before becoming Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley (~2007).

nodes.label: Robert Cummings Neville
nodes.summary: Robert Cummings Neville is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1957–1963) and subsequently held academic posts at Yale (~1964–1965), Fordham University (~1968–1971), and Boston University (~1982).

nodes.label: David A. Dilworth
nodes.summary: David A. Dilworth works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

nodes.label: Giuliana Martini
nodes.summary: Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.

nodes.label: Keith Dowman
nodes.description: Dzogchen teacher, translator of Tibetan Buddhist texts
nodes.summary: Keith Dowman is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and trained under traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

nodes.label: David Ralph Quinter
nodes.summary: David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Japanese religions and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD from Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later joining the University of Alberta.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies in Yokohama
Inter-University Center for Advanced Language Study
Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies

nodes.label: Kenji Matsuo
nodes.summary: Kenji Matsuo (born 1954) works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973-1986) and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.

nodes.label: Sonja Arntzen
nodes.summary: Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a Japanologist who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1979), completing her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under teachers Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

nodes.label: Shuichi Kato
nodes.summary: Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) studied medicine at the University of Tokyo and also attended the University of Paris. Active in Japanology, history, and philosophy, he held posts at Tokyo, Sophia, British Columbia, Berlin, Brown, Ritsumeikan, and Kyoto Museum for World Peace.

nodes.label: Wenhui Yang
nodes.summary: Wenhui Yang (1837–1911) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), the Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), serving as the latter's head.

nodes.label: Qichao Liang
nodes.summary: Qichao Liang worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology, studying at Xuehai Academy, under Youwei Kang, and at National Tsing Hua University. He held posts at Shiwu School, Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and National Library of China.

nodes.label: Youwei Kang
nodes.summary: Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from approximately 1891 to 1898.

nodes.label: Cameron Bailey
nodes.summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), working under Richard F. Nance, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Ulrike Roesler, among others.

nodes.label: Lucia Galli
nodes.summary: Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Rory Lindsay
nodes.summary: Rory Lindsay works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and Harvard University, completing his Ph.D. at Harvard under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp in 2011 alongside numerous other teachers.

nodes.label: Donald K. Swearer
nodes.summary: Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who taught Rory Lindsay and Thomas Adams Borchert. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1976–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010).

nodes.label: Amanda K. Goodman
nodes.summary: Amanda K. Goodman specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
variants: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science & Technology

nodes.label: Mamoru Tonami
nodes.summary: Mamoru Tonami was a historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, he earned a doctorate and served at Kobe University (1971), Kyoto University (1965–2001, professor from 1984), and Otani University (2003).

nodes.label: Jeffery D. Long
nodes.summary: Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, joining Elizabethtown College as associate professor of religion and Asian studies in 2000.

nodes.label: Angela Sumegi
nodes.summary: Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities.

nodes.label: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under numerous masters including Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1959–1968).

nodes.id: I:Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
nodes.label: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
variants: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre

nodes.label: Lucia Dolce
nodes.summary: Lucia Dolce specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held posts at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and Associate Professor (attested 2015), and is attested as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University (2026).

nodes.label: Grace S. Fong
nodes.summary: Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1974–1984). She served as professor at Smith College (~1985–1989) and as associate professor and department chair at McGill University (~1992).

nodes.label: Ching-mei Shyu
nodes.summary: Ching-mei Shyu is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (awarded 2008) supervised by Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

nodes.label: Jane-Marie Law
nodes.summary: Jane-Marie Law specializes in Japanology and religious studies. At Cornell University, she served as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ellison Banks Findly
nodes.summary: Ellison Banks Findly works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held posts at Mount Holyoke College as well as Trinity College, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kazuo Okabe
nodes.summary: Kazuo Okabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Zen Studies (1969) and Komazawa University (assistant professor 1973; professor 1979–2006).

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Ñāṇasaṃvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร

nodes.label: Vajirañāṇavarorasa
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระมหาสมณเจ้า กรมพระยาวชิรญาณวโรรส

nodes.label: Hanung Kim
nodes.summary: Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Ruth Gamble
nodes.summary: Ruth Gamble is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the Australian National University (by 2014) and has held posts as a Research Associate at the Australian National University and as a Post-doctoral Researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Petra Maurer
nodes.summary: Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist and Indologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the University of Munich, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Cuilan Liu
nodes.summary: Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held posts as an assistant professor at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emanuela Garatti
nodes.summary: Emanuela Garatti is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Pragati Sahni
nodes.summary: Pragati Sahni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Damien Keown and is attested as an associate professor at the University of Delhi in 2026.

nodes.label: Satya Narayan Goenka
variants: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.image: The Kalyanmitra Satyanarayan Goenka who brought Vipassana Meditation technique to India after 2500 years is seen with his wife while speaking at a talk on "Values in Education - Good Governance through Vipassana Meditation" in.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.summary: Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1969). He founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

nodes.label: Phramonchai Saitanaporn
nodes.summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Luang Por Dhammajayo and earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle.

nodes.label: Jeff Wilson
nodes.summary: Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under Taitetsu Unno and Myosei Tatsuguchi.

nodes.label: Luang Por Dhammajayo
nodes.native: พระธรรมชโย

nodes.label: Shuman Chen
nodes.summary: Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Northwestern University under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

nodes.label: Brook Ziporyn
nodes.summary: Brook Ziporyn works in sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan under Donald J. Munro, he held posts at Northwestern University (~1999–2012) and the University of Chicago (~2013).

nodes.label: Sarah E. Fraser
nodes.summary: Sarah E. Fraser works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and she held appointments as Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at EPHE (2000).

nodes.label: Anne Ruth Hansen
nodes.summary: Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison as Associate Professor (attested 2012) and Professor of History (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Thomas Nathan Patton
nodes.summary: Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Anne M. Blackburn
nodes.summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago (1991) and held appointments as Assistant Professor at Cornell University (~2000) and later as Professor at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Hoseok Leigh
nodes.summary: Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and traditional teacher Cheonghwa.

nodes.label: Carol S. Anderson
nodes.summary: Carol S. Anderson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

nodes.label: Catherine Bell
nodes.summary: Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University from 1985 to 2008.

nodes.label: Hsiang-Kuang Chou
nodes.summary: Hsiang-Kuang Chou, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied under Swami Sivananda. He held posts at the University of Delhi, the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy, the University of Allahabad, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

nodes.id: I:Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
nodes.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
Kin Cheung
nodes.summary: Kin Cheung works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: James Blumenthal
nodes.summary: James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

nodes.label: Kosen Imakita
nodes.summary: Kosen Imakita (1816–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Togai Fujisawa, Kyokuso Hirose, Shoen Daisetsu, and Gisan Zenrai, served as abbot at Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and taught Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and Soyen Shaku.

nodes.label: Beatrice Erskine Lane
variants: ベアトリス・アースキン・レイン・スズキ
nodes.jawiki: ベアトリス・レイン・スズキ
nodes.summary: Beatrice Erskine Lane (1878–1939) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under William James and Josiah Royce at Radcliffe College and earned an M.A. from Columbia University, later becoming a professor at Otani University in 1921.

nodes.label: Josiah Royce
nodes.summary: Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at UC Berkeley, Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

nodes.label: George Santayana
variants: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.summary: George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Boston Latin School, Harvard (PhD under William James), Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge. He served on the philosophical faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.

nodes.label: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche
variants: ティンレー・ノルブ・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche wearing a white shirt, red zen, pink curtain in background.jpg
nodes.summary: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje), and later founded the White Lotus School.

nodes.label: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist figure. He studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Thubten Chodron
nodes.summary: Thubten Chodron (born 1950) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery. She held positions at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey.

nodes.label: Daniel R. Tuzzeo
nodes.summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his graduate thesis research at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

nodes.label: George A. Keyworth
nodes.summary: George A. Keyworth works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed his PhD at UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, and Shuizhao Wang. He held posts at CU Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.

nodes.label: Ronald Egan
nodes.summary: Ronald Egan (b. 1948) is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held posts at Harvard (~1978–1987), Wellesley College, UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

nodes.label: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen
nodes.summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1991 and was attested as a research fellow there in 1996.

nodes.label: Namio Egami
nodes.summary: Namio Egami was a historian and archaeologist of Central Asian and Iranian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1927–1930), taught there (~1935–1967), and later served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Ulrike Roesler
nodes.summary: Ulrike Roesler works in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of Münster, she taught at Marburg and Freiburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Nalini Devdas
nodes.summary: Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at Concordia University under Leslie C. Orr and held an academic post at Carleton University.

nodes.label: Paul David Devanandan
nodes.summary: Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Nizam College, Presidency College, and Yale University, he taught philosophy and religions at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and directed CISRS beginning in 1956.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Gyatso
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Hozen Seki
nodes.summary: Hozen Seki (1904–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church, attested in 1998.

nodes.label: Susan Meinheit
nodes.summary: Susan Meinheit is a Tibetologist who held posts at the Library of Congress (attested in 1998 and 2007).

nodes.label: Sergey Oldenburg
variants: セルゲイ・フョードロウィッチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・フョードロヴィチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.jawiki: セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.description: Russian scholar of Sanskrit and Buddhism (1863-1934)
nodes.summary: Sergey Oldenburg specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Russian Academy of Sciences, the State Hermitage Museum, and the Asiatic Museum, which he founded.

nodes.label: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov
nodes.summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1920–1925) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1925–1933).

nodes.label: Jørn Borup
nodes.summary: Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (circa 1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, subsequently serving there as Associate Professor from circa 2007 to 2023.

nodes.label: Ian Reader
nodes.summary: Ian Reader (born 1949) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Leeds. He held positions at Kansai Gaidai, Kobe University of Commerce, Stirling, Hawaiʻi, Lancaster, and Manchester.

nodes.id: I:Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies
nodes.label: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies
variants: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies of Tribhuvan University

nodes.label: Michaela Haas
nodes.summary: Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Peter Schwieger, Jigme Namgyal, and Rechungpa, completing her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Jigme Namgyal
variants: ‘Jigs med rNam rgyal ‘Dzi sgar Kong sprul

nodes.label: Günter Grönbold
nodes.summary: Günter Grönbold is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He had a long career at the Bavarian State Library from around 1974 to 2008, where he served as head of the Oriental Section from around 1988 to 2008.

nodes.label: Rudolf Kaschewsky
nodes.summary: Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn. He held teaching posts in Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt and served as an academic councilor at Bonn (1974–2004).

nodes.label: Andreas Doctor
nodes.summary: Andreas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima, Tsikey Chokling, and Phakchok Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche
nodes.description: tibetan teacher and religious ritual master
nodes.summary: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at the Young Lamas Home School, he served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and sat on the board of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

nodes.label: Phakchok Rinpoche
nodes.description: Vajra Master of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling monastery
nodes.summary: Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (ca. 1997–2004), studied under numerous traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and served as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

nodes.label: Susan Niditch
nodes.summary: Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served as a faculty member in the religion department at Amherst College from ~1978 to 2020.

nodes.label: Tenzin L. Mullin
nodes.summary: Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar in religious studies and Japanology. Mullin completed a Master of Arts at the University of Otago under the supervision of Elizabeth Guthrie and primary supervisor Erica Baffelli.

nodes.label: Will Sweetman
nodes.description: professor of religion in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1993-1997), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

nodes.label: Dongchu
nodes.summary: Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1934–1945) and abbot at Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949).

nodes.label: Craig Preston
nodes.summary: Craig Preston works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Paul
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Paul works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann and was taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

nodes.label: Philadelphia Museum of Art
variants: フィラデルフィア美術館

nodes.label: David Jones
nodes.summary: David Jones, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. Attested in 2007, he was professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

nodes.id: I:Center for the Development of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Center for the Development of Asian Studies
variants: Center for the Development of Asian Studies

nodes.id: I:East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies
nodes.label: East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies
variants: East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies

nodes.label: Max Kaltenmark
nodes.summary: Max Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études sinologiques de Pékin (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), holding later posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris.

nodes.label: Léon Vandermeersch
nodes.summary: Léon Vandermeersch was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, Paris Law Faculty, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held positions at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE (1979–1993), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1981–1984), and directed the EFEO (1989–1993).

nodes.label: Wen-ling Jane
nodes.summary: Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a PhD at Columbia University, attested in 2009, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Geshe Lobsang Jamspal.

nodes.label: Kammie Morrison Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kammie Morrison Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned her PhD from the University of Virginia in 2009 under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama.

nodes.label: Sabine Löhr
nodes.summary: Sabine Löhr works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing an M.A. and doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at Hamburg.

nodes.label: Graham Lock
nodes.summary: Graham Lock is a scholar in the fields of linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

nodes.label: Robert Barnett
nodes.summary: Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Tibet University, Columbia University (1999–2018), SOAS University of London, and King's College London.

nodes.label: Arthur F. Buehler
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

nodes.label: Halle O'Neal
nodes.summary: Halle O'Neal specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas (attested 2011) under Sherry Fowler. As of 2026, she is Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Palden Sherab
nodes.summary: Palden Sherab was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).

nodes.label: David W. Tien
nodes.summary: David W. Tien is a sinologist and philosopher. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, where he earned his PhD under the supervision of James Robson (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Jim Rheingans
nodes.summary: Jim Rheingans, a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from the University of Hamburg, Bath Spa University, and University of the West of England. He holds posts attested in 2026 at the universities of Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney.

nodes.id: I:University of the West of England
nodes.label: University of the West of England
variants: University of the West of England, Bristol
University of the West of England

nodes.label: Stephen Suen
nodes.summary: Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Mark Unno
nodes.summary: Mark Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Oberlin College (~1977–1981) and Stanford University (~1987–1994), he has held posts at Brown University and the University of Oregon (assistant professor around 2000).

nodes.label: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir
nodes.summary: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.

nodes.label: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska
nodes.summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies who conducted research at the Universities of Oslo (1993) and Bonn (1995). She has held academic posts at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2008 and 2026.

nodes.label: Moscow State University
variants: Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies
Institute of Asian and African Studies

nodes.label: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz
nodes.summary: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yu Yan Pang
nodes.summary: Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

nodes.label: Miranda Shaw
nodes.summary: Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies under Masatoshi Nagatomi, was taught by Robert A. F. Thurman, and had Bratindra Nath Mukherjee as a postdoctoral mentor.

nodes.label: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
nodes.summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza studied theology at the Universities of Würzburg (1958–1962) and Münster (~1963–1970). She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (appointed 1988).

nodes.label: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee
nodes.description: Indian historian, numismatist, epigraphist and iconographist
nodes.summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) studied history and Indology at Calcutta, Cambridge, and SOAS, earning a doctorate under A. L. Basham. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

nodes.label: Sulak Sivaraksa
nodes.native: สุลักษณ์ ศิวรักษ์
nodes.summary: Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an author and activist in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Assumption College, Bangkok, and the University of Wales Lampeter, and held visiting posts at Berkeley, Harvard, Cornell, and Toronto.

nodes.label: Subhadradis Diskul
nodes.native: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล
variants: モムチャオ＝スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.image: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล.jpg
nodes.jawiki: スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.summary: Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL. He served as professor and rector at Silpakorn University and president of the Siam Society.

nodes.label: David Kerman Tomlinson
nodes.summary: David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2019) under Daniel A. Arnold, and held a post at Smith College.

nodes.label: Sven Wittemann
nodes.summary: Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Juichiro Tanabe
nodes.summary: Juichiro Tanabe studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000-2001) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

nodes.label: Bong Seok Joo
nodes.summary: Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying under Jacqueline I. Stone, Yang Lu, Lewis R. Lancaster, Ding-hwa Hsieh, and Morio Hamada.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Stout
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Brown University (~1968–1972) and Princeton University (PhD ~1972–1976), he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

nodes.label: Jann Ronis
nodes.summary: Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.

nodes.label: Faren
nodes.summary: Faren works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Faren completed a PhD at Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Wenbiao Mai
nodes.summary: Wenbiao Mai specializes in Indology and linguistics. Mai completed a PhD at Peking University and also studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University. In 2013, Mai was attested as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Zhonghui Cui
nodes.summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London, earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, and served as a teaching consultant there (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Christopher D. Emms
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2012–2026).

nodes.label: Jampa Samten
nodes.summary: Jampa Samten specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as Director (attested 2015) and later as a re-employed Professor (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Gin Ling Liu
nodes.summary: Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Kim Knott
nodes.summary: Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

nodes.label: Eleanor Nesbitt
nodes.summary: Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College and the University of Oxford, founded the Punjab Research Group, and became emerita professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989).

nodes.label: John Berthrong
nodes.summary: John Berthrong was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under graduate supervisor Alfonso Verdu. He held a post at Boston University from ca. 1989 to 2013.

nodes.label: Elizabeth J. Harris
nodes.summary: Elizabeth J. Harris earned her doctorate from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya (~1988–1993). Working in Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at Westminster College (attested 1996) and University of Birmingham (~2015).

nodes.label: Michael Harack
nodes.summary: Michael Harack is a scholar in religious studies and sinology. He earned his Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Defense Language Institute
variants: アメリカ陸軍の語学学校

nodes.label: Robert J. Topmiller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Topmiller was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Kentucky, where he studied under doctoral supervisor George C. Herring.

nodes.label: George C. Herring
nodes.image: Dr. George Herring, Alumni Professor of History Emeritus at the University of Kentucky 2015 (cropped).jpg

nodes.label: Jang-Kil Chun
nodes.summary: Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances Wilson.

nodes.label: Alexander Rödel
nodes.summary: Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2008) under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

nodes.label: University of Rhode Island
variants: ロードアイランド大学

nodes.label: Christian Matthias Boehm
nodes.summary: Christian Matthias Boehm specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) under the supervision of John T. Carpenter, and also studied under Toshifumi Konno.

nodes.label: Yongtong Tang
nodes.summary: Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Irving Babbitt and Charles Rockwell Lanman, he taught at Southeast, Nankai, and National Central universities before serving as professor and vice-president at Peking University.

nodes.label: UNESCO
variants: International Commission for a History of the Scientific and Cultural Development of Mankind

nodes.label: Hsueh-li Cheng
nodes.summary: Hsueh-li Cheng works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Ohio University from circa 1974 to 1976 and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo from circa 1976 to 2010.

nodes.label: Troy Organ
nodes.summary: Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (circa 1938–1941). He held positions at Chatham University (circa 1944–1945), Parsons College (circa 1945–1946), University of Akron (circa 1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

nodes.label: Surya Das
nodes.summary: Surya Das (1950–) is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University at Buffalo (~1968–1971) and trained under traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1980–1999).

nodes.label: Aristotle C. Dy
nodes.summary: Aristotle C. Dy specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: University of Miami
variants: University of Miami School of Medicine

nodes.label: University of Tehran
variants: Faculty of Political and Social Sciences in Tehran

nodes.label: Jacob Neusner
nodes.description: American scholar of Judaism and Rabbinic literature (1932–2016)
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee (~1961–1962), Brandeis (~1962–1964), the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

nodes.label: Kristin Scheible
nodes.summary: Kristin Scheible works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Colby College and Harvard under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey. She has held posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

nodes.label: Bruce Chilton
nodes.summary: Bruce Chilton is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (~1971–1977). He held a post at Yale University (~1985–1987) and served as a director at Bard College from around 1987.

nodes.label: Matthew Steven Mitchell
nodes.summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, the IUC, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015 under Richard M. Jaffe).

nodes.label: Richard M. Jaffe
nodes.summary: Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) before serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University from circa 2000.

nodes.label: Chong Go
nodes.summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Bongkil Chung
nodes.summary: Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts at Florida International University, including in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Woosung Huh
nodes.summary: Woosung Huh works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and served as a philosophy professor at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Patrick R. Uhlmann
nodes.summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he was attested as a PhD candidate in 2012, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Woncheol Yun
nodes.summary: Woncheol Yun works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jin Y. Park
nodes.summary: Jin Y. Park is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012).

nodes.label: E. D. Hirsch
nodes.image: E. D. Hirsch at Policy Exchange Education Lecture (3).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エリック・ドナルド・ハーシュ
nodes.summary: E. D. Hirsch is a philosopher and scholar educated at Metairie Park Country Day School and Cornell University (~1946–1950). He held academic posts at Wesleyan University (~1966–1969) and the University of Virginia (~1966–2012).

nodes.label: Pema Chödrön
nodes.summary: Pema Chödrön works in Buddhist studies. She was educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley, studied under Chime Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Chögyam Trungpa, and Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and served as director of Boulder Shambhala Center and abbess of Gampo Abbey.

nodes.label: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Khenpo Rinchen, and was a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

nodes.label: Geo Widengren
variants: ゲオ・ヴィデングレン
nodes.summary: Geo Widengren (1907–1996) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, earning his doctorate at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He held a professorship at Uppsala (1940–1973) and served as president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

nodes.label: Benoît Vermander
nodes.summary: Benoît Vermander (born 1960) is a Sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University as professor in 2009.

nodes.label: Taipei Ricci Institute
variants: Taipei Ricci Institute for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Chiko Corona
nodes.summary: Chiko Corona is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

nodes.label: Mikaël Bauer
nodes.summary: Mikaël Bauer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Paul Hoornaert, and earned his PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe. He is an associate professor at McGill University.
