nodes.label: Hyon Gak Sunim
nodes.summary: Hyon Gak Sunim (born 1964) is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Yale, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard, and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

nodes.label: Walther Heissig
variants: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.jawiki: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.summary: Walther Heissig (1913–2005) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, earning degrees at Vienna and Göttingen. He taught at Fu Jen and Peking University, later holding the Chair of the Central Asian seminar at Bonn from 1964.

nodes.label: Nicholas Poppe
nodes.summary: Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991), a linguist and Central Asian specialist, studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He was a professor at Saint Petersburg (1923, 1925–1941) and later served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Heidi Fjeld
nodes.summary: Heidi Fjeld is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Signe Howell. She later worked as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Ben Jiao
nodes.summary: Ben Jiao is a Tibetology and archaeology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University in 2001 under Melvyn C. Goldstein. As of 2008, he was Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Alexander Ong Hsu
nodes.summary: Alexander Ong Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2017) supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

nodes.label: Anthony C. Yu
nodes.description: American scholar of literature and religion (1938-2015)
nodes.summary: Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD around 1963–1969). He spent his career at the University of Chicago from around 1968 to 2005.

nodes.label: National Museum of Natural History
variants: National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution
Museum National d’Histoire Naturelle in Paris

nodes.label: Joan Halifax
nodes.summary: Joan Halifax is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tulane and Union Institute & University under teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Bernie Glassman. She worked at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and as a visiting scholar at the Library of Congress.

nodes.label: Ajahn Sucitto
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, later serving as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

nodes.label: Franz Aubrey Metcalf
nodes.summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

nodes.label: California State University, Los Angeles
variants: California State University at Los Angeles

nodes.label: Paul David Numrich
nodes.summary: Paul David Numrich is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he was attested at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

nodes.label: Ann Gleig
nodes.summary: Ann Gleig is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Geshe Losang Chödar
nodes.summary: Geshe Losang Chödar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics (both attested 2010).

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Everding
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and joined the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Sharma
nodes.summary: Shri Krishna Sharma worked in Indology and linguistics. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

nodes.label: John B. Cobb Jr.
nodes.summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago and founded the Center for Process Studies. He was attested in 1989 holding professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University.

nodes.label: John Hick
nodes.description: English philosopher of religion and theologian (1922-2012)
nodes.summary: John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies, having studied at Scarborough College, the University of Edinburgh, and Oriel College, Oxford. His career included posts at Cornell, Princeton Theological Seminary, Cambridge, the University of Birmingham (~1967–1982), and Claremont Graduate University (~1982–1992).

nodes.label: Joseph Prabhu
nodes.summary: Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Bernard Williams. He held posts at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held visiting professorships at United Theological College, UC Santa Barbara, and the Ecumenical Institute of Bossey.

nodes.label: Ecumenical Institute of Bossey
variants: Ecumenical Institute of the World Council of Churches

nodes.label: Sushanta Sen
nodes.summary: Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986, and served as a lecturer in Indian religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

nodes.label: Shinobu Arai Apple
nodes.summary: Shinobu Arai Apple is a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and academic adviser Robert Bickner.

nodes.label: Robert Warren Clark
nodes.summary: Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Daniel Aaron Getz
nodes.summary: Daniel Aaron Getz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has held a post as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kelsey Alise Seymour
nodes.summary: Kelsey Alise Seymour is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and held a visiting predoctoral fellowship at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.

nodes.label: Sue Hamilton
nodes.summary: Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and held a post at King's College London attested in 2001–2003.

nodes.label: Tsukasa Mizushima
nodes.summary: Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

nodes.label: Ankur Barua
nodes.summary: Ankur Barua is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong under Dorothy C. Wong. He held a post at the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Dorothy C. Wong
nodes.summary: Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She has held posts as a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and as affiliate faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Randall Studstill
nodes.summary: Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was educated under the instruction of Irene Woodward and Steven D. Goodman, and completed doctoral research under the supervision of Richard Payne.

nodes.label: Chisan Kohō
nodes.summary: Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He directed the Saijō-ji and Nagano training monasteries, served as abbot at Sōji-ji (circa 1944–1967), and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

nodes.label: Maurine Stuart
nodes.summary: Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba, under Nadia Boulanger, and with traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani, Eido Shimano, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of Cambridge Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Eido Shimano
nodes.summary: Eido Shimano was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, and attended the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and master at New York Zendo Shobo-ji.

nodes.label: Gesshin Myoko Prabhasa Dharma Cheney
nodes.summary: Gesshin Myoko Prabhasa Dharma Cheney was a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1967) and Seikaku Hirata.

nodes.label: Seikaku Hirata
nodes.summary: Seikaku Hirata worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, and also studied under Bokuo Seki. He later held a post at Hanazono University from around 1969 to 1994.

nodes.label: Shi Yong Hua
nodes.summary: Shi Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Hyoung Seok Ham
nodes.summary: Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

nodes.label: Kyu-Eon Jang
nodes.summary: Kyu-Eon Jang works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Jang has held posts as an HK research professor at Geumgang University (attested 2015) and as a professor at Peking University.

nodes.label: Charles H. Long
nodes.description: African-American cultural historian and religious studies scholar (1926–2020)
nodes.summary: Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar educated at Dunbar Junior College and the University of Chicago (PhD 1962). He held posts at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill, Duke (~1974–1987), Syracuse (~1987–1991), and UC Santa Barbara (~1991–1996).

nodes.label: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
nodes.summary: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Yoshihiro Hayashi
nodes.summary: Yoshihiro Hayashi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Ritsumeikan University
variants: 立命館大学総合心理学部
立命館大学白川静記念東洋文字文化研究所
立命館大学国際関係学部

nodes.label: Erik Braun
nodes.summary: Erik Braun is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He held a faculty post at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Wendy Palace
nodes.summary: Wendy Palace is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. Palace earned a PhD at Durham University under the doctoral supervision of David Sweet.

nodes.label: Anagarika Munindra
nodes.summary: Anagarika Munindra worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

nodes.label: Philip Novak
nodes.summary: Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Syracuse University and the University of Notre Dame. He became a teacher at Dominican University of California around 1980.

nodes.label: Zuigan Goto
nodes.summary: Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1900–1914), later serving as president of Hanazono University (1932).

nodes.label: Dominic Sur
nodes.summary: Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chonam, and held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Prasarn Lao-areun
nodes.summary: Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Shrivatsa Goswami
nodes.summary: Shrivatsa Goswami (born 1950) studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he later taught philosophy and religion. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University, founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana, and held an attested post at Vrindaban Research Institute.

nodes.label: Sylvie Hureau
nodes.summary: Sylvie Hureau is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Trevor Leggett
nodes.summary: Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (circa 1946–1970) and lectured for the Buddhist Society.

nodes.label: Tibetan Children's Villages
variants: Central Tibetan Children's Village (TCV) school in Dharamsala

nodes.label: Jack C. Laughlin
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Jack C. Laughlin earned his PhD at McMaster University (-1999) and held a post at the University of Sudbury.

nodes.label: Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho
nodes.summary: Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

nodes.label: Takeo Hibino
nodes.summary: Takeo Hibino was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He worked at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (1948–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980) as professor and president.

nodes.label: Abigail I. MacBain
nodes.summary: Abigail I. MacBain works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald. As of 2026, she holds a post at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Flavio Geisshuesler
nodes.summary: Flavio Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD ~2013–2019 under David Germano), holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019, attested 2026) and the University of Sydney (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Farzand Ali Durrani
nodes.summary: Farzand Ali Durrani (1933–2003) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of the Punjab, University of Peshawar (~1954–1958), and University of London (~1961–1964), and was a professor at the University of Peshawar (~1958–1993).

nodes.label: Yu-min Lee
nodes.summary: Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed graduate studies under John C. Huntington. Lee served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Yaping Dou
nodes.summary: Yaping Dou works in religious and Buddhist studies. Dou completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xue Yu (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Steffen Döll
nodes.summary: Steffen Döll works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich, where he was an assistant (2008–2015), and became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

nodes.label: Stefania Travagnin
nodes.image: Stefania Travagnin in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) before joining SOAS University of London in ~2020.

nodes.label: Koen Wellens
nodes.summary: Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned a PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.

nodes.label: Yuguang Liu
nodes.summary: Yuguang Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Samten, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Jialuo, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).

nodes.label: James H. Austin
nodes.summary: James H. Austin is a specialist in Buddhist studies. He trained under Katsujo Terayama and Nanrei Sohaku Kobori (~1974–1992), and held neurology posts at the University of Oregon/OHSU (~1960–1967) and the University of Colorado (~1967–1992).

nodes.label: Carmen Blacker
variants: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.jawiki: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.summary: Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) worked in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Oxford, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge and president of The Folklore Society (1982–1984).

nodes.label: Shigeru Gorai
nodes.summary: Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, later holding posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, and Otani University (1955–1978).

nodes.label: Vladimir Tikhonov
nodes.image: Prof. Vladimir Tikhonov (Pak Noja) San-Peterbur Khanon-214.jpg
nodes.summary: Vladimir Tikhonov is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Korea, and Moscow State universities under Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, and later held posts at Kyung Hee University and the University of Oslo (Professor from 2006).

nodes.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
variants: International Affairs Office of Dharma Drum Mountain
International Cultural and Educational Foundation of Dharma Drum Mountain

nodes.label: Hyejeong Choi
nodes.summary: Hyejeong Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 2015) and served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara
variants: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture

nodes.label: Karl Brunnhölzl
nodes.summary: Karl Brunnhölzl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He received his training under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, 10th Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Lama Thubten.

nodes.label: Tenga Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery, founded Benchen Monastery in 1976, and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1962–1979).

nodes.label: Ringu Tulku
nodes.summary: Ringu Tulku is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His teachers included Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and he has taught at Naropa University.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
variants: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
Max-Planck-Institut zur Erforschung multireligiöser und multiethnischer Gesellschaften

nodes.label: Peter van der Veer
nodes.summary: Peter van der Veer is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Groningen and Utrecht. He held chairs at Amsterdam and Utrecht and was Director of the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity (~2007–2021).

nodes.label: Polish Academy of Sciences
variants: Committee on Oriental Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: John M. Rosenfield
variants: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド3世
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド
nodes.summary: John M. Rosenfield worked in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Berkeley, SMU, Iowa, and Harvard under Benjamin Rowland, he taught at Iowa, UCLA, and Harvard (1965–1991), where he also curated at the Harvard Art Museums.

nodes.label: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā
nodes.summary: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned her Doctor of Philosophy from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.

nodes.label: Toshiichi Endo
nodes.summary: Toshiichi Endo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and earned a doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 1995 under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

nodes.label: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit
nodes.summary: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (1939–1999) worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded as Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.

nodes.label: Tara Doyle
nodes.summary: Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She served at Emory University as a lecturer in religious studies and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003), later becoming Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jared Rhoton
nodes.summary: Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Richard D. McBride II
nodes.summary: Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at UCLA, was mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Seiichi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Seiichi Mizuno worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, later serving as an assistant professor and researcher at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, and professor at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Toshio Nagahiro
nodes.summary: Toshio Nagahiro was a historian, archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He held positions at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (circa 1955–1968), and Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Lucy Annette Jones
nodes.summary: Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University, where she was supervised by Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

nodes.label: Edith Wyschogrod
nodes.summary: Edith Wyschogrod (1930–2009) worked in philosophy and religious studies. She earned degrees from Hunter College and Columbia University, and served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.

nodes.label: Helena Michie
nodes.summary: Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania between 1979 and 1984. She held a post at Rice University beginning around 1990.

nodes.label: John Vincent Bellezza
nodes.summary: John Vincent Bellezza specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under tutor Yungdrung Tenzin and teacher Tshering Choephel, and was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

nodes.label: Konchok Gyatso
nodes.summary: Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an affiliation with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Zayn Kassam
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Zayn Kassam held multiple roles at Pomona College, including department chair, Associate Dean for DEI, and John Knox McLean Professor of Religious Studies (1995). She also directed the Pacific Basin Institute and served as director of the Institute of Ismaili Studies in 2023.

nodes.label: MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
variants: Lutheran School of Theology in Oslo
MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society

nodes.label: Paul W. Kroll
nodes.summary: Paul W. Kroll (born 1948) is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan from circa 1971 to 1976. He served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chairman at the University of Colorado Boulder between 1979 and 1989.

nodes.label: Anna M. Shields
nodes.image: Anna M. Shields (born 1966) at the Center for Chinese Studies Annual Lim Lecture.png
nodes.summary: Anna M. Shields is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015), and Princeton University (~2015).

nodes.label: Jonathan Karam Skaff
nodes.summary: Jonathan Karam Skaff studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and Xiaofu Wang, and earned a PhD at Michigan. A scholar of sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history, he joined Shippensburg University and the Institute for Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Douglas Allen
nodes.summary: Douglas Allen is a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt universities. His posts include Southern Illinois University Carbondale, Central Connecticut State, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2020.

nodes.id: I:State University of New York at Oneonta
nodes.label: State University of New York at Oneonta
variants: Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality at SUNY Oneonta

nodes.label: Rawi Bhavilai
nodes.native: ระวี ภาวิไล
variants: ラウィー・パーウィライ
nodes.summary: Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and physics who studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University. He was a physics professor (1945–1986) and director (attested 2002) at Chulalongkorn University.

nodes.label: Gary Snyder
nodes.jawiki: ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.summary: Gary Snyder (b. 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and other fields. He studied at Reed College, UC Berkeley, and with traditional teachers Isshu Miura and Sesso Oda, later serving as professor at the University of California, Davis from 1986.

nodes.label: Enamul Haque
nodes.summary: Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka and Oxford (PhD). He directed the Bangladesh National Museum (1962–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art, ICOM, and Independent University, Bangladesh.

nodes.label: Matthew W. King
nodes.summary: Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (ending 2014) under the supervision of Frances Garrett.

nodes.label: Natalie Rothman
nodes.summary: Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She held a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

nodes.label: Marylin Martin Rhie
nodes.summary: Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology who was mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She held a professorship at Smith College (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Pramod Chandra
nodes.summary: Pramod Chandra specialized in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College, Georgetown University, and the University of Mumbai. He served as professor at the University of Chicago (1971–1980) and Harvard University (1980–2004).

nodes.label: Richard Foltz
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・フォルツ
nodes.summary: Richard Foltz (born 1961) works in Iranian, religious, and historical studies. He studied at the University of Utah and Harvard (PhD ~1996), taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida, and became Founding Director of Concordia University's Centre for Iranian Studies (~2006–2026).

nodes.label: Louise Child
nodes.summary: Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under traditional teacher Ringu Tulku, and taught at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Linda Hogan
nodes.summary: Linda Hogan (born 1964) is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Trinity College Dublin in 1991. She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, where she was appointed Chair of Ecumenics and Vice-Provost.

nodes.label: Tyler Dewar
nodes.summary: Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and with traditional teachers Tashi Wangchuk, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Mettanando Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

nodes.label: Franz Xaver Erhard
nodes.summary: Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist. He completed his MA studies at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned his PhD from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Noa Gal
nodes.summary: Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the doctoral supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
variants: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
Buddhist and Pali College in Singapore

nodes.label: Julian Schott
nodes.summary: Julian Schott works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His attested academic posts include research fellow at the University of Hamburg (2026) and faculty member at the University of Vienna (2026).

nodes.label: Lama Jabb
nodes.summary: Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist. He served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and held the post of Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Andrew P. Tuck
nodes.summary: Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton III.

nodes.label: Huaiyu Chen
nodes.summary: Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later serving as assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (circa 2007–2013).

nodes.label: Sally McAra
nodes.summary: Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she was supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

nodes.label: Karen Nero
nodes.description: professor of education in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Karen Nero has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago, and she taught Sally McAra.

nodes.label: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung
nodes.summary: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

nodes.label: Nikolai Solmsdorf
nodes.summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and Alexander von Rospatt. He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Martin Lowenthal
nodes.summary: Martin Lowenthal works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and he has held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Signe Howell
nodes.summary: Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1972–1974) and the University of Oxford (~1975–1980). She was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

nodes.label: René Gothóni
nodes.summary: René Gothóni is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1971 to 1982 and held an academic post there from circa 1975 to 2014.

nodes.label: Simo Knuuttila
nodes.description: Finnish professor (emeritus) of theological ethics and the philosophy of religion at the University of Helsinki, academy professor (Academy of Finland)
nodes.summary: Simo Knuuttila was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (1976), where he served as Professor from ~1981 to 2014, and held a post at the Academy of Finland (1994–2004).

nodes.label: Michael Pye
nodes.summary: Michael Pye is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies who earned degrees from Cambridge and Leeds. He held teaching posts at Leeds and Lancaster, a professorship at the University of Marburg (1982–2004), and a visiting professorship at Otani University.

nodes.label: Hung-Yi Yang
nodes.summary: Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Sydney, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Roy Tzohar
nodes.summary: Roy Tzohar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2005) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2005–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He took up a post at Tel Aviv University around 2011.

nodes.label: V. P. Bhatta
nodes.summary: V. P. Bhatta is a scholar of Indology and linguistics based at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he has headed the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and served as Professor-Editor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Penghao Sun
nodes.summary: Penghao Sun specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He completed his doctoral studies under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, having also studied under scholars including Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Jay Jasanoff, and Qingying Chen (2009–2011).

nodes.label: Kuntala Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra (attested 2009). She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Prabal Kumar Sen
nodes.summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as professor in 2009.

nodes.label: Yoshinori Takeuchi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of religion and philosopher (1913-2002)
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1946) under Hajime Tanabe. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988), and joined the Japan Academy in 1995.

nodes.label: Shu-chen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Karen Christina Lang, Bradley Reed, and Ronald G. Dimberg, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

nodes.label: Soorakkulame Pemarathana
nodes.summary: Soorakkulame Pemarathana is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Saranindranath Tagore.

nodes.label: Joy Brennan
nodes.summary: Joy Brennan works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. She earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, where she studied under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard A. Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

nodes.label: Paul Mendes-Flohr
nodes.summary: Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history. After earning his doctorate at Brandeis University, he served as a director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and as a professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Zhiyi Yang
nodes.summary: Zhiyi Yang specializes in Sinology. After undergraduate studies at Peking University, she earned her PhD at Princeton University under Martin Kern, and has held posts at the International Consortium for Research in the Humanities and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuharu Mizuno
nodes.summary: Kazuharu Mizuno is a geography and Tibetology scholar who studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc, ~1990). He became a professor in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University around 2009.

nodes.label: Martha C. Nussbaum
nodes.summary: Martha C. Nussbaum (b. 1947) is a philosopher educated at NYU and Harvard, where she studied under Bernard Williams. Her career includes faculty posts at Harvard, Brown, and the University of Chicago, where she became a distinguished service professor in 1995.

nodes.label: Yasuo Yuasa
nodes.summary: Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Tetsuro Watsuji and at the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Tokyo, Yamanashi, Osaka, Tsukuba (1981–1989), and J. F. Oberlin University.

nodes.summary: Inyoung Chung works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Seunghak Koh
nodes.summary: Seunghak Koh specializes in Buddhist studies. Koh earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and served as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: James Legge
nodes.summary: James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College (~1836–1839). He served as Professor at the University of Oxford beginning in 1876.

nodes.label: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under numerous masters, including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, becoming abbot of Palpung Sherabling Monastery around 1998.

nodes.label: Sarah Harding
nodes.summary: Sarah Harding works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (1972) and Lama Tenpa. She was a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2001) and taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018).

nodes.label: Lars Fogelin
nodes.summary: Lars Fogelin is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, later holding positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Lilla Russell-Smith
nodes.summary: Lilla Russell-Smith is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and earned her PhD from SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Anne Farrer
nodes.summary: Anne Farrer is a scholar of sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She served as Assistant Keeper in the Department of Oriental Antiquities at the British Museum and held a post at Sotheby's Institute of Art (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Wenjie Duan
nodes.summary: Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1945), he held multiple posts at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946, serving as its director in 1991.

nodes.label: Helen Wang
nodes.summary: Helen Wang specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London from around 1984 to 1988 and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.

nodes.label: Jennifer Jung-Kim
nodes.summary: Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Her academic career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she served as assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: David A. Hall
nodes.summary: David A. Hall studied under Shōshin Ichishima and earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and Chair of Science, Engineering and Technology at Montgomery College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Guy G. Stroumsa
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Lycée Voltaire, ENIO, University of Paris, Hebrew University, Harvard, and EPHE. A founder of Hebrew University, he held posts there (1978–2009), at the University of Oxford (2009–2013), and Lady Margaret Hall (~2009).

nodes.label: Heather Stoddard
nodes.summary: Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology, sinology, and history and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London and under D. C. Lau, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas.

nodes.label: John Daishin Buksbazen
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Buksbazen studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao.

nodes.label: Bernie Glassman
nodes.summary: Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He earned degrees from NYU and UCLA, and studied under traditional teachers Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

nodes.label: Soiku Shigematsu
nodes.summary: Soiku Shigematsu (b. 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He was professor of English Literature at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and professor at Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Tuyet
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who received a PhD from Punjabi University (attested 2012) under Inder Mohan Singh, having also studied under Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.

nodes.label: Wei Lin
nodes.summary: Wei Lin works in sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University (PhD attested 2007), she has held appointments at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan University, University of Michigan, and Transylvania University.

nodes.label: Dagmar Schwerk
nodes.summary: Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg from 2007 to 2017 under Dorji Wangchuk. She became a professor at Leipzig University around 2022.

nodes.label: Eva Wilden
nodes.summary: Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2004). She served as Maître de conférences at the EFEO (2003) and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

nodes.label: Julie A. Gifford
nodes.summary: Julie A. Gifford, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an attested post at Miami University in 2011.

nodes.label: Scott A. Mitchell
nodes.summary: Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne and has held professorial and presidential appointments at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.

nodes.label: Marybeth White
nodes.summary: Marybeth White is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed a double major honors degree at York University and became a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Araki
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Araki specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD in 2013, at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University and Osaka University, and served as Professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

nodes.label: Margarita Kleibel
nodes.summary: Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

nodes.label: Siu-tong Kwan
nodes.summary: Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where he was supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Zhihua Yao.

nodes.label: Marc-Henri Deroche
nodes.summary: Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein, having also studied with Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: In-gun Kang
nodes.summary: In-gun Kang is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, and under Michael Barnes at Heythrop College, University of London.

nodes.label: Aloysius Pieris
nodes.summary: Aloysius Pieris, a religious and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from London, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg, among other institutions. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre from 1974 and held visiting chairs at several theological institutes.

nodes.label: Stanley Abe
nodes.summary: Stanley Abe is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

nodes.label: Wei-Cheng Lin
nodes.summary: Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he joined the faculty at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Rafał Felbur
nodes.summary: Rafał Felbur works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University, studying under Paul Harrison, John R. McRae, and Luis O. Gómez.

nodes.label: Vincent Lefèvre
nodes.summary: Vincent Lefèvre works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes, completed his habilitation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 2007 under Bruno Dagens, and served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

nodes.label: Jean-François Jarrige
nodes.summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the École du Louvre and the University of Paris. He served as director (1986–2004) and museum president (~1986–2008) at the Guimet Museum.

nodes.label: Namita Das
nodes.summary: Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her Ph.D. at Gauhati University under the doctoral supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

nodes.label: Alexander Coburn Soper
nodes.summary: Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Hamilton College and Princeton University (Ph.D. 1944), he taught at Bryn Mawr College, became a professor at New York University in 1960, and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

nodes.label: Edwin Francis Bryant
nodes.summary: Edwin Francis Bryant works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1990–1997), taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003), and was appointed Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

nodes.label: Koenraad Elst
nodes.summary: Koenraad Elst works in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992) and earned an MA from KU Leuven (completed by 1998).

nodes.label: Braj Basi Lal
nodes.summary: Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Allahabad University and trained under Mortimer Wheeler (1943). He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

nodes.label: Diane A. Lichtenstein
nodes.summary: Diane A. Lichtenstein completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She held positions as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Jim G. Shaffer
nodes.summary: Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his B.A. from Arizona State University (~1961–1965), his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1972), and served as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1975–2017).

nodes.label: Chris Clark
nodes.summary: Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon, where he was attested as an honorary associate in 2019.

nodes.label: Amod Jayant Lele
nodes.summary: Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

nodes.label: Rudolf G. Wagner
nodes.summary: Rudolf G. Wagner was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Bonn, Munich, Paris, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (~1972–1987) and Heidelberg University (~1987–2019), including its Cluster of Excellence (~2007–2012).

nodes.label: Andrew William Kennedy
nodes.summary: Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

nodes.label: Philip A. Mellor

nodes.label: Marianne Pieper

nodes.label: Seong-Uk Kim
nodes.summary: Seong-Uk Kim specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr. for doctoral studies, Kim was Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Eviatar Shulman
nodes.summary: Eviatar Shulman is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1998–2008). He became chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion there in 2009.

nodes.label: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul
nodes.summary: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He worked as a researcher at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Huishan Lin
nodes.summary: Huishan Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Lin completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Guowei Liu, and also studied under teachers Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.

nodes.label: Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā
nodes.summary: Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā works in Buddhist studies. She served as an Assistant Researcher at Dharma Drum Buddhist College (attested 2012) and held a post at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Jeff Shore
nodes.summary: Jeff Shore works in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1991 to 2019, later becoming professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah
nodes.summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah studied under Bryce Ryan at the University of Ceylon, and earned his PhD at Cornell. He held academic posts at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and served as professor of anthropology at Harvard (1976-2001).

nodes.label: Peter J. Wilson
nodes.summary: Peter J. Wilson earned his PhD from Yale University (~1956–1961), where he taught from ~1961 to 1963. He later taught at Vassar College, the University of Washington, Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1973–1999).

nodes.label: Linda Penkower
nodes.summary: Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993 and was a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Don Alvin Pittman
nodes.summary: Don Alvin Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago. He served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

nodes.label: Chun-min Yen
nodes.summary: Chun-min Yen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello, teacher Todd Brown, and traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Stephen A. Murphy
nodes.summary: Stephen A. Murphy is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA and doctoral studies under Elizabeth H. Moore at SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Masamichi Sakai

nodes.label: Takami Inoue

nodes.label: Imre Hamar
nodes.summary: Imre Hamar is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University (~2006) and director of its Confucius Institute (2006).

nodes.summary: Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied as a PhD student at Eötvös Loránd University under advisor Masanori Yamaji and teachers Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

nodes.label: G. V. Aston
nodes.summary: G. V. Aston specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy from the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under doctoral supervisor B. Jack Copeland and teacher Paul Harrison.

nodes.label: Pori Park

nodes.label: Cornelis Jan Kuiken

nodes.label: Colette Sciberras
nodes.summary: Colette Sciberras works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
