nodes.label: D. C. Lau
nodes.summary: Sinologist and philosopher D. C. Lau studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow. He held appointments at SOAS, University College London, and the University of London, before serving as Chair at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Jeannine Auboyer
nodes.summary: Jeannine Auboyer worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at École du Louvre, EPHE, University of Paris, and under Philippe Stern and Paul Pelliot, later serving at the Guimet Museum (1936; 1965–1980) and CNRS (~1952–1977).

nodes.label: Mauli Chand Prasad
nodes.summary: Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who earned his doctorate from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. In 1984, he was attested as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

nodes.label: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger
nodes.summary: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Mark Teeuwen
nodes.summary: Mark Teeuwen (b. 1966) specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and was appointed professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

nodes.label: Martino Dibeltulo
nodes.summary: Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also been mentored by Ester Bianchi.

nodes.label: Gary Urton
nodes.summary: Gary Urton works in history, archaeology, and related fields. He studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held posts at Colgate University and Harvard University, alongside a visiting post at EHESS.

nodes.label: Hongyue Guo
nodes.summary: Hongyue Guo, working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied under Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp.

nodes.label: Yawen Yang
nodes.summary: Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Yang studied at Fo Guang University, completing an MA under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Patricia Berger
nodes.summary: Patricia Berger is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, where she became Professor Emerita. She also worked at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco and the Numata Center.

nodes.label: Cynthia Col
nodes.summary: Cynthia Col specializes in religious studies, sinology, and tibetology. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

nodes.label: Yongshan He
nodes.summary: Yongshan He works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at McMaster University, where he was supervised by James A. Benn and also studied under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Joseph A. Marino
nodes.summary: Joseph A. Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017) under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, and held a post as assistant professor at the same university (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christian Lee Novetzke
nodes.summary: Christian Lee Novetzke specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia University, he taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and became Director of the South Asia Center at the University of Washington in 2007.

nodes.label: John Hurrell Crook
nodes.summary: John Hurrell Crook studied at Southampton, Cambridge, and under Sheng Yen, working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at the University of Bristol (~1963–1989), held a fellowship at CASBS (~1968–1969), and was affiliated with the Université Bouddhique Européenne.

nodes.label: Université Bouddhique Européenne
variants: Groupe de Recherches et d'Etudes sur le Zen of the Universite Bouddhique Europeene

nodes.label: Akong Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he served as abbot (attested 2009).

nodes.id: I:Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre
nodes.label: Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre
variants: サムエ・リン瞑想センター

nodes.label: Zaifu Liu
nodes.summary: Zaifu Liu (1941–2026) studied at Xiamen University and worked in Sinology. He directed the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1985–1989) and lectured at the University of Chicago, Stockholm University, and the University of Colorado Boulder.

nodes.label: Junko Minamoto
nodes.summary: Junko Minamoto is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who completed a master's at Ryukoku University and doctoral coursework at Otani University. Minamoto held a post as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.

nodes.label: Baatr U. Kitinov
nodes.summary: Baatr U. Kitinov is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

nodes.label: Peoples' Friendship University of Russia
variants: Peoples' Friendship at University of Russia in Moscow

nodes.label: Uranchimeg Tsultem
nodes.summary: Uranchimeg Tsultem specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and UC Berkeley (PhD ~2003–2009), later holding posts at Berkeley, National University of Mongolia, Yonsei, and Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Uranchimeg Borjigd Ujeed
nodes.summary: Uranchimeg Borjigd Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and served as a research associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Ngagyur Nyingma Institute
variants: Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in Bylakuppe, Mysore

nodes.label: Ayako Nakamura-Walbeck
nodes.summary: Ayako Nakamura-Walbeck specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she also served as a research fellow (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Alicia Turner
nodes.summary: Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under supervisors Steven Collins and Bruce Lincoln, also studying under Saw Tun, Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

nodes.label: Than Than Win
nodes.native: သန်းသန်းဝင်း

nodes.label: Northern Illinois University
variants: Center for Burma Studies, Northern Illinois University

nodes.label: Yoel Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and earned a PhD from Kyoto University. He was a professor at the University of Haifa (~1983–2003).

nodes.label: Richard Barron
nodes.summary: Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul III.

nodes.label: Ajahn Amaro
nodes.summary: Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho after graduating from Bedford College. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) before becoming abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.

nodes.label: Terry Kleeman
nodes.description: professor of religious studies; scholar of Daoism
nodes.summary: Terry Kleeman is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his studies at the University of British Columbia (~1981–1988) and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.

nodes.label: Hank Glassman
nodes.summary: Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has been a faculty member at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

nodes.label: Ryan Matthew Jacobson
nodes.summary: Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Master of Arts in Religious Studies at Naropa University, where his teachers included Judith Simmer-Brown, D. Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, and Jirka Hladis.

nodes.label: Amelia Hall
nodes.summary: Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford in 2012. Her appointments include Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online religious studies faculty at Central Michigan University.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Allione
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Allione is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner and author. She earned a master's degree from Antioch University and studied under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Apho Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu.

nodes.label: Elijah Sacvan Ary
nodes.summary: Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University, completing his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and studied under Geshe Karma Sonam.

nodes.label: St Bartholomew's Hospital Medical College
variants: St Bartholomew's Medical School, London University

nodes.label: Cynthea J. Bogel
nodes.summary: Cynthea J. Bogel works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Katharina Sabernig
nodes.summary: Katharina Sabernig is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017. She has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Medical University of Vienna
variants: Center for Public Health, Medical University of Vienna

nodes.label: Do Ngak Kunphen Ling
variants: DNKL Tibetan Buddhist Center for Universal Peace (Redding, CT)

nodes.id: I:Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies
variants: Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies (Ithaca, NY)

nodes.label: Claudia Weber
nodes.summary: Claudia Weber is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit as her teacher and Gregor Ahn as her project supervisor.

nodes.label: Gregor Ahn
nodes.summary: Gregor Ahn (born 1958) studied at Copenhagen and Bonn, completing his PhD and Habilitation under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. Working in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he taught at Münster, Tartu, and served as professor at Heidelberg University (1996–2025).

nodes.label: Fa Yao
nodes.summary: Fa Yao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). He is attested as a visiting lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Michael Hookham
nodes.summary: Michael Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

nodes.label: Fred Pfeil
nodes.summary: Fred Pfeil earned degrees from Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at Stanford, Stephens College (~1975–1983), Oregon State University (~1983–1985), and Trinity College (~1985–2005).

nodes.label: Gary Goh Wee Kian
nodes.summary: Gary Goh Wee Kian specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisor Hui-Chieh Loy, foster supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

nodes.label: Amber D. Carpenter
nodes.summary: Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under teachers including M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte. Her appointments include posts at the University of York, University of St Andrews, and an associate professorship at Yale-NUS College.

nodes.label: Rachael Wiseman
nodes.summary: Philosopher Rachael Wiseman studied at the University of York. Around 2013, she served as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

nodes.label: Bronwyn Finnigan
nodes.summary: Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, she studied under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop, and held posts at Auckland, Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

nodes.label: Christopher Kelley
nodes.summary: Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia University and has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

nodes.label: Trine Brox
nodes.summary: Trine Brox is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer. She was attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Copenhagen in 2026.

nodes.label: Heidi I. Koppl
nodes.summary: Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer, and also studied under Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.

nodes.label: Eugen Pander
nodes.summary: Eugen Pander was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga. In 1881, he held a post at Tongwen Guan as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.

nodes.label: Qiang Ning
nodes.summary: Qiang Ning is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies who was supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter. He has held positions at the Dunhuang Academy, San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Shuhong Chang
nodes.summary: Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) studied in China and France, including at the École des Beaux-Arts. He taught at Zhejiang University, the Central Academy of Fine Arts, and the National Academy of Art, and long directed the Dunhuang Academy.

nodes.label: Ives Waldo
nodes.summary: Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988), and taught David P. Jackson.

nodes.id: I:Starr King School for the Ministry
nodes.label: Starr King School for the Ministry
variants: Starr King School for the Ministry

nodes.label: Wing-tsit Chan
nodes.summary: Wing-tsit Chan worked in philosophy and sinology, studying at Harvard (~1924–1929). He held positions at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1937–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

nodes.label: Brandon J. Harwood
nodes.summary: Brandon J. Harwood earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015), where he studied under advisors Patrick Arthur Pranke and John Gibson.

nodes.label: Patrick Arthur Pranke
nodes.summary: Patrick Arthur Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor Lieberman.

nodes.label: Andree Dominique Messent
nodes.summary: Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Messent completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams, also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

nodes.label: Tan Poh Beng
nodes.summary: Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College, where he studied under Charles Willemen, Tilak Kariyawasam, Sumanasiri, and Shengshou.

nodes.label: Ayya Khema
nodes.summary: Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Phra Khantipalo, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

nodes.label: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh
nodes.native: ฉัตรสุมาลย์ กบิลสิงห์
nodes.summary: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University, and taught in Thammasat University's Department of Philosophy and Religion (~1973–2000).

nodes.label: John D'Arcy May
nodes.summary: A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, May completed a doctorate in theology at the University of Münster in 1975. He later held academic appointments at Trinity College Dublin, including Associate Professor of Interfaith Dialogue and Professor at the Irish School of Ecumenics.

nodes.label: Thích Thiện Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued higher education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1972–1977).

nodes.id: I:Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue
nodes.label: Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue
variants: Tulana-Forschungszentrum (Tulana Research Center for Encounter and Dialogue)
Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue

nodes.label: Hla Pe
nodes.summary: A linguist, Hla Pe studied at the University of Yangon (~1931–1938), University College London (~1938–1939), and SOAS (~1940–1944). At SOAS, he taught Burmese language and culture from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.

nodes.label: Dungkar Lozang Trinlé
nodes.summary: Dungkar Lozang Trinlé (1927–1997) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Yönten. He held posts at Minzu University (~1960–1965), Tibet University (~1985–1997), and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (~1985–1997).

nodes.label: Gisela Emma Full
nodes.summary: Gisela Emma Full is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. She studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster and served as a research fellow at the University of Frankfurt (Oder) and the Samueli Institute (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Samueli Institute
variants: Samueli-Institute of Brain, Mind and Healing

nodes.label: Mingyu Fu
nodes.summary: Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist Association of the United States
nodes.label: Buddhist Association of the United States
variants: Buddhist Association of the United States

nodes.label: Joey Hung
nodes.summary: Joey Hung is a computational and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College and serves as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Vidya Dehejia
nodes.summary: Vidya Dehejia works in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1963–1968), later holding positions at the Smithsonian Institution and Columbia University (associate professor 1982; endowed chair 2002).

nodes.label: American Museum of Natural History
variants: アメリカ自然史博物館

nodes.label: James Miller
nodes.summary: James Miller is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge (-1997) and a Ph.D. from Boston University (-2000), and served as Professor at Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Emily T. Yeh
nodes.summary: Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist. She studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the faculty of the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

nodes.label: Surendra Man Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

nodes.label: Yungfen Ma
nodes.summary: Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Ma completed a PhD at Columbia University, studying under Chun-fang Yu.

nodes.label: Paul Debes
nodes.summary: Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), where he was a board member, and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955), and taught Hellmuth Hecker.

nodes.label: Hari Shankar Prasad
nodes.summary: Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ramakant Tripathi, completing his doctorate under Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Mark Andrew Nathan
nodes.summary: Mark Andrew Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and has held positions at UCLA, Samcheok National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Leopold Pospisil
nodes.summary: Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956-1993).

nodes.label: Harold C. Conklin
nodes.summary: Harold C. Conklin (1926–2016) was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University. He taught at Columbia University and Yale University (1962–1996), also serving as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History.

nodes.label: Mirjan Damaška
nodes.summary: Mirjan Damaška studied law at the University of Zagreb, the Hague Academy of International Law, the Faculté Internationale de Droit Comparé, and the University of Ljubljana (PhD 1960). His career included professorships at the University of Pennsylvania and Yale University.

nodes.label: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak
nodes.summary: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the University of Paris, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He was a lecturer and then Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Fu-shih Lin
nodes.summary: Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a long-term post at Academia Sinica (~1994-2021).

nodes.label: Hwansoo Kim
nodes.summary: Hwansoo Kim is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He has held appointments as a professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Helena Blankleder
nodes.summary: Helena Blankleder works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Marek Zemánek
nodes.summary: Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Tu
nodes.image: TT. Thích Nhật Từ phát biểu trong lễ bế mạc Đại lễ Vesak 2014.JPG

nodes.label: Yunshan Tan
nodes.summary: Yunshan Tan (1898–1983) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at institutions including Hunan First Normal University and under teachers such as Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, later serving as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Kshitimohan Sen
variants: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.jawiki: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.summary: Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, he served in the Chamba State Education Department (~1904–1908), at Patha Bhavana, and as Adhyaksha at Visva-Bharati University (1953–1954).

nodes.label: Paul Kingsbury
nodes.summary: Paul Kingsbury is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

nodes.label: John Stevens
nodes.description: Buddhist priest, teacher of Buddhist studies and aikido teacher

nodes.label: Piotr Klafkowski
nodes.summary: Piotr Klafkowski is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under doctoral supervisor Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under Lozang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatso, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelsang Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jerzy Bańczerowski
nodes.summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski was a scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961), where he served as professor from 1969 and director from 1977 to 1991.

nodes.label: Ruixuan Chen
nodes.summary: Ruixuan Chen works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed a PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018) under Paul Harrison, with earlier study under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and holds a faculty post at Peking University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Adelheid Mette
nodes.summary: Adelheid Mette (1934–2023) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held professorships at the University of Munich (1978, 1980) and held the Indology chair at the University of Münster (1971, 1988–2000).

nodes.label: Olav Hackstein
nodes.summary: Olav Hackstein is a linguistics, Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Freiburg and UPenn, and held posts at UPenn, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Munich, and EPHE.

nodes.label: Linda Learman
nodes.summary: Linda Learman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).

nodes.label: David W. Chappell
nodes.summary: David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale (Ph.D.), he was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1972–2000) and taught at Soka University of America (~2000–2004).

nodes.label: Hajime Tanabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Tanabe studied at Tokyo, Kyoto, Berlin, and Freiburg under Raphael von Koeber, Kitaro Nishida, Martin Heidegger, and Heinrich Rickert. A philosopher, he taught at Tohoku University and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University from 1919 to 1945.

nodes.label: Cuma Ozkan
nodes.summary: Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Stephan Marcus Salzberg
nodes.summary: Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of American Religion
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of American Religion
variants: Institute for the Study of American Religion

nodes.label: Edmund Leach
nodes.summary: Edmund Leach (1910–1989) worked in religious studies and related fields. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE, he held posts as lecturer at the LSE, professor at Cambridge (1953–1978), provost of King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979), and RAI president (1971–1975).

nodes.label: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt
nodes.summary: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and held teaching posts at Ohio State and Denison University.

nodes.label: Yanfei Zhou
nodes.summary: Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies and sinology, and completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

nodes.label: Yiliang Zhou
nodes.summary: Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard universities, as well as under Yinke Chen, and served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).

nodes.label: Yinke Chen
nodes.summary: Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who studied widely, including at Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Lanman, Lüders, and Müller. He held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking, National Southwestern Associated, Yenching, and Sun Yat-sen universities.

nodes.label: Norio Fujisawa
nodes.summary: Norio Fujisawa was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950). He held a post at Kyoto University (~1966–1989) and later served as director of the Kyoto National Museum (~1992–2001).

nodes.label: Eberhard Fischer
nodes.image: The President, Smt. Pratibha Devisingh Patil presenting the Padma Shri Award to Dr. Eberhard Fischer, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 04, 2012.jpg
nodes.summary: Eberhard Fischer is a scholar of Indology and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and later held posts with the Rietberg Society and the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation.

nodes.label: Kyotaro Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Kyotaro Nishikawa was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Educated at Keio University, he served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from approximately 1990 to 1996.

nodes.label: Université libre de Bruxelles
variants: Center for Study of South and Southeast Asia at the University of Brussels

nodes.label: Chack-fan Lee
nodes.summary: Chack-fan Lee is a scholar active in Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario, he served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.

nodes.label: Sze-bong Tso
nodes.summary: Sze-bong Tso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

nodes.label: Loukram Ibempishak Devi
nodes.summary: Loukram Ibempishak Devi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma and also studied under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

nodes.label: Chirapat Prapandvidya
nodes.summary: Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, where he served as Director in 1996.

nodes.label: Dawn Mountain
variants: Dawn Mountain Community Center & Research Institute

nodes.label: Phra Sigambhirayan
nodes.native: พระศรีคัมภีรญาณ
nodes.summary: Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Riika J. Virtanen
nodes.summary: Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.

nodes.label: Sandra Hochwarter
nodes.summary: Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Anne MacDonald.

nodes.label: August Johan Bernet Kempers
nodes.image: Installatie nieuwe directeur van het Rijksmuseum voor Volkenkunde Het Nederland, Bestanddeelnr 909-2587.jpg
nodes.summary: August Johan Bernet Kempers worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. After studying at Leiden University (c. 1924–1933), he served as director of Dinas Purbakala (c. 1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Jan Fontein
nodes.summary: Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and art history. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin and served as curator at the Rijksmuseum and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

nodes.label: Theodoor van Erp
nodes.image: Portret van Dr Th. van Erp, luitenant der genie en restaurator van de Borobudur, RP-F-2013-61-1.jpg

nodes.label: Madhu Khanna
nodes.summary: Madhu Khanna is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. Her career includes posts attested in 2012 at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen (born 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Suk Fun Ng
nodes.summary: Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014). Ng studied under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, and teacher K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Sarat Sarma
nodes.summary: Sarat Sarma works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under the supervision of S. Shyamkishor Singh, having also studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.

nodes.label: Jan Dolensky
nodes.summary: Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Ming Mei
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Ming Mei earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan. Ming Mei also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

nodes.label: Andrey Terentyev
nodes.summary: Andrey Terentyev specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970-1975) and held a post at the Museum of History of Religion from ~1978 to 1994.

nodes.label: Wulstan Fletcher
nodes.summary: Wulstan Fletcher is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Pei-jung Wu
nodes.summary: Pei-jung Wu works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at UCLA in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum, having also studied under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

nodes.label: Ng-Fung Yuen
nodes.summary: Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tsoknyi Rinpoche studied at Khampagar Monastery (~1979) and under several teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Ling Ji
nodes.summary: Ling Ji is a Sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Notto R. Thelle
nodes.summary: Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from circa 1986 to 2006.

nodes.id: I:NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: National Christian Council (NCC) Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in Kyōto

nodes.label: Kiattisak Ponampon
nodes.summary: Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and was taught in 2013 by Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, John Kieschnick, Barend J. ter Haar, and Seishi Karashima.

nodes.label: Somchai Thanavuddho
nodes.native: สมชาย ฐานวุฑฺโฒ

nodes.label: Win Than Tun
nodes.summary: Win Than Tun works in history and archaeology, having studied at the National University of Singapore under Myo Myint.

nodes.label: Ann Grodzins Gold
nodes.summary: Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She completed her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. in anthropology at the University of Chicago (1973–1984) and held posts at Cornell University and Syracuse University.

nodes.label: Mumon Yamada
variants: Mumon Yamada (山田 無文, Yamada Mumon)
nodes.summary: Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1988), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

nodes.label: Gianpaolo Vetturini
nodes.summary: Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

nodes.label: Keir Strickland
nodes.summary: Keir Strickland is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who completed a PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Zeng Yang
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Zeng Yang studied as a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under supervisor Jinhua Chen.

nodes.label: Tsering Shakya
nodes.summary: A Tibetology and history scholar, Tsering Shakya earned his BA, MPhil, and BA degrees at SOAS University of London. He was a research fellow at SOAS (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and joined the University of British Columbia (~2007).

nodes.label: Kang-nam Oh
nodes.summary: Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

nodes.label: Hsu-feng Lee
nodes.summary: Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's degree under Huimin at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies and a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Yoshiaki Shimizu
nodes.summary: Yoshiaki Shimizu (1936–2021) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1969–1974), he held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1979) and served as a professor at Princeton University (~1984–2009).

nodes.label: Filippo Marsili
nodes.summary: Filippo Marsili is a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and held an academic post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Jane Bunnag
nodes.summary: Jane Bunnag works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, studying under supervisors Nathaniel Tarn and Barbara E. Ward.

nodes.label: Barbara E. Ward
nodes.summary: Barbara E. Ward (1919–1983) studied at Newnham College, the LSE, and the University of London. Working in Sinology, she taught history at London (~1948–1955), lectured at Cambridge (~1973–1983), and was a visiting professor at CUHK (1978–1982).

nodes.label: David M. DiValerio
nodes.summary: David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the SIT Graduate Institute and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, holding a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hubert Decleer
nodes.summary: Hubert Decleer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Alliance Française, SIT Graduate Institute, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Maria Heim
nodes.summary: Maria Heim works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, later serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Lloyd W. Pflueger
nodes.summary: Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kshanika Saha
nodes.summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

nodes.label: Michael Baxandall
variants: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.jawiki: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.summary: Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) studied at Cambridge and under Ernst Gombrich. He held academic posts at the Warburg Institute, Courtauld Institute of Art, the University of Oxford, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Drège
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet, and served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

nodes.label: Mohammad Ashraf Dar
nodes.summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who earned an MPhil from Vikram University and was attested there as a research scholar in 2014.

nodes.label: Nyingcha Duoji
nodes.summary: Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Boston University and earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.

nodes.label: Chih-fu Li
nodes.summary: Chih-fu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who served as director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Stephen Fuchs
nodes.summary: Stephen Fuchs (1908–2000) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and was a visiting scholar at the University of San Carlos.

nodes.label: Ronald Neufeldt
nodes.summary: Ronald Neufeldt (b. 1941) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Calgary, beginning as Associate Professor around 1977, attested in 2001, and attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Yoshinori Yasuda
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Yasuda (1946–2026) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Ritsumeikan University and Tohoku University. He served as Professor Emeritus at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2012) and as professor at Tohoku University (~2012–2014).

nodes.label: Fumio Tamamuro
nodes.summary: Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University from ~1954 to 1963 and subsequently held a post there from ~1976 to 2006.

nodes.label: Yuan Ren
nodes.summary: Yuan Ren works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Doris Unterthurner
nodes.summary: Doris Unterthurner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Manfred Taube
nodes.summary: Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig University under Friedrich Weller and served as Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig University starting in 1991.

nodes.label: Diane L. Howard
nodes.summary: Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied as a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso
nodes.summary: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Loden Sherab Dagyab
nodes.summary: Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, worked at the University of Bonn (1966), and founded Tibet House Germany (2005).

nodes.label: Douglas Ober
nodes.summary: Douglas Ober is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes and others, and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi.

nodes.label: Harjot Oberoi
nodes.summary: Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies, history, and Indology. Educated at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, he was appointed to the Chair of Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Ter Ellingson
nodes.description: American ethnomusicologist and professor of music
nodes.summary: Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving as a professor of music at the University of Washington (1981–2016).

nodes.label: Alnis Dickson
nodes.summary: Alnis Dickson, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed an MA at McGill University, attested in 2009. His studies were supervised by Lara Braitstein, and he was taught by G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Rita M. Gross
nodes.summary: Rita M. Gross was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. She held posts at UW–Madison and served as Professor Emerita at UW–Eau Claire (1979–1998).

nodes.label: Ösel Tendzin
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies practitioner, Ösel Tendzin studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He became executive vice president of Vajradhatu in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

nodes.label: Chamnong Adivadhanasit
nodes.summary: Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University, where he later served as a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and was a professor of social science at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Le Manh That
nodes.summary: Le Manh That (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a BA from the University of Saigon (~1962-1965), a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965-1974), and held a post at Van Hanh University (~1974-1975).

nodes.label: Pataraporn Sirikanchana
nodes.summary: Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania. She has served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Ryoshin Nakao
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Ryoshin Nakao served at the Research Institute of Soto Zen Buddhism and Hanazono University, where he was a professor (attested 1998) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nobumi Iyanaga
nodes.summary: Nobumi Iyanaga is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969). He taught at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and held a research contract at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014).

nodes.label: Phillip Emmanual Bloom
nodes.summary: Phillip Emmanual Bloom works in Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

nodes.label: John Corrigan
nodes.summary: A religious studies scholar, Corrigan earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He held appointments at the University of Virginia (~1982–1989), Arizona State University (~1990–2001), and Florida State University as department chair (~2001), among other institutions.

nodes.label: Françoise Robin
nodes.summary: Tibetologist Françoise Robin studied at INALCO and completed her doctorate under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). She served as director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership roles at INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).

nodes.label: Maurice Frank Wiles
nodes.summary: Maurice Frank Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Christ's College and Ridley Hall, Cambridge. He held posts at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, University of Cambridge, King's College London, and was Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford (1970–1991).

nodes.label: Iso Kern
nodes.summary: Iso Kern (born 1937) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Louvain, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University, and held academic posts at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, Zurich, Fribourg, and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: David Fiordalis
nodes.summary: David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD under Luis O. Gómez). In 2017, he was attested as associate professor and department chair at Linfield University.

nodes.label: Burton Watson
nodes.summary: Burton Watson studied at Columbia University (B.A. 1946–1951, PhD ~1950–1956) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. Specializing in Sinology and Japanology, he taught at Doshisha, Kyoto, Columbia (Professor, 1961), and Stanford (~1964–1965).

nodes.label: Victor Forte
nodes.summary: Victor Forte works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Temple University (-2004) and was attested in 2007 as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

nodes.label: Robert Magliola
nodes.summary: Robert Magliola works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from Princeton (~1966–1970), he held posts at Purdue (1969), Tamkang (1983–1984), Assumption (1985), National Taiwan University (~1989–2003), and Columbia (2002–2011).

nodes.label: Roy W. Perrett
nodes.description: philosopher at the University of Melbourne
nodes.summary: Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago (~1980–1984). He held posts at Massey University (~1987–2004), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2001–2011), and the University of Melbourne.

nodes.label: Yingshan Chen
nodes.summary: Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen served as a professor (attested 1996) and later as an honorary research fellow (retired February 2023) at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Nile Green
nodes.summary: Nile Green is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Manchester (~2004–2007) and serves as Professor and Ibn Khaldun Endowed Chair in World History at UCLA (~2007).

nodes.label: Rinzin Thargyal
nodes.summary: Rinzin Thargyal is a Tibetologist who earned a Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

nodes.label: Fredrik Barth
nodes.summary: Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), Emory University (1989–1996), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

nodes.label: John Buescher
nodes.summary: John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982. He served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

nodes.label: James Duerlinger
nodes.summary: James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1964) under Sheldon Pollock and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa (~1971–2012).

nodes.label: Marshall Sahlins
nodes.jawiki: マーシャル・サーリンズ
nodes.summary: Marshall Sahlins (1930–2021) was an anthropologist and historian. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), later holding faculty appointments at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (appointed 1973).

nodes.label: Jinping Liao
nodes.summary: Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: Gary D. DeAngelis
nodes.summary: Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: George Rupp
nodes.summary: George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School. Later, he held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).

nodes.label: Daud Rahbar
nodes.summary: Daud Rahbar studied at Government College University, Lahore, and Cambridge. He held positions at University of the Punjab, Oriental College, McGill, Ankara University, and University of Wisconsin-Madison, before serving at Boston University (~1968–1998).

nodes.label: Thomas Adams Borchert
nodes.summary: Thomas Adams Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. A PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he studied under Bruce Lincoln, Alan Berkowitz, and Donald K. Swearer, among others. He was Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Anna Brown
nodes.summary: Anna Brown is a scholar in religious studies and other fields who studied Zen under Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). As of 2017, she served at Saint Peter's University as chair of political science and director of social justice.

nodes.label: Robert Kennedy
nodes.description: American Jesuit priest, psychoanalyst and Zen rōshi

nodes.label: Hsiao-Lan Hu
nodes.summary: Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Richard Sylvan
nodes.summary: Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1954–1958) and Princeton University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University (fellow in 1971).

nodes.label: Mei Ching Hsuan
nodes.summary: Mei Ching Hsuan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger, also studying under Dieter Schuh, and served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

nodes.label: Matthieu Ricard
nodes.summary: Matthieu Ricard is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob, earning a doctorate, and trained under Kangyour Rinpoché and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He became a Mind and Life Institute board member (~1991).

nodes.label: Meei-Hwa Chern
nodes.summary: Meei-Hwa Chern works in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under John C. Raines and served as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Karolinska Institute
variants: Department of Histology at the Karolinska Institute

nodes.id: I:National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
nodes.label: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
variants: National Hospital for the Paralysed and Epileptic

nodes.label: Akita Cerebrovascular and Cardiovascular Center
variants: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels

nodes.id: I:National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
nodes.label: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
variants: National Institute of Neurology and Psychiatry

nodes.label: Levi McLaughlin
nodes.summary: Levi McLaughlin, a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University. His appointments include Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, the University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University (2012).

nodes.label: Takashi Nakao
nodes.summary: Takashi Nakao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Rissho University and the Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, the Society of Japanese Historical Manuscripts, and Rissho University (emeritus professor 1979–2002).

nodes.label: Axel Klein
nodes.summary: Axel Klein specializes in Japanology. He studied and worked at the University of Bonn, was a researcher at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and was appointed professor of modern East Asian social studies at Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

nodes.label: Michael J. Tetreault
nodes.summary: Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under supervisor Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Natasha Reichle
nodes.summary: Natasha Reichle is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Joanna Gottfried Williams, alongside teachers Amin Sweeney, Lewis R. Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.

nodes.label: Amin Sweeney
nodes.summary: Amin Sweeney (1938–2010) worked in linguistics and related fields. He earned his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970), taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977), and served as Department Chair and emeritus professor at UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Luboš Bělka
nodes.summary: Luboš Bělka is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from around 1978 to 1983 and later held an academic post there around 1993.

nodes.label: Masaryk University
variants: Institute for the Study of Religions at Masaryk University of Brno

nodes.label: Diana Lange
nodes.summary: Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet, and Humboldt universities and EPHE, she held posts at TU Berlin, Leipzig, Zurich, Hamburg, and was named Professorin at Humboldt University in 2025.

nodes.label: Solomon George FitzHerbert
nodes.summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar in Tibetology who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford. He served as a Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and was a researcher at the CNRS (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kathleen McDonald
nodes.summary: Kathleen McDonald is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2010, she studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Adam Pearcey
nodes.summary: Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and studied under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers, including the 14th Dalai Lama.

nodes.label: Trulshik Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trulshik Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and taught prominent figures including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Daijaku Judith Kinst
nodes.summary: Daijaku Judith Kinst is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and is attested as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

nodes.label: Raimon Panikkar
nodes.summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Complutense University of Madrid under Juan Zaragüeta, Pontifical Lateran University, Mysore, and Banaras Hindu University. He held teaching posts at Complutense, Harvard, and UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Zenkei Blanche Hartman
nodes.summary: Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. After studying at UC Berkeley (~1943–1947), she trained under teachers including Richard Baker, Mel Weitsman, and Joshin Kasai, later serving as co-abbess of the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).

nodes.label: Victor Lieberman
nodes.summary: Victor Lieberman is a historian who earned his BA at Yale (~1963–1967) and his PhD at SOAS (~1971–1976). In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History and Professor of Asian and Comparative History at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Christopher Jon Jensen
nodes.summary: Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD -2018), where his doctoral supervisor was James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Kathrin Holz
nodes.summary: Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Shri Singha Shedra
variants: Shri Singha Shedra at Dzogchen Monastery

nodes.label: Hammalawa Saddhatissa
nodes.image: Most Venerable Hammalawa Saddhatissa Maha Thera (1914–1990).jpg
nodes.summary: Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990), an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Mahabodhi College, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (ca. 1957–1990).

nodes.label: Cheng Yen
nodes.summary: Cheng Yen is a religious figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yinshun starting in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.

nodes.label: Tzu Chi Foundation
variants: Buddhist Compassion Relief Tzu Chi Foundation

nodes.label: Shenghai Li
nodes.summary: Shenghai Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., and studied with teachers including Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Ram Shankar Tripathi.

nodes.label: Bradley L. Herling
nodes.summary: Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. He held the post of Assistant Director at Boston University and was affiliated with Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Sumi Lee
nodes.summary: Sumi Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA under Alexander Leonhard Mayer at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and a PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr. at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Christmas Humphreys
nodes.summary: Christmas Humphreys worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Malvern College (~1914–1919) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1919–1922), and served as President of the Buddhist Society from around 1924 to 1983.

nodes.label: Michael von Brück
nodes.description: German Protestant theologian and pastor, religious scientist and author, and Zen and yoga teacher
nodes.summary: Michael von Brück (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and studied at the University of Madras (~1980–1985). He held chairs in comparative religion at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Mehlman
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held faculty posts at Yale University (~1968–1970), Cornell University (~1970–1973), Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983), and Boston University (from ~1983) as professor of French literature.

nodes.label: Tim Dean
nodes.summary: Tim Dean (born 1964) is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of East Anglia, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held posts at Stanford University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the University of Washington, and the University at Buffalo.

nodes.label: Stephanie Kaza
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kaza specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry under Thích Nhất Hạnh and Joanna Macy, later serving as professor at the University of Vermont (1991–2015).

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Xinh
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Kathleen D. Morrison
nodes.summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Notre Dame, University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, and held posts at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

nodes.label: Joseph Walser
nodes.summary: Joseph Walser works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.

nodes.label: Khenpo Dazer
nodes.summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both Shrisingha Shedra and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Hisao Kanaseki
nodes.summary: Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University and worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as a professor at Kobe University (circa 1952–1968), Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1968–1982), and Komazawa University (circa 1982–1989).

nodes.label: King Chung Lo
nodes.summary: King Chung Lo works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leipzig University, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco (2009).

nodes.label: Jinling He
nodes.summary: Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.

nodes.label: Limei Chi
nodes.summary: Limei Chi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Jinhua Chen. Attested in 2026, she held faculty posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and as Professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Karma Sonam Palmo
nodes.summary: Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Yui Suzuki
nodes.summary: Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanese art history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Suzuki studied at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Davis Schoening
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Davis Schoening works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington, where he studied under Collett Cox and Sanghasena Singh.

nodes.label: Chönyi Drolma
nodes.summary: Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Lama Ngawang Zangpo.

nodes.label: Lama Tsering Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Lama Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Mark Owen
nodes.summary: Mark Owen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Stuart
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She was appointed Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

nodes.label: Jürgen Renn
nodes.description: German physicist, historian of science and university professor
nodes.summary: Jürgen Renn is a historian of science who earned his PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and became Director of the MPI of Geoanthropology in 2022.

nodes.label: Yulian Zeng
nodes.summary: Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under Kirill Solonin and Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Phibul Choompolpaisal
nodes.native: พิบูลย์ ชุมพลไพศาล

nodes.label: Graham E. Clarke
nodes.summary: Graham E. Clarke (died 1998) was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a senior member in 1998.

nodes.label: Gelek
nodes.summary: Gelek is a scholar of Tibetology. He held a researcher post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and served as a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford and visiting lecturer at UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Nancy E. Levine
nodes.summary: Nancy E. Levine is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, as Associate Professor of anthropology (attested 1998) and Professor of Anthropology (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Angela Manderscheid
nodes.summary: Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

nodes.label: Ronald D. Schwartz
nodes.summary: Ronald D. Schwartz works in Tibetology and sociology. His appointments include Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Klaus-Josef Notz
nodes.summary: Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied theology at PTH Benediktbeuern (1966–1971), earned a doctorate in theology at the University of Munich (1978–1984), and served as a lecturer at Munich in 1996.

nodes.label: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen
variants: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München

nodes.label: Holmes Welch
nodes.summary: Holmes Welch, a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Harvard University (~1940–1957). He taught at Yale University (~1962–1963) and Harvard University (~1964–1981).

nodes.label: Chuan-ying Yen
nodes.summary: Chuan-ying Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield.

nodes.label: Chu-tsing Li
nodes.summary: Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He held teaching posts at the University of Nanking (1943–1947), the University of Iowa (~1955–1966), and the University of Kansas (from 1966).

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Saunders
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Saunders (1883-1937) was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara (~1908-1912) and taught at the Pacific School of Religion and UC Berkeley (~1921-1935).

nodes.label: Takamaro Shigaraki
nodes.summary: Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. He served as professor and president (1989–1995) of Ryukoku University and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008).

nodes.label: Ontario Tech University
variants: University of Ontario Institute of Technology
