nodes.label: Vienna University of Economics and Business
variants: Institut für Wirtschafts- und Sozialgeschichte, Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien

nodes.label: Monika Nowakowska
nodes.summary: Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who has held posts at the University of Warsaw (attested 2010 and 2026).

nodes.label: Kuno Lorenz
nodes.summary: Philosopher Kuno Lorenz completed his PhD at Kiel University (1961) and his Habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1969). He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

nodes.label: Claus Oetke
nodes.summary: Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg, later teaching there, at the universities of Vienna and Kiel, and at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

nodes.label: Rolf Scheuermann
nodes.summary: Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Edward H. Schafer
nodes.summary: Edward H. Schafer was a Sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He was a faculty member in Oriental Languages at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947-1984) and president of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Paul Carus
nodes.summary: Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Günther Grassmann, earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen (~1875–1876), and worked at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Thomas B. Ellis
nodes.summary: Thomas B. Ellis works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Jos Gommans
nodes.summary: Jos Gommans studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. A historian and indologist, he held posts at the Dutch Research Council, the Kern Institute, and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Dirk H. A. Kolff
nodes.summary: Dirk H. A. Kolff is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he taught at the Kern Institute (1967–1991) and held the Chair of Indian History (1991–2003).

nodes.label: Delhi School of Economics
variants: Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi

nodes.label: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph
nodes.summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology and history scholar. She studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard, and Radcliffe. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), was a professor at the University of Chicago (1964), and presided over APSA (2003–2004).

nodes.id: I:Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
nodes.label: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
variants: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
Fine Arts Institute, Academy of Sciences, Uzbekistan

nodes.label: Eiki Hoshino
nodes.summary: Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1971). He later served at Taisho University as Director and Professor in the Faculty of Humanities (~1980–2013).

nodes.label: Phanit Jetjiravat
nodes.summary: Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under academic advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

nodes.label: Yuri Parfionovich
nodes.summary: Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a Tibetologist. He studied under George de Roerich and under traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.

nodes.label: Francis N. J.
nodes.summary: Francis N. J. is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut, where he also completed doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

nodes.label: M. R. Raghava Varier
nodes.summary: M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar in Indology, history, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and served as a professor at the University of Calicut (~1980–1996).

nodes.label: Rajan Gurukkal
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Rajan Gurukkal studied at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He was the Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and Sundararajan Visiting Professor at the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).

nodes.label: Harold Scheub
nodes.summary: Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Following teaching posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was a long-time humanities professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1970–2013).

nodes.label: Thomas J. Mazanec
nodes.summary: Thomas J. Mazanec works in sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Calvin University, the University of Colorado Boulder (MA), and Princeton University (PhD), he studied under Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, Paul W. Kroll, and Ping Wang, among others.

nodes.label: Jeff Dolven
nodes.summary: Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He held positions at Harvard University (~1995–1998), Brandeis University (~1998–1999), and Princeton University, where he became a professor of English (~1999).

nodes.label: Joshua Timothy Katz
nodes.summary: Joshua Timothy Katz is a linguist who earned degrees at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.

nodes.label: Christopher Braider
nodes.description: American French and Italian language professor

nodes.label: Nalini Bhushan
nodes.description: Andrew W. Mellon Professor in the Humanities at Smith College

nodes.label: Wilburn Hansen
nodes.summary: Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Hansen pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and completed further studies at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

nodes.label: Yu-kwan Ng
nodes.summary: Yu-kwan Ng (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later teaching at National Central University (~2001–2011).

nodes.label: Bruce Charles Williams
nodes.summary: Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. His studies included training under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

nodes.label: Sodo Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji from 1949 to 1957 under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Eko Hashimoto.

nodes.label: Elena France Hanson
nodes.summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Hanson earned a Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Narraway
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Narraway studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at McGill University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Cheryl A. Crowley
nodes.summary: Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, Ryuichi Abe, and Barbara Ruch.

nodes.label: Dawa Tsering
nodes.summary: Dawa Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026), and held a post at Tibet University.

nodes.label: Wolfram Eberhard
nodes.summary: Sinologist Wolfram Eberhard studied in Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. After teaching at several Chinese institutions, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Ankara University (1937–1948), he was Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).

nodes.label: Dörte Kamarid
nodes.summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

nodes.label: U Dhammissara
nodes.summary: U Dhammissara works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Sanu Mahatthanadull, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Asen Balikci
nodes.summary: Asen Balikci was a historian, archaeologist, and anthropologist who completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1956. He held posts at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel, the Canadian Museum of History, and the University of Montreal (1963–1993).

nodes.label: Bo-Kwang Han
nodes.summary: Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar of Buddhist studies and a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015). He taught Silwon Suk.

nodes.label: Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
variants: Norwegian Institute for Palaeography and Historical Philology

nodes.label: Regent Hotel and Technical School
variants: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend

nodes.label: Anne Nishimura Morse
nodes.summary: Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Taka Yanagisawa, Yutaka Hirata, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, later holding visiting posts at Tokyo National Research Institute (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

nodes.label: Taka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Yanagisawa studied at Japan Women's University (~1943–1947) and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1952–1991).

nodes.label: Yutaka Hirata
nodes.summary: Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who earned a doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at the Nara National Cultural Properties Research Institute (~1956–1973), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2004).

nodes.label: Bunsaku Kurata
nodes.description: born:1918|died:1983|; 倉田, 文作, 1918-1983; Kurata, Bunsaku, 1918-....; 倉田, 文作; Kurata, Bunsaku
nodes.summary: Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda universities, working in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He served at the Tokyo National Museum, National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Nara National Museum Director in 1975.

nodes.label: Takeo Izumi
nodes.summary: Takeo Izumi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1981) and later served as a professor there (~1996–2017).

nodes.label: Keizaburo Mizuno
nodes.summary: Keizaburo Mizuno is a scholar of Japanese art history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He worked at the Tokyo National Museum, became professor emeritus at Tokyo Fine Arts School, and directed two art museums.

nodes.label: Seiji Nemoto
nodes.summary: Seiji Nemoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1968 to 1978 and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from circa 2006 to 2014.

nodes.label: Martin T. Adam
nodes.summary: Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002). He also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a McGill instructor.

nodes.label: Michael P. Berman
nodes.summary: Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Bela Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Bela Bhattacharya (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Bernard Williams
nodes.jawiki: バーナード・ウィリアムズ (哲学者)
nodes.summary: Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He later held academic posts at University College London (~1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

nodes.label: Bruno Galasek
nodes.summary: Bruno Galasek specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Palmo Kyi
nodes.summary: Palmo Kyi is a Tibetologist who studied under Per Kværne, Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

nodes.label: Hiroo Sato
nodes.summary: Hiroo Sato (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1982). He held posts at Morioka College (~1985–1993) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~1996–2019).

nodes.label: Hsiu-hui Ji
nodes.summary: Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree from Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: David Patt
nodes.summary: David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Ngan-che Chan
nodes.summary: Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2007), where they were supervised by Jing Yin and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Geshe Lhakdor
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhakdor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He worked at Tibet House New Delhi and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

nodes.label: Meiping Li
nodes.summary: Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Sakyong Mipham Rinpoche
variants: サキョン・ミパム・リンポチェ
サワン・ウーセル・ランジュン・ムクポ
nodes.summary: Sakyong Mipham Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Penor Rinpoche; he succeeded Chögyam Trungpa and served on Naropa University's board until 2018.

nodes.label: Tao Jin
nodes.summary: Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander Leonhard Mayer.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Munich and was a professor at Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Carlo Jamelle Harris
nodes.summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Richard P. Boyle
nodes.summary: Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was affiliated with the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tenshin Tanouye
nodes.summary: Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was a figure in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sogen Omori, whom he succeeded, and founded Chozen-ji.

nodes.label: Sogen Omori
nodes.summary: Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, studying at Nihon University and under masters including Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1978–1982) and head priest of Koho-in.

nodes.label: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach
nodes.summary: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

nodes.label: Johannes Beltz
nodes.summary: Johannes Beltz completed his PhD in 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst. His fields include Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies.

nodes.label: Esben Andreasen
nodes.summary: Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Copenhagen. In 1992, he served as a visiting researcher at Otani University.

nodes.label: Sonam Tsering
nodes.summary: Sonam Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle. As of 2026, he is Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Sudhir Kakar
nodes.summary: Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Gujarat University, University of Mannheim, and University of Vienna. He held positions at Harvard, IIM Ahmedabad, and IIT Delhi, alongside numerous international visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Naman P. Ahuja
nodes.summary: Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his doctorate at SOAS University of London. He became Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Jens Schlieter
nodes.summary: Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1994–1999) under Josef Simon, he became Professor and Institute Managing Director at the University of Bern (~2009).

nodes.label: Yeshi Dhonden
nodes.summary: Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) worked in Tibetology and traditional medicine. He studied under Khyenrab Norbu at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine, and later founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director until 1966.

nodes.label: Chi Chen Ho
nodes.summary: Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Hsuan Hua and Robert E. Buswell Jr., completing a PhD at UCLA in 2010, where Ho also served as a teaching assistant.

nodes.label: K. Venkata Ramanan
nodes.summary: K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, earned a Doctor of Letters from Visva-Bharati University, and held a teaching post there.

nodes.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
variants: サティエンドラ・ナート・ボース
nodes.jawiki: サティエンドラ・ボース
nodes.summary: Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at Dhaka University (1921–1945), Calcutta University (1945–1956), and served as Vice-Chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

nodes.label: Walter Liebenthal
nodes.summary: Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his doctorate at Breslau. He held academic posts at Yenching, Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Tübingen (1965–1982).

nodes.label: Norman Fischer
nodes.description: American Soto Zen roshi, poet and Buddhist author practicing in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Norman Fischer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. In 2000, he founded the Everyday Zen Foundation.

nodes.label: Kichinosuke Ito
nodes.summary: Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg. He served as professor and assistant at Tokyo, held deanships at Hokkaido University, and was a professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).

nodes.label: Huynh Thi Ha Vy
nodes.summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: Douglas Gildow
nodes.summary: Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University, studying under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and supervisor Qi Zhou.

nodes.label: David Gonsalez
nodes.summary: David Gonsalez works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra
nodes.summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and under Yeshe Paldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, later teaching numerous disciples.

nodes.label: Warrin Ratanamalai
nodes.summary: Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007). His studies were supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside teachers Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

nodes.label: Haeju Sunim
nodes.summary: Haeju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University from 1996 to 1997 and was an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University in 1999.

nodes.label: Dietmar Rothermund
nodes.summary: Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 2001.

nodes.label: Alan Watts
nodes.image: Alan Watts UVM 15 June 1958 Hon. D.D (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seabury-Western Theological Seminary, served as Northwestern University's chaplain (1944–1950), taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), and held a Harvard fellowship (1962–1964).

nodes.label: Amar Singh
nodes.summary: Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963), doctoral supervisor A. K. Warder (attested 1984), and teachers Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, Masafumi Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

nodes.label: Alasdair Urquhart
nodes.summary: Alasdair Urquhart (born 1945) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (MA) and the University of Pittsburgh (PhD). He taught as an assistant professor at University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at Toronto (1986).

nodes.label: Tianshu Zhu
nodes.summary: Tianshu Zhu specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed degrees at Northwest University and Ohio State University, the latter under John C. Huntington, and held positions at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and Ohio State University.

nodes.label: Paul Tillich
nodes.summary: Paul Tillich (1886–1965) was a philosopher and theologian educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He taught at Dresden, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard University (1955–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1965).

nodes.label: Jacob N. Kinnard
nodes.summary: Jacob N. Kinnard works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

nodes.label: Bryce Ryan
nodes.summary: Bryce Ryan (1911–1993) was a scholar in Indology and other fields. Over his career, he held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Thuong
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Thuong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

nodes.label: Xinru Liu
nodes.summary: Xinru Liu works in history, archaeology, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing a PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), Liu held posts at CASS (~1985–2002) and The College of New Jersey (~2002).

nodes.label: Janet R. Goodwin
nodes.summary: Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held posts attested in 1994 at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.

nodes.label: Lawrence William Nelson
nodes.summary: Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies, having also studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, St. John's College, and other institutions.

Bryan D. Lowe
nodes.summary: Bryan D. Lowe specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under mentors including Jacqueline I. Stone and Martin Collcutt, holding a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Andrew Watsky
nodes.summary: Andrew Watsky is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Oberlin College (~1975-1979) and Princeton University (~1986-1994). He held a post at Vassar College from ~1994 to 2008.

nodes.label: Towao Sakaehara
nodes.summary: Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his undergraduate and doctoral degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University and Osaka City University (from 1981 to 2010), and directed the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

nodes.label: Ben Joffe
nodes.summary: Ben Joffe is a religious studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Saba Mahmood
nodes.description: American anthropologist, Professor, University of California, Berkeley
nodes.summary: Saba Mahmood was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (c. 1999–2004) and as professor of sociocultural anthropology at UC Berkeley (2004–2018).

nodes.label: Winnifred Fallers Sullivan
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan studied at Cornell and Chicago (J.D., Ph.D.). She held faculty posts at Washington and Lee (1994–2000), Chicago (2000–2005), University at Buffalo (2006–2012), and Indiana University Bloomington (~2012).

nodes.label: Martin Riesebrodt
nodes.summary: Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar educated at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (doctorate ~1969–1973), and Munich (Habilitation ~1986–1990). He was a professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and later taught at the Geneva Graduate Institute (2013).

nodes.label: Mark I. Wallace
nodes.summary: Mark I. Wallace (born 1956) is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Chicago under Paul Ricœur (1986). He held posts at Princeton Theological Seminary, Merrimack College, and Georgia State University, and serves as Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College.

nodes.label: Joanne Punzo Waghorne
nodes.summary: Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She held posts at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

nodes.label: Takahiko Kameyama
nodes.summary: Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, both attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Courtney Bruntz
nodes.summary: Courtney Bruntz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She has held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Wes Borton
nodes.summary: Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied under Derek F. Maher at East Carolina University and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer
nodes.summary: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under supervisor Linda Penkower and also studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.

Biología del Conocer (Biology of Knowing) research center

nodes.label: Yangdon Dhondup
nodes.summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in tibetology who completed a PhD under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao at SOAS University of London (~1999–2004).

nodes.label: Christopher Byrne
nodes.summary: Christopher Byrne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), where he studied under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.

nodes.label: Alexander James O'Neill
nodes.summary: Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and held a post as a research fellow at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012, and his students included Keith Dowman and Phakchok Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Guest
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and Sinology. Educated at Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY Graduate Center, he also studied at Peking University and held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

nodes.label: Institut d'histoire et de philosophie des sciences et des techniques
variants: The Institut d'Histoire et Philosophie des sciences et des Techniques

nodes.label: Vishwanath Prasad Varma
nodes.summary: Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) works in philosophy, Indology, and history. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942–1944), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1947–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

nodes.label: Dhirendra Mohan Datta
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).

nodes.label: Joachim Wach
nodes.summary: Joachim Wach was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Leiden, Leipzig, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Leipzig University, Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

nodes.label: Don Handelman
nodes.summary: Don Handelman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, he served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from ~1972 to 2006.

nodes.label: Charles Malamoud
nodes.description: French historian of religion and orientalist
nodes.summary: Charles Malamoud (b. 1929) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was educated at the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon (~1960–1972) and was Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).

nodes.label: Laren Hogen Bays
nodes.summary: Laren Hogen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies specialist. Having studied under traditional teacher Shōdō Harada, Bays co-founded and served as co-abbot of the Great Vow Zen Monastery.

nodes.label: Mikio Otsuki
nodes.summary: Mikio Otsuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Attested in 2007, he held appointments as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

nodes.label: Mary Margaret McCabe
nodes.summary: Mary Margaret McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), later joining University College London.

nodes.label: Verity Harte
nodes.summary: Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1994). After posts at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London, she was appointed Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale University in 2006.

nodes.label: Raimond Gaita
nodes.summary: Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

nodes.label: Jonathan Lear
nodes.summary: Philosopher Jonathan Lear studied at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University (Ph.D.), and Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held academic posts at Yale, Cambridge, Clare College, and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

nodes.label: Susan Neiman
nodes.description: American philosopher, essayist and cultural commentator (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and became Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.

nodes.label: Jonathan Glover
nodes.summary: Jonathan Glover studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. A philosopher, he served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1965–1996), and held posts at King's College London (~1996–2013), Hastings Center, and Oxford.

nodes.label: Songeun Choe
nodes.summary: Songeun Choe works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Myung-dae Moon and doctoral studies under Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Michael W. Meister
nodes.summary: Michael W. Meister is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who earned his BA, MA, and PhD from Harvard University and studied at the University of Pennsylvania. In 1976, he became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.

nodes.label: Melissa R. Kerin
nodes.summary: Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

nodes.label: Tashi Samphel
nodes.summary: Tashi Samphel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director at Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Manfred B. Steger
nodes.summary: Manfred B. Steger works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and Rutgers University, he held professorships at Illinois State University, RMIT University, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Keenan W. Cox
nodes.summary: Keenan W. Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Brian Bocking
nodes.summary: Brian Bocking works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.

nodes.label: André Couture
nodes.summary: André Couture is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Laval University (~1965-1970), EPHE (~1972-1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972-1977), later holding a post at Laval University from ~1979 to 2010.

nodes.label: Shi Xianda
nodes.summary: Shi Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a BA at the University of Kelaniya and earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Seung-yeon Lee
nodes.summary: Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Yunxi Wang
nodes.summary: Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinology scholar. Wang studied at Fudan University from around 1947 to 1952 and held a post there from around 1952 to 2014.

nodes.label: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart
nodes.summary: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Norihisa Baba
nodes.summary: Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda, later becoming a professor at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

nodes.label: Kate Sullivan de Estrada
nodes.summary: Kate Sullivan de Estrada works in Indology and international relations. As attested in 2026, she is an Associate Professor in the International Relations of South Asia at both Wolfson College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Alessandro Giudice
nodes.summary: Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist with posts attested in 2026 at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter and at the University of Munich as Dr.

nodes.label: Athanaric Huard
nodes.summary: Athanaric Huard is an Indologist who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. He is an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yannick Laurent
nodes.summary: Yannick Laurent works in tibetology, history, and archaeology. Laurent held posts at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Danping Long
nodes.summary: Danping Long works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at both the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Richard Bowring
nodes.summary: Richard Bowring (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge, taught at Columbia and Princeton, served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012), and became Emeritus Professor at Cambridge in 1985.

nodes.label: Sherry B. Ortner
nodes.summary: Sherry B. Ortner (born 1941) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan. She held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and UCLA.

nodes.label: Anuj Misra
nodes.summary: Anuj Misra works in Indology and history/archaeology. Having studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, he holds a post as an external researcher at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Dan Li
nodes.summary: Dan Li is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso. Li serves as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hoko Kuwana
nodes.summary: Hoko Kuwana, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hoju Shioda
nodes.summary: Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts attested in 2026 at Minobusan University and the Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Gyoon Iotani
nodes.summary: Gyoon Iotani works in Buddhist studies. Having studied at Waseda University (attested 2015), Iotani held an appointment as deputy director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Fumihiro Okada
nodes.summary: Fumihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and was appointed as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Akiko Kikuchi
nodes.summary: Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).

nodes.summary: Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Koyasan University, with his post attested in 2015 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies at Koyasan University. He held positions at Koyasan University as a researcher (attested 2005) and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).

variants: トーマス・ドライトライン

nodes.label: Jun Yang
nodes.summary: Jun Yang is a sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2026, affiliations are attested as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Bożena Śliwczyńska
nodes.summary: Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She held a faculty post at the University of Warsaw circa 1991.

nodes.label: Zev Handel
nodes.description: professor of Asian languages and literature
nodes.summary: Zev Handel works in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998), and has served as a professor at the University of Washington since circa 1999.

nodes.label: Fuyuan Luo
nodes.summary: Fuyuan Luo is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who is a PhD student at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jampa Lhundup
nodes.summary: Jampa Lhundup works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at and holds a faculty post as Assistant Professor of Art History at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jan Christian Schaffert
nodes.summary: Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational studies. Attested in 2026, he studied as a Bearbeiter and served as a project collaborator (Mitarbeiter) on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Xiaoming Hou
nodes.summary: Xiaoming Hou specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jens Peter Laut
nodes.summary: Jens Peter Laut works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He served on the Leitungskommission of the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008) and held a post at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2020).

nodes.label: Paul R. Brass
nodes.summary: Paul R. Brass (1936–2022) was an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard College, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of Washington from circa 1967 to 2001.

nodes.label: Nima Repper
nodes.summary: Nima Repper is an Indology scholar who studied at and served as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Purnima Dhavan
nodes.summary: Purnima Dhavan works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (1996) and the University of Virginia (1998, 2003), later holding posts at Bowdoin College, St. John's University, and the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Anand A. Yang
nodes.summary: Anand A. Yang works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Swarthmore College (~1966–1970) and the University of Virginia (~1970–1976), he held posts at Sweet Briar College, the University of Utah, and the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Chris Williams
nodes.summary: Chris Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was attested in 2026 as an MPhil and PhD student and teaching staff member at the University of Bristol, supervised by Rita Langer.

variants: カロリーネ ベルグマン

nodes.label: Heidi R. M. Pauwels
nodes.summary: Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA (1983) and studied at KU Leuven, Cologne, and Vrindaban, completing a PhD at Washington (1994) under Alan Entwistle. She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) and Washington (Professor from 2002).

nodes.label: Qian Cao
nodes.summary: Qian Cao works in Indology and philosophy. Attested in 2026, Cao is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Kate Kragh
nodes.summary: Kate Kragh works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She is attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Corinna May Lhoir
nodes.summary: Corinna May Lhoir specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student at Ghent University and Hamburg University, where she also serves as a lecturer and yoga studies program coordinator.

nodes.label: Simon Winant
nodes.summary: Simon Winant works in Indology and linguistics. Attested as a PhD student at Ghent University in 2026, he also served on the faculty there.

nodes.label: Yifan Zhang
nodes.summary: Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. Affiliated with Ghent University (attested 2026), Zhang has been both a PhD student and a faculty member there.

nodes.label: Edwin Arnold
variants: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.jawiki: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology, Edwin Arnold studied at King's College London and the University of Oxford. He served as a schoolmaster at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and became Principal of Poona Sanskrit College/Deccan College in 1856.

nodes.label: Francis William Bain
nodes.summary: Francis William Bain was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889), he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

nodes.label: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (born 1859) was an Indology scholar. He served at Deccan College as assistant to the professor of Sanskrit (1884), and held posts as professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.

nodes.label: Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia
nodes.summary: Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at University College London (~1934–1936) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1973).

nodes.label: Irawati Karve
nodes.description: Indian sociologist, anthropologist, educationist, and writer (1905-1970)
nodes.summary: Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and related fields. She studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology (~1939–1970) and at the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

nodes.label: Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held positions at Pune University, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1967–1989).

nodes.label: Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar
nodes.summary: Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar (1895–1963) was an Indian historian and Indologist. Educated at the University of Mumbai, he served as a faculty member at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from ~1939 to 1955.

nodes.label: Divyaraj Amiya
nodes.summary: Divyaraj Amiya is an Indology and linguistics scholar. His career includes posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Koji Shindo
nodes.summary: Koji Shindo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who was a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

nodes.label: Amara Ali
nodes.summary: Amara Ali works in Indology and linguistics. As of 2026, she is attested as a Lecturer in Urdu at both the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

nodes.label: Munis D. Faruqui
nodes.summary: Munis D. Faruqui (born 1967) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He has served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2003) and as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Martha Ann Selby
nodes.summary: Martha Ann Selby (b. 1954) is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, she is professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and serves at Harvard University as Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies, Comparative Literature professor, and department chair.

nodes.label: Orion Klautau
variants: オリオン・クラウタウ

nodes.label: Kyōko Fujii
nodes.summary: Kyōko Fujii works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In posts attested in 2026, she served as faculty at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Marielle Harrison
nodes.summary: Marielle Harrison specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago, she is attested in 2026 as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Eiichi Otani
nodes.summary: Eiichi Otani is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Toyo University (~1987–1998). He served as professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University (~2004–2010).

nodes.label: Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran
nodes.summary: Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is an Indologist. Parmeswaran pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026) and held a research post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: August Sundin
nodes.summary: August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been active at Ghent University as a PhD student and faculty member, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Iona Macgregor
nodes.summary: Iona Macgregor works in Indology. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nantu Shaw
nodes.summary: Nantu Shaw is an Indologist and philosopher who studied as a Visiting Scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christopher Framarin
nodes.summary: Christopher Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (-2001) and a PhD at the University of New Mexico (-2005), and held faculty posts at the University of Calgary (attested 2014, 2026).

nodes.label: Imre Bangha
nodes.description: Hungarian orientalist, Indologist, translator, university lecturer (1967–)
nodes.summary: Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University. He has served as Associate Professor of Hindi at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College since circa 2003, and honorary professor at ELTE (~2017).

nodes.label: Huabei Tan
nodes.summary: Huabei Tan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Tan pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under doctoral supervisor Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Caixi Chen
nodes.summary: Caixi Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Amelia Bonea

nodes.label: Wayne Chandira
nodes.summary: Wayne Chandira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Joshua Ereshefsky
nodes.summary: Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Benjamin Goldstein

nodes.label: Pema Sherpa

nodes.label: Olli Littunen

nodes.label: Kexin Zheng

nodes.label: Litian Fang

nodes.label: Zhengyan Fan

nodes.label: Balram Shukla

nodes.label: Sambhavi Ganesh

nodes.label: Geetha K. Wilson

nodes.label: Adrienne Wallman

nodes.label: Takahiro Kato

nodes.label: Fumi Yao

nodes.label: Hiroshi Arami

nodes.label: Shunji Hosaka

nodes.label: Iwao Ishikawa

nodes.label: Yasuko Kojima

nodes.label: Shoko Miyata
nodes.summary: Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. As of 2026, Miyata is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Ryuken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryuken Nawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryushin Sudo
nodes.description: Japanese bhikkhu, historian and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Ryushin Sudo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University. He later served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Masataka Suzuki
nodes.summary: Masataka Suzuki (born 1949) works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1980–2015), later serving as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama

nodes.label: Masayuki Tsukimoto

nodes.label: Shuichi Nara
nodes.summary: Shuichi Nara (born 1961) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University and held posts as a full-time researcher at the Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jifu Lan
nodes.summary: Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University from around 1965 to 1969 and served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from around 1985 until retiring in 2019.

nodes.label: Zack Beer
nodes.summary: Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger

nodes.label: Maanasa Visweswaran
nodes.summary: Maanasa Visweswaran is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at and served as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ferenc Ruzsa
nodes.summary: Ferenc Ruzsa (born 1957) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982) and has served as a faculty staff member there since approximately 1989.

nodes.label: Roland Ferenczi
nodes.summary: Roland Ferenczi is an Indologist and historian. His academic posts include serving as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and as a project researcher at the University of Hamburg (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chuichi Kimura
nodes.summary: Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Ryoji Kishino
nodes.summary: Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yuki Sasaki
nodes.summary: Yuki Sasaki is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who served as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yoshimi Nozawa
nodes.summary: Yoshimi Nozawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Taichi Tado
nodes.summary: Taichi Tado specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and indology. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Vinay Lal
nodes.summary: Vinay Lal is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1987–1992) and became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA around 1993.

nodes.label: Saloni Mathur
nodes.summary: Saloni Mathur works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Her career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was Associate Professor of Art History (attested 2011) and later Professor of Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art and Department Chair.

nodes.label: Monica L. Smith
nodes.summary: Monica L. Smith is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan (circa 1992–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before becoming a professor at UCLA in 2002.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Neuman
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Neuman (born 1944) works in Indology and ethnomusicology, holding degrees from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He taught at Dartmouth (1971–1980), University of Washington (1980–1995), and UCLA (~1994–2018).

nodes.label: Cynthia Talbot
nodes.summary: Cynthia Talbot is an indologist and historian who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1979 to 1988. She became a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin, where she held a post from around 1997.

nodes.label: Winfred P. Lehmann
nodes.summary: Winfred P. Lehmann was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941). He later served as professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).

nodes.label: Edgar Polomé
nodes.summary: Edgar Polomé (1920–2000) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the Catholic University of Louvain from around 1940 to 1949, he served at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1961 to 2000, becoming professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Mirella Lingorska
nodes.summary: Mirella Lingorska specializes in Indology and linguistics. She has held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Rebecca Hufen

nodes.label: Andrew Ollett

nodes.label: Uta Reinöhl
nodes.description: researcher in the field of digital humanities
nodes.summary: Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sarah Merkle-Schneider

nodes.label: Klaus Butzenberger
nodes.summary: Klaus Butzenberger worked in Indology, philosophy, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He taught at Munich, the Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University before serving as Lehrstuhlinhaber at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

nodes.label: Mahiro Ito

nodes.label: Hironobu Minami

nodes.label: Ryushin Saito
nodes.summary: Ryushin Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and serves as a faculty member at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Danuta Stasik

nodes.label: Y. B. Damle

nodes.label: Amartya Sen

nodes.label: Sabine Klein-Schwind

nodes.label: Nandini Gooptu

nodes.label: Sondra L. Hausner

nodes.label: Mallica Kumbera Landrus
