nodes.summary: Praggnaparamita Biswas is a scholar of Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Ratna Basu. She is attested as a research scholar/fellow at the Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Imran Philip
nodes.summary: Imran Philip is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Kaustubh Mani Sengupta. He was awarded a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at the Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni
nodes.summary: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni works in linguistics and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and has been affiliated with the Asiatic Society as a Research Scholar/Fellow (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Biswajit Biswas
nodes.summary: Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Moumita Hossain
nodes.summary: Moumita Hossain is a history and archaeology researcher who studied under Ranjit Sen and serves as a research fellow at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Poulami Ray
nodes.summary: Poulami Ray is a historian and archaeologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. She is attested as a research scholar/fellow at the Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Sulagna Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Sulagna Bhattacharya is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Pratap Bandyopadhyay. She holds an H P Shastri Research Fellowship at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tanaya Afroz
nodes.summary: Tanaya Afroz works in linguistics, having conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya, and served as a research scholar and fellow at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay works in linguistics and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and is a Research Scholar/Fellow at the Asiatic Society (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Minakshi Banerjee
nodes.summary: Minakshi Banerjee, an Indologist, completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar and held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ankita Chakraborty
nodes.summary: Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami. Attested in 2026, she holds a position as a Research Scholar/Fellow at the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Neelima Mundayar
nodes.summary: Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology, attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Wilfried Swenden.

nodes.label: Jiaqi Wang
nodes.summary: Jiaqi Wang was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He was a disciple of Gangkar Rinpoche and was also recorded as a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sravani Kanamarlapudi
nodes.summary: Sravani Kanamarlapudi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the University of Washington (2019), under Richard G. Salomon, and as a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christophe Jaffrelot
nodes.summary: Christophe Jaffrelot specializes in Indology. He studied at Sciences Po (~1985–1991) under Jean Leca, took posts at Sciences Po and CNRS in ~1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London around 2015.

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Chevillard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Chevillard specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli, later holding posts as a researcher at the CNRS (~1991) and lecturer at the University of Hamburg (~2012).

nodes.label: Charles Li
nodes.summary: Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020) and a project research post at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Koichi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Koichi Hiraoka works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he is attested as a guest professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

nodes.label: Alastair Gornall
nodes.summary: Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013). He has served at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2015), SOAS (attested 2019), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tom Ginsburg
nodes.summary: Tom Ginsburg (born 1968) works in law, political science, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999), he taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before joining the University of Chicago around 2008.

nodes.label: Puritat Hongwiwat
nodes.native: ภูริทัต หงษ์วิวัฒน์

nodes.label: Aritri Dutta
nodes.summary: Aritri Dutta works in Tibetology and religious studies. Attested in 2026, she is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Henk Blezer.

nodes.label: S. N. Krishna
nodes.summary: S. N. Krishna is an Indology scholar who studied for a Ph.D. at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: R. Gayathri
nodes.summary: R. Gayathri is an Indology scholar who, as of 2026, is a PhD scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: V. R. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who pursued PhD research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: P. S. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vijayalakshmi Mani
nodes.summary: Vijayalakshmi Mani works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: Lavanya V. Eswar
nodes.summary: Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, she is attested as a Ph.D. scholar studying at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: Yukihiko Asayama
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Ernst Gombrich
variants: エルンスト・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Art historian Ernst Gombrich earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Josef Strzygowski. He spent his career primarily at the Warburg Institute as research assistant, fellow, lecturer, reader, and director from 1959 to 1976.

nodes.label: Toshihiko Izutsu
nodes.description: Japanese author of many books on Islam and other religions (1914–1993)
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) studied at Keio University, where he taught linguistics and Islamic philosophy (1954–1981). He also held posts at McGill University (1961, 1969–1975) and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979), working in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies.

nodes.label: Tadashi Inoue
nodes.summary: Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (director, 1988–2006), Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

nodes.id: I:K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
Sally Mellick Cutler
nodes.summary: Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993. She served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Hamamatsu University
variants: 常葉学園浜松大学経営情報学部

nodes.label: Kempon Hokke Shu Research Institute
variants: 顕本法華宗教学研究所

nodes.id: I:Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale
nodes.label: Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale
variants: イタリア国立東方学研究所

nodes.label: Kansei Tamura
nodes.summary: Kansei Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (both attested 1962).

nodes.label: Katsuji Fujioka
nodes.summary: Katsuji Fujioka was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and Leipzig University (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.

nodes.label: Leonard Bloomfield
variants: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago under Francis A. Wood and Carl Darling Buck, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1910-1921), Ohio State (1921-1927), Chicago (1927-1940), and Yale (1940-1949).

nodes.label: Kaigen Noritake
nodes.summary: Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyo Mitomo. He served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Daito Shimaji
nodes.summary: Daito Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Ryukoku and Otani Universities. He taught at Komazawa University (~1904–1927), Toyo University (~1906–1927), Rissho University (~1924–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

nodes.label: Toho Gakkai
variants: Gesellschaft für Ostasienwissenschaft (東方学会; Tōhōgaku-kai)

nodes.label: Amalia Pezzali
nodes.summary: Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied as a doctoral student under T. R. V. Murti and also studied under Michel Hulin.

nodes.label: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff
nodes.summary: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology. Educated in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he served as professor of Greek language and literature at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

nodes.label: Fumio Masutani
nodes.summary: Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1954–1968) and Taisho University (~1968–1973), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

nodes.label: Kumataro Kawada
nodes.summary: Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held teaching posts at Japan Women's University (1927), Tokyo University of Literature and Science (1943), University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).

nodes.label: Daegu University
variants: 大邱大学校日語日文学科

nodes.label: Hoseong Kim
nodes.summary: Hoseong Kim (born 1960) is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He founded the Japan Buddhist History Research Institute and served as a professor at Dongguk University as attested in 2011.

nodes.label: Chandima
nodes.summary: Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Jogendra Singh
nodes.summary: Jogendra Singh is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under teacher Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.id: I:Shitennoji Research Institute of Buddhist Doctrine
nodes.label: Shitennoji Research Institute of Buddhist Doctrine
Hartmut Scharfe
nodes.summary: Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Carl Friedrich Gauss
variants: ヨハン・カール・フリードリヒ・ガウス
カール・フリードリヒ・ガウス
nodes.summary: Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at TU Braunschweig, Göttingen under Lichtenberg and Heyne, and Helmstedt (PhD). From 1807 to 1855, he served as a full professor at the University of Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.

nodes.label: Daijo Tokiwa
nodes.summary: Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and founded the Koa Buddhist Culture Research Institute.

nodes.label: Yuishin Ito
nodes.summary: Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha universities. He taught at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (1770–1774), he served as professor of Oriental languages at Jena (1775) and professor of philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

nodes.id: I:Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University
nodes.label: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University
variants: 東北大学金属材料研究所

nodes.label: Keiki Yabuki
nodes.summary: Keiki Yabuki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Tohoku Gakuin University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Shukyo University, the University of Tokyo, and served as professor at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Shigeru Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1961) and Harvard University (~1963–1967). He held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1970–1998) and Tenri University.

nodes.label: Unsho Shaku
nodes.summary: Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Koyasan in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juze-kai (1884), Kairitsu Gakko, and Jūzen hōkutsu.

nodes.label: Kozen Shaku
nodes.summary: Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), founded Shakuson Shofukai, and taught Ekai Kawaguchi and Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki.

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
variants: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.summary: Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, the University of Tübingen and Tübinger Stift (~1788–1793), and the University of Jena under F. W. J. Schelling. He held academic posts at Jena (~1801–1807), Heidelberg (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

nodes.label: Bernhard Kölver
nodes.summary: Bernhard Kölver worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne, he held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (1974–1993), and Leipzig University as professor of Indology (1993–2001).

nodes.label: Tübingen University Library
variants: テュービンゲン大学図書館

nodes.label: Georges Dumézil
variants: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.jawiki: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.summary: Georges Dumézil worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss, later holding posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the EPHE (~1933–1968), and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
variants: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.jawiki: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.summary: Claude Lévi-Strauss worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the Paris Law Faculty (~1927–1931) and under Marcel Mauss (~1928–1935). He held posts at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, EHESS, and the Collège de France (1959–1982).

nodes.label: Antoine Meillet
variants: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.summary: Antoine Meillet was a linguist specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Paris under Ferdinand de Saussure, James Darmesteter, and Sylvain Lévi, he taught at INALCO and held chairs at the EPHE and Collège de France (1905–1936).

nodes.label: Émile Benveniste
variants: エミール・バンヴニスト
エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.jawiki: エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Émile Benveniste studied at EPHE and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at EPHE (1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1969).

nodes.label: Theodore Dwight Woolsey
nodes.description: American jurist; president of Yale University (1801–1889)
nodes.summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) studied at Hopkins School, Yale College, Yale University, and Princeton University. He served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from around 1861 to 1881.

nodes.label: Sures Chandra Banerji
nodes.description: born:1917-08-04|died:2000|; Sureśa Candra Bandyopādhyāya 1917-; Banerji, Sures Chandra; Banerji, Sures Chandra 1917-2000

nodes.label: Toru Takahashi
nodes.summary: Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) studied at the University of Tokyo (1898–1902). A specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

nodes.label: Seok-hyeong Kim
nodes.summary: Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University, he served as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Kubo (1883–1972) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University (1953). He taught at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

nodes.label: Ernest Renan
variants: ジョゼフ・エルネスト・ルナン
nodes.summary: A scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and history, Ernest Renan studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and the Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and served as professor and administrator at the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Gyoei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University, as a lecturer at Toyo University, and was appointed professor at the University of Tokyo in 1928.

nodes.label: Victor Henry
nodes.summary: Victor Henry was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the University of Douai (~1880–1887), the University of Lille (~1887–1889), and the University of Paris, where he was appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar in 1888.

nodes.label: Auguste Barth
nodes.summary: Auguste Barth was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his licence at the University of Strasbourg (c. 1853–1856). He taught at Collège de Saverne (c. 1856–1861) and was a member of the Institut de France.

nodes.label: Jean Deloche
nodes.summary: Jean Deloche was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Suryavarman II High School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Anna Seidel
nodes.summary: Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology and religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She joined EFEO (1969), worked at Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991), and founded Cahiers d'Extrême-Asie in 1985.

nodes.label: Götz von Selle
nodes.summary: Götz von Selle studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen. A historian and Central Asian specialist, he worked at the Göttingen and Berlin state libraries before becoming a professor at the University of Göttingen (1938) and the University of Königsberg (ca. 1938–1945).

nodes.label: John Borthwick Gilchrist
variants: ジョン・ボースウィック・ギルクリスト
nodes.image: John Borthwick Gilchrist, cropped from UCL portrait by Blanconi.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・ギルクリスト
nodes.summary: John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist educated at Edinburgh. He served as principal of Fort William College (1800–1804), Oriental Professor at East India Company College (1806), and first Professor of Hindustani at University College London (ca. 1828–1831).

nodes.label: Claudius Buchanan
nodes.summary: Claudius Buchanan worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Cambridge (Queens' College, ~1791–1795), later serving as Vice-Provost at Fort William College in 1801.

nodes.label: Bruno Petzold
variants: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.jawiki: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.summary: Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig and Berlin, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he taught at First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

nodes.label: Seiichiro Ono
nodes.summary: Seiichiro Ono worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and law. He studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino and others, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo and Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Haya Akegarasu
nodes.summary: Haya Akegarasu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He later served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).

nodes.label: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar
variants: ビームラーオ・ラームジー・アンベードカル
nodes.jawiki: ビームラーオ・アンベードカル
nodes.description: Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer (1891–1956)
nodes.summary: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, the University of London, and LSE. He served as professor at Sydenham College (1918, 1920) and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai (1935).

nodes.label: Siddharth College
variants: シッダールタ女子大学

nodes.label: Poerbatjaraka
nodes.summary: Poerbatjaraka worked in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He was a professor at Gadjah Mada University, the University of Indonesia, and Udayana University, which he also founded.

nodes.label: Herman Kellgren
nodes.summary: Herman Kellgren worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf, Philippe-Édouard Foucaux, and Hermann Brockhaus, and held a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1849 to 1856.

nodes.label: David Brown
variants: デイヴィッド・ブラウン
nodes.summary: David Brown was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge (~1782–1785). He served as Provost of Fort William College in 1800.

nodes.label: Magdalene College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学のモードリン・カレッジ

nodes.label: Francis Gladwin
variants: フランシス・グラッドウィン
nodes.description: British scholar of the Persian language
nodes.summary: Francis Gladwin was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as a professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde

nodes.label: Albert Thumb
nodes.image: Professor Albert Thumb 18.05.1865 bis 14.08.1915 Sohn von Ida Schanzenbach und Albert Alois Thump.jpg
nodes.summary: Albert Thumb was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his habilitation at the University of Freiburg (~1888–1891) and held posts at Freiburg (1891, 1895), the University of Marburg (~1901–1909), and the University of Strasbourg (1909).

nodes.label: Genro
nodes.summary: Genro was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of head monk (第一座) at Myōshin-ji.

nodes.label: Hakuin Ekaku
nodes.summary: Hakuin Ekaku was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711, later teaching Suiō Genro.

nodes.label: Julius Klaproth
nodes.jawiki: ユリウス・ハインリヒ・クラプロート

nodes.label: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland
nodes.summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He served as a professor of law at Presidency College, Kolkata.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
nodes.label: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
variants: ノルウェー科学文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Benkyo Shiio
nodes.summary: Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (-1915). He served as president of Taisho University (1926) and was the first director of the Sanko Cultural Institute (~1960–1971).

nodes.label: Karl Ferdinand Johansson
nodes.summary: Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860–1926) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University, where he later served as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages (~1893–1925).

nodes.id: I:W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
nodes.label: W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
variants: American School of Oriental Research in Jerusalem
オルブライト考古学研究所

nodes.label: Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland
variants: Dutch Oriental Society (Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland)

nodes.label: Louis Herbert Gray
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Louis Herbert Gray studied at Princeton (c. 1892–1896) and Columbia University (PhD c. 1896–1900). He held posts at Princeton University (c. 1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

nodes.id: I:Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
nodes.label: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
variants: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH Research
Centre for Bhutan Studies and Gross National Happiness Research
Centre for Bhutan and GNH Studies

nodes.label: Sangay Dorji
nodes.summary: Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies. He taught at ILCS and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Language and Culture Studies
nodes.label: Institute of Language and Culture Studies
Ugyen Pelgen
nodes.summary: Ugyen Pelgen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

nodes.label: John A. Ardussi
nodes.summary: John A. Ardussi is a historian and Tibetologist who studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned his PhD from Australian National University (attested 1977). He has served as a research team member at the CNRS.

nodes.label: Phuntsok Tashi
nodes.summary: Phuntsok Tashi (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (BA) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (MA), and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

nodes.label: George van Driem
variants: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.summary: George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia and Leiden (BA 1987). He held a chair in descriptive linguistics at Leiden University (~2001–2009) and was professor of historical linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Kees W. Bolle
nodes.summary: Kees W. Bolle studied religious studies and Indology at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University (~1961–1964) and was a professor of history at UCLA (~1969–1994).

nodes.label: Thinley Dorji Bhutia
nodes.summary: Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji
nodes.summary: Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a General Council member there from 1964 to 1965.

nodes.label: Henry Creswicke Rawlinson
nodes.image: Rawlinson, Sir Henry Creswick, par Arthur J.Melhuish, BNF Gallica.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・ローリンソン (初代準男爵)
nodes.summary: Henry Creswicke Rawlinson was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, later serving with the East India Company, Foreign Office, and Royal Asiatic Society as director and president.

nodes.label: Georg von der Gabelentz
variants: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
ハンス・ゲオルク・コーノン・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.summary: Georg von der Gabelentz worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Jena, TU Dresden, and Leipzig University. He held professorships at Leipzig University (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1889).

nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
variants: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.jawiki: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.description: British army engineer and amateur archaeologist (1814-1893)
nodes.summary: Alexander Cunningham specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep (1837–1838), founded the Archaeological Survey of India, and served as its first director (1861–1865) and director-general (1871–1885).

nodes.label: Robert Hyde Colebrooke
nodes.description: British infantry officer and surveyor in India (1762–1808)

nodes.label: John Herbert Harington
nodes.description: British administrator in India and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: John Herbert Harington worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of the Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801–1823).

nodes.label: Amaranatha Jha
nodes.summary: Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his B.A. from Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

nodes.label: Charles Elliott
nodes.summary: Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist. He served in the East India Company (~1795–1819) and later held the post of Treasurer at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1837–1856).

nodes.label: George Thomas Staunton
nodes.summary: George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797). He served as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1823 to 1859.

nodes.label: Andover Theological Seminary
variants: アンドーヴァー神学校

nodes.label: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder
nodes.summary: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder (1863–1896) was an Indologist. He graduated from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

nodes.label: Flinders Petrie
nodes.jawiki: フリンダーズ・ピートリー

nodes.label: British School at Athens
variants: British School of Archaeology in Athens

nodes.label: J. Irving Manatt
nodes.summary: J. Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history and archaeology. He studied under William Dwight Whitney and served as a professor at Brown University, attested in 1897.

nodes.label: James Hadley
nodes.summary: James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Yale College and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849. He held posts as a tutor at Middlebury College (1845) and Professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872).

nodes.label: Francis Robinson
nodes.summary: Francis Robinson is a historian of South Asia and Indology. He completed his PhD at Trinity College, Cambridge (-1970), served as a professor and history department head at Royal Holloway (1990–2004), and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1997–2000).

nodes.label: Royal Holloway, University of London
variants: Royal Holloway College der University of London

nodes.label: Gordon Johnson
nodes.summary: Gordon Johnson (born 1943) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, he served as Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge (1974–2010), President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

nodes.label: Kurfürst-Ruprecht-Gymnasium Neustadt
variants: Gymnasium at Neustadt an der Haardt

nodes.label: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe
nodes.summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at Richmond College and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, he worked as an epigraphist for the Government of Sri Lanka (~1899–1929) and at the University of London (~1918–1930).

nodes.label: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at King's College London and Heidelberg, he served as Principal of Government College University, Lahore (1864), and first Registrar of the University of the Punjab (circa 1882–1885).

nodes.label: George Uglow Pope
nodes.summary: George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist. He headed St. Peter's Higher Secondary School, Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870), and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), later lecturing in Tamil at Oxford University (~1884–1908) and Balliol College (1888).

nodes.label: Rewata Dhamma
nodes.summary: Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees, including a PhD, from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, as well as a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Narada Maha Thera
nodes.image: Portrait Of Most Venerable Narada Maha Thera (1898-1983).jpg
nodes.summary: Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Ceylon University College, and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya from circa 1955 to 1983.

nodes.label: C. R. Krishnamacharlu
nodes.summary: C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Madras Christian College (F. A.) and Pachaiyappa's College.

nodes.label: Oliver Codrington
nodes.summary: Oliver Codrington was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

nodes.label: José Gerson da Cunha
nodes.description: Indo-Portuguese physician, orientalist, historian, linguist, and numismatist

nodes.label: Dermot Killingley
nodes.summary: Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. He held posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and Newcastle University (~1970–2000), also serving as visiting professor at the University of Vienna (2008).

nodes.label: Institute of Economic Growth
variants: Institute of Economic Growth (University of Delhi)

nodes.label: Sumathi Ramaswamy
nodes.summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, and held faculty positions at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Declan Quigley
nodes.summary: Declan Quigley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.label: Gauri Viswanathan
nodes.summary: Gauri Viswanathan is a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University. She taught English at the University of Delhi and was appointed Class of 1933 Professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia.

nodes.label: Henry Herbert Dodwell
nodes.summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell was a historian and Indologist educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS.

nodes.label: Madan Mohan Malaviya
nodes.summary: Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indology scholar who studied at Muir Central College, University of Calcutta, and University of Allahabad. He taught at Government Inter College, Prayagraj, founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and served as its Vice Chancellor (1919–1938).

nodes.label: Suzanne Karpelès
nodes.summary: Suzanne Karpelès studied at the EPHE under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot. She served at EFEO (1922–1925), was the first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925), and became the Buddhist Institute's first secretary-general (1930).

nodes.label: Henry Sullivan Jarrett
nodes.summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in history and archaeology. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta from circa 1870 to 1896, succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

nodes.label: Heinrich Blochmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leipzig under Fleischer, Paris under Hase, and Calcutta. He held posts at Fort William College, Doveton College, and Aliah University, serving as principal from 1865.

nodes.label: Ian James Coghlan
nodes.summary: Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate in Asian Studies at La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Holly Gayley
nodes.summary: Holly Gayley works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

nodes.label: Heinz Adolf Mode
nodes.description: German art historian, orientalist and indologist (1913-1992)
nodes.summary: Heinz Adolf Mode worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at Basel. He was a professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

nodes.id: I:Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
nodes.label: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
variants: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR

nodes.label: Otto Fischer
nodes.description: German art historian, director of Kunstmuseum Basel (1886–1948)
nodes.summary: Otto Fischer specialized in sinology and history/archaeology, studying at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He was director of Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920), head of Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and associate professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

nodes.label: Willem Bollée
nodes.summary: Willem Bollée was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1947-1956) and the University of Hamburg (habilitated by 1975). He held posts at the University of Münster (1971-1978) and Heidelberg University (~1972-1992).

nodes.label: William Frederic Sinclair
nodes.summary: William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and held a post with the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フォン・ハンマー・プルグスタル
nodes.summary: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799), taught Friedrich Rückert, and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).

nodes.label: Dilli Raman Regmi
nodes.summary: Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University (-1961), and worked as a teacher at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: William Rainey Harper
nodes.summary: A linguist and religious studies scholar, Harper studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Denison and Yale before serving as president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (~1897–1906).

nodes.label: Daniel Coit Gilman
nodes.summary: Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of UC Berkeley (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

nodes.label: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh
nodes.summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

nodes.label: Thomas Jülch
nodes.summary: Thomas Jülch (born 1975) works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Hull (MA), Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD circa 2006–2011), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).

nodes.id: I:Singapore University of Technology and Design
nodes.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design
variants: Singapore University of Technology and Design

nodes.label: Thomas Roebuck
nodes.summary: Thomas Roebuck (1781–1819) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School. He was assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George (1811) and a member of the Asiatic Society (circa 1811–1819).

nodes.id: I:Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
nodes.label: Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
variants: Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies (慶應大學言語文化研究所)
Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies

nodes.label: Lionel Obadia
nodes.summary: Lionel Obadia (born 1968) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Lille (1997). He held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille III, and as Professor at Lumière University Lyon 2.

nodes.label: Richard Hughes Seager
nodes.summary: Richard Hughes Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD), and was appointed Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.

nodes.label: Michelle Spuler
nodes.summary: Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2001) and has taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington.

nodes.label: William Muir
nodes.summary: Active in history and archaeology, Muir was educated at Kilmarnock Academy, the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1836), and Haileybury (~1836–1837). He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).

nodes.label: Robert Maclagan
nodes.description: British Army officer and military engineer (1820–94)
nodes.summary: Robert Maclagan was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering, and served as Principal at Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (1847–1860).

nodes.label: Erberto Lo Bue
nodes.description: Italian indologist, tibetologist, translator and university teacher
nodes.summary: Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1981. He held academic posts at the University of Milan and the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Corpus Christi College, Cambridge
variants: Corpus Christi College der Universität Cambridge
ケンブリッジ大学コーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Edward Delavan Perry
nodes.summary: Edward Delavan Perry worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (A.B. ~1871-1875) and the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil. ~1877-1879), and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

nodes.label: Rajendralal Mitra
nodes.summary: Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Medical College and Hospital and the University of Calcutta. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary and later president of the Asiatic Society, and directed the Wards' Institution.

nodes.label: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
nodes.jawiki: フランシス・ブキャナン＝ハミルトン
nodes.summary: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history and archaeology after receiving his MD at the University of Edinburgh (~1780–1783). He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815) and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

nodes.label: Mona Schrempf
nodes.summary: Mona Schrempf works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin (2001) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jogindra Nath Samaddar
nodes.summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency College, Kolkata. He held teaching posts at Pramatha Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College, and Patna University.

nodes.label: Winfred Robert Martin
nodes.summary: Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

nodes.label: Daniel John Gogerly
nodes.summary: Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He ran the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (1838), and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1856–1858).

nodes.label: Graves Chamney Haughton
nodes.summary: Graves Chamney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Fort William College. He co-founded and served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was Professor of Hindú Literature at East India Company College (1819–1827).

nodes.label: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study
variants: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences

nodes.label: John Leyden
nodes.summary: John Leyden was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Edinburgh and under Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He served at the Asiatic Society (~1806–1811) and was a professor of Hindustani at Fort William College in 1808.

nodes.label: J. M. E. McTaggart
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マクタガート
nodes.summary: J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1891–1925) and taught Surendranath Dasgupta.

nodes.label: Parul Dave-Mukherji
nodes.summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji is an Indologist and art historian who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991). She has served as a professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: John Hallett Batten
nodes.summary: Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, Batten was educated at Charterhouse School and the East India Company College (~1827–1829).

nodes.label: Kazuaki Komine
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Komine worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees including a doctorate from Waseda University. He taught at Waseda Jitsugyo Gakko, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and served as professor at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

nodes.label: Hermann Sauppe
nodes.summary: Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann, later holding posts at the University of Zurich, University of Vienna, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and University of Göttingen (1855).

nodes.label: Addiscombe Military Seminary
variants: Hon. East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
Honourable East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
アディスコム軍事神学校

nodes.label: Henry George Keene
nodes.description: English employee of the East India Company and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: Henry George Keene worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, served with the East India Company, and was Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College.

nodes.label: William Price
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Price was Professor of Hindūstaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830) and a member of the Asiatic Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: John Shakespear
nodes.summary: John Shakespear worked in linguistics and Indology after studying under John Richardson. He held professorships at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809), and Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).

nodes.label: David Shea
nodes.summary: David Shea was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (1793) and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at the East India Company College until 1836.

nodes.label: Sensho Murakami
nodes.summary: Sensho Murakami worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University, Higashi Honganji Kyoshi Gakko, and Toyo University, and later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1917–1923) and lecturer at Otani University.

nodes.label: Emil Rödiger
variants: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.jawiki: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.summary: Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. After earning his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. at Halle-Wittenberg, he became professor there and later at Humboldt University of Berlin, also serving the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

nodes.label: Alfred Master
nodes.description: Master, Alfred (1883-1978) Lecturer in Indian Philology

nodes.label: William Erskine
nodes.summary: William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1787-1792).

nodes.label: James Atkinson
nodes.description: English surgeon, artist and Persian scholar (1780–1852)
nodes.summary: James Atkinson was an Indologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College.

nodes.label: Dayong
nodes.summary: Dayong (1893–1929) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he also taught in 1923, and studied under Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, Taixu, Puren Bai, and Geshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Buddhist Academy of China
variants: Institute of Buddhist Studies of Beijing

nodes.label: Eberhard Schrader
nodes.summary: Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1854–1858). He held posts at Zurich, Giessen, Jena, and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

nodes.label: John Thompson Platts
variants: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.summary: Platts was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at Bedford School and Balliol College. He held teaching and administrative posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Saugor High School before becoming Teacher of Persian at Oxford (1880).

nodes.id: P:Richard Fleming St Andrew St John
nodes.label: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John
nodes.enwiki: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John

nodes.label: Finnian M. M. Gerety
nodes.summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety works in Indology and religious studies. After earning a doctorate from Harvard University by 2015 and completing a postdoc at Yale (2017–2018), he became a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Andrea R. Jain
nodes.summary: Andrea R. Jain is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010), holding posts at the University of Houston, Rice University, IUPUI, and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became professor.

nodes.label: Hidehiko Kurita
nodes.summary: Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University and was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.

nodes.label: Kwangsoo Park
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Kwangsoo Park earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Samani Pratibha Pragya
nodes.summary: Samani Pratibha Pragya is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and later worked there as a research assistant (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Julian Strube
nodes.summary: Julian Strube, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, habilitated at Heidelberg University. He taught at Vienna (2021-2024) before being appointed professor of religious studies and intercultural theology at the University of Göttingen in 2024.

nodes.label: Edward Clive Bayley
nodes.summary: Edward Clive Bayley worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and the East India Company College (~1840-1842), and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

nodes.label: Henry Miers Elliot
nodes.summary: Henry Miers Elliot worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Winchester College, he served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

nodes.label: Justus Olshausen
variants: ユストゥス・オルスハウゼン
nodes.summary: Justus Olshausen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, later serving as professor at Kiel University (1823) and Chief Librarian and Professor of Oriental Languages at Königsberg (1852).

nodes.label: Étienne Marc Quatremère
nodes.image: Portret van de oriëntalist Étienne Marc Quatremère Quatremère, Etienne-Marc (titel op object) Leden van het Institut Royal de France (serietitel) Iconographie de l'Institut royal de France (serietitel op object), RP-P-1911-978.jpg
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, history, and archaeology, Étienne Marc Quatremère studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held a post at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

nodes.label: Christopher Andreas Holmboe
nodes.summary: Christopher Andreas Holmboe worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1814–1818) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval in 1821, later serving as Reader (1822) and Professor of Oriental Languages (1828) at Oslo.

nodes.label: Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval
nodes.summary: Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He served as professor of modern Arabic at INALCO from 1821, professor of Arabic at the Collège de France from 1833, and held a post at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from 1849.

nodes.label: Carl Paul Caspari
nodes.summary: Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin. At the University of Oslo, he was appointed lektor in 1847 and professor in 1857.

nodes.label: Hokkaido University of Education

nodes.label: Doranne Jacobson
nodes.summary: Doranne Jacobson is a scholar in Indology and other fields. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University, where she also held a post as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

nodes.label: McKim Marriott
variants: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.jawiki: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.summary: McKim Marriott (1924–2024) worked in Indology and anthropology. He studied at Harvard under Clyde Kluckhohn and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1948–1955), where he served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences from ~1957 to 1998.

nodes.label: Gore Ouseley
nodes.summary: Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (circa 1810–1815) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (circa 1823–1844).

nodes.label: S. Sankaranarayanan
nodes.summary: S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian who served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from circa 1986 to 1999, and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

nodes.label: Chinmaya International Foundation
variants: Adi Sankara Nilayam, Chinmaya International Foundation

nodes.label: R. Thangaswami Sarma
nodes.summary: R. Thangaswami Sarma worked in Indology and philosophy after studying at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. He held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

nodes.label: Sree Sarada Education Society
variants: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre

nodes.label: Geoffrey Goble
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington, later serving as Assistant Professor at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

nodes.label: August Boeckh
nodes.summary: August Boeckh was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg under Wolf and Schleiermacher (c. 1803–1806). He taught at Grauen Kloster (1806–1807), Heidelberg (1807–1811), and the University of Berlin (1811–1861; Humboldt c. 1810–1867).

nodes.label: Max Leopold Margolis
nodes.summary: Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from Columbia University (1891). He held positions at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and Dropsie College for Hebrew and Cognate Learning (1909–1932).

variants: 和歌山赤十字看護専門学校

nodes.label: Yuka Otani
nodes.summary: Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: George Cœdès
nodes.summary: George Cœdès worked in Indology, Sinology, and archaeology. He studied at EPHE and Berlin under Finot, Lévi, Foucher, and Pischel. He served as director of EFEO (1929–1947), headed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and held posts in Paris.

nodes.id: I:Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
nodes.label: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
