Sri Lanka branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Arthur Emanuel Christensen
nodes.summary: Arthur Emanuel Christensen was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding the first chair of Oriental studies at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.

nodes.label: Friedrich Carl Andreas
nodes.jawiki: フリードリッヒ・カール・アンドレアス
nodes.summary: Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1867-1868) and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887-1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903-1930).

nodes.label: Henrik Samuel Nyberg
variants: エンリコ・サムエリ・ニーベリ
nodes.summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg studied at Uppsala University, beginning in 1908. He taught at Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919) and served as Dozent and Professor of Semitic languages at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).

nodes.label: Otto Höfler
nodes.summary: Otto Höfler worked in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology, studying at Vienna, Lund, and Kiel under Rudolf Much. He held posts at Uppsala, Lund, Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).

nodes.label: George Shirt
nodes.summary: George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his education at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1864.

nodes.label: Jean Humbert
nodes.description: academic (1792 - 1851), member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino since 1832

nodes.label: Syed Ali Bilgrami
nodes.summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Patna College, Canning College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and Lucknow and London universities, he served Hyderabad State (~1879–1901) and Cambridge University (1901).

nodes.label: Sukumari Bhattacharji
nodes.summary: Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University, and held teaching posts at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

nodes.label: Johann Tobias Beck
nodes.summary: Johann Tobias Beck studied at the University of Tübingen from circa 1822 to 1826. Working in religious studies, he held posts at the University of Basel (circa 1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (circa 1843–1878).

nodes.label: Gerardus van der Leeuw
variants: ヘラルドゥス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.jawiki: ゲラルダス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.description: Dutch religious studies scholar and politician (1890–1950)
nodes.summary: Gerardus van der Leeuw was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916). He spent his career as a professor at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

nodes.label: Edward Albert Gait
nodes.summary: Edward Albert Gait (1863–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at University College London, founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914, and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

nodes.label: Frederick James Furnivall
nodes.summary: Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1910), and founded several literary societies.

nodes.label: Royal Masonic School for Boys
variants: Royal Masonic School for Boys at Wood Green

nodes.label: Tanzan Hara
nodes.summary: Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He was appointed professor of Buddhist doctrine at the University of Tokyo in 1879 and served as superintendent of Komazawa University in 1891.

nodes.id: P:Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo
nodes.label: Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo
13th Dalai Lama
nodes.summary: 13th Dalai Lama (1876–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Terton Sogyal, Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, and Yeshe Chopel, and taught numerous disciples, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

nodes.label: Kumja Paik Kim
nodes.summary: Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a doctorate at Stanford University and was appointed curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco in 1989.

nodes.label: Leedom Lefferts
nodes.summary: Leedom Lefferts specializes in Buddhist studies and anthropology. He has served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University (attested 2011) and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Kavita Singh
nodes.summary: Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Lady Shri Ram College, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, Panjab University, and University of the Punjab. She held posts at Marg Publications, San Diego Museum of Art, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.id: I:Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures
nodes.label: Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures
variants: Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures
Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures (SISJAC), University of East Anglia

nodes.label: Jules Michelet
nodes.description: French historian; popularized the historical concept of the Renaissance
nodes.summary: Historian Jules Michelet studied at Lycée Charlemagne before teaching at the École Normale Supérieure from 1827. He later served as section chief at the Archives nationales (1831-1852) and Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838-1852).

nodes.label: Raghu Ananthanarayanan
nodes.summary: Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. He taught at the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad.

nodes.label: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Mysore, Queen's College, Oxford, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1952).

nodes.label: T. K. V. Desikachar
nodes.summary: T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

nodes.label: Catherine Cornille
nodes.summary: Catherine Cornille is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later serving as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College around 2005.

nodes.label: Manshi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served at Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School and became the founding president of Otani University (1901–1902).

nodes.label: Ernest Fenollosa
variants: アーネスト・フランシスコ・フェノロサ
nodes.jawiki: アーネスト・フェノロサ
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy, Japanology, and history and archaeology, Ernest Fenollosa graduated from Harvard and studied at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He taught at the University of Tokyo from 1878, was curator at Boston's MFA (1890–1896), and founded Tokyo Fine Arts School.

nodes.label: Kyoto Prefectural First Middle School
variants: Jinjō Middle School 尋常中学校

nodes.id: I:Institute of Oriental Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Oriental Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences
Yasunori Ejima
nodes.summary: Yasunori Ejima (1939-1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Göttingen, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1987-1999) and head of the JAIBS.

nodes.label: The Eastern Buddhist
variants: イースタン・ブディスト

nodes.label: Gembo Dorji
nodes.summary: Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Monastery, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving training from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

nodes.id: P:Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
nodes.label: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
variants: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drimé Lekpé Lodrö

nodes.label: Khenpo Gangshar
nodes.summary: Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Shechen Monastery under Jamgon Kongtrul II, Shechen Kongtrul, and Karsé Kongtrul, later serving as senior teacher there and as founding dean at Surmang Monastery (~1957–1958).

nodes.label: Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Ngawang Nyima, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and Thubten Jigme Norbu.

nodes.label: Khakyab Dorje
nodes.summary: Khakyab Dorje was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught figures such as Kalu Rinpoche and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo.

nodes.id: P:11th Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo
nodes.label: Pema Wangchok Gyalpo
Karuna Kusalasaya
nodes.native: กรุณา กุศลาสัย
nodes.summary: Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Fafang
nodes.summary: Fafang (1904–1951) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Taixu and served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Kwei-Sun Wei
nodes.summary: Active in Sinology and Indology, Kwei-Sun Wei completed a PhD at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a professor at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satiranjan Sen
nodes.summary: Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Indology, studying at Peking University. He was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

nodes.id: P:Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho
nodes.label: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho
variants: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Yuexia
nodes.summary: Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Avatamsaka University, where he also served as a teacher.

nodes.label: Dixian
nodes.summary: Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu. He served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

nodes.label: Nicholas Roerich
nodes.jawiki: ニコライ・リョーリフ
nodes.description: Russian painter, writer, archaeologist and philosopher (1874–1947)
nodes.summary: Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947), active in history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies, studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and founded the Urusvati Institute.

nodes.label: New Asia College
variants: New Asia College der Chinesischen Universität Hongkong
New Asia College in Hong Kong
香港中文大学新亜書院

nodes.id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
nodes.label: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
John Lockwood Kipling
nodes.image: John Lockwood Kipling és Rudyard Kipling.jpg
nodes.summary: John Lockwood Kipling was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875), served as Principal of the National College of Arts, and was Curator of the Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

nodes.label: Alfonsa Ferrari
nodes.summary: Alfonsa Ferrari worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi at Sapienza University of Rome from around 1937 to 1941, continuing there with post-graduate research until approximately 1948.

nodes.label: Jacques Bacot
nodes.image: Tchraker lama, Jacques Bacot et moines.png
nodes.summary: Jacques Bacot was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

nodes.label: Daoquan Yu
nodes.summary: Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Jacques Bacot. He served as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China.

nodes.label: Lorna Dewaraja
nodes.summary: Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, she held posts at the University of Colombo and served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Peradeniya.

nodes.label: Senarat Wijayasundara
nodes.summary: Senarat Wijayasundara worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Geshe Dorje
variants: Duojie gexi zunzhe 多傑格西尊者

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wundt
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.description: German physician, physiologist, philosopher and professor (1832–1920)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wundt, a scholar of philosophy, studied at Tübingen (~1851–1852), Heidelberg (~1852–1855), and Berlin (~1856). He held posts at the University of Zurich (1857), Leipzig University (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

nodes.label: Edvard Westermarck
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・ウェスターマーク
nodes.summary: Edvard Westermarck (1862–1939) was a philosopher and scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki (circa 1881–1889). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (circa 1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (circa 1918–1932).

nodes.label: Dedong Wei
nodes.summary: Dedong Wei (born 1968) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies (~2002).

nodes.label: Claude Jacques
nodes.summary: Claude Jacques was an Indologist and historian who studied under George Cœdès. He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1998).

nodes.label: Amy Paris Langenberg
nodes.image: Amy Paris Langenberg in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her Ph.D. from Columbia University and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014–2020).

nodes.id: P:sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
variants: sGangs ru tshul khrims rgyal mtshan

nodes.label: Marsha Weidner
nodes.summary: Marsha Weidner works in Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts as assistant professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and professor at the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Damdin Badaraev
nodes.summary: Damdin Badaraev was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

nodes.label: Adhémard Leclère
nodes.summary: Adhémard Leclère (1853–1917) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as Résident de France at Kratie in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société d'ethnologie, which he founded.

nodes.label: Giovanni Gentile
variants: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.jawiki: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.description: Italian philosopher, educator, fascist theoretician and politician (1875-1944)
nodes.summary: Giovanni Gentile was a philosopher educated at the Scuola Normale Superiore and University of Pisa. He was a professor at Palermo (1906–1914), Pisa (1914–1917), and Sapienza (1917–1944), and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (1933).

nodes.id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
nodes.label: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro studied under traditional teachers Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

nodes.label: First Zen Institute of America
variants: Kyoto branch of the First Institute of America
First Zen Institute of America in Japan
First Zen Institute of America in Kyoto

nodes.label: Bart Gruzalski
nodes.summary: Bart Gruzalski is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 1974. He later served as a professor of philosophy at Northeastern University.

nodes.label: Emmanuel College, Toronto
variants: Emmanuel College of Victoria University in the University of Toronto

nodes.label: Tao Pan
nodes.summary: Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Nicholas Witkowski
nodes.summary: Nicholas Witkowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at Stanford University in 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Yingguang Qu
nodes.summary: Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1905–1907) and under traditional teachers Nordan Hutuktu (1926) and Puren Bai (1929).

nodes.label: Yuanxing Guo
nodes.summary: Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche. Guo held posts as a researcher at the Buddhist Association of China and at Jinling Scriptural Press.

nodes.label: Buddhist Association of China
variants: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism (Zhongguo Fojiao Wenhua Yanjiusuo 中國佛教文化研究所)

nodes.label: Nianzu Huang
nodes.summary: Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia, Hsu Yun, and Gongga Rinpoche. In Buddhist studies, he headed the Central Broadcasting Station and was a professor at BUPT (~1953).

nodes.label: Voice of America
variants: Tibetan Broadcast Service for Voice of America

nodes.label: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz
nodes.summary: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Vienna, SOAS, Berlin, and LSE, he studied under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock, and served at Weltmuseum Wien in 1958.

nodes.label: Pieter Hendrik Pott
nodes.summary: Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. He served as curator at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

nodes.label: Constantin Regamey
nodes.summary: Constantin Regamey was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Warsaw and Paris under Schayer, Turczyński, Przyluski, and Lalou, and later taught at Warsaw, Lausanne, and Fribourg, also serving as president of the Swiss Asia Society.

nodes.label: Lajos Ligeti
nodes.summary: Lajos Ligeti studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and the University of Paris under scholars including Paul Pelliot. Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Inner Asian studies, he held the chair of Inner Asian Studies at Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Chogye Shabdrung
nodes.summary: Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso and attended Sakya College in 2003.

nodes.label: Rustam Sabirov
nodes.summary: Rustam Sabirov works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned a doctorate in history at Moscow State University by 2004 and has served there as a Senior Researcher.

nodes.label: Krisztina Teleki
nodes.description: (1978–) Hungarian literary translator, linguist, orientalist, tibetologist and mongolist
nodes.summary: Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her MA at Eötvös Loránd University (~1996–2009), where she also served as a research fellow (~2009).

nodes.label: King's College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学キングズコレッジ
ケンブリッジ大学キングズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Immanuel Kant
nodes.summary: Immanuel Kant was a philosopher who was educated at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He was appointed to the chair of logic and metaphysics at the University of Königsberg in 1770.

nodes.label: August Conrady
variants: アウグスト・コンラーディ
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・コンラーディ (中国学者)
nodes.summary: August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Würzburg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig. He held posts at Leipzig University from 1891 (becoming Ordinariat in 1922) and taught at Peking University (1903–1904).

nodes.label: Berthold Laufer
variants: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.image: Annual report of the Director to the Board of Trustees for the year .. (1933) (17811378703).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.summary: Berthold Laufer worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Iranian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady and others. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History (1907).

nodes.label: Bruno Schindler
variants: ブルーノ・シンドラー
nodes.summary: Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a Sinologist who completed his doctorate under August Conrady (~1912–1919). He founded Asia Major in 1923 and served as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries from ~1939 to 1964.

nodes.label: Johannes Schubert
nodes.summary: Johannes Schubert specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at Leipzig University and under August Conrady and Friedrich Weller. He worked at the Leipzig University Library (ca. 1927–1954) and held teaching posts and a professorship at Leipzig University (1934–1962).

nodes.label: Stanisław Schayer
nodes.summary: Stanisław Schayer was an Indologist and philosopher. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of both the Warsaw Scientific Society (~1930-1941) and the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences (~1933-1941).

nodes.label: Jan Jaworski
nodes.summary: Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw and under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

nodes.label: Ludwik Skurzak
nodes.summary: Ludwik Skurzak is an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held an academic post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

nodes.label: Maryla Falk
nodes.description: Polish indologist and historian of religions
nodes.summary: Maryla Falk was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1934–1938) and was a member of the Polish Oriental Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz
nodes.summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1928). He held posts at the University of Lviv (~1934–1944), Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1969), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

nodes.label: Paul Ekman
nodes.summary: Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He served on the faculty at the University of California, San Francisco from circa 1960 to 2004.

nodes.label: Somchai Kusalacitto
nodes.summary: Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: François Jacob
variants: フランソワ・ジャコブ
nodes.summary: François Jacob earned doctoral degrees at the University of Paris (~1938–1947, ~1950–1954). He held posts at the Pasteur Institute (1960), Collège de France (1964), the Cabanel Center, and was elected to the Académie Française in 1996.

nodes.label: Stephen Addiss
nodes.summary: Stephen Addiss specialized in Japanology and art history. He earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan, subsequently serving as professor of art history at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and Tucker-Boatwright Professor at the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

nodes.label: Juan Wu
nodes.summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Laurence Austine Waddell
nodes.summary: Laurence Austine Waddell (1854-1938) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow (~1874-1878). He served in the Indian Medical Service and Indian Army, taught at Kolkata's Medical College, and was Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906-1908).

nodes.label: Yuanying
nodes.summary: Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under several teachers, including Tongzhi and Bazhi Toutuo. He was abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, and served as first Venerable Master of the Buddhist Association of China.

nodes.label: Marian Ury
nodes.summary: Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis (1969–1995).

nodes.label: Eric J. Sharpe
nodes.summary: Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Hartley Victoria College, the University of Manchester, and Uppsala University, he held posts at Manchester (1966), Lancaster (1970), Uppsala (1978–1981), and Sydney (1977–1996).

nodes.label: Phra Rajavaramuni
nodes.native: พระราชวรมุนี
nodes.summary: Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. As of 2012, he served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Tampalawela Dhammaratana
nodes.summary: Tampalawela Dhammaratana (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sunethradevi Pirivena, the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

nodes.label: Liqian Liu
nodes.summary: Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University, the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, and the Ethnic Publishing House.

nodes.label: West China Union University
variants: Border Area Institute of Research of the West China University

nodes.id: I:State Council of the People's Republic of China
nodes.label: State Council of the People's Republic of China
Genzao
nodes.summary: Genzao (d. 1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and received instruction from traditional teachers Gyang rtse Rin po che (in 1948) and Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Monastery
variants: monastische Kolleg Shri Singha des Dzogchen-Klosters

nodes.id: I:Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.label: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
variants: Beijing Institute of Post and Telecommunications

nodes.label: Charles Alfred Bell
nodes.summary: Charles Alfred Bell was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

nodes.label: Augustus William Heyde
nodes.description: German missionary to Tibetans in Northern India; b. Wilhelm Heide, Feb. 16, 1825; later changed surname to Heyde; d. Aug. 27, 1907

nodes.label: Edward Sapir
nodes.summary: Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910-1925) and taught at the University of Chicago (~1925-1931) and Yale University (~1931-1939).

nodes.label: Friedrich Schleiermacher
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュライアマハー
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and biblical scholar (1768-1834)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787-1790), where he later held a post (~1804-1807), before holding a chair at the University of Berlin (~1810-1834).

nodes.label: Kazan Federal University
variants: Oriental department of the Kazan University
Department of Mongolian Studies at Kazan University

nodes.label: Józef Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Józef Kowalewski worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan universities, he headed Mongol studies and became rector at Kazan Federal University (1833–1860) before serving as professor and dean at the University of Warsaw from 1862.

nodes.label: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Akyong Tokden Lodrö Gyatso.

nodes.label: Longlian
nodes.summary: Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun beginning in 1939 and also studied under Nenghai Shi.

nodes.label: Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies
variants: Institut d'études du bouddhisme sino-tibétain (Hanzang jiaoli yuan)
Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (Hanzang Jiaoliyuan 漢藏教理院)

nodes.label: Guankong
nodes.summary: Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

nodes.label: D. Neil Schmid
nodes.summary: D. Neil Schmid works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student of Victor H. Mair.

nodes.label: Rachel H. Pang
nodes.summary: Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and was attested in 2019 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

nodes.label: Sangseraima Ujeed
nodes.summary: Sangseraima Ujeed is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2012–2017). She held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

nodes.label: Sokatsu Shaku
nodes.summary: Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Zen figure who studied under Kosen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Tōkyō Ryōbōkai, Ryobokai Dojo of North America, and Ningen Zen, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki and Zuigan Goto.

nodes.label: Peter Connolly
nodes.summary: Peter Connolly works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

nodes.label: Lynn Thomas
nodes.summary: Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Lancaster University and a D. Phil from the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Pratap Kumar Penumala
nodes.summary: Pratap Kumar Penumala is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a visiting professor at Colorado College (both attested 2010).

nodes.label: Eiichi Makino
nodes.summary: Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy and law who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Chuo University, Tohoku University, Kyushu University, and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College.

nodes.label: Shigemitsu Dando
nodes.summary: Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974), and served on the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Foy, and later taught Yinke Chen.

nodes.label: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal
nodes.summary: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the universities of Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from ~1836 to 1845.

nodes.label: Shenphen Nangwa
nodes.summary: Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Önpo Tenzin Norbu, and Mipam Gyatso, among others. He held teaching posts at Shri Singha Shedra, Dzogchen Monastery, and Dzongsar Monastery.

nodes.label: Patrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu from around 1830 to 1842 and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught prominent figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Terton Sogyal.

nodes.label: Denise Bernot
nodes.summary: Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar of linguistics. She studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and later held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1960–1989).

nodes.label: Georg Ruppelt
nodes.image: Georg Ruppelt Direktor der Gottfried-Wilhelm-Leibniz Bibliothek anläßlich der Buchvorstellung Alles über Wikipedia im Werner Kraft Vortragssaal.jpg

nodes.label: Sven Hedin
nodes.description: Swedish geographer, topographer, explorer, photographer, travel writer and illustrator (1865-1952)
nodes.summary: Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a Central Asian and Tibetan studies explorer and scholar. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the Humboldt University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen (~1889–1892), and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1892).

nodes.label: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart
variants: Württembergische Museum der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart

nodes.label: Eileen Power
nodes.summary: Eileen Power (1889–1940) was a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Oxford High School, Girton College, and the University of Paris, and later held posts at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

nodes.label: James Darmesteter
nodes.jawiki: ジャーム・ダルメステテール
nodes.summary: James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal (~1872–1877), later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

nodes.label: Émile Durkheim
variants: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.jawiki: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.summary: A scholar in religious studies and sociology, Émile Durkheim studied at ENS, University of Bordeaux, and Leipzig University under Wilhelm Wundt. He held academic posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), EPHE (1905), and the University of Paris (professor in 1902).

nodes.label: Marcel Cohen
nodes.summary: Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954), the University of Paris, and the newspaper L'Humanité (~1944–1974).

nodes.label: Lucien Tesnière
nodes.jawiki: ルシアン・テニエール
nodes.summary: Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig University, and under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the universities of Ljubljana (1920–1924), Strasbourg (1924–1937), and Montpellier (1937).

nodes.label: Pierre Chantraine
nodes.summary: Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between 1920 and 1927. He later held a post at the University of Paris from around 1937 to 1969.

nodes.label: Michel Lejeune
nodes.summary: Michel Lejeune (1907–2000) was a French linguist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1931). He later held posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1941), the University of Paris (~1947–1955), and the EPHE (~1951–1977).

nodes.label: Jerzy Kuryłowicz
variants: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.jawiki: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.summary: Jerzy Kuryłowicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1926) and under Antoine Meillet (~1921–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1927–1945) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).

nodes.label: André Martinet
nodes.jawiki: アンドレ・マルティネ
nodes.summary: André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne (~1928-1937) under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938-1946), Columbia University (~1947-1955), and the University of Paris (~1955-1977).

nodes.label: Joseph Vendryes
nodes.image: Réunion des doyens des facultés dans le bureau du recteur, décembre 1940. M. Bruhat M. Gidel M. Baudouin M. Carcopino M. Maurain M. Vendryès M. Damiens (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョゼフ・ヴァンドリエス
nodes.summary: Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901-1960), University of Paris (~1907-1946), and École Normale Supérieure (~1920-1946).

nodes.label: Alfred Ernout
nodes.summary: Alfred Ernout was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1951), the University of Paris (~1927–1949), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

nodes.label: Rakuhoku High School
variants: Kyōto Prefectural Ordinary Junior High School

nodes.label: Jacques André
nodes.summary: Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (-1948). He held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

nodes.label: Raphael Kühner
nodes.summary: Raphael Kühner was a linguist who was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1821 to 1825.

nodes.label: Peter K. Austin
nodes.summary: Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He later held a position at SOAS University of London from circa 2002 to 2018.

nodes.label: Matthias Alexander Castrén
nodes.jawiki: マティアス・カストラン
nodes.summary: Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki / Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and held a post there from ~1840 to 1852.

nodes.id: I:Yasodhara: Newsletter on International Buddhist Women's Activities
nodes.label: Yasodhara: Newsletter on International Buddhist Women's Activities
variants: Yasodhara: The Newsletter on International Buddhist Women's Activities

variants: École nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer
École nationale de la France d’Outre-Mer
フランス海外領国立学校

nodes.label: Robert Göbl
nodes.summary: Robert Göbl was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1955 to 1989.

nodes.label: Karl Lachmann
nodes.summary: Karl Lachmann worked in linguistics and related fields. After studying at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen, he held a long-term academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.

nodes.label: Tulane University
variants: H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College der Tulane University
Harriet Sophie Newcomb College at Tulane University

nodes.label: Alan Lomax
nodes.jawiki: アラン・ローマックス
nodes.summary: Alan Lomax (1915–2002) completed his education at St. Mark's School of Texas, Choate Rosemary Hall, Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1934–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).

nodes.label: Stanislav Grof
nodes.image: Крістіна і Станіслав Грофи (Christina and Stanislav Grof) (cropped).JPG
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラフ・グロフ
nodes.summary: Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (~1950-1956). His career included posts at several psychiatric institutions, Johns Hopkins University (1967-1969), Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969-1973), Esalen Institute (1973-1987), and California Institute of Integral Studies (1994-2015).

variants: American School of Classical Studies in Rome
School of Classical Studies in the American Academy in Rome

nodes.label: Alfred Körte
nodes.summary: Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig University between circa 1895 and 1934.

nodes.label: Friedrich Leo
nodes.summary: Friedrich Leo was a linguist who studied at Bonn under Hermann Usener and at Göttingen. He held posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889-1914).

nodes.label: Walter Porzig
nodes.summary: Walter Porzig (1895–1961) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jena and under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at Leipzig University, University of Bern, University of Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

nodes.id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark

variants: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark

nodes.description: anthropologist, specialising in Tibetan beliefs and customs
nodes.summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics, later serving in the Office of Strategic Services from ~1942 to 1945.

nodes.label: Rudolf Thurneysen
nodes.summary: Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University (~1877–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1898), the University of Freiburg (~1898–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

nodes.label: Bedřich Hrozný
nodes.jawiki: ベドジフ・フロズニー
nodes.summary: Bedřich Hrozný (1879–1952) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1897–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1901–1902), later holding posts at Vienna (~1905–1919) and Charles University (~1919–1952).

nodes.id: I:Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis
nodes.label: Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis

nodes.label: Friedrich Nietzsche
variants: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Nietzsche worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn and Leipzig University under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and held a faculty post at the University of Basel (1869-1878).

nodes.label: Friedrich Delitzsch
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・デーリッチュ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Delitzsch specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig under Fleischer, Brockhaus, Curtius, and Windisch (~1868-1873) and in Berlin (~1871-1872). He held posts at the Universities of Breslau (~1893-1899) and Berlin (~1899-1920).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Roscher
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ロッシャー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ロッシャー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Roscher studied at the University of Göttingen (~1835–1838) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1838–1840). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1840–1848), Leipzig University (~1848–1894), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Gustav Mensching
nodes.summary: Gustav Mensching was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under Rudolf Otto. He held posts at the University of Latvia from 1927 to 1936 and the University of Bonn starting in 1936.

nodes.label: Rudolf Otto
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and comparative religionist (1869–1937)
nodes.summary: Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).

nodes.label: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer
nodes.summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (c. 1967–1969) and the University of Munich (c. 1969–1973), later holding posts at Munich (c. 1981–1993) and Göttingen (c. 1993–2015).

nodes.label: Franz Boas
nodes.summary: Franz Boas (1858–1942) was a linguist and anthropologist who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (circa 1896–1942).

nodes.label: Otto Jahn
nodes.description: German classical philologist, archaeologist and musicologist (1813-1869)
nodes.summary: Otto Jahn was a scholar of history/archaeology and related fields who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held positions at Kiel (~1839–1842), Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

nodes.label: Hans Küng
nodes.description: Swiss Catholic priest, theologian and author (1928-2021)
nodes.summary: Hans Küng (1928–2021) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and the Catholic University of Paris, and held a post at the University of Tübingen (ca. 1960–1996).

nodes.label: Clemente Merlo
nodes.summary: Clemente Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Pavia (~1899–1903) and held a post at the University of Pisa from circa 1908 to 1953.

nodes.label: Hermann Olshausen
nodes.summary: Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University (1814) and the University of Berlin (1816). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Königsberg (1827-1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834-1839).

nodes.id: I:Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
nodes.label: Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
variants: Musée national des arts et des traditions populaires

nodes.label: Dipa Ma
nodes.summary: Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Anagarika Munindra (circa 1967–1969) and Mahasi Sayadaw (circa 1967–1970).

nodes.label: Bernhard Forssman
nodes.description: German Indo-Europeanist, professor and non-fiction writer (born 1934)
nodes.summary: Bernhard Forssman specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1959–1964), and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

nodes.label: Rüdiger Schmitt
nodes.summary: Rüdiger Schmitt specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann from circa 1960 to 1965 and held a position at Saarland University from circa 1979 to 2004.

nodes.label: Heiner Eichner
nodes.summary: Heiner Eichner was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1964–1974) under Karl Hoffmann and later served on the faculty at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร
variants: Somdet Phra Sangharaja Chao Krommaluang Vajirañāṇasaṃvara
nodes.jawiki: ワシラガーナサンバラ
nodes.summary: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) studied Buddhism at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1933–1941) under Vajirayanavangsa and Satyananda Puri. He led Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961), taught meditation at Kasetsart University (1976), and served as abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013).

nodes.label: Vajirayanavangsa
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระสังฆราชเจ้า กรมหลวงวชิรญาณวงศ์

nodes.label: Boris Turayev
nodes.summary: Boris Turayev (1868–1920) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (circa 1887–1891). He taught at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1898–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920), where he instructed Otto Neugebauer and George de Roerich.

nodes.label: Abraham Sachs
variants: エイブラハム・ザックス
nodes.summary: Abraham Sachs (1914–1983) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1934–1939) and held appointments at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).

nodes.label: Zentralblatt MATH
variants: Zentralblatt für Mathematik und ihre Grenzgebiete (Zbl)
